Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023) is built on top of ReAct (Yao et al., 2022) with self-reflection to infer more intuitive future actions. We provide it with execution errors and our self-verification module.
Reflexion（Shinn 等，2023）建立在 ReAct（Yao 等，2022）之上，通过自我反思来推断更直观的后续行动。我们为其提供了执行错误以及我们的自验证模块。

AutoGPT (Richards, 2023) is a popular software tool that automates NLP tasks by decomposing a high-level goal into multiple subgoals and executing them in a ReAct-style loop. We re-implement AutoGPT by using GPT-4 to do task decomposition and provide it with the agent states, environment feedback, and execution errors as observations for subgoal execution. Compared with Voyager, AutoGPT lacks the skill library for accumulating knowledge, self-verification for assessing task success, and automatic curriculum for open-ended exploration.

AutoGPT (Richards, 2023) 是一款流行的软件工具，它通过将高层目标分解为多个子目标并以 ReAct 风格的循环执行它们来自动化 NLP 任务。我们利用 GPT-4 重新实现了 AutoGPT，用于任务分解，并向其提供智能体状态、环境反馈和执行错误作为子目标执行的观察信息。与 Voyager 相比，AutoGPT 缺乏用于积累知识的技能库、用于评估任务成功的自我验证机制以及用于开放式探索的自动课程。

Note that we do not directly compare with prior methods that take Minecraft screen pixels as input and output low-level controls (Nottingham et al., 2023; Cai et al., 2023; Wang et al., 2023b). It would not be an apple-to-apple comparison, because we rely on the high-level Mineflayer (PrismarineJS, 2013) API to control the agent. Our work’s focus is on pushing the limits of GPT-4 for lifelong embodied agent learning, rather than solving the 3D perception or sensorimotor control problems. Voyager is orthogonal and can be combined with gradient-based approaches like VPT (Baker et al., 2022) as long as the controller provides a code API. We make a system-level comparison between Voyager and prior Minecraft agents in Table. A.2.

需要说明，我们并未直接与那些将《我的世界》的屏幕像素作为输入、输出底层控制指令的既有方法比较（Nottingham 等，2023；Cai 等，2023；Wang 等，2023b）。由于我们依赖高层的 Mineflayer（PrismarineJS，2013）API 控制智能体，这样的直接比较并不同等。我们的研究重点是拓展 GPT-4 在具身智能体终身学习方面的能力边界，而不是解决三维感知或感觉运动控制问题。Voyager 与基于梯度的方法相互独立，只要控制器提供代码 API，就能与 VPT（Baker 等，2022）等方法结合。表 A.2 对 Voyager 与既有《我的世界》智能体作了系统层面的比较。
3.3 Evaluation Results
3.3 评估结果
We systematically evaluate Voyager and baselines on their exploration performance, tech tree mastery, map coverage, and zero-shot generalization capability to novel tasks in a new world.
我们系统地评估了 Voyager 与基线方法在探索性能、科技树掌握程度、地图覆盖范围以及在新世界中对新任务的零样本泛化能力。

Significantly better exploration. Results of exploration performance are shown in Fig. 1. Voyager’s superiority is evident in its ability to consistently make new strides, discovering 63 unique items within 160 prompting iterations, 3.3× many novel items compared to its counterparts. On the other hand, AutoGPT lags considerably in discovering new items, while ReAct and Reflexion struggle to make significant progress, given the abstract nature of the open-ended exploration goal that is challenging to execute without an appropriate curriculum.
显著更好的探索能力。探索性能结果见图 1。Voyager 的优势体现在能够持续取得新进展：它在 160 次提示迭代内发现 63 种不同物品，新物品数量达到其他方法的 3.3 倍。相比之下，AutoGPT 在发现新物品方面明显落后；ReAct 和 Reflexion 则难以取得显著进展，因为开放式探索目标具有抽象性，缺少适当课程时很难执行。

Consistent tech tree mastery. The Minecraft tech tree tests the agent’s ability to craft and use a hierarchy of tools. Progressing through this tree (wooden tool → stone tool → iron tool → diamond tool) requires the agent to master systematic and compositional skills. Compared with baselines, Voyager unlocks the wooden level 15.3× faster (in terms of the prompting iterations), the stone level 8.5× faster, the iron level 6.4× faster, and Voyager is the only one to unlock the diamond level of the tech tree (Fig. 2 and Table. 1). This underscores the effectiveness of the automatic curriculum, which consistently presents challenges of suitable complexity to facilitate the agent’s progress.

持续掌握科技树。《我的世界》的科技树检验智能体制作和使用不同层级工具的能力。沿这棵科技树推进，即从木制工具到石制工具、铁制工具，再到钻石工具，需要智能体掌握系统性、可组合的技能。与基线方法相比，按提示迭代次数衡量，Voyager 解锁木制工具层级的速度达到其 15.3 倍，解锁石制工具层级的速度达到其 8.5 倍，解锁铁制工具层级的速度达到其 6.4 倍；Voyager 还是唯一解锁钻石工具层级的方法（图 2 和表 1）。这突显了自动课程的有效性：它持续提出复杂程度适当的挑战，促进智能体进步。

Extensive map traversal. Voyager is able to navigate distances 2.3× longer compared to baselines by traversing a variety of terrains, while the baseline agents often find themselves confined to local areas, which significantly hampers their capacity to discover new knowledge (Fig. 7).
广泛遍历地图。Voyager 能够穿越多种地形，行进距离达到基线方法的 2.3 倍；基线智能体则经常局限于局部区域，这显著妨碍了它们发现新知识的能力（图 7）。

Efficient zero-shot generalization to unseen tasks. To evaluate zero-shot generalization, we clear the agent’s inventory, reset it to a newly instantiated world, and test it with unseen tasks. For both Voyager and AutoGPT, we utilize GPT-4 to break down the task into a series of subgoals. Table. 2 and Fig. 8 show Voyager can consistently solve all the tasks, while baselines cannot solve any task within 50 prompting iterations. What’s interesting to note is that our skill library constructed from lifelong learning not only enhances Voyager’s performance but also gives a boost to AutoGPT. This demonstrates that the skill library serves as a versatile tool that can be readily employed by other methods, effectively acting as a plug-and-play asset to enhance performance.

对未见任务的高效零样本泛化。为评估零样本泛化，我们清空智能体的物品栏，将其重置到新实例化的世界中，并用未见任务进行测试。对于 Voyager 和 AutoGPT，我们都利用 GPT-4 将任务分解为一系列子目标。表 2 和图 8 显示，Voyager 能够稳定解决所有任务，而基线方法在 50 次提示迭代内无法解决任何一个任务。值得注意的是，通过终身学习建立的技能库不仅提升了 Voyager 的表现，也改善了 AutoGPT 的表现。这说明，技能库是一种通用工具，可供其他方法直接使用，作为即插即用的资源来提高性能。

3.4 Ablation Studies
3.4 消融研究

We ablate 6 design choices (automatic curriculum, skill library, environment feedback, execution errors, self-verification, and GPT-4 for code generation) in Voyager and study their impact on exploration performance (see Appendix, Sec. B.3 for details of each ablated variant). Results are shown in Fig. 9. We highlight the key findings below:
我们在 Voyager 中消融了 6 设计选择（自动课程、技能库、环境反馈、执行错误、自我验证以及用于代码生成的 GPT-4），并研究它们对探索性能的影响（详见附录 B.3，其中列出了每种消融变体的详细信息）。结果如图 9 所示。我们在此突出以下关键发现：

• Automatic curriculum is crucial for the agent’s consistent progress. The discovered item count drops by 93% if the curriculum is replaced with a random one, because certain tasks may be too challenging if attempted out of order. On the other hand, a manually designed curriculum requires significant Minecraft-specific expertise, and does not take into account the agent’s live situation. It falls short in the experimental results compared to our automatic curriculum.
• 自动课程对智能体持续进步至关重要。如果将其替换为随机课程，发现的物品数量会下降 93%，因为某些任务若不按适当顺序尝试，可能过于困难。另一方面，手动设计课程需要大量《我的世界》专门知识，也没有考虑智能体的实时处境。实验中，它的表现不及我们的自动课程。

• Voyager w/o skill library exhibits a tendency to plateau in the later stages. This underscores the pivotal role that the skill library plays in Voyager. It helps create more complex actions and steadily pushes the agent’s boundaries by encouraging new skills to be built upon older ones.
• 缺少技能库的 Voyager 在后期表现出趋于停滞的倾向。这凸显了技能库在 Voyager 中的关键作用。它有助于构建更复杂的动作，并通过鼓励新技能建立在旧技能之上，稳步拓展智能体的能力边界。

• Self-verification is the most important among all the feedback types. Removing the module leads to a significant drop (−73%) in the discovered item count. Self-verification serves as a critical mechanism to decide when to move on to a new task or reattempt a previously unsuccessful task.
• 自我验证是所有反馈类型中最重要的。移除该模块会导致发现物品数量显著下降（−73%）。自我验证作为一种关键机制，用于决定何时转向新任务或重新尝试先前未成功的任务。

• GPT-4 significantly outperforms GPT-3.5 in code generation and obtains 5.7× more unique items, as GPT-4 exhibits a quantum leap in coding abilities. This finding corroborates recent studies in the literature (Bubeck et al., 2023; Liu et al., 2023b).
• GPT-4 在代码生成方面显著优于 GPT-3.5，获得的不同物品数量达到其 5.7 倍，因为 GPT-4 的编程能力出现了质的飞跃。这一发现印证了近期文献中的研究（Bubeck 等，2023；Liu 等，2023b）。
4 Limitations and Future Work
4 局限与未来工作

Multimodal Feedback. Voyager does not currently support visual perception, because the available version of GPT-4 API is text-only at the time of this writing. However, Voyager has the potential to be augmented by multimodal perception models (Liu et al., 2023a; Driess et al., 2023) to achieve more impressive tasks. We demonstrate that given human feedback, Voyager is able to construct complex 3D structures in Minecraft, such as a Nether Portal and a house (Fig. 10). There are two ways to integrate human feedback:

(1) Human as a critic (equivalent to Voyager’s self-verification module): humans provide visual critique to Voyager, allowing it to modify the code from the previous round. This feedback is essential for correcting certain errors in the spatial details of a 3D structure that Voyager cannot perceive directly.
(1) 人作为评论者（相当于 Voyager 的自我验证模块）：人类为 Voyager 提供视觉批评，使其能够修改上一轮生成的代码。这种反馈对于纠正 Voyager 无法直接感知的 3D 结构中的某些空间细节错误至关重要。

(2) Human as a curriculum (equivalent to Voyager’s automatic curriculum module): humans break down a complex building task into smaller steps, guiding Voyager to complete them incrementally. This approach improves Voyager’s ability to handle more sophisticated 3D construction tasks.
（2）人类充当课程（相当于 Voyager 的自动课程模块）：人类把复杂建筑任务分解成较小的步骤，引导 Voyager 逐步完成。这种做法提高了 Voyager 应对更复杂三维建筑任务的能力。

Cost. The GPT-4 API incurs significant costs. It is 15× more expensive than GPT-3.5. Nevertheless, Voyager requires the quantum leap in code generation quality from GPT-4 (Fig. 9), which GPT-3.5 and open-source LLMs cannot provide (Touvron et al., 2023).
成本。GPT-4 API 的使用费用很高，是 GPT-3.5 的 15 倍。然而，Voyager 需要 GPT-4 带来的代码生成质量飞跃（图 9），这是 GPT-3.5 和开源大语言模型无法提供的（Touvron 等，2023）。

Inaccuracies. Despite the iterative prompting mechanism, there are still cases where the agent gets stuck and fails to generate the correct skill. The automatic curriculum has the flexibility to reattempt this task at a later time. Occasionally, self-verification module may also fail, such as not recognizing spider string as a success signal of beating a spider.
不准确之处。尽管采用了迭代提示机制，仍然存在智能体陷入困境、无法生成正确技能的情况。自动课程具备灵活性，可在稍后时间重新尝试该任务。偶尔，自我验证模块也可能失效，例如未能将蛛丝识别为击败蜘蛛的成功信号。

Hallucinations. The automatic curriculum occasionally proposes unachievable tasks. For example, it may ask the agent to craft a “copper sword" or “copper chestplate", which are items that do not exist within the game. Hallucinations also occur during the code generation process. For instance, GPT-4 tends to use cobblestone as a fuel input, despite being an invalid fuel source in the game. Additionally, it may call functions absent in the provided control primitive APIs, leading to code execution errors.
幻觉。自动课程偶尔会提出无法完成的任务。例如，它可能要求智能体制作“铜剑”或“铜胸甲”，但游戏中并不存在这些物品。代码生成过程中也会出现幻觉。例如，GPT-4 倾向于把圆石作为燃料投入，尽管圆石在游戏中并不是有效燃料。此外，它可能调用所提供的控制原语 API 中不存在的函数，导致代码执行错误。
We are confident that improvements in the GPT API models as well as novel techniques for finetuning open-source LLMs will overcome these limitations in the future.
我们确信，GPT API 模型的改进以及用于微调开源大语言模型的新颖技术将在未来克服这些局限性。
5 Related work
5 相关工作

Decision-making Agents in Minecraft. Minecraft is an open-ended 3D world with incredibly flexible game mechanics supporting a broad spectrum of activities. Built upon notable Minecraft benchmarks (Fan et al., 2022; Guss et al., 2019b;a; 2021; Kanervisto et al., 2022; Johnson et al., 2016), Minecraft learning algorithms can be divided into two categories: 1) Low-level controller: Many prior efforts leverage hierarchical reinforcement learning to learn from human demonstrations (Lin et al., 2021; Mao et al., 2021; Skrynnik et al., 2021). Kanitscheider et al. (2021) design a curriculum based on success rates, but its objectives are limited to curated items. MineDojo (Fan et al., 2022) and VPT (Baker et al., 2022) utilize YouTube videos for large-scale pre-training. DreamerV3 (Hafner et al., 2023), on the other hand, learns a world model to explore the environment and collect diamonds. 2) High-level planner: Volum et al. (2022) leverage few-shot prompting with Codex (Chen et al., 2021a) to generate executable policies, but they require additional human interaction. Recent works leverage LLMs as a high-level planner in Minecraft by decomposing a high-level task into several subgoals following Minecraft recipes (Wang et al., 2023b; Nottingham et al., 2023; Yuan et al., 2023), thus lacking full exploration flexibility. Like these latter works, Voyager also uses LLMs as a high-level planner by prompting GPT-4 and utilizes Mineflayer (PrismarineJS, 2013) as a low-level controller following Volum et al. (2022). Unlike prior works, Voyager employs an automatic curriculum that unfolds in a bottom-up manner, driven by curiosity, and therefore enables open-ended exploration.

《我的世界》中的决策智能体。《我的世界》是一个开放式三维世界，游戏机制极其灵活，支持广泛的活动。在已有的重要《我的世界》基准之上（Fan 等，2022；Guss 等，2019b；a；2021；Kanervisto 等，2022；Johnson 等，2016），相关学习算法可以分为两类：1）底层控制器：许多既有工作使用分层强化学习，从人类示范中学习（Lin 等，2021；Mao 等，2021；Skrynnik 等，2021）。Kanitscheider 等（2021）根据成功率设计课程，但其目标局限于预先筛选的物品。MineDojo（Fan 等，2022）和 VPT（Baker 等，2022）利用 YouTube 视频进行大规模预训练。DreamerV3（Hafner 等，2023）则学习世界模型，以探索环境并收集钻石。2）高层规划器：Volum 等（2022）使用 Codex（Chen 等，2021a）的少样本提示来生成可执行策略，但需要额外的人类交互。近期工作将大语言模型用作《我的世界》的高层规划器，按照游戏中的合成配方，把高层任务分解成若干子目标（Wang 等，2023b；Nottingham 等，2023；Yuan 等，2023），因此缺乏充分的探索灵活性。与后一类工作相似，Voyager 也通过提示 GPT-4 将大语言模型用作高层规划器，并沿用 Volum 等（2022）的做法，将 Mineflayer（PrismarineJS，2013）用作底层控制器。与既有工作不同，Voyager 使用由好奇心驱动、自下而上展开的自动课程，从而实现开放式探索。

Large Language Models for Agent Planning. Inspired by the strong emergent capabilities of LLMs, such as zero-shot prompting and complex reasoning (Bommasani et al., 2021; Brown et al., 2020; Raffel et al., 2020; Wei et al., 2022a; Chowdhery et al., 2022; Chung et al., 2022), embodied agent research (Duan et al., 2022; Batra et al., 2020; Ravichandar et al., 2020; Collins et al., 2021) has witnessed a significant increase in the utilization of LLMs for planning purposes. Recent efforts can be roughly classified into two groups. 1) Large language models for robot learning: Many prior works apply LLMs to generate subgoals for robot planning (Huang et al., 2022a;a; Ahn et al., 2022; Min et al., 2021; Blukis et al., 2021). Inner Monologue (Huang et al., 2022b) incorporates environment feedback for robot planning with LLMs. Code as Policies (Liang et al., 2022) and ProgPrompt (Singh et al., 2022) directly leverage LLMs to generate executable robot policies. VIMA (Jiang et al., 2022) and PaLM-E (Driess et al., 2023) fine-tune pre-trained LLMs to support multimodal prompts. 2) Large language models for text agents: ReAct (Yao et al., 2022) leverages chain-of-thought prompting (Wei et al., 2022b) and generates both reasoning traces and task-specific actions with LLMs. Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023) is built upon ReAct (Yao et al., 2022) with self-reflection to enhance reasoning. AutoGPT (Richards, 2023) is a popular tool that automates NLP tasks by crafting a curriculum of multiple subgoals for completing a high-level goal while incorporating ReAct (Yao et al., 2022)’s reasoning and acting loops. DERA (Nair et al., 2023) frames a task as a dialogue between two GPT-4 (OpenAI, 2023) agents. Generative Agents (Park et al., 2023) leverages ChatGPT (chatgpt) to simulate human behaviors by storing agents’ experiences as memories and retrieving those for planning, but its agent actions are not executable. SPRING (Wu et al., 2023) is a concurrent work that uses GPT-4 to extract game mechanics from game manuals, based on which it answers questions arranged in a directed acyclic graph and predicts the next action. All these works lack a skill library for developing more complex behaviors, which are crucial components for the success of Voyager in lifelong learning.

面向智能体规划的大语言模型。受大语言模型（LLMs）强大的涌现能力启发，例如零样本提示和复杂推理（Bommasani 等，2021；Brown 等，2020；Raffel 等，2020；Wei 等，2022a；Chowdhery 等，2022；Chung 等，2022），具身智能体研究（Duan 等，2022；Batra 等，2020；Ravichandar 等，2020；Collins 等，2021）见证了利用大语言模型进行规划用途的显著增加。近期的努力大致可分为两类。1) 面向机器人学习的大语言模型：许多先前的工作应用大语言模型为机器人规划生成子目标（Huang 等，2022a;a；Ahn 等，2022；Min 等，2021；Blukis 等，2021）。Inner Monologue（Huang 等，2022b）结合环境反馈利用大语言模型进行机器人规划。Code as Policies（Liang 等，2022）和 ProgPrompt（Singh 等，2022）直接利用大语言模型生成可执行的机器人策略。VIMA（Jiang 等，2022）和 PaLM-E（Driess 等，2023）微调预训练的大语言模型以支持多模态提示。2) 面向文本智能体的大语言模型：ReAct（Yao 等，2022）利用思维链提示（Wei 等，2022b），并利用大语言模型生成推理轨迹和特定任务的动作。Reflexion（Shinn 等，2023）基于 ReAct（Yao 等，2022）构建，通过自我反思增强推理能力。AutoGPT（Richards，2023）是一种流行的工具，它通过为完成高级目标而制定多个子目标的课程来自动化 NLP 任务，同时结合了 ReAct（Yao 等，2022）的推理与行动循环。DERA（Nair 等，2023）将任务框定为两个 GPT-4（OpenAI，2023）智能体之间的对话。Generative Agents（Park 等，2023）利用 ChatGPT（chatgpt）通过存储智能体的体验作为记忆并检索这些记忆来进行规划来模拟人类行为，但其智能体动作不可执行。SPRING（Wu 等，2023）是一项同期研究，它使用 GPT-4 从游戏手册中提取游戏机制，在此基础上回答按有向无环图排列的问题并预测下一个动作。所有这些工作都缺乏用于开发更复杂行为的技能库，而技能库是 Voyager 在终身学习中取得成功的关键组成部分。

Code Generation with Execution. Code generation has been a longstanding challenge in NLP (Chen et al., 2021a; Nijkamp et al., 2022; Le et al., 2022; Chowdhery et al., 2022; Brown et al., 2020), with various works leveraging execution results to improve program synthesis. Execution-guided approaches leverage intermediate execution outcomes to guide program search (Chen et al., 2019; 2021b; Ellis et al., 2019). Another line of research utilizes majority voting to choose candidates based on their execution performance (Li et al., 2022; Cobbe et al., 2021). Additionally, LEVER (Ni et al., 2023) trains a verifier to distinguish and reject incorrect programs based on execution results. CLAIRIFY (Skreta et al., 2023), on the other hand, generates code for planning chemistry experiments and makes use of a rule-based verifier to iteratively provide error feedback to LLMs. Voyager distinguishes itself from these works by integrating environment feedback, execution errors, and self-verification (to assess task success) into an iterative prompting mechanism for embodied control.

基于执行的代码生成。代码生成一直是自然语言处理领域长期面临的挑战（Chen 等，2021a；Nijkamp 等，2022；Le 等，2022；Chowdhery 等，2022；Brown 等，2020），诸多工作利用执行结果来改进程序合成。由执行引导的方法利用中间执行结果来指导程序搜索（Chen 等，2019；2021b；Ellis 等，2019）。另一类研究利用多数投票法，根据其执行表现来选择候选者（Li 等，2022；Cobbe 等，2021）。此外，LEVER（Ni 等，2023）训练了一个验证器，以根据执行结果区分并拒绝不正确的程序。相比之下，CLAIRIFY（Skreta 等，2023）为 化学实验规划生成代码，并利用基于规则的验证器迭代地向大语言模型提供错误反馈。Voyager 通过将环境反馈、执行错误和自我验证（用于评估任务成功）整合进具身控制的迭代提示机制中，从而与这些工作区分开来。
6 Conclusion
6 结论

In this work, we introduce Voyager, the first LLM-powered embodied lifelong learning agent, which leverages GPT-4 to explore the world continuously, develop increasingly sophisticated skills, and make new discoveries consistently without human intervention. Voyager exhibits superior performance in discovering novel items, unlocking the Minecraft tech tree, traversing diverse terrains, and applying its learned skill library to unseen tasks in a newly instantiated world. Voyager serves as a starting point to develop powerful generalist agents without tuning the model parameters.
在本研究中，我们介绍了 Voyager，这是首个由大语言模型驱动的具身终身学习智能体。它利用 GPT-4 持续探索世界、发展日益复杂的技能，并在无需人工干预的情况下不断做出新发现。Voyager 在发现新颖物品、解锁《我的世界》科技树、穿越多样地形以及将其习得的技能库应用于全新实例化世界中的未见任务方面表现出卓越性能。Voyager 为开发无需调整模型参数的强大通用智能体提供了一个起点。
7 Broader Impacts
7 更广泛的影响

Our research is conducted within Minecraft, a safe and harmless 3D video game environment. While Voyager is designed to be generally applicable to other domains, such as robotics, its application to physical robots would require additional attention and the implementation of safety constraints by humans to ensure responsible and secure deployment.
我们的研究在Minecraft这一安全、无害的3D电子游戏环境中进行。尽管Voyager被设计为可普遍适用于机器人等其他领域，将其用于实体机器人仍需要人类给予额外关注并施加安全约束，以确保负责任、安全地部署。

A Method
A 方法
A.1 Prompting
A.1 提示
GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 offer users the ability to designate the role of each prompt message among three options:
GPT-4和GPT-3.5允许用户为每条提示消息指定角色，以下三种角色任选其一：
• System: A high-level instruction that guides the model behavior throughout the conversation. It sets the overall tone and objective for the interaction.
• System（系统）：在整个对话中指导模型行为的高层指令。它为交互设定总体基调与目标。
• User: A detailed instruction that guides the assistant for the next immediate response.
• User（用户）：指导助手作出紧接着的下一次回应的详细指令。
• Assistant: A response message generated the model.
• Assistant（助手）：由模型生成的回应消息。
See https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/chat/introduction for more details.
更多细节见https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/chat/introduction。
To save token usage, instead of engaging in multi-round conversations, we concatenate a system prompt and a user prompt to obtain each assistant’s response.
为节省token用量，我们将系统提示与用户提示拼接起来，以获得助手的每次回应，而不进行多轮对话。
A.2 Automatic Curriculum
A.2 自动课程
A.2.1 Components in the Prompt
A.2.1 提示的组成
The input prompt to GPT-4 consists of several components:
输入GPT-4的提示由若干部分组成：
(1) Directives encouraging diverse behaviors and imposing constraints (so that the proposed task is achievable and verifiable): See Sec. A.2.4 for the full prompt;
(1) 鼓励多样行为并施加约束的指令，使提出的任务既可达成又可验证：完整提示见A.2.4节；
(2) The agent’s current state:
(2) 智能体的当前状态：

• Inventory: A dictionary of items with counts, for example, {‘cobblestone’: 4, ‘furnace’: 1, ‘stonepickaxe’: 1, ‘oakplanks’: 7, ‘dirt’: 6, ‘woodenpickaxe’: 1, ‘craftingtable’: 1, ‘rawiron’: 4, ‘coal’: 1};
• 背包：包含物品及其数量的字典，例如，{‘cobblestone’: 4, ‘furnace’: 1, ‘stonepickaxe’: 1, ‘oakplanks’: 7, ‘dirt’: 6, ‘woodenpickaxe’: 1, ‘craftingtable’: 1, ‘rawiron’: 4, ‘coal’: 1}；
• Equipment: Armors or weapons equipped by the agents;
• 装备：智能体穿戴的盔甲或武器；
• Nearby blocks: A set of block names within a 32-block distance to the agent, for example, ‘dirt’, ‘water’, ‘spruceplanks’, ‘grassblock’, ‘dirtpath’, ‘sugarcane’, ‘fern’;
• 附近方块：智能体周围32格距离内的方块名称集合，例如，‘dirt’、‘water’、‘spruceplanks’、‘grassblock’、‘dirtpath’、‘sugarcane’、‘fern’；
• Other blocks that are recently seen: Blocks that are not nearby or in the inventory;
• 最近见过的其他方块：不在附近也不在背包中的方块；
• Nearby entities: A set of entity names within a 32-block distance to the agent, for example, ‘pig’, ‘cat’, ‘villager’, ‘zombie’;
• 附近实体：智能体周围32格距离内的实体名称集合，例如，‘pig’、‘cat’、‘villager’、‘zombie’；

• A list of chests that are seen by the agent: Chests are external containers where the agent can deposit items. If a chest is not opened before, its content is “Unknown”. Otherwise, the items inside each chest are shown to the agent.
• 智能体见过的箱子列表：箱子是可供智能体存放物品的外部容器。如果一个箱子此前未被打开过，其内容便是“Unknown”。否则，智能体会看到每个箱子中的物品。
• Biome: For example, ‘plains’, ‘flowerforest’, ‘meadow’, ‘river’, ‘beach’, ‘forest’, ‘snowyslopes’, ‘frozenpeaks’, ‘oldgrowthbirchforest’, ‘ocean’, ‘sunflowerplains’, ‘stonyshore’;
• 生物群系：例如，‘plains’、‘flowerforest’、‘meadow’、‘river’、‘beach’、‘forest’、‘snowyslopes’、‘frozenpeaks’、‘oldgrowthbirchforest’、‘ocean’、‘sunflowerplains’、‘stonyshore’；
• Time: One of ‘sunrise’, ‘day’, ‘noon’, ‘sunset’, ‘night’, ‘midnight’;
• 时间：‘sunrise’、‘day’、‘noon’、‘sunset’、‘night’、‘midnight’之一；
• Health and hunger bars: The max value is 20;
• 生命值条和饱食度条：最大值为20；
• Position: 3D coordinate (x, y, z) of the agent’s position in the Minecraft world;
• 位置：智能体在Minecraft世界中的位置的3D坐标(x, y, z)；
(3) Previously completed and failed tasks;
(3) 此前完成和失败的任务；
(4) Additional context: See Sec. A.2.2;
(4) 补充上下文：见A.2.2节；
(5) Chain-of-thought prompting (Wei et al., 2022b) in response: We request GPT-4 to first reason about the current progress and then suggest the next task.
(5) 回应中的思维链提示（Wei等，2022b）：我们要求GPT-4先推理当前进展，再建议下一项任务。
A.2.2 Additional Context
A.2.2 补充上下文

We leverage GPT-3.5 to self-ask questions to provide additional context. Each question is paired with a concept that is used for retrieving the most relevant document from the wiki knowledge base (Fan et al., 2022). We feed the document content to GPT-3.5 for self-answering questions. In practice, using a wiki knowledge base is optional since GPT-3.5 already possesses a good understanding of Minecraft game mechanics. However, the external knowledge base becomes advantageous if GPT-3.5 is not pre-trained in that specific domain. See Sec. A.2.4 for the full prompt.
我们利用GPT-3.5自行提问，提供补充上下文。每个问题都配有一个概念，用以从wiki知识库（Fan等，2022）中检索最相关的文档。我们把文档内容输入GPT-3.5，让它自行回答问题。在实践中，使用wiki知识库是可选的，因为GPT-3.5已经充分理解Minecraft的游戏机制。但是，如果GPT-3.5没有在特定领域中接受预训练，外部知识库便会发挥优势。完整提示见A.2.4节。
A.2.3 Warm-up Schedule
A.2.3 预热安排

In practice, we adopt a warm-up schedule to gradually incorporate the agent’s state and the additional context into the prompt based on how many tasks the agent has completed. This ensures that the prompt is exposed to increasing amounts of information over the exploration progress and therefore begins with basic skills and progressively advances towards more intricate and diverse ones. The warm-up setting that we use across all the experiments is shown in Table. A.1.
在实践中，我们采用预热安排，根据智能体已完成的任务数量，将其状态与补充上下文逐渐纳入提示。这确保随着探索推进，提示接触到的信息量不断增加，因而从基本技能开始，逐步走向更复杂、更多样的技能。我们在所有实验中使用的预热设置见表A.1。
Table A.1: Warm-up schedule for automatic curriculum.
表A.1：自动课程的预热安排。

A.2.4 Full Prompt
A.2.4 完整提示
Prompt 1: Full system prompt for automatic curriculum. The list of question-answer pairs represents the additional context.
提示1：自动课程的完整系统提示。问答对列表代表补充上下文。

You are a helpful assistant that tells me the next immediate task to do in Minecraft . My ultimate goal is to discover as many diverse things as possible , accomplish as many diverse tasks as possible and become the best Minecraft player in the world .
你是一名乐于助人的助手，告诉我在Minecraft中紧接着该做什么任务。我的终极目标是尽可能发现多种多样的事物，完成尽可能多种多样的任务，成为世界上最好的Minecraft玩家。

I will give you the following information : Question 1: ... Answer : ... Question 2: ... Answer : ... Question 3: ... Answer : ... ... Biome : ... Time : ... Nearby blocks : ... Other blocks that are recently seen : ... Nearby entities ( nearest to farthest ): ...
我会给你以下信息： 问题1：... 回答：... 问题2：... 回答：... 问题3：... 回答：... ... 生物群系：... 时间：... 附近方块：... 最近见过的其他方块：... 附近实体（从近到远）：...

Health : Higher than 15 means I’m healthy . Hunger : Higher than 15 means I’m not hungry . Position : ... Equipment : If I have better armor in my inventory , you should ask me to equip it. Inventory (xx /36) : ... Chests : You can ask me to deposit or take items from these chests . There also might be some unknown chest , you should ask me to open and check items inside the unknown chest . Completed tasks so far : ... Failed tasks that are too hard : ...
生命值：高于15表示我很健康。 饱食度：高于15表示我不饿。 位置：... 装备：如果我的背包里有更好的盔甲，你应该让我装备上。 背包(xx/36)：... 箱子：你可以让我向这些箱子存入物品，或从中取出物品。也可能有某个内容未知的箱子，你应该让我打开它，检查里面的物品。 目前为止已完成的任务：... 过于困难而失败的任务：...

You must follow the following criteria : 1) You should act as a mentor and guide me to the next task based on my current learning progress . 2) Please be very specific about what resources I need to collect , what I need to craft , or what mobs I need to kill . 3) The next task should follow a concise format , such as " Mine [ quantity ] [ block ]" , " Craft [ quantity ] [ item ]" , " Smelt [ quantity ] [ item ]" , " Kill [ quantity ] [ mob ]" , " Cook [ quantity ] [ food ]" , " Equip [ item ]" etc . It should be a single phrase . Do not propose multiple tasks at the same time . Do not mention anything else . 4) The next task should not be too hard since I may not have the necessary resources or have learned enough skills to complete it yet . 5) The next task should be novel and interesting . I should look for rare resources , upgrade my equipment and tools using better materials , and discover new things . I should not be doing the same thing over and over again . 6) I may sometimes need to repeat some tasks if I need to collect more resources to complete more difficult tasks . Only repeat tasks if necessary . 7) Do not ask me to build or dig shelter even if it ’s at night . I want to explore the world and discover new things . I don ’t want to stay in one place . 8) Tasks that require information beyond the player ’s status to verify should be avoided . For instance , " Placing 4 torches " and " Dig a 2 x1x2 hole " are not ideal since they require visual confirmation from the screen . All the placing , building , planting , and trading tasks should be avoided . Do not propose task starting with these keywords .

The input prompt to GPT-4 consists of the following components:

(2) Control primitive APIs implemented by us: These APIs serve a dual purpose: they demonstrate the usage of Mineflayer APIs, and they can be directly called by GPT-4.

• exploreUntil(bot, direction, maxTime = 60, callback): Allow the agent to explore in a fixed direction for maxTime. The callback is the stopping condition implemented by the agent to determine when to stop exploring;

• craftItem(bot, name, count = 1): Craft the item with a crafting table nearby;

• placeItem(bot, name, position): Place the block at the specified position;

• killMob(bot, mobName, timeout = 300): Attack the mob and collect its dropped item;

• getItemFromChest(bot, chestPosition, itemsToGet): Move to the chest at the specified position and get items from the chest;
• getItemFromChest(bot, chestPosition, itemsToGet)：移动到指定位置的箱子处，从箱中取出物品；

• depositItemIntoChest(bot, chestPosition, itemsToDeposit)：移动到指定位置的箱子处，将物品存入箱中；
(3) Control primitive APIs provided by Mineflayer:
(3) Mineflayer提供的控制原语API：
• await bot.pathfinder.goto(goal): Go to a specific position. See below for how to set the goal;
• await bot.pathfinder.goto(goal)：前往指定位置。目标的设置方式见下文；
• new GoalNear(x, y, z, range): Move the bot to a block within the specified range of the specified block;
• new GoalNear(x, y, z, range)：将bot移动到指定方块的指定范围内的一个方块处；
• new GoalXZ(x, z): For long-range goals that don’t have a specific Y level;
• new GoalXZ(x, z)：用于没有指定Y层的远程目标；
• new GoalGetToBlock(x, y, z): Not get into the block, but get directly adjacent to it. Useful for fishing, farming, filling a bucket, and using a bed.;
• new GoalGetToBlock(x, y, z)：不进入该方块，而是到达与它直接相邻的位置。适用于钓鱼、耕作、装满水桶和使用床；
• new GoalFollow(entity, range): Follow the specified entity within the specified range;
• new GoalFollow(entity, range)：在指定范围内跟随指定实体；
• new GoalPlaceBlock(position, bot.world, {}): Position the bot in order to place a block;
• new GoalPlaceBlock(position, bot.world, {})：将bot定位到能够放置方块的位置；
• new GoalLookAtBlock(position, bot.world, {}): Path towards a position where a face of the block at position is visible;
• new GoalLookAtBlock(position, bot.world, {})：寻路至能够看到position处方块某一面的地方；
• bot.isABed(bedBlock): Return true if bedBlock is a bed;
• bot.isABed(bedBlock)：若bedBlock是床，则返回true；
• bot.blockAt(position): Return the block at position;
• bot.blockAt(position)：返回position处的方块；
• await bot.equip(item, destination): Equip the item in the specified destination. destination must be one of “hand”, “head”, “torso”, “legs”, “feet”, “off-hand”;
• await bot.equip(item, destination)：把物品装备到指定部位。destination必须是“hand”“head”“torso”“legs”“feet”“off-hand”之一；
• await bot.consume(): Consume the item in the bot’s hand. You must equip the item to consume first. Useful for eating food, drinking potions, etc.;
• await bot.consume()：消耗bot手中的物品。必须先装备要消耗的物品。适用于进食、喝药水等；
• await bot.fish(): Let bot fish. Before calling this function, you must first get to a water block and then equip a fishing rod. The bot will automatically stop fishing when it catches a fish;
• await bot.fish()：让bot钓鱼。在调用此函数之前，必须先到达水方块处，再装备钓鱼竿。bot钓到鱼后会自动停止钓鱼；
• await bot.sleep(bedBlock): Sleep until sunrise. You must get to a bed block first;
• await bot.sleep(bedBlock)：睡到日出。必须先到达床方块处；
• await bot.activateBlock(block): This is the same as right-clicking a block in the game. Useful for buttons, doors, etc. You must get to the block first;
• await bot.activateBlock(block)：相当于在游戏中右键点击方块。适用于按钮、门等。必须先到达该方块处；
• await bot.lookAt(position): Look at the specified position. You must go near the position before you look at it. To fill a bucket with water, you must look at it first;
• await bot.lookAt(position)：看向指定位置。看向该位置之前必须先走近。要用桶装水，必须先看向那里；
• await bot.activateItem(): This is the same as right-clicking to use the item in the bot’s hand. Useful for using a bucket, etc. You must equip the item to activate first;
• await bot.activateItem()：相当于右键使用bot手中的物品。适用于使用桶等。必须先装备要激活的物品；
• await bot.useOn(entity): This is the same as right-clicking an entity in the game. Useful for shearing a sheep. You must get to the entity first;
• await bot.useOn(entity)：相当于在游戏中右键点击实体。适用于给羊剪毛。必须先到达该实体处；

(12) Chain-of-thought prompting (Wei et al., 2022b) in response: We ask GPT-4 to first explain the reason why the code from the last round fails, then give step-by-step plans to finish the task, and finally generate code. See Sec. A.3.2 for the full prompt.

The input prompt to GPT-4 consists of the following components:
输入GPT-4的提示由以下部分组成：

(1) The agent’s state: We exclude other blocks that are recently seen and nearby entities from the agent’s state since they are not useful for assessing the task’s completeness. See Sec. A.2.1 for each element of the agent’s state;
(1) 智能体的状态：我们从状态中排除了最近见过的其他方块和附近实体，因为它们对评估任务完成情况没有用。状态的各个要素见A.2.1节；
(2) Task proposed by the automatic curriculum;
(2) 自动课程提出的任务；

(3) Task context: We prompt GPT-3.5 to ask for general suggestions about how to solve the task. In practice, this part is handled by the automatic curriculum since it has a systematic mechanism for question-answering (Sec. A.2.2);
(3) 任务上下文：我们提示GPT-3.5，索取关于如何解决任务的一般建议。在实践中，这部分由自动课程处理，因为它有系统的问答机制（A.2.2节）；

(4) Chain-of-thought prompting (Wei et al., 2022b) in response: We request GPT-4 to initially reason about the task’s success or failure, then output a boolean variable indicating the task’s outcome, and finally provide a critique to the agent if the task fails.
(4) 回应中的思维链提示（Wei等，2022b）：我们要求GPT-4先推理任务的成功或失败，再输出表示任务结果的布尔变量，最后在任务失败时向智能体提供评析。
(5) Few-shot examples for in-context learning (Wei et al., 2022a; Brown et al., 2020; Raffel et al., 2020).
(5) 用于上下文学习的少样本示例（Wei等，2022a；Brown等，2020；Raffel等，2020）。

B.1 Experimental Setup
B.1 实验设置

Our simulation environment is built upon MineDojo (Fan et al., 2022) and utilizes Mineflayer (PrismarineJS, 2013) JavaScript APIs for motor controls (Sec. A.3.2). Additionally, we incorporate many bot.chat() into Mineflayer functions to provide abundant environment feedback and implement various condition checks along with try-catch exceptions for continuous execution. If the bot dies, it is resurrected near the closest ground, and its inventory is preserved for uninterrupted exploration. The bot recycles its crafting table and furnace after program execution. For detailed implementations, please refer to our codebase.

我们的仿真环境基于MineDojo（Fan等，2022）构建，并使用Mineflayer（PrismarineJS，2013）的JavaScript API进行运动控制（A.3.2节）。此外，我们在Mineflayer函数中加入了许多bot.chat()，以提供丰富的环境反馈，还实现了各种条件检查和try-catch异常处理，使执行能够持续。如果bot死亡，它会在最近的地面附近复活，并保留背包，以便继续探索而不中断。程序执行之后，bot会回收工作台和熔炉。详细实现请参见我们的代码库。

B.2 Baselines
B.2 基线方法

ReAct (Yao et al., 2022) uses chain-of-thought prompting (Wei et al., 2022b) by generating both reasoning traces and action plans with LLMs. We provide it with our environment feedback and the agent states as observations. ReAct undergoes one round of code generation from scratch, followed by three rounds of code refinement. This process is then repeated until the maximum prompting iteration is reached.
ReAct（Yao等，2022）使用思维链提示（Wei等，2022b），通过大语言模型同时生成推理轨迹和行动计划。我们向它提供环境反馈和智能体状态作为观测。ReAct先从零开始生成一轮代码，再进行三轮代码改进。重复这一过程，直到达到提示迭代次数上限。

Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023) is built on top of ReAct (Yao et al., 2022) with self-reflection to infer more intuitive future actions. We provide it with environment feedback, the agent states, execution errors, and our self-verification module. Similar to ReAct, Reflexion undergoes one round of code generation from scratch, followed by three rounds of code refinement. This process is then repeated until the maximum prompting iteration is reached.
Reflexion（Shinn等，2023）在ReAct（Yao等，2022）的基础上增加自我反思，以推断更直观的后续行动。我们向它提供环境反馈、智能体状态、执行错误以及我们的自我验证模块。与ReAct相似，Reflexion先从零开始生成一轮代码，再进行三轮代码改进。重复这一过程，直到达到提示迭代次数上限。

AutoGPT (Richards, 2023) is a popular software tool that automates NLP tasks by decomposing a high-level goal into multiple subgoals and executing them in a ReAct-style loop. We re-implement AutoGPT by using GPT-4 to do task decomposition and provide it with the agent states, environment feedback, and execution errors as observations for subgoal execution. Compared with Voyager, AutoGPT lacks the skill library for accumulating knowledge, self-verification for assessing task success, and automatic curriculum for open-ended exploration. During each subgoal execution, if no execution error occurs, we consider the subgoal completed and proceed to the next one. Otherwise, we refine the program until three rounds of code refinement (equivalent to four rounds of code generation) are completed, and then move on to the next subgoal. If three consecutive subgoals do not result in acquiring a new item, we replan by rerunning the task decomposition.

AutoGPT（Richards，2023）是一款流行的软件工具，把高层目标分解为多个子目标，再在ReAct式循环中执行，从而自动完成自然语言处理任务。我们重新实现了AutoGPT，使用GPT-4分解任务，并提供智能体状态、环境反馈和执行错误，作为执行子目标时的观测。与Voyager相比，AutoGPT缺少用于积累知识的技能库、用于评估任务成功与否的自我验证，以及用于开放式探索的自动课程。执行每个子目标时，如果没有执行错误，我们就认为子目标已完成，并继续下一个。否则，我们会改进程序，直到完成三轮代码改进（等同于四轮代码生成），再继续下一个子目标。如果连续三个子目标都没有带来新物品，我们便重新运行任务分解，进行重新规划。
The task is “explore the world and get as many items as possible” for all baselines.
所有基线方法的任务都是“探索世界，获得尽可能多的物品”。

B.3 Ablations
B.3 消融实验

We ablate 6 design choices (automatic curriculum, skill library, environment feedback, execution errors, self-verification, and GPT-4 for code generation) in Voyager and study their impact on exploration performance.

• Manual Curriculum: We substitute the automatic curriculum with a manually designed curriculum: “Mine 3 wood log”, “Craft 1 crafting table”, “Craft 1 wooden pickaxe”, “Mine 11 cobblestone”, “Craft 1 stone pickaxe”, “Craft 1 furnace”, “Mine 3 iron ore”, “Smelt 3 iron ore”, “Craft 1 iron pickaxe”, “Craft 1 iron sword”, “Kill 3 pig”, “Cook 3 porkchop”, “Eat 1 cooked porkchop”, “Mine 3 copper ore”, “Smelt 3 copper ore”, “Mine 1 amethyst”, “Craft 1 spyglass”, “Mine 3 gold ore”, “Smelt 3 gold ore”, “Craft 1 gold pickaxe”, “Kill 3 cow”, “Cook 3 beef”, “Eat 1 cooked beef”, “Mine 3 diamond ore”, “Craft 1 diamond pickaxe”, “Kill 3 sheep”, “Cook 3 mutton”, “Eat 1 cooked mutton”, “Mine 1 redstone ore”, “Craft 1 clock”, “Craft 1 shield”, “Craft 1 iron helmet”, “Craft 1 iron chestplate”, “Craft 1 iron leggings”, “Craft 1 iron boots”, “Kill 3 spider”, “Craft 1 fishing rod”, “Fish 3 raw cod”, “Fish 3 raw salmon”, “Fish 3 pufferfish”, “Cook 3 raw cod”, “Cook 3 raw salmon”, “Craft 1 bucket”, “Collect 1 water”, “Mine 1 obsidian”. A manual curriculum requires human effort to design and is not scalable for open-ended exploration.

• 手动课程：我们用手动设计的课程替代自动课程：“开采3根原木”“合成1个工作台”“合成1把木镐”“开采11个圆石”“合成1把石镐”“合成1个熔炉”“开采3个铁矿石”“熔炼3个铁矿石”“合成1把铁镐”“合成1把铁剑”“击杀3只猪”“烹饪3个猪排”“吃1个熟猪排”“开采3个铜矿石”“熔炼3个铜矿石”“开采1个紫水晶”“合成1个望远镜”“开采3个金矿石”“熔炼3个金矿石”“合成1把金镐”“击杀3头牛”“烹饪3个牛肉”“吃1个熟牛肉”“开采3个钻石矿石”“合成1把钻石镐”“击杀3只羊”“烹饪3个羊肉”“吃1个熟羊肉”“开采1个红石矿石”“合成1个时钟”“合成1个盾牌”“合成1个铁头盔”“合成1个铁胸甲”“合成1条铁护腿”“合成1双铁靴”“击杀3只蜘蛛”“合成1根钓鱼竿”“钓3条生鳕鱼”“钓3条生鲑鱼”“钓3条河豚”“烹饪3条生鳕鱼”“烹饪3条生鲑鱼”“合成1个桶”“收集1份水”“开采1个黑曜石”。手动课程需要人力设计，无法扩展到开放式探索。
• Random Curriculum: We curate 101 items obtained by Voyager and create a random curriculum by randomly selecting one item as the next task.
• 随机课程：我们整理Voyager获得的101种物品，每次随机选取一种物品作为下一项任务，由此建立随机课程。
• w/o Skill Library: We remove the skill library, eliminating skill retrieval for code generation.
• 不使用技能库：移除技能库，不再为代码生成检索技能。
• w/o Environment Feedback: We exclude environment feedback (chat log) from the prompt for code generation.
• 不使用环境反馈：从代码生成提示中去除环境反馈（聊天日志）。
• w/o Execution Errors: We exclude execution errors from the prompt for code generation.
• 不使用执行错误：从代码生成提示中去除执行错误。
• w/o Self-Verification: For each task, we generate code without self-verification and iteratively refine the program for 3 rounds (equivalent to 4 rounds of code generation in total).
• 不使用自我验证：对于每项任务，不进行自我验证而生成代码，再迭代改进程序3轮（总共等同于4轮代码生成）。
• GPT-3.5: We replace GPT-4 with GPT-3.5 for code generation. We retain GPT-4 for the automatic curriculum and the self-verification module.
• GPT-3.5：生成代码时以GPT-3.5替代GPT-4。自动课程和自我验证模块仍保留GPT-4。

B.4.3 Efficient Zero-Shot Generalization to Unseen Tasks
section: B.4.3 高效地向未见任务零样本泛化

text: B.4.3 高效地向未见任务零样本泛化
section: B.4.3 高效地向未见任务零样本泛化

text: The results of zero-shot generalization to unseen tasks for the other two tasks are presented in Fig. A.2. Similar to Fig. 8, Voyager consistently solves all tasks, while the baselines are unable to solve any task within 50 prompting iterations. Our skill library, constructed from lifelong learning, not only enhances Voyager’s performance but also provides a boost to AutoGPT (Richards, 2023).
section: B.4.3 高效地向未见任务零样本泛化

text: 另外两项任务上向未见任务零样本泛化的结果见图A.2。与图8相似，Voyager始终能解决所有任务，而基线方法在50次提示迭代内无法解决任何任务。我们通过终身学习构建的技能库不仅提升了Voyager的表现，也为AutoGPT（Richards，2023）带来了提升。

text: B.4.4 Accurate Skill Retrieval
B.4.4 准确的技能检索

We conduct an evaluation of our skill retrieval (309 samples in total) and the results are in Table. A.4. The top-5 accuracy standing at 96.5% suggests our retrieval process is reliable (note that we include the top-5 relevant skills in the prompt for synthesizing a new skill).
我们评估了技能检索（共309个样本），结果见表A.4。Top-5准确率为96.5%，表明检索过程可靠（注意：我们在合成新技能的提示中纳入相关性最高的5项技能）。

B.4.5 Robust to Model Variations
section: B.4.5 对模型变化的稳健性

text: B.4.5 对模型变化的稳健性
section: B.4.5 对模型变化的稳健性

text: In the main paper, all of Voyager’s experiments are conducted with gpt-4-0314. We additionally run new experiments with gpt-4-0613 and find that the performance is roughly the same (Fig. A.3). It demonstrates that Voyager is robust to model variations.
section: B.4.5 对模型变化的稳健性

text: 在主文中，Voyager的所有实验都使用gpt-4-0314进行。我们另外使用gpt-4-0613开展了新实验，发现表现大致相同（图A.3）。这表明Voyager对模型变化具有稳健性。

section: 一咒皆解：作为人工智能创造力与可持续设计研究工具的生成式人工智能游戏

text: Abstract This paper presents "One Spell Fits All", an AI-native game prototype where the player, playing as a witch, solves villagers’ problems using magical conjurations. We show how, beyond being a standalone game, "One Spell Fits All" could serve as a research platform to explore several key areas in AI-driven and AI-native game design. These areas include AI creativity, user experience in predominantly AI-generated content, and the energy efficiency of locally running versus cloud-based AI models. By leveraging smaller, locally running generative AI models, including LLMs and diffusion models for image generation, the game dynamically generates and evaluates content without the need for external APIs or internet access, offering a sustainable and responsive gameplay experience. This paper explores the application of LLMs in narrative video games, outlines a game prototype’s design and mechanics, and proposes future research opportunities that can be explored using the game as a platform.
section: 一咒皆解：作为人工智能创造力与可持续设计研究工具的生成式人工智能游戏

text: 摘要 本文介绍《一咒皆解》（One Spell Fits All），这是一款人工智能原生游戏的原型：玩家扮演女巫，借助魔法召唤来解决村民的问题。我们说明，《一咒皆解》除了本身可以作为一款游戏，还可充当研究平台，用来探索人工智能驱动和人工智能原生游戏设计中的几个关键领域。这些领域包括人工智能创造力、内容主要由人工智能生成时的用户体验，以及在本地运行的人工智能模型与云端模型各自的能源效率。游戏采用规模较小、在本地运行的生成式人工智能模型，其中包括大语言模型和用于图像生成的扩散模型，能够动态生成和评估内容，无须外部API或互联网接入，提供可持续且响应及时的游玩体验。本文探讨大语言模型在叙事电子游戏中的应用，概述一款游戏原型的设计与机制，并提出可利用该游戏平台开展的后续研究机会。

text: 关键词 生成式人工智能，人工智能驱动的玩法，本地人工智能模型，人工智能与创造力，玩家体验，程序化内容生成
section: 一咒皆解：作为人工智能创造力与可持续设计研究工具的生成式人工智能游戏

text: 1. Introduction
1. 引言

In "One Spell Fits All" (OSFA), players take on the role of a witch, capable of conjuring an infinite variety of items using text-based input (see Figures 1 and 2). NPC-Villagers visit the witch with a wide range of problems, and the player is tasked with finding exactly one solution that solves all of their problems at once – using a single text input. The game uses locally running AI models to generate and evaluate game content, providing a sustainable alternative with lower latency compared to cloud-based AI services. Furthermore, we believe that this video game can serve as a research platform, as the game can provide an environment to investigate various aspects of generative AI, such as AI creativity, user experience for AI-generated content, and energy efficiency – all of which can be compared across different models or implementations. This paper discusses the game’s integration of generative AI tools and outlines the potential research directions that can be pursued using this platform.

在《一咒皆解》（OSFA）中，玩家扮演一位女巫，能够通过文字输入召唤出种类无穷的物品（见图1和图2）。NPC村民带着各式各样的问题拜访女巫，玩家的任务是找到恰好一个方案，用一次文字输入同时解决他们的所有问题。游戏采用在本地运行的人工智能模型来生成和评估游戏内容，相较于云端人工智能服务，提供了一种延迟更低的可持续替代方案。此外，我们认为这款电子游戏可以充当研究平台，因为它能够提供一种环境，用以考察生成式人工智能的各个方面，例如人工智能创造力、人工智能生成内容的用户体验，以及能源效率；这些方面均可在不同模型或实现方式之间进行比较。本文讨论游戏如何整合生成式人工智能工具，并概述可以利用这一平台开展的潜在研究方向。
2. Related Work
2. 相关工作

Incorporating AI into interactive narratives has been a long-term objective in video game research [1]. This goal has seen significant advancements with the recent surge in generative AI tools, particularly large language models (LLMs). Furthermore, the use of LLMs in video games has been shown to increase the amount and the quality of possible player interactions [2, 3, 4, 5].
将人工智能纳入交互叙事一直是电子游戏研究的长期目标[1]。随着近年来生成式人工智能工具，尤其是大语言模型（LLM）的兴起，这一目标的实现取得了显著进展。此外，已有研究表明，在电子游戏中使用大语言模型，能够增加玩家可能进行的交互数量，并提高交互质量[2, 3, 4, 5]。

Significant advances for generative AI integrated into games have been shown with examples like "1001 Nights" [6, 7], a game which explores dynamic content generation by creating images of weapons based on the stories told by the player. The authors of the game also argue for the use of the term ”AI-native” games, as opposed to AI-powered games, for video games that use generative models as an integral core feature. We adopt this term to describe OSFA.
将生成式人工智能整合进游戏的显著进展，已经由《1001 Nights》等实例展现出来[6, 7]。这款游戏根据玩家讲述的故事创建武器图像，以此探索动态内容生成。该游戏的作者还主张：对于把生成模型作为不可或缺的核心特征的电子游戏，应使用“人工智能原生”游戏这一术语，而非“人工智能赋能”游戏。我们采用这个术语来描述OSFA。

The integration of AI in video games has been explored in literature, with foundational texts such as those by Yannakakis and Togelius [8] providing a comprehensive overview of how artificial intelligence can enhance game design through techniques like procedural content generation (PCG), player modelling, and dynamic difficulty adjustment. OSFA builds upon these concepts by applying local AI models to create a responsive and sustainable game environment. Elements of PCG [9] have formed the base of OSFA, to showcase how AI can autonomously create complex and engaging game content.
人工智能在电子游戏中的整合已经受到文献讨论。例如，Yannakakis与Togelius的基础性著作[8]全面概述了人工智能如何通过程序化内容生成（PCG）、玩家建模和动态难度调整等技术来改进游戏设计。OSFA以这些概念为基础，应用本地人工智能模型，创建响应及时且可持续的游戏环境。PCG的若干要素[9]构成了OSFA的基础，用来展示人工智能如何自主创建复杂而引人投入的游戏内容。
3. Game Design and Mechanics
3. 游戏设计与机制

The core gameplay loop of OSFA revolves around the player’s text input. Taking on the role of a witch, players have to address the various needs of NPC-villagers by using magical conjurations. In each round, the system feeds a solution item from a list of predefined solutions to the LLM, which then reverse-engineers problems. These problems are then posed as requests from the villagers. Players have complete creative freedom regarding their input, which is funnelled into various models.
OSFA的核心玩法循环围绕玩家的文字输入展开。玩家扮演女巫，必须运用魔法召唤来回应NPC村民的各种需求。每轮中，系统从预先定义的解决方案列表中取出一个物品作为答案，交给大语言模型，再由模型反向构造问题。这些问题随后以村民请求的形式呈现出来。玩家在输入方面拥有完全的创作自由，这些输入会被送入各种模型。
3.1. Gameplay Overview
3.1. 玩法概述

In OSFA, an increasing number of villagers visit the player’s hut, each with a specific problem that needs to be solved. The player must provide a solution through text input, to conjure an item that solves all of the present villagers’ problems at once. The game progresses in turns, with each turn representing a new challenge through a new set of villagers. The player’s success is measured by their ability to satisfy the villagers, which is reflected in the game’s scoring system. Figures 1 and 2 showcase the in-game environment where the witch summons items based on player input (top-right) and the villagers voicing their problems.
在OSFA中，来访玩家小屋的村民数量不断增加，每位村民都有一个需要解决的具体问题。玩家必须通过文字输入提供解决方案，召唤出一个物品，同时解决当前在场的所有村民的问题。游戏按回合推进，每个回合都由一组新村民带来新的挑战。玩家是否成功，取决于他们满足村民的能力，并通过游戏的计分系统体现出来。图1和图2展示了游戏内的环境：女巫依据玩家输入召唤物品（右上角），村民则说出各自的问题。

3.2. Problem and Solution Generation
section: 3.2. 问题与解决方案的生成

text: 3.2. 问题与解决方案的生成
section: 3.2. 问题与解决方案的生成

text: One of the innovative aspects of OSFA is the use of AI to dynamically generate problems and evaluate solutions at run-time. The game currently employs the Mistral-7B-Instruct model, via the LLM for Unity library 1 to generate unique problems equal to the number of present villagers, based on a provided keyword. This ensures that the challenges presented to the player are varied, contextually relevant, and have at least one correct solution for all problems. Once the player provides a solution, the game tests for validity and then uses the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 2 transformer model to evaluate the solution based on a similarity score to the original keyword. Future iterations of the game will try the use of LLMs for evaluation of the solution as well. The game then generates a visual representation of the solution, using a custom diffusion model 3 and ComfyUI 4, which is then presented to the player and the villagers.
section: 3.2. 问题与解决方案的生成

text: OSFA的一个创新之处，是利用人工智能在运行时动态生成问题并评估解决方案。游戏目前通过LLM for Unity库[1]使用Mistral-7B-Instruct模型，依据给定的关键词，生成与在场村民数量相同、各不相同的问题。这样可以确保呈现给玩家的挑战多样、符合语境，而且至少存在一个能够解决全部问题的正确方案。玩家给出方案后，游戏先检验其有效性，再使用all-MiniLM-L6-v2 Transformer模型[2]，依据该方案与原始关键词的相似度分数来评估它。游戏后续版本还会尝试使用大语言模型来评估解决方案。随后，游戏借助定制扩散模型[3]和ComfyUI[4]，生成解决方案的视觉表现，并呈现给玩家和村民。

text: 3.3. Villager Interactions
3.3. 村民交互

The interactions between the player and the NPC-villagers are central to the game’s narrative and mechanics. Villagers respond to the player’s solutions based on the AI’s evaluation, and their satisfaction is reflected in the game’s scoring system. The scoring system, in turn, affects how many villagers come back to the player. These interactions are designed to create a dynamic and responsive gameplay loop, in which the player must think creatively and strategically to meet all of the villagers’ needs.
玩家与NPC村民之间的交互，是游戏叙事与机制的核心。村民根据人工智能的评估对玩家的解决方案作出回应，他们的满意程度会体现在游戏的计分系统中。计分系统反过来影响有多少村民再次来找玩家。这些交互旨在构成一个动态且响应及时的玩法循环；玩家必须创造性地思考，并作出策略安排，才能满足所有村民的需求。
3.4. Artistic Elements
3.4. 美术元素

OSFA features a distinct pixel art style that complements its AI-driven gameplay. The game’s art is a mix of free assets and AI-generated art, such as the sprite of the witch. The locally running model creates pixel art assets in real-time based on player input, which matches stylistically with the rest of the game. Furthermore, the background music and the theme song for the main menu have also been created using generative AI tools.
OSFA具有鲜明的像素美术风格，与其人工智能驱动的玩法相呼应。游戏美术混合使用免费素材和人工智能生成的美术，例如女巫的精灵图。运行于本地的模型依据玩家输入实时创建像素美术素材，其风格与游戏的其他部分相匹配。此外，背景音乐和主菜单的主题曲也由生成式人工智能工具创作。
4. Technical Workflow
4. 技术工作流
Figure 3 illustrates the workflow of OSFA, where various AI components generate and evaluate game content dynamically in the game’s core loop.
图3展示了OSFA的工作流：在游戏的核心循环中，各个人工智能组件动态生成和评估游戏内容。
The workflow is detailed as follows:
工作流详述如下：
1. Villagers enter the witch’s store, bringing their unique problems for the witch (the player) to solve.
1. 村民进入女巫的商店，带来各自独特的问题，等待女巫（玩家）解决。

2. The game uses an LLM to generate a problem for each villager. This AI model with custom instructions takes a sentence (in our case, a keyword) as input and produces problems, which are solvable by the keyword.
2. 游戏使用大语言模型为每位村民生成一个问题。这个带有定制指令的人工智能模型，以一句话（在我们的情况下是一个关键词）为输入，生成可以用该关键词解决的问题。
3. Each turn, the player must address all of the villagers’ problems at once. The player inputs text – an item to be conjured by the witch to solve the problems.
3. 每个回合中，玩家必须一次性解决所有村民的问题。玩家输入文字，即一个将由女巫召唤出来解决问题的物品。

4. The game then evaluates the player’s solution using the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 transformer model. This model checks the similarity between the player’s input and the original keyword to determine if the problem has been correctly addressed. Note that this step could also be given to the LLM instead, which would then be able to evaluate the solution on a per-villager basis.
4. 接着，游戏使用all-MiniLM-L6-v2 Transformer模型评估玩家的解决方案。该模型检查玩家输入与原始关键词的相似度，以判断问题是否得到正确处理。请注意，这一步也可以改由大语言模型完成，届时便能逐个村民地评估解决方案。
5. The game generates an image representing the solution. This image visually depicts the outcome of the player’s input.
5. 游戏生成一幅表现解决方案的图像。这幅图像直观呈现玩家输入的结果。

6. The game then calculates the player’s score based on the success of their solution. The villagers give visual feedback on whether the solution was considered successful or not, leave the store, and a new loop begins.
6. 随后，游戏根据解决方案的成功程度计算玩家分数。村民用视觉反馈表明该方案是否被视为成功，然后离开商店，新的循环开始。
5. AI Integration
5. 人工智能整合

OSFA uses multiple AI models running locally and at the same time to create a dynamic gameplay experience. The integration of these models is central to the game’s ability to generate problems, evaluate solutions, and provide visual feedback. This section gives more details on how various AI components are implemented and interact within the game. Notably, the game’s architecture was designed with modularity in mind – which means that each model can be swapped out separately.
OSFA采用多个在本地同时运行的人工智能模型，创造动态的游玩体验。这些模型的整合，是游戏能够生成问题、评估解决方案和提供视觉反馈的关键。本节进一步说明各个人工智能组件如何在游戏中实现及相互作用。需要特别指出，游戏架构在设计时考虑了模块化，这意味着各个模型均可单独替换。

The Mistral-7B-Instruct model, used as the LLM within the game, is responsible for generating the unique problems that each villager presents to the player. The model operates locally on the player’s computer, limiting energy consumption and eliminating the need for external API calls. The use of such a local implementation can also reduce the latency between player input and feedback, as well as improve data privacy concerns, as no data is sent to third parties.
游戏中的大语言模型Mistral-7B-Instruct，负责生成每位村民向玩家提出的独特问题。该模型在玩家电脑上本地运行，从而限制能源消耗，并免去外部API调用。由于不向第三方发送数据，这种本地实现还能够缩短玩家输入与反馈之间的延迟，并改善数据隐私方面的问题。
Figure 3: Workflow diagram showing game loop for OSFA and the interaction between AI components and user input in the game.
图3：工作流程图，展示OSFA的游戏循环，以及游戏中人工智能组件与用户输入之间的交互。

To evaluate the player’s solutions, OSFA integrates the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 transformer model. After the player provides a solution to a villager’s problem, the model calculates a similarity score compared to a ’perfect’ solution, thus determining whether the player’s input sufficiently addresses the problem. Currently, all villagers’ problems are evaluated at once, but future implementations will aim to evaluate them on a case-by-case basis (e.g., by using an LLM instead of a transformer), thus allowing for partially correct answers as well.
为了评估玩家的解决方案，OSFA整合了all-MiniLM-L6-v2 Transformer模型。玩家为村民的问题提供方案后，模型计算该方案与一个“完美”方案相比的相似度分数，借此判断玩家输入是否充分解决了问题。目前，所有村民的问题会被同时评估；未来实现则将争取逐个案例进行评估（例如改用大语言模型，而非Transformer），从而也能接受部分正确的答案。

Based on the player’s input, the conjured items are generated using a pixel-art diffusion model and a custom ComfyUI workflow. This tool is integrated into the game’s AI pipeline, allowing it to dynamically create pixel art assets based on the input in real time.
依据玩家输入，召唤出的物品由一个像素美术扩散模型和定制的ComfyUI工作流生成。该工具被整合进游戏的人工智能流水线，使游戏能够依据输入实时、动态地创建像素美术素材。

The AI models in OSFA are implemented within a framework that supports real-time interaction and processing. The models run locally on the player’s machine and the game was made using the Unity Game Engine, using scripts, plugins, and libraries to control the AI models. By running the AI components locally, the game minimizes latency and increases security through the lack of network communication, although the player’s hardware specification can still cause delays.
OSFA的人工智能模型实现在一个支持实时交互与处理的框架中。模型在玩家机器上本地运行；游戏使用Unity游戏引擎制作，通过脚本、插件和库来控制人工智能模型。在本地运行人工智能组件，可以最大限度降低延迟，并因不进行网络通信而提升安全性，不过玩家的硬件配置仍然可能造成延迟。
6. User Experience and Feedback
6. 用户体验与反馈

Initial testing indicates that players appreciate the dynamic problem-solving elements, though challenges such as model latency were encountered and mitigated through optimization techniques. The game was developed and showcased during a game jam event, where it won second place. More than ten people at a time engaged with the game, often collaborating to guess and influence the player’s decisions. This collective engagement fostered curiosity and a fun, cooperative atmosphere. Players found it challenging to discover the correct solutions but remained persistent, continually attempting new ideas. When the villagers left satisfied with a solution, it elicited cheers and a sense of accomplishment among the group. Participants particularly enjoyed the generated images, highlighting them as a standout feature. However, some areas of improvement were noted. There was ambiguity when players felt their solutions were appropriate but unacknowledged by the system. Enhancing the feedback mechanism to provide clearer guidance when solutions are rejected could significantly improve user experience.

初步测试表明，玩家欣赏动态解决问题的要素，不过也遇到了模型延迟等挑战，并通过优化技术加以缓解。游戏在一次游戏创作马拉松活动中开发并展示，获得了第二名。现场有十余人同时参与，常常合作猜测，并影响玩家的决策。这种集体参与激发了好奇心，形成了有趣、协作的氛围。玩家觉得找出正确方案颇具挑战，但依然坚持，不断尝试新的想法。当村民带着对方案的满意离去时，现场人群会发出欢呼，并产生一种成就感。参与者尤其喜欢生成的图像，将其视为突出的特色。不过，也发现了一些有待改进之处。当玩家认为自己的方案合适，而系统却不予认可时，就会产生含混不清的体验。若增强反馈机制，在方案被拒绝时提供更明确的指引，就能显著改善用户体验。
7. Future Work
7. 后续工作

Future work will focus on evaluating and enhancing the AI-driven creativity within the game, assessing user experience and satisfaction through comprehensive playtesting, and analyzing the cost-benefit ratio of using local AI models compared to cloud-based solutions. We aim to ensure an engaging and satisfying player experience while at the same time promoting sustainable AI practices in game development.
后续工作将着重评估和增强游戏中由人工智能驱动的创造力，通过全面的游玩测试评估用户体验与满意度，并分析使用本地人工智能模型与云端方案相比的成本收益比。我们旨在确保游玩体验既吸引人又令人满意，同时推动游戏开发中的可持续人工智能实践。
7.1. AI Creativity
7.1. 人工智能创造力

Creativity, especially in the context of generative AI, is a rich and interdisciplinary research field [10, 11, 12]. As OSFA uses an LLM to generate villagers’ wishes and requests based on specific keywords, we believe that it opens up new possibilities for exploring AI creativity. The ability of AI to generate novel and varied problems from similar inputs is understood to be a form of creativity, presenting several interesting research questions. The first step could be defining and quantifying AI creativity in the context of the game prototype. One approach could be to develop a creativity score to evaluate the LLM’s performance in generating unique and contextually appropriate problems. This score would be based on the similarity of problems generated by the AI across various playthroughs and different versions of the game.

创造力，尤其是生成式人工智能语境中的创造力，是一个丰富的跨学科研究领域[10, 11, 12]。由于OSFA使用大语言模型，依据特定关键词生成村民的愿望和请求，我们认为，它为探索人工智能创造力开辟了新的可能。人工智能能够从相似输入中生成新颖而多样的问题，这种能力被理解为创造力的一种形式，提出了几个有趣的研究问题。第一步可以是在这一游戏原型的语境中定义并量化人工智能创造力。一种做法是建立创造力分数，用于评估大语言模型生成独特且符合语境的问题的表现。这个分数将以人工智能在多次游玩和游戏不同版本中生成的问题之间的相似度为基础。

To explore this, data on AI-generated problems needs to be collected across multiple sessions and then compared against several types of solutions: those manually crafted by human designers, those generated solely by the LLM, and a mix of human and AI-generated content. This comparison could reveal how closely AI outputs align with expected creative standards, as well as how AI can complement human creativity.
为探索这一点，需要收集多次游玩中人工智能生成的问题数据，再将其与几类方案比较：由人类设计者手工创作的方案、完全由大语言模型生成的方案，以及人类与人工智能共同生成的内容。这样的比较可以揭示，人工智能输出在多大程度上符合预期的创造力标准，以及人工智能如何补充人类创造力。

In addition to a creativity score, other metrics can help to better understand and measure AI creativity. Novelty can assess how often the AI produces entirely new problems not seen in previous playthroughs. Diversity measures the range of different problem types generated in response to similar keywords within a single playthrough. Consistency can evaluate the AI’s ability to maintain high-quality, contextually relevant problems across different scenarios. Adaptability assesses how well the AI adjusts its problem generation to varying game contexts or player actions, ensuring that the problems remain appropriate and challenging.
除了创造力分数，其他指标也有助于更好地理解和衡量人工智能创造力。新颖性可以衡量人工智能生成此前游玩中从未出现的全新问题的频率。多样性衡量同一次游玩中，针对相似关键词所生成的不同问题类型的范围。一致性可以评估人工智能在不同情境下维持高质量、符合语境的问题的能力。适应性评估人工智能能否根据不同游戏情境或玩家行动，适当地调整问题生成，确保问题仍然合适且富有挑战。

This leads to another question – how do different LLM models compare in terms of their creative outputs? By systematically comparing these metrics across various LLMs, we could gain insights into which models are better suited for generating creative content in games. This could also inform the future development of AI systems designed specifically for creative tasks. Developing these metrics and comparing different models should deepen our understanding of how AI can be used to generate novel and engaging content. This research could have broader implications for AI applications in creative industries, such as game design, storytelling, and digital art.
这又引出另一个问题：不同的大语言模型在创造性输出方面表现如何？通过系统比较不同大语言模型在这些指标上的表现，我们可以了解哪些模型更适合为游戏生成创造性内容。这也可以为专门面向创造性任务的未来人工智能系统开发提供信息。开发这些指标、比较不同模型，应能加深我们对于如何使用人工智能生成新颖且引人投入的内容的理解。这项研究可能对游戏设计、故事讲述、数字艺术等创意产业中的人工智能应用产生更广泛的影响。
7.2. User Experience and Satisfaction
7.2. 用户体验与满意度

Understanding user experience (UX) and satisfaction can help in evaluating the success of OSFA, especially given its integration of AI-generated content. This section explores methods to assess how players interact with and perceive the game, particularly in the context of its AI elements. One approach to evaluating UX in OSFA is heuristic evaluation. By having experts review the game based on established usability principles, it’s possible to identify both strengths and potential issues within the game. Key considerations include ensuring that AI-generated content maintains consistency and adheres to the game’s internal rules.
理解用户体验（UX）与满意度，有助于评估OSFA是否成功，尤其考虑到它整合了人工智能生成的内容。本节探讨评估玩家如何与游戏交互、如何看待游戏的方法，特别关注其中的人工智能元素。评估OSFA用户体验的一种方法是启发式评估：让专家依据既有可用性原则审查游戏，就有可能识别游戏中的优点和潜在问题。关键考虑包括确保人工智能生成的内容保持一致，并遵循游戏的内部规则。

Beyond heuristic evaluation, another important aspect is understanding how players’ awareness of AI-generated content influences their enjoyment. It is worth investigating whether players perceive the AI elements (referring to both the pre-generated content such as music and visuals, as well as dynamically generated content) as positive additions to the game or if knowing that most of the content is AI-generated affects their perception of the game’s creativity and quality. For instance, surveys or interviews could be conducted to explore whether this awareness impacts players’ overall satisfaction and engagement and how AI-driven design challenges their expectations. In summary, understanding user experience and satisfaction in a predominantly AI-generated game like OSFA can help answer other important research questions regarding players’ perceptions of AI content.

除了启发式评估，另一个重要方面，是理解玩家知晓内容由人工智能生成，会如何影响他们的乐趣。值得考察的是，玩家是否把人工智能元素——包括音乐与视觉素材等预先生成的内容，以及动态生成的内容——看作对游戏的积极补充；或者，知道大部分内容由人工智能生成，会不会影响他们对游戏创造力与质量的看法。例如，可以开展问卷调查或访谈，探究这种知情是否影响玩家的总体满意度与投入程度，以及人工智能驱动的设计如何挑战玩家的预期。总之，理解OSFA这类内容主要由人工智能生成的游戏中的用户体验与满意度，有助于回答有关玩家如何看待人工智能内容的其他重要研究问题。
7.3. Energy Efficiency of Local AI Models vs. Cloud-Based Solutions
section: 7.3. 本地人工智能模型与云端方案的能源效率

text: 7.3. 本地人工智能模型与云端方案的能源效率
section: 7.3. 本地人工智能模型与云端方案的能源效率

text: As AI-native games like OSFA continue to develop, an important question arises: How does the utilization of local AI models compare to cloud-based solutions in terms of energy efficiency? This question is particularly relevant for our game, which operates AI models locally. While it is generally accepted that running smaller LLMs locally would be faster and more power efficient than remote calls to larger cloud-based models (such as GPT-5), this claim still warrants further investigation, especially in terms of broader scalability and environmental impact. A more detailed comparative analysis could explore the trade-offs between local and cloud-based solutions, considering the quality of the generated content, latency, and also the total energy consumption involved. This includes power requirements for both local machines and cloud-based servers, as well as the energy costs of data transmission between clients and remote servers. The goal would be to determine which approach offers greater energy efficiency, considering factors such as scalability, environmental impact, and the trade-offs between performance, quality, latency, and energy use.
section: 7.3. 本地人工智能模型与云端方案的能源效率

text: 随着OSFA这样的人工智能原生游戏继续发展，一个重要问题随之出现：在能源效率方面，使用本地人工智能模型与采用云端方案相比如何？这个问题与我们的游戏尤其相关，因为游戏在本地运行人工智能模型。虽然人们普遍认为，在本地运行较小的大语言模型，会比远程调用较大的云端模型（例如GPT-5）速度更快、耗电更少，但这一主张仍需进一步研究，尤其要考察更广泛的可扩展性与环境影响。更详细的比较分析可以探索本地与云端方案之间的取舍，将生成内容的质量、延迟及涉及的总能源消耗纳入考虑。这包括本地机器和云端服务器的电力需求，以及客户端与远程服务器之间数据传输的能源成本。目标是判断哪一种方式具有更高的能源效率，同时考虑可扩展性、环境影响，以及性能、质量、延迟与能源使用之间的取舍等因素。
section: 7.3. 本地人工智能模型与云端方案的能源效率

text: Understanding these differences can have significant implications for game development. If local AI models prove to be more energy-efficient while guaranteeing sufficient quality of experience, they could become the preferred choice for sustainable game design. However, if their quality remains lacking, and cloud-based solutions offer better efficiency, this will influence how AI resources are deployed in future projects as well. Exploring the energy efficiency of AI models is important for many reasons – not only for improving game performance but also for advancing sustainability in the AI and video game industry. By comparing the energy use of local AI models with server-based and cloud-based solutions, this research could guide future developments in AI-driven game design, promoting more environmentally conscious practices.
section: 7.3. 本地人工智能模型与云端方案的能源效率

text: 理解这些差异，可能对游戏开发产生重大影响。如果事实证明，本地人工智能模型在保证足够体验质量的同时更节能，它们就可能成为可持续游戏设计的首选。但如果它们的质量仍然不足，而云端方案的效率更高，这同样会影响未来项目部署人工智能资源的方式。探索人工智能模型的能源效率，有诸多重要原因：既是为了改善游戏性能，也是为了推进人工智能与电子游戏产业的可持续性。通过比较本地人工智能模型与基于服务器、基于云端的方案的能源使用，这项研究可以为未来人工智能驱动的游戏设计提供指引，推动更具环境意识的实践。

text: 8. Conclusion
8. 结论

OSFA demonstrates the potential of locally-run AI models in game development, offering both an engaging gameplay experience and a versatile platform for research. By reducing reliance on cloud-based services, the game opens up new avenues for studying AI creativity, UX, and energy efficiency. This paper outlines the game’s design and mechanics, while also proposing several research directions that can be explored using the game as a platform, thus contributing to the broader discourse on AI in games and digital creativity.
OSFA展示了在本地运行的人工智能模型用于游戏开发的潜力，既提供了引人投入的游玩体验，也提供了用途广泛的研究平台。通过降低对云端服务的依赖，游戏为研究人工智能创造力、用户体验和能源效率开辟了新的途径。本文概述游戏的设计与机制，同时提出可利用这一游戏平台探索的若干研究方向，从而为围绕游戏人工智能和数字创造力的更广泛讨论作出贡献。

Abstract
摘要

Quest to Dungeon (QtD) is a tool designed to bridge the gap between narrative design and procedural level generation in games, two processes that are typically developed in isolation from each other. QtD connects narrative design with level design by enabling designers to create quests by combining tasks in a grid interface, where each narrative task automatically generates corresponding dungeon rooms using task-specific algorithms. We evaluated QtD through a user study (N=8) where all participants created first a quest with two endings, and then a quest without constraints. Our results showed that participants found the tool intuitive and effective in visualizing how narrative objectives translate into level design. QtD helped enable faster iteration cycles for the participants, who speculated about its possible benefits for collaboration and communication between narrative and level designers.

Quest to Dungeon（QtD）是一种旨在弥合游戏中叙事设计与程序化关卡生成之间鸿沟的工具；这两个过程通常彼此独立开展。QtD允许设计师在网格界面中组合任务环节来创建任务，由此把叙事设计与关卡设计连接起来；每个叙事环节都会采用针对该环节的算法，自动生成相应的地牢房间。我们通过一项用户研究（N=8）评估了QtD，所有参与者先创建一个有两种结局的任务，再创建一个不受约束的任务。结果显示，参与者认为工具直观，能够有效地把叙事目标如何转化为关卡设计呈现出来。QtD帮助参与者加快了迭代周期；他们也推测了它可能为叙事设计师与关卡设计师之间的协作和沟通带来的益处。

1. Introduction
1. 引言

Collaboration and communication challenges permeate game development at different levels and development stages [1, 2, 3]. One reason for this is how heterogeneous teams are, with developers from distinct disciplines working together towards a shared goal. Yet, they might not have a shared understanding, language, and terminology. In this paper we present Quest to Dungeon (QtD), a tool developed for quest-constrained generation focusing on how manually placed quest-task actions can influence level generation and vice-versa in early prototyping. We also focus on a significant real-world problem that persists in game development, PCG systems and narrative (and narrative elements such as quests) design are typically developed in isolation, resulting in disconnected deployment. In QtD, designers use a node grid to make quests that then are automatically turned into levels. Designers can compose a main quest and subquests with alternative routes and optional tasks. These tasks are then used to generate a proposed level layout relevant to the tasks and that interconnects them. The spatial layout of the quests and levels is the same in a 6x6 grid, which forces the level layout to track 1-to-1 the layout of the quests. The level layout, while not modifiable, is created with the possibility to be used as-is, or as a way for designers to communicate their ideas to different teams on what they imagine the level design or narrative to be. QtD’s long-term goal is to help the communication and collaboration between narrative and level designers at early production stages.

协作与沟通挑战，贯穿游戏开发的不同层面和开发阶段[1, 2, 3]。原因之一，是团队具有高度异质性：来自不同学科的开发者，为共同目标而一起工作，但未必拥有共同的理解、语言与术语。本文介绍Quest to Dungeon（QtD），一种为受任务约束的生成而开发的工具，重点考察在早期原型制作中，手动放置的任务环节行动如何影响关卡生成，反之又如何。我们也关注游戏开发中持续存在的一个重要现实问题：PCG系统与叙事设计，包括任务等叙事要素，通常彼此独立开发，导致部署时相互脱节。在QtD中，设计师使用节点网格制作任务，然后将其自动转化为关卡。设计师可以编排主线任务和支线任务，包含替代路线与可选环节。随后，系统利用这些环节生成与之相关、并将其连接起来的建议关卡布局。任务与关卡在同一个6×6网格中具有相同的空间布局，迫使关卡布局与任务布局形成一对一对应。虽然关卡布局无法修改，但设计时考虑了两种使用可能：直接使用生成结果，或让设计师借此向不同团队传达自己对关卡设计或叙事的设想。QtD的长期目标，是在制作早期帮助叙事设计师与关卡设计师沟通、协作。

We focus on quest design and its implication within the overall game design, particularly the impact on level design. This is because narrative and level (or space) facets are linked and complement each other [4, 5]; thus, the design of either and their generation benefits from a more holistic design. Within research there exist many examples of these being interconnected for Procedural Content Generation (PCG) [5, 6, 7]. Similarly, the game industry has worked with similar objectives, mainly trying to either fit generated quests in the gameworld or human-authored quests in generated levels. For instance, The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim[8] infamously uses radiant quests (procedural objectives) but deploys them in generic, repetitive dungeons, creating a disconnect between narrative goals and level design [9]. This approach leads to inefficiencies: level designers constantly need to align environments with quest requirements, while narrative designers lack tools to ensure their objectives are supported by the generated content. The result is increased iteration time, inconsistent player experiences, and missed opportunities for fun replayability.

我们关注任务设计及其对整体游戏设计的意义，尤其是对关卡设计的影响。原因是，叙事与关卡，或空间，这两个面向彼此相连、相互补充[4, 5]；因此，无论设计还是生成，都能从更整体的设计方式中受益。研究中，已有许多为程序化内容生成（PCG）而将二者互联的例子[5, 6, 7]。同样，游戏业也曾围绕类似目标开展工作，主要是试图把生成的任务嵌入游戏世界，或把人工编写的任务放进生成的关卡。例如，《The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim》[8]因使用辐射任务，即程序化目标，却将其安置在通用、重复的地牢中而广受诟病，造成叙事目标与关卡设计脱节[9]。这种做法导致效率低下：关卡设计师必须不断使环境与任务要求对齐，叙事设计师却缺少工具，来确保生成内容能够支持自己的目标。结果是，迭代时间增加、玩家体验不一致，也错失了创造有趣重玩体验的机会。

We evaluated the effectiveness of QtD and how it could be used through a user study (N=8) where we collected qualitative feedback and tool logs. Our results indicate that QtD was easy-to-use, helped visualise how quests and tasks could be placed in level design with faster iteration cycles. Participants also speculated about how it could be used in practice and for collaboration between departments and designers, emphasizing its role in brainstorming, setting a clearer plan, and communication.
我们通过一项用户研究（N=8），评估QtD的有效性及其可能的使用方式，并收集了质性反馈与工具日志。结果表明，QtD易于使用，能够以更快的迭代周期，帮助人们看清任务及其环节可以怎样安排进关卡设计。参与者还推测了它在实践中，以及部门和设计师之间协作中的用途，强调了它在头脑风暴、明确计划和沟通方面的作用。
2. Related Work
2. 相关工作

Narrative is a key facet in games and has a strong relation with the gameworld, levels, and in general spaces where the game will take place [10]. Within the narrative facet and PCG, quests have been the target of a large body of research for generating them such as Questbrowser [11], a quest design tool where users can query the system for ideas and alternatives and the work by Grinblat and Bucklew [12] in “Caves of Qud”, dynamically generating quests constrained by the world and authored templates. Combining quests and level generation has also been explored with interesting results. Questgram [13] enable designers to create quests and receive recommendations on what task to add next based on their current quest and the dungeon composed of both human-authored and generated rooms. Taksim [14] focuses on combining generated mission graphs with game spaces using answer-set programming. Dormans and Bakkes [5] generated missions and spaces with grammars have also been used for Unexplored and Unexplored 2. While these systems show the possibilities of connecting the two facets, how content limits and interact with each other is unclear as well as how human-authored content could fit with generated content, which is one of the goals with QtD. Yet, significant challenges remain when trying to connect quests and levels automatically as well as the communication and collaboration challenges that exist when designing these. Mixed-initiative PCG systems could help mitigate some of these challenges by giving designers control leveraging automatic generation.

叙事是游戏的一个关键面向，与游戏世界、关卡，以及更一般地说游戏发生的空间，有着紧密关系[10]。在叙事面向与PCG研究中，大量工作以任务生成为对象，例如Questbrowser[11]，这是一种任务设计工具，用户可以向系统查询构想与替代方案；又如Grinblat和Bucklew[12]在《Caves of Qud》中的工作，根据世界与预先编写的模板约束，动态生成任务。任务与关卡生成的结合，也已有一些有趣成果。Questgram[13]允许设计师创建任务，并根据当前任务，以及由人工制作和生成房间共同构成的地牢，推荐接下来应添加什么环节。Taksim[14]着重使用答案集编程，把生成的任务图与游戏空间结合起来。Dormans和Bakkes[5]用文法生成任务与空间的方法，也被用于《Unexplored》和《Unexplored 2》。这些系统展示了连接两个面向的可能性，但内容如何相互限制、相互作用，以及人工制作内容如何与生成内容相配合，仍不清楚；这也是QtD的目标之一。然而，无论是自动连接任务与关卡，还是设计它们时存在的沟通与协作问题，仍有重大挑战。混合主动式PCG系统，通过在利用自动生成的同时赋予设计师控制权，可能有助于缓解其中一些挑战。

The interest and challenge of aligning quests and levels, as well as human-authored content (either quest or levels) with automatic generation has also being the object of discussion within the game industry. Levine [15] described the process required to align BioShock’s narrative objectives with level design, while Smith and Colantonio [16] discussed Arkane Studios’ “narrative ecology” approach that places story elements within environmental design for Dishonored[17]. Games such as Hitman (2016) [18] uses “opportunity” structures that place narrative moments within level design, allowing players to discover and trigger quests through environmental interaction. The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild [19] uses “chemistry engine” principles where quest objectives interact with environmental systems, creating narrative possibilities within designed spaces.

如何将任务与关卡对齐，以及如何将人工制作的任务或关卡，与自动生成结合起来，也一直是游戏业讨论的兴趣点和挑战。Levine[15]描述了使《BioShock》的叙事目标与关卡设计对齐所需的过程；Smith和Colantonio[16]则讨论了Arkane Studios的“叙事生态”方法，即把故事要素安置在《Dishonored》[17]的环境设计中。《Hitman》（2016）[18]等游戏使用“机遇”结构，把叙事时刻放在关卡设计之中，让玩家通过与环境互动，发现并触发任务。《The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild》[19]采用“化学引擎”原则，使任务目标与环境系统互动，在设计好的空间中创造叙事可能性。
3. Quest to Dungeon Tool
3. Quest to Dungeon工具

QtD takes a narrative-first approach where quest structures drive level generation, in contrast to most prior systems that combine the two facets, which integrate narrative within the level generation. QtD follows a modular architecture that separates the quest structure definition from dungeon generation, giving users full control over the quest structure, while the AI system procedurally generates the dungeons. QtD was developed in Unity using version 6000.0.36f1.
QtD采取叙事先行的方法，由任务结构驱动关卡生成；这与此前大多数结合两个面向、却在关卡生成过程中整合叙事的系统不同。QtD采用模块化架构，把任务结构定义与地牢生成分开，用户完全控制任务结构，AI系统则以程序化方式生成地牢。QtD使用Unity 6000.0.36f1版本开发。
