3.1. Quest Structure Module
3.1. 任务结构模块

The quest assignment interface uses Unity’s UI system to create an interactive 6×6 grid shown in figure 3 top row. Each grid node consists of a drop-down menu containing multiple task types users can choose from. For this iteration, users can choose between: Blank - used as placeholder and no task needs to be done, Gather - tasks related to gathering resources, Find - tasks related to finding resources or quest items, Fight - tasks related to engaging in combat, Key and Lock - enable a key and lock task sequence represented as separated tasks that condition each other, Boss - task associated to final encounters and Custom - placeholder task for users to add their own quest task idea. Once a task type is selected for a node, a subsequent drop-down appears that allows users to further specialize that task type and that is related to the task itself (e.g., prototypical quest items appear for a Find task). After creating a grid node, users can add adjacent grid nodes to the previous one, linking these two nodes together. Through this graphical process, users can shape diverse sequence of tasks with optional tasks, secondary objectives, and multiple paths to complete a quest. When a user finalizes a quest structure by pressing Generate, the system then takes all the tasks and their relative position to generate the rooms and interconnect them.

任务分配界面使用Unity的UI系统，创建一个可交互的6×6网格，如图3上排所示。每个网格节点都包含一个下拉菜单，用户可以从多种环节类型中选择。在这一迭代版本中，用户可以选择：Blank，空白，用作占位，无须完成任何环节；Gather，采集，与收集资源相关；Find，寻找，与寻找资源或任务物品相关；Fight，战斗，与参与战斗相关；Key与Lock，钥匙与锁，形成一个钥匙—锁环节序列，被表示为相互施加条件的独立环节；Boss，首领，与最终遭遇相关；Custom，自定义，作为占位环节，让用户加入自己的任务环节构想。为节点选定环节类型后，会出现另一个与该环节本身有关的下拉菜单，允许进一步细化类型，例如寻找环节会出现典型任务物品。创建网格节点后，用户可以在前一个节点旁添加相邻节点，把二者连接起来。通过这一图形化过程，用户能够塑造多样的环节序列，包含可选环节、次要目标和完成任务的多条路径。用户按下Generate，完成任务结构后，系统便利用全部环节及其相对位置，生成并连接房间。
3.2. Dungeon Generation Module
3.2. 地牢生成模块

The level layout is the same as the task graph as shown in figure 3 bottom row. The dungeon generation utilizes Unity’s tile-map system to transform all stored data into 2D tile-based rooms, using the same dungeon layout as the quest interface. Each task has an analogous level design algorithm for the creation of the room. The room generation process follows a template-based approach with controlled randomization to create visual variety while preserving functional requirements. This approach ensures that, while rooms of the same task type share common characteristics, they maintain visual distinctiveness. Each room is 25x25 tiles consisting of wall, floor, and treasure tiles as well as special key tiles for key-lock mechanisms. Patterns with these tiles such as “corridors”, “cages” and “pillars” are also generated depending on which room to add visual representation to the dungeon layout. The level cannot be edited as it is meant as the automatic projection of the set of tasks designed by the user, but can be fully regenerated at any time.

关卡布局与任务图相同，如图3下排所示。地牢生成利用Unity的瓦片地图系统，把全部已储存数据转化为二维瓦片房间，地牢布局与任务界面一致。每种环节都有相应的关卡设计算法，用来创建房间。房间生成过程采用基于模板、带受控随机化的方法，在保留功能要求的同时，创造视觉变化。这保证了同一环节类型的房间虽然共享某些特征，却仍保持视觉上的区别。每间房间为25×25块瓦片，由墙、地板和宝物瓦片，以及用于钥匙—锁机制的特殊钥匙瓦片构成。根据房间类型，还会用这些瓦片生成“走廊”“笼状围构”和“柱子”等模式，为地牢布局增加视觉表征。关卡无法编辑，因为它被设定为用户所设计环节集合的自动投影，但随时都可以完整重新生成。

For each task type, we define a set of room templates that satisfy the fundamental requirements of that task, Core Structural Elements such as walls and pathways between connected rooms, and Task-specific Features such as number of enemies and item spawn locations.
对于每种环节类型，我们都定义了一组满足其基本要求的房间模板，包括核心结构要素，例如墙壁与相连房间之间的通路，以及环节专属特征，例如敌人数量和物品生成位置。
3.3. Room Generation
3.3. 房间生成

Rooms are generated based on the tasks that users manually add. Each room pattern includes specific constraints to ensure that every generated room is feasible. For rooms that include corridors, these are always fixed in size for the algorithm to guarantee navigability. For rooms that can generate pillars, additional constraints are applied to ensure that pillars are never placed adjacent to each other or to walls. The QtD tool contains eight different room types and they are exemplified in figure 1.
房间根据用户手动添加的环节生成。每种房间模式都包含特定约束，以确保每间生成的房间都可行。对于包含走廊的房间，走廊尺寸始终固定，使算法能够保证可通行性。对于能够生成柱子的房间，还会施加额外约束，确保柱子既不与彼此相邻，也不与墙壁相邻。QtD工具包含八种不同房间类型，示例见图1。
Blank Pattern Room (fig. 1.a): The Blank pattern is the default task for every room. It consists only of an empty layout surrounded by walls and acts more as a room without a task.
空白模式房间（图1.a）：空白模式是每间房间的默认环节。它只有一个四周围墙的空布局，更像是一间没有任务环节的房间。

Gather Pattern Room (fig. 1.b): The Gather Pattern Room creates centralized room layouts centered around a core area with radiating branches. The design features a central hub with a wall structure in its middle, connected to 3-4 main corridors that extend outward. These main corridors may branch into smaller side passages, creating exploration opportunities. Items are then placed throughout the room.
采集模式房间（图1.b）：采集模式房间创建以核心区域为中心、分支向外辐射的集中式布局。设计有一个中央枢纽，中间是一处墙体结构，连接着向外延伸的3—4条主走廊。这些主走廊可以再分出较小的侧通道，创造探索机会。随后，物品被放置在房间各处。

Find Pattern Room (fig. 1.c): The Find Pattern Room generates a maze based on a modified recursive backtracking approach. The algorithm carves paths through an initially solid block, ensuring all areas remain connected while maintaining sufficient wall thickness between passages.
寻找模式房间（图1.c）：寻找模式房间采用一种经修改的递归回溯方法生成迷宫。算法从最初的实心块中凿出路径，在通道之间保留足够墙厚的同时，确保所有区域保持连通。

Fight Pattern Room (fig. 1.d): The Fight Pattern Room generates layouts with an outer square boundary and an inner “cage” structure. This creates a room-within-a-room design. The inner area contains dynamically placed pillars whose number and size adapt based on the number of enemies the user chose to add to the task.
战斗模式房间（图1.d）：战斗模式房间生成具有外部方形边界和内部“笼状”结构的布局，形成房中房的设计。内部区域包含动态放置的柱子，其数量与尺寸，会根据用户选择加入该环节的敌人数量调整。

Key Pattern Room (fig. 1.e): The Key pattern Room creates a layout with color-coded shapes in the center of the room. The room features a colored square in the center that is hollowed out by a specific shape chosen by the user (triangle (red), square (green), circle (blue), and hexagon (yellow)).
钥匙模式房间（图1.e）：钥匙模式房间创建一种在房间中央放置颜色编码形状的布局。房间中央有一个有色方块，按用户选择的特定形状挖空：三角形为红色，正方形为绿色，圆形为蓝色，六边形为黄色。

Lock Pattern Room (fig. 1.f): The Lock Pattern Room generates rooms that restrict access to other areas. The layout features a specific color-coded shape in the center of the room chosen by the user. Shapes and colors are the same as for the key pattern rooms.
锁模式房间（图1.f）：锁模式房间生成限制通往其他区域的房间。布局中央有一个由用户选择、以特定颜色编码的形状。形状和颜色与钥匙模式房间相同。

Boss Pattern Room (fig. 1.g): The Boss Pattern Room creates a spacious, symmetrical layout designed for boss encounters. The algorithm produces a square room with an outer perimeter of walls and an open central area. Within this space, eight pillars are positioned in a symmetrical pattern.
首领模式房间（图1.g）：首领模式房间创建宽敞、对称、为首领遭遇设计的布局。算法生成一个外围是墙、中央区域开放的方形房间。在这个空间中，八根柱子以对称模式摆放。

Custom Pattern Room (fig. 1.h): The Custom Pattern Room consists of a blank room with a white square in the center of the room, where users can write whatever they want inside this white square. It is primarily used as placeholder of not implemented tasks.
自定义模式房间（图1.h）：自定义模式房间由一间空白房间构成，中央有一个白色方块，用户可以在其中写下任何内容。它主要用作尚未实现的任务环节的占位符。
4. Experiment
4. 实验

We conducted a user evaluation and collected both data from surveys and data logs from the tool as participants used the tool. Quantitative metrics (total nodes, branch depth, grid usage percentage, regenerate events) were logged. Qualitative survey responses were manually analyzed. Quotes were collected from qualitative questions during the survey. Our study setup consist of first, an online pilot study with two participants following the same procedure as in-person participants to understand if the tool required any revision or something in the survey was unclear, and an in-person user study with eight participants that used the tool for up to 13 minutes. Our goal was to assess the usability of QtD, its effectiveness in bridging the gap between quest-based narrative approaches and level design, and understand how it could be used as a communication device by using its automatic level generation.

我们进行了用户评估，在参与者使用工具时，收集问卷数据与工具数据日志。记录的量化指标包括总节点数、分支深度、网格使用百分比和重新生成事件。质性问卷回答由人工分析，引语来自问卷中的质性问题。研究安排首先包括一项有两名参与者的在线先导研究，他们遵循与现场参与者相同的程序，以了解工具是否需要修改、问卷是否有不清楚之处；随后是一项有八名参与者的现场用户研究，使用工具的时间最多为13分钟。我们的目标，是评估QtD的可用性、它在弥合基于任务的叙事方法与关卡设计之间鸿沟方面的有效性，并了解它如何借助自动关卡生成，充当沟通媒介。

Participants were given an explanation of the project and informed consent was collected. They then viewed an on-screen tutorial pop-up (up to 5 minutes), explaining tool features and task types. During the evaluation they had first 3 minutes to create a quest with two possible endings to get used to the tool followed by a 5 minutes free-exploration phase to create a quest without constraints.
参与者先听取项目说明，并提供知情同意。随后，他们观看屏幕上的教程弹窗，最多5分钟，了解工具功能与环节类型。评估中，他们先有3分钟创建一个具有两种可能结局的任务，以熟悉工具；接着进入5分钟自由探索阶段，创建一个不受约束的任务。
5. Result
5. 结果

All participants studied or were students of a game development program, had between 2 and 3 years of game development experience and 6 out of 8 self assessed as programmers while the other 2 as game designers. 6 out of 8 had worked within narrative design or level design to some extent, while two others have not worked on that area. Finally, 5 out of 8 (all self-assessed as programmers and with experience in narrative or level design) have previously worked with PCG tools and algorithms.
所有参与者都曾就读或正在就读游戏开发项目，拥有2至3年的游戏开发经验；八人中六人自认是程序员，另外两人自认是游戏设计师。八人中六人在某种程度上做过叙事设计或关卡设计，另外两人没有这方面经历。最后，八人中五人此前使用过PCG工具和算法；这五人全都自认为程序员，并有叙事或关卡设计经验。

5.1. Data from the QtD tool
5.1. QtD工具的数据

Data collected from the tool logs shows the total distribution of task types across the two quest creation tasks (Quest 1 - 3 minutes, and Quest 2 - 5 minutes). For Quest 1, which consisted of users designing a dungeon with two separate endings, the Fight task was the most frequently utilized (31 instances), followed by nearly equal usage of Blank (19), Gather (19), and Find (18) tasks. Key (16), Lock (14), and Boss (13) tasks were moderately used, while the Custom task was used sparingly (5 instances). This distribution suggests that combat-focused narrative elements were prioritized in the first quest design, which is expected as the tasks are biased towards this type of quests. Quest 2, which consisted of users being able to freely explore and design a dungeon, showed a slight difference in design approach. Fight tasks still dominated but with less frequency (45 instances), a significant rise in Find tasks however occurred (39 instances compared to 18 in Quest 1). Gather tasks also increased from 19 to 26 instances. This shift could indicate that as designers gained familiarity with the tool, they incorporated more exploration and collection-based narrative elements, creating more complex quest structures.

工具日志数据展示了两次任务创建活动中各环节类型的总分布，任务1为3分钟，任务2为5分钟。在任务1中，用户设计一个具有两个独立结局的地牢；战斗环节最常使用，共31次；空白、采集和寻找的使用量几乎相同，分别为19、19和18次。钥匙16次、锁14次、首领13次，使用程度居中；自定义环节很少使用，只有5次。这种分布表明，第一次任务设计优先采用了以战斗为中心的叙事要素；由于这些环节本就偏向这类任务，这也是预期之中的。任务2允许用户自由探索和设计地牢，设计方法略有不同。战斗环节仍占主导，但频率更低，共45次；寻找环节则显著增多，从任务1的18次升至39次。采集环节也从19次增至26次。这种转变可能表明，随着设计师逐渐熟悉工具，他们纳入了更多基于探索和收集的叙事要素，创建了更复杂的任务结构。

The average dungeon size also increased from 17.2 rooms in Quest 1 to 23.5 rooms in Quest 2, resulting in more elaborated quest structures. The dimensional consistency across sessions, despite the increased room count, indicates that designers focused on creating denser and more interconnected quest structures. This suggests that creating more dense and eventful quests are more prioritized than creating linear quest lines. Lastly, since the tool allows users to switch back and forth between the quest and dungeon modules, multiple iterations of the same quests were saved each time users moved back and forth to analyse the different ways of using QtD. Figure 3 shows an example of a participant development process for Quest 2, consisting of four iterations.

地牢平均规模也从任务1的17.2间房间，增加到任务2的23.5间，形成更复杂的任务结构。尽管房间数量增加，各轮活动的空间尺寸保持一致，这表明设计师着力创建更密集、联系更紧密的任务结构。这意味着，相比线性任务线，他们更优先考虑更密集、事件更丰富的任务。最后，由于工具允许用户在任务与地牢模块之间来回切换，每次切换时，同一任务的多次迭代都会被保存，以便分析QtD的不同使用方式。图3展示了一名参与者制作任务2的过程示例，包含四次迭代。
5.2. Survey Results
5.2. 问卷结果

Tool usability, effectiveness, and interface: The task assignment interface was rated highly intuitive by participants, with the average score being 7.88/10 (SD=1.25). Most participants highlighted its ease to use and beneficial visualization, emphasizing that QtD was “easy to understand and [had a] very good visualization”(p1) and “easy to use, I would probably use it in an early stage of my game”(p2). This strong usability score indicates that the 6x6 grid system and the node-based design provided an accessible framework for quest design without requiring extensive technical knowledge. Tasks included variables that affected generated rooms and gave more control to users. 7 out of 8 participants found them to have a significant impact on their design process, with the average score being 8.13/10 (SD=1.73). This suggests that the additional task-specific parameters were successful at enhancing the tool’s flexibility while maintaining its accessibility.

工具的可用性、有效性与界面：参与者高度评价任务分配界面的直观程度，平均得分为7.88/10，标准差为1.25。大多数参与者强调其易用性和有益的可视化，认为QtD“容易理解，而且［有］非常好的可视化”（p1），以及“容易使用，我大概会在游戏开发早期使用它”（p2）。这一较高可用性评分表明，6×6网格系统与基于节点的设计，为任务设计提供了一个易于接近的框架，无须具备大量技术知识。环节包含会影响生成房间的变量，让用户拥有更多控制。八名参与者中七人认为，这些变量显著影响了自己的设计过程，平均得分为8.13/10，标准差为1.73。这表明，额外的环节专属参数，成功增强了工具的灵活性，同时维持了易用性。

Participants felt that generated rooms were representative of the specific task (avg. score of 7.63/10 (SD=1.6)) and most of the participants felt that the tool helped them visualize how narrative objectives translate to physical spaces (avg. score of 8/10 (SD=2.27)). This suggest that the translation from narrative task to spatial design was clear and coherent with participants highlighting “the visualization gave the feeling of how the game could look like/time it takes to play,”(p1) and “I was thinking about patterns, what room should come after another, trying not to have repetivness.”(p2), which show how their process was influenced by the QtD workflow and that the system successfully conveyed gameplay pacing and narrative progression.

参与者认为，生成房间能够代表相应的具体环节，平均得分为7.63/10，标准差为1.6；大多数参与者也认为，工具帮助自己看清叙事目标如何转化为实体空间，平均得分为8/10，标准差为2.27。这表明，从叙事环节到空间设计的转化是清楚且连贯的。参与者强调：“可视化让人感觉到游戏会是什么样子／玩起来需要多长时间”（p1），以及“我在想各种模式，哪个房间应当接在哪个之后，尽量避免重复”（p2）。这些回答显示，他们的设计过程受到QtD工作流的影响，系统也成功传达了玩法节奏与叙事推进。

Participants also highlighted how tools like QtD “... can make it faster to make levels”(p8) and “would give a clear plan of what to do and how to do it. leaving no holes in the proccess”(p1) as well as the tool “give ideas of a level where you can have smaller quest together with a broader quest”(p4) and how “it could be effective as a “brain storming” tool to help narrative designers easily explain their vision and ideas to the development team and improving the communication between the two.”. This shows that having a tool that allows for quick iterative quest development and how that could be seen within level design is appreciate and could be an important tool to understand design process and collaboration. However, participants felt mixed about the control over the generation from task to room (avg. score of 5.63/10 (SD=1.51)). This was expected as the room generation takes follow a specific pattern that is not adapted or controllable by designers, which will be explored in future work.

参与者还强调，QtD这样的工具“……能让制作关卡更快”（p8），“会给出一份清楚的计划，说明做什么、怎样做，让过程不留空缺”（p1）；工具也会“给人关于关卡的点子，可以把较小任务放进一个更大的任务里”（p4），并且“它可以有效地充当一种‘头脑风暴’工具，帮助叙事设计师轻松向开发团队解释自己的愿景与想法，改善二者之间的沟通”。这显示，人们欣赏一种能快速迭代开发任务、并展示它们如何出现在关卡设计中的工具；它也可能成为理解设计过程与协作的重要工具。不过，对于从环节到房间的生成控制，参与者感受不一，平均得分为5.63/10，标准差为1.51。这在预期之中，因为房间生成遵循一种特定模式，既不按设计师需求调整，也不能由设计师控制；未来工作将对此进行探索。

Participants highly rated the tool’s potential to reduce dungeon creation iteration time, giving it an average score of 7.63/10 (SD=1.69). This suggests the tool could effectively reduce iteration time between quest narration and map design during planning phases.
参与者高度评价工具减少地牢创建迭代时间的潜力，平均给出7.63/10，标准差为1.69。这表明，在规划阶段，工具可能有效缩短任务叙述与地图设计之间的迭代时间。

Design Process and Workflow Patterns: The qualitative responses revealed consistent patterns in how participants approached quest design using the QtD tool. In the pre-defined task (Quest 1), where designers were asked to create a quest with two different endings, most participants adopted a branching structure approach. One participant described their process as creating “a level layout that had two different types of ending, one being focused on fighting, and one being focused on finding the key and the exit.”(p6) Another mentioned, “Two separate paths, each one with different approaches or types of rooms before reaching the last rooms.” (p5).
设计过程与工作流模式：质性回答显示，参与者使用QtD进行任务设计时，呈现出一些一致模式。在预先规定的任务，即任务1中，设计师被要求创建一个有两种不同结局的任务，大多数人采用分支结构。一位参与者把自己的过程描述为创建“一个具有两种不同结局的关卡布局，一种着重战斗，另一种着重寻找钥匙和出口”（p6）。另一位则提到：“两条独立路径，各自在抵达最后房间之前，有不同的做法或房间类型。”（p5）

For the free-roam task (Quest 2), participants demonstrated more diverse and complex design approaches. Many described creating more interconnected pathways and utilizing a broader range of task types. One participant explained, “I wanted to create a ’World of Warcraft’ type quest, that followed a linear path, and taking the player on a journey through the different tasks that were available to me.”(p6) Another mentioned focusing on “a puzzle focused dungeon with a lot of locked doors and keys.”(p3) This evolution in design complexity from Quest 1 to Quest 2 aligns with the quantitative data showing larger, more diverse dungeons in the second session.

对于自由探索任务，即任务2，参与者展示出更多样、更复杂的设计方法。许多人描述了更相互连通的路径，以及对更广泛环节类型的运用。一位参与者解释：“我想创建一个《World of Warcraft》式的任务，沿着一条线性路径，让玩家经历我能使用的不同环节，走上一段旅程。”（p6）另一位提到，自己专注于“一座以解谜为中心、有许多锁门和钥匙的地牢”（p3）。从任务1到任务2，设计复杂性出现的这种变化，与第二轮地牢更大、更多样的量化数据相吻合。

Several participants described an iterative workflow where they would first establish a layout using basic tasks and then refine it. One participant explained: “Create a bunch of empty rooms, find a structure that I liked and then swapped those empty rooms into either fights, gathers, or finds, wherever I felt like it would fit.”(p2). This suggests that QtD supported a layered design process from a more draft version towards something participants envisioned in a quick iterative manner.
几位参与者描述了一种迭代工作流：先用基本环节建立布局，再加以细化。一位参与者解释：“先创建一堆空房间，找到一个我喜欢的结构，然后在我觉得合适的地方，把空房间换成战斗、采集或寻找。”（p2）这表明，QtD支持一种分层设计过程，通过快速迭代，从较粗略的草稿走向参与者所设想的东西。
6. Discussion
6. 讨论
6.1. Integration of Narrative and Level Design
section: 6.1. 叙事与关卡设计的整合

text: 6.1. 叙事与关卡设计的整合
section: 6.1. 叙事与关卡设计的整合

text: Our results show the value of coupling game facets such as narrative and level, and the potential of these to mediate design and collaborative decision-making. Users could quickly see how their quest choices affected the physical layout, allowing for immediate adjustments. The high rating for effectiveness of generated rooms that represents the tasks indicates that the translation from narrative design to level design was largely successful. QtD was able to show how participants process was influenced by the QtD workflow and that the system successfully conveyed gameplay pacing and narrative progression. QtD and similar tools could help address challenges with isolated facet development, particularly when affected by procedural systems such as side quests in Skyrim to create better gameplay.
section: 6.1. 叙事与关卡设计的整合

text: 我们的结果展示了耦合叙事、关卡等游戏面向的价值，以及它们在设计和协作决策中充当中介的潜力。用户可以迅速看见任务选择如何影响实体布局，从而立即调整。生成房间代表任务环节的有效性获得高分，表明叙事设计向关卡设计的转化大体成功。QtD能够展示参与者的过程如何受QtD工作流影响，以及系统如何成功传达玩法节奏与叙事推进。QtD和类似工具，可能有助于应对各面向孤立开发带来的挑战，尤其是当它们受到《Skyrim》支线任务等程序化系统影响时，从而创造更好的玩法。
section: 6.1. 叙事与关卡设计的整合

text: The varying effectiveness of different task pattern rooms provided insight into what designers value in procedurally generated content. The Find and Gather algorithms for example rated significantly higher than the Fight algorithm in terms of how interesting the room layout were, suggesting that designers prefer room layouts with more complex structural elements. The tool could therefore help designers to create more complex patterns automatically as a starting point that would be time-consuming to design manually, rather than simpler and more open layouts. The effectiveness of the specific room generation algorithms could also suggest how procedural techniques can enhance gameplay in the context of narrative generated rooms. For example, the Gather pattern algorithm with strategically placed collection points effectively communicates a scavenger hunt experience, while the Find pattern’s maze communicates exploration and discovery.
section: 6.1. 叙事与关卡设计的整合

text: 不同环节模式房间的有效性差异，让我们了解设计师重视程序化生成内容的哪些方面。例如，在房间布局有多有趣这一问题上，寻找和采集算法的评分显著高于战斗算法，这表明设计师更喜欢结构要素较复杂的房间布局。因此，工具可以帮助设计师自动创建更复杂的模式，作为起点；这些模式若手工设计会很耗时，而不是提供更简单、更开放的布局。具体房间生成算法的有效性，也可能说明，程序化技术如何在叙事生成房间的情境中增强玩法。例如，采集模式算法通过策略性放置收集点，有效传达了寻宝搜集的体验；寻找模式的迷宫，则传达了探索与发现。
section: 6.1. 叙事与关卡设计的整合

text: 6.2. Collaborative Design Workflows
6.2. 协作设计工作流

Collaboration and communication challenges permeate game development [1] and tools like QtD could enable a better workflow. While QtD was evaluated with a single designer to create quests and see how generated rooms affected their design and expressed their ideas, our final goal is to explore how QtD and similar tools might transform collaborative workflows between different design specialties. First steps were taken in that direction as participants expressed that the tool could be used effectively as a communication medium, for early development phases, and planning work in teams.
协作与沟通挑战贯穿游戏开发[1]，QtD这样的工具可能带来更好的工作流。虽然QtD的评估，是让单个设计师创建任务，观察生成房间如何影响其设计、表达其想法，但我们的最终目标，是探索QtD及类似工具，可能怎样改变不同设计专长之间的协作工作流。我们已朝这个方向迈出第一步，因为参与者表示，工具可以有效充当沟通媒介，用于开发早期，以及团队中的规划工作。

Further, our usability results also suggests that QtD simplifies the design process, lowering the technical barrier to expressing design intent, potentially enabling narrative designers that could have limited technical skills to communicate layout requirements effectively. This direct translation of task-types to room structures could also create a vocabulary that can be shared between narrative and level designers, potentially reducing miscommunication and iteration cycles typically required to align these two aspects of game design.
此外，可用性结果也表明，QtD简化了设计过程，降低了表达设计意图的技术门槛，可能使技术能力有限的叙事设计师，也能有效传达布局要求。从环节类型到房间结构的直接转化，还可能创造一种叙事设计师与关卡设计师共享的词汇，从而减少为对齐这两个游戏设计方面，通常需要的沟通误差和迭代周期。
6.3. User Development Process
6.3. 用户的开发过程

The data logs showed that most users had an iterative approach to quest development. Users frequently moved back and forth between the quest and dungeon modules, making adjustments to their quest structures after seeing the generated layouts (seen in figure 3). This iterative process suggests that the visual feedback from the dungeon generation could have influenced quest design decisions. Participants approached the quest development using both a layout-first and narrative-first approach. Some participants began by establishing a physical dungeon layout of empty rooms that was later populated with appropriate tasks. One participant described it as: “I just clicked out rooms in a random pattern then I connected the different branches into a flow that would seem nice. After that I began choosing different rooms that would fit together to create a nice game experience.” (p8). However, some users took a narrative-first approach instead, conceptualizing the quest story before considering dungeon layout. A participant described: “My idea for the quest was already in my mind when I started to build the level, so the quest did influence the level but not as much the other way around.” (p4). This shows that the QtD tool can be flexible enough to be utilized in different design approaches.

数据日志显示，大多数用户采用迭代方法开发任务。他们经常在任务与地牢模块之间来回移动，看到生成布局后，再调整任务结构，如图3所示。这种迭代过程表明，地牢生成的视觉反馈可能影响任务设计决策。参与者既采用布局先行，也采用叙事先行的方法。一些人先建立由空房间组成的实体地牢布局，再填入合适环节。一位参与者这样描述：“我只是按随机模式点出一些房间，再把不同分支连接成一种看起来不错的流程。然后，我开始选择能放在一起、创造良好游戏体验的不同房间。”（p8）不过，有些用户采取了叙事先行的方法，在考虑地牢布局之前，就先构思任务故事。一位参与者描述：“开始搭建关卡时，我心里已经有任务的构想，所以任务确实影响了关卡，但反过来的影响没有那么大。”（p4）这显示，QtD能够灵活到足以用于不同设计方法。
6.4. Limitations and Future Work
6.4. 局限与未来工作

Our evaluation showed the possibilities of using QtD to bridge quest design and level design. Participants emphasized its possible use to help communication and collaboration between designers as they speculated about it, and gave us a good insight into how the tool is used, its effectiveness and the design process. Yet since we only tested with single users and not with a team, we cannot conclude its usability as a communication and collaboration tool, which would be the next step for this project.
我们的评估展示了用QtD连接任务设计与关卡设计的可能性。参与者通过推测，强调了它可能帮助设计师沟通、协作的用途，并让我们很好地了解工具怎样使用、其有效性以及设计过程。不过，由于我们只测试了单个用户，没有测试团队，因此不能就它作为沟通与协作工具的可用性作出结论；这将是项目的下一步。

The implementation has several structural and expressive limitations. The fixed 6×6 grid, while being easy to understand, could constraint the scope and complexity of dungeons that designers can create. Participants created increasingly dense quest structures between quest 1 and 2, suggesting that the grid size may become a bottleneck for more complex narrative designs. Further, users can only select eight task types and the room generation follows similar templates for these tasks which could hinder designers’ expressivity. While participants responded positively to the Find and Gather tasks/rooms, the scope of narrative expression is still constrained compared to the full spectrum of quest possibilities in modern game design. The rigid, tile-based room generation also produces geometric layouts that, while functional, lack the organic feel that many games have.

当前实现具有若干结构与表达方面的局限。固定6×6网格虽然容易理解，却可能限制设计师能够创建的地牢的范围与复杂性。参与者从任务1到任务2创建了越来越密集的任务结构，这表明，对于更复杂的叙事设计，网格大小可能成为瓶颈。此外，用户只能选择八种环节类型，而各类型的房间生成遵循相近模板，这可能妨碍设计师的表达。虽然参与者对寻找与采集环节及房间反应积极，但与现代游戏设计中完整的任务可能性范围相比，叙事表达仍受限制。刚性的瓦片房间生成，也产生了一种虽然可用、却缺乏许多游戏所拥有的有机感的几何布局。

Therefore, in future iterations of QtD we aim at increasing task-types to include more nuanced narrative elements such as npc rooms, dialogue, important events etc. as well as common quest task types that could be extracted from previous research [20, 11] as well as improving the interface for easier development such as being able to delete entire tree of task nodes or quickly show key-lock combinations. We also aim at giving more control to designers with the generated rooms such as providing more granular control over room generation parameters while maintaining the tool’s accessibility. We aim at using color-coding and quest structure terms such as satellites and kernels [4] to help structure linear quests and alternative paths.

因此，在QtD的未来迭代中，我们希望增加环节类型，纳入更细腻的叙事要素，例如NPC房间、对话、重要事件等，也纳入可以从既有研究[20, 11]提取的常见任务环节类型；同时改进界面，让开发更容易，例如能够删除整棵环节节点树，或快速显示钥匙—锁组合。我们还希望在维持工具易用性的同时，让设计师对生成房间拥有更多控制，例如更细粒度地控制房间生成参数。我们计划利用颜色编码，以及“卫星”和“核心”等任务结构术语[4]，帮助组织线性任务与替代路径。
7. Conclusions
7. 结论

This paper presented Quest to Dungeon, a tool that connects human-authored quest design with procedural generation of levels constrained by the designed quests. Our overarching goal is to address collaboration challenges at design-phase (e.g., communication between departments and design specialties, brainstorming and pre-production development) and deployment-phase (e.g., misaligned content, combination of human-authored content with PCG tools). Our tool enables designers to define quest structures through a node grid that directly impacts the procedural generation of a dungeon layout and through this, we have demonstrated how narrative-driven level design can be achieved by translating quest tasks into interconnected rooms with task-specific properties. Our evaluation emphasized the easy-to-use and effectiveness of QtD to represent quests and tasks, as well as their level and room representation. By coupling quest logic with procedural generation, the tool demonstrates how quest design can guide PCG to create dynamic, task-aligned dungeons while also making it easier for developers to iterate rapidly. While limitations exist in the current implementation, the positive reception from participants suggests that tools such as QtD approach could meaningfully contribute to more efficient and cohesive game development workflows.

本文介绍了Quest to Dungeon，一种把人工编写的任务设计，与受这些任务约束的程序化关卡生成连接起来的工具。我们的总体目标，是应对设计阶段的协作挑战，例如部门与设计专长之间的沟通、头脑风暴和前期制作开发，以及部署阶段的协作挑战，例如内容失配、人工制作内容与PCG工具的结合。工具让设计师通过节点网格定义任务结构，直接影响地牢布局的程序化生成；我们由此展示了，如何把任务环节转化为相互连接、具有环节专属属性的房间，实现叙事驱动的关卡设计。评估强调了QtD在表示任务及其环节，以及相应关卡与房间方面的易用性和有效性。通过把任务逻辑与程序化生成耦合，工具展示了任务设计怎样引导PCG创建动态、与环节对齐的地牢，同时让开发者更容易快速迭代。虽然当前实现存在局限，参与者的积极反应表明，QtD这类工具方法，可能有意义地推动更高效、更连贯的游戏开发工作流。

从任务到地牢：支持叙事与关卡设计师协作的工具 Quest to Dungeon (QtD): Towards a Tool that Supports Collaboration between Narrative and Level Designers 从任务到地牢：支持叙事与关卡设计师协作的工具 Oscar Boutani 奥斯卡·布塔尼 Sam Shariati 萨姆·沙里亚蒂 Alberto Alvarez 阿尔韦托·阿尔瓦雷斯 2025 2026

任务故事希望玩家寻找什么、经历什么，关卡空间却未必能及时把这些意图表达出来。本文提出Quest to Dungeon（QtD）：设计师在6×6网格里组合空白、采集、寻找、战斗、钥匙、锁、首领和自定义环节，系统再以不同模板生成相应房间，使任务关系与空间布局一一对应。八名具有游戏开发背景的参与者，分别完成双结局任务和自由设计任务；问卷与操作日志显示，工具有助于可视化设计意图，也支持先搭布局再填任务、或先有故事再组织空间的迭代方式。生成房间不能直接编辑，控制感评价也较低；研究只测试了单个用户，因此跨设计岗位的协作效果仍是参与者的预期和后续研究目标。

text: Abstract Video games have historically been limited in the number of characters under AI control. This is all the more true for games that use declarative systems which are generally used for turn-based or otherwise non-real-time games. While a declarative system can obviously be used for a real-time simulation, we wanted to test the limits of how far it can be scaled for large numbers of characters. This paper shows how 5000 characters can run simultaneously and in real-time with 60fps performance on a modern laptop using a declarative logic programming language.

text: 摘要 电子游戏中受人工智能控制的角色数量，历来受到限制。对于使用声明式系统的游戏来说，这一点尤为明显，因为此类系统通常用于回合制游戏或其他非实时游戏。声明式系统显然可以用于实时模拟，但我们希望测试：当角色数量很大时，这种系统的规模究竟能够扩展到什么程度。本文展示了如何使用一种声明式逻辑编程语言，在现代笔记本电脑上让5000个角色同时实时运行，并达到60fps的性能。

text: 1. Introduction
1. 引言

Performance considerations have traditionally restricted the number of simultaneous NPCs, particularly when those characters are driven by symbolic rules or other declarative methods. Many systems that do support this kind of character AI are also turn-based rather than real-time. In this paper, we show that 5000 The Sims-style characters can be run simultaneously on a modern laptop using a version of logic programming.
性能方面的考虑，历来限制了能够同时存在的NPC数量，尤其当这些角色由符号规则或其他声明式方法驱动时。许多确实支持这类角色人工智能的系统，同样采用回合制而非实时运行。本文展示，使用逻辑编程的一种实现，可以在现代笔记本电脑上同时运行5000个《The Sims》式的角色。

Although Sims-style ‘needs-based AI’ is relatively simple, and the rendering of the characters in our demo is extremely simple (particle-like dots on the screen), this still demonstrates that symbolic, declarative techniques can be pushed well beyond what would have been though possible. In this paper, we will discuss the system, and the techniques used to make it so efficient.
尽管《The Sims》式的“基于需求的人工智能”相对简单，我们的演示中角色的渲染也极为简单——只是屏幕上类似粒子的圆点——但这依然说明，符号式、声明式技术能够被推进到远远超出原先可能设想的程度。本文将讨论这一系统，以及使它如此高效的技术。
2. Related Work
2. 相关工作

Many AI-based games have used symbolic declarative systems - logic, symbolic rules, or some kind of rule engine - for social reasoning and character control. Façade [1] used a reactive planner, ABL [2], that incorporated a forward-chaining production system. Prom Week [3] also used a forward-chaining production system, Comme Il Faut [4]. CiF’s successor the Ensemble Engine [5] is similarly a forward-chaining production system. The Sims 3 [6] used a rule system to script the interactions between situations, personality traits, and actions available to a given character [7]. MKULTRA [8] and City of Gangsters [9] both used logic programming to implement social reasoning [10]. F.E.A.R. makes use of a planner, GOAP, that allows for declarative definitions of various AIs in the GDBEdit database tool [11].

许多以人工智能为基础的游戏，都曾使用符号式的声明式系统——逻辑、符号规则或某种规则引擎——来进行社会推理和角色控制。《Façade》[1]使用了反应式规划器ABL[2]，其中包含一个前向链接产生式系统。《Prom Week》[3]同样使用前向链接产生式系统Comme Il Faut[4]。CiF的后继者Ensemble Engine[5]也是一种前向链接产生式系统。《The Sims 3》[6]使用规则系统，编写情境、人格特质和特定角色可用行动之间的相互关系[7]。《MKULTRA》[8]与《City of Gangsters》[9]均使用逻辑编程实现社会推理[10]。《F.E.A.R.》使用GOAP规划器，可以在GDBEdit数据库工具中，以声明式方式定义各种人工智能[11]。

One of the earliest and most influential symbolic systems for games is the Inform 7 language [12], [13] that allows designers to build interactive narrative systems using declarative statements. The Versu simulationist narrative system [14], [15] used a custom logic programming language, Praxis, based on an exotic modal logic called eremic logic (aka exclusion logic) [16]. The Lume system [17] made extensive use of Prolog’s definite clause grammars [18], [19] for text generation. Lapeyrade has also used Prolog for better character decision making [20].

用于游戏的最早、最具影响力的符号系统之一，是Inform 7语言[12], [13]；设计者可以用声明式语句构建交互叙事系统。模拟主义叙事系统Versu[14], [15]使用了一种定制的逻辑编程语言Praxis，它以一种特别的模态逻辑eremic logic（又称排除逻辑）为基础[16]。Lume系统[17]广泛使用Prolog的定子句文法[18], [19]来生成文本。Lapeyrade也曾使用Prolog来改善角色决策[20]。

All these games and systems use declarative programming for either some component of character control and/or social reasoning. Some are turn-based games like in the Versu platform, others are batch like jobs used in Townlikes (that still need to run fast but not at any particular frame rate), and others are real-time systems like with GOAP in F.E.A.R.. Even when used for real-time character control the number of NPCs is usually relatively low and the portion of the game logic that is declarative are the relations between possible actions and the world state. The code for how a Goal executes is still usually written in an imperative manner [11].

所有这些游戏和系统，都在角色控制的某些组成部分和／或社会推理中使用声明式编程。其中一些是Versu平台那样的回合制游戏，一些是Townlikes中使用的批处理式任务（仍然需要快速运行，但无须满足某一特定帧率），还有一些是实时系统，例如《F.E.A.R.》中的GOAP。即便用于实时角色控制，NPC数量通常仍相对较少，而且游戏逻辑中采用声明式表达的部分，是可能采取的行动与世界状态之间的关系。某个目标具体如何执行，其代码通常仍以命令式方式编写[11]。

There are also entire games that have been built using declarative languages, such as those built with the video game description language - VGDL [21]. Currently this technique is used to generate 2D tile arcade style games with the help of ASP and evolutionary search [22], [23]. These games are playable by a human and are fully declarative - everything from character controls to game logic to the tilemap itself are declared in text files that are used to generate a game. The purpose of these games is largely to allow for testing of general video game playing (GVGP) algorithms on several different games [24].
还有一些游戏，整个游戏都是用声明式语言构建的，例如使用电子游戏描述语言VGDL[21]制作的游戏。目前，这种技术在ASP与演化搜索的辅助下，用于生成二维图块式街机游戏[22], [23]。这些游戏可以由人类游玩，而且是完全声明式的：从角色控制、游戏逻辑到图块地图本身，所有内容都在用于生成游戏的文本文件中声明。这些游戏主要是为了能够在若干不同游戏上，测试通用电子游戏游玩（GVGP）算法[24]。

In large part because of the expense of AI simulation, games involving large-scale character simulation are relatively rare. The best known is Dwarf Fortress [25], which supports real-time simulation of small hundreds of characters. Achieving this level of performance requires implementation in C++ and significant programmer effort to optimize cache locality and minimize pointer chasing. RimWorld is a very similar game that also involves social simulation for the purpose of storytelling [26]. Caves Of Qud is a game that is more like adventure mode in DF and, similarly, features hundreds of characters that all have various social relations and need to choose what action to take each tick [27]. Unlike DF Fortress mode and RimWorld, this roguelike experience is turn based and as such doesn’t need to run at a particular frame rate. While all these games feature large numbers of characters acting in a world, none use declarative systems for the control of these NPCs.

涉及大规模角色模拟的游戏相对罕见，很大程度上是因为人工智能模拟的开销高昂。其中最著名的是《Dwarf Fortress》[25]，它支持数百个、但数量不算多的角色的实时模拟。要达到这种性能水平，需要用C++实现，并由程序员投入大量精力，优化缓存局部性、尽量减少指针追踪。《RimWorld》是一款非常相似的游戏，同样为了故事讲述而进行社会模拟[26]。《Caves Of Qud》更接近《Dwarf Fortress》（DF）的冒险模式，同样包含数百个具有各种社会关系的角色，而且每次更新都需要选择行动[27]。与DF的要塞模式和《RimWorld》不同，这种roguelike体验采用回合制，因此无须以某一特定帧率运行。虽然这些游戏都有大量角色在世界中行动，但它们都没有使用声明式系统来控制这些NPC。

Some large-scale crowd simulation exist for use in film and other rendered media forms [28], [29]. Some of these tools even allow the behaviors of the agents to be stated in sentence form for specific decision nodes [30]. These tools target rendered scenes for film and television and as such do not need to run in real-time.
一些大规模群体模拟系统用于电影及其他渲染媒介[28], [29]。其中一些工具甚至允许在特定决策节点上，以句子的形式描述智能体行为[30]。这些工具面向电影和电视的渲染场景，因此无须实时运行。

Some crowd simulation techniques have been used to study crowd dynamics and the creation of autonomous agents for visualization [31], [32]. Shao have claimed real-time performance at 30fps when animating up to 1400 characters moving and pathfinding around a 3D scene on 2007 hardware [31]. This was done with over 50,000 lines of C++ and uses a simple action selection method reminiscent of needs-based AI.
一些群体模拟技术曾用于研究群体动力学，以及为可视化创建自主智能体[31], [32]。Shao曾报告：使用2007年的硬件，为多达1400个在三维场景中移动、寻路的角色制作动画时，可以达到30fps的实时性能[31]。这一实现使用了超过50,000行C++代码，以及一种让人联想到基于需求的人工智能的简单动作选择方法。
3. Needs-based AI
3. 基于需求的人工智能

Needs-based AI is a famous technique for controlling characters in video games that was created for The Sims [33], [34], and has been used in other games like Roller Coaster Kingdom and an RPG for Lord Of the Rings [34].
基于需求的人工智能，是一种著名的电子游戏角色控制技术，最初为《The Sims》创立[33], [34]，也用于《Roller Coaster Kingdom》和一款《Lord Of the Rings》角色扮演游戏等其他游戏[34]。

Needs-based AI attempts to fulfill various needs for NPCs by searching over the actions of each object available to them (i.e. advertisements) and weighting the cost of completing the action against each character’s needs with some scoring function [34]. Each character goes about completing actions that have been selected/assigned to them, potentially getting rewarded for the various tasks. When no more actions remain in the queue of selected actions the NPC searches for all the advertisements on all the objects around them then scores each action based on their needs and selects the best scoring advertisement. The equation for selecting the best scoring advertisement is argmax(S) where S is the set of all scored advertisements for a given character.

基于需求的人工智能尝试满足NPC的各种需求：它搜索NPC可用的各个物体所提供的行动（即“广告”，advertisements），再通过某种评分函数，结合每个角色的需求，对完成行动的成本进行权衡[34]。每个角色会去完成已为自己选择或分配的行动，并可能因完成不同任务而获得奖励。当已选行动的队列中不再有待执行行动时，NPC便搜索周围所有物体上的全部广告，依据自身需求为各个行动评分，并选择得分最高的广告。选择最高分广告的公式为argmax(S)，其中S是某个角色的所有已评分广告所构成的集合。

The complexity of scoring all advertisements is O(NLM), where N is the number of people, L is the objects nearby, and M is the advertisements at each location. Once you have scored all advertisements for all characters, you can run the argmax equation for each character. Since argmax is operating on the set of all advertisements for each person, the complexity of selecting an action from the scored set is O(NLM), where N is the number of people, L is the objects nearby, and M is the advertisements. Given that these two steps are each of the same complexity, and that the two iterations are sequential, the total complexity of action selection is O(NLM).

为全部广告评分的复杂度为O(NLM)，其中N是人数，L是附近的物体数，M是每个地点上的广告数。为全部角色的所有广告评分之后，就可以对每个角色运行argmax公式。由于argmax处理的是每个人的全部广告所构成的集合，从已评分集合中选择一个行动的复杂度也是O(NLM)，其中N是人数，L是附近的物体数，M是广告数。鉴于这两个步骤的复杂度相同，而且两次迭代是顺序执行的，因此动作选择的总复杂度为O(NLM)。

The selected advertised action sequence is then added to the queue of actions to be completed. Needs-based AI has always had the ability to sequence actions, a technique called action chaining [34], but in The Sims 4 the developers wanted to be able to have more interesting action sequences. To accomplish this the developers allowed the system to simultaneously dispatch multiple actions from the queue when those actions would not interfere with one another [35].
接着，被选中的广告行动序列会加入待完成行动的队列。基于需求的人工智能一直具备把行动排成序列的能力，这种技术称为动作链[34]；不过，《The Sims 4》的开发者希望能够拥有更有趣的行动序列。为此，开发者允许系统在多个行动彼此不会干扰时，从队列中同时派发这些行动[35]。

The Sims 3 had a goal of creating a larger varied living world, and to do this while remaining playable several optimizations were employed [36]. Some execution optimizations such as hierarchical planning and commodity-interaction maps as well as some level of detail (LoD) optimizations such as auto-satisfy curves and story progression [36]. Hierarchical planning takes the usually O(NLM) approach of searching for every person (N), for every location (L), and then for every advertised action (M), and makes it O(N + L + M) by instead selecting each step one at a time. Commodity-interaction maps are essentially dictionaries of needs and the actions that satisfy those needs, and they are used to trade off compute time searching over all advertisements on all objects to see if they satisfy a sim’s needs with storage cost. The LoD optimizations tick the actions of sims not in the current focused level when they come into focus (auto-satisfy), and tick certain subsystems like the wants of the town itself at a lower rate (story progression). As a result, although the simulation notionally supports hundreds of characters, the vast majority of them are effectively idle at any given time. As well, although The Sims 3 has many more possible motives (needs) than the 8 used in previous versions, any individual character has a small number of those possible motives.

《The Sims 3》以创建一个更庞大、更多样的鲜活世界为目标，为了在做到这一点的同时保持可玩性，它采用了若干优化[36]。其中包括分层规划、需求资源与交互的映射等执行优化，以及自动满足曲线、故事进展等细节层次（LoD）优化[36]。通常的O(NLM)方法，会依次搜索每个人（N）、每个地点（L）、每个广告行动（M）；分层规划则改为每次只选择其中一个步骤，将复杂度变为O(N + L + M)。需求资源与交互的映射，本质上是需求及满足这些需求的行动所构成的字典；它们以存储成本，换取搜索所有物体的全部广告、判断是否满足某个模拟市民需求所需的计算时间。LoD优化会在当前关注层级之外的模拟市民进入关注范围时，更新其行动（自动满足），并以较低频率更新某些子系统，例如城镇本身的愿望（故事进展）。因此，虽然模拟在名义上支持数百个角色，但任一时刻，绝大多数角色实际上处于闲置状态。此外，虽然《The Sims 3》可能具有的动机（需求）远多于此前版本中的8种，但每个具体角色只具有这些可能动机中的少数几种。

3.1. Scoring functions
3.1. 评分函数

The scoring function that we use here is the most sophisticated function listed in Zubeks description of needs-based AI, an attenuated need-delta scoring function that is additionally attenuated based on distance [34]. One difference in our version is that each action can only satisfy one need. In the version of action performance outlined by Zubek, some actions can be sequences, and this can potentially allow for multiple needs to be fulfilled by an advertisement. As such, the algorithm for calculating an advertised action score must sum the attenuated scoring across all needs. Instead of summing across all needs, with each action only satisfying one need, we can simplify the attenuated need-delta scoring with distance attenuation to: $$\mathit{score}=D(A{need}(\nu{current})-A{need}(\nu{current}+\delta))$$

我们这里使用的评分函数，是Zubek对基于需求的人工智能的介绍中列出的最复杂函数：它是一种经过衰减处理的需求增量评分函数，还会根据距离进一步衰减[34]。我们的版本有一处不同：每个行动只能满足一种需求。在Zubek概述的行动执行版本中，一些行动可以构成序列，因此一个广告可能满足多种需求。这样，计算某个广告行动分数的算法，就必须对所有需求的衰减后分数求和。而在每个行动只满足一种需求的情况下，我们不再对所有需求求和，可以把带有距离衰减的需求增量衰减评分简化为： $$\mathit{score}=D(A{need}(\nu{current})-A{need}(\nu{current}+\delta))$$

where $\nu{current}$ is the current need value of a particular need type, $\delta$ advertised need delta, $A{need}$ is an attenuation function, and $D$ is the distance attenuation function. $A{need}(x)=\frac{10}{x}$ as is discussed in Zubek, but instead of the mentioned $D(x)=\frac{x}{distance^2}$ function ours is $D(x)=\frac{x}{1+(\frac{distance^2}{2870})}$ to tune down the degree to which NPCs attenuate distance. The value 2870 was not chosen at random, it relates to the size of the map that the characters move on and effectively scales $distance^2$ to be between 1 and 30 (as opposed to a max of 82369).

其中，$\nu{current}$是某种需求类型的当前需求值，$\delta$是广告所给出的需求增量，$A{need}$是衰减函数，$D$是距离衰减函数。与Zubek所讨论的一样，$A{need}(x)=\frac{10}{x}$；但我们没有使用其中提到的$D(x)=\frac{x}{distance^2}$函数，而是采用$D(x)=\frac{x}{1+(\frac{distance^2}{2870})}$，以减弱NPC对距离进行衰减的程度。2870这个值并非随机选择，它与角色移动的地图大小有关，实际上把$distance^2$缩放到1至30之间（而不是最大达到82369）。

One more simplification in the current demo is that all locations only advertise a single action. In effect, a location has a type that correlates to a need. As such, the complexity of this scoring algorithm can be given as O(NL), where N is the number of NPCs that need to select actions and L is the number of locations to search over.
当前演示还作了一项简化：所有地点都只发布一种行动广告。实际上，每个地点都有一个与某种需求相对应的类型。因此，这一评分算法的复杂度可以写作O(NL)，其中N是需要选择行动的NPC数量，L是需要搜索的地点数量。
4. Real-time logic programming
4. 实时逻辑编程

To test the scaling limits of declarative symbolic logical methods for real-time NPC control, we built a state-fair simulator, as one might find in a tycoon game, using a logic-programming implementation of needs-based AI. NPC’s wander through the state fair eating, drinking, seeking entertainments, and so on. The simulation consists of a map with 367 locations, onto which we spawn a few thousand NPCs. Each character has 6 motivations (hunger, bathroom, games, amusement, music, and shopping) that influence their action selection.
为了测试声明式符号逻辑方法用于实时NPC控制时的规模极限，我们以逻辑编程实现基于需求的人工智能，构建了一款州博览会模拟器，类似于大亨类游戏中可能出现的那种模拟器。NPC在博览会中闲逛，吃东西、喝饮料、寻找娱乐，等等。模拟包含一张具有367个地点的地图，我们在地图上生成数千个NPC。每个角色都有6种动机（饥饿、如厕、游戏、游乐、音乐和购物），它们会影响角色的动作选择。

text: 4.2. Implementation optimizations
4.2. 实现层面的优化

The performance of the system is dependent on several optimizations. Many of these have to do with the specific programming language implementation: strong typing, bottom-up execution, parallel execution, native code compilation. The details of the language implementation are outside the scope of this paper but see [37], [38] for more information.
系统性能取决于若干优化。其中许多与具体的编程语言实现有关：强类型、自底向上执行、并行执行、原生代码编译。语言实现的细节不在本文讨论范围之内，更多信息见[37], [38]。

Another important optimization might be called implicit need decay. Normally, a needs-based AI system would update each need state of each character on every tick. For our system, this would be prohibitively expensive. Instead, we store timestamped need values; a need value is represented as a tuple of $(v,t,ho)$ stating that the need had value $
u$ at time $t$, and was decaying at rate $ho$. We can then compute the current need value on demand as: $$
u{current}=\max(
u-(t-t{now})ho)$$

另一项重要优化，可以称为隐式需求衰减。通常，基于需求的人工智能系统会在每次更新时，更新每个角色的每一种需求状态。对于我们的系统，这样做的成本高到无法承受。因此，我们改为保存带有时间戳的需求值：需求值由一个元组$(v,t,ho)$表示，意为该需求在时刻$t$具有值$
u$，并以速率$ho$衰减。这样便可以按需计算当前需求值： $$
u{current}=\max(
u-(t-t{now})ho)$$

with $t{now}$ being the current time. Since these values are read infrequently but would otherwise be updated frequently, this is much more efficient. As is recommended by Zubek, decay rates for a given need vary slightly from character to character to give them slightly different “personalities”. These decay rates are chosen randomly (Appendix A, Code Fragment 3).
其中，$t{now}$是当前时间。由于这些值读取频率不高，而采用另一种做法却需要频繁更新它们，因此这样做高效得多。按照Zubek的建议，同一种需求的衰减速率，在不同角色之间略有差异，以赋予角色稍有不同的“个性”。这些衰减速率随机选取（附录A，代码片段3）。
4.3. Action States
4.3. 行动状态

For characters to perform a selected action they must move to the location of the selected action and then take some steps to complete the action before the need is satisfied. While we could allow for completion of actions instantaneously, to be more in line with The Sims implementation - as specified by Zubek – we instead have some action performance before a need is satisfied.
要执行已选行动，角色必须移动到该行动所在地点，再经过若干步骤来完成行动，之后需求才得到满足。我们原本可以让行动瞬间完成，但为了更贴近Zubek所描述的《The Sims》实现，我们选择先让角色执行一段行动，再满足需求。

When an action is initiated, the system tells the unity code to start moving the character, and then marks the character as being in progress towards that location. When the character arrives at the location they are marked as no longer moving towards their destination. When the action is completed, unity informs the system, and the system updates the need states, and generates a new next action (Appendix A, Code Fragment 6, 7, 8, 11). In place of the animations that would normally be running when performing an action, we simulate an animation running by starting a timer that indicates the selected action is being done (Appendix A, Code Fragment 9).
当一个行动开始时，系统告知Unity代码开始移动角色，再把角色标记为正在前往该地点。角色到达地点后，会被标记为不再向目的地移动。行动完成时，Unity通知系统，系统便更新需求状态，并生成下一个新的行动（附录A，代码片段6、7、8、11）。执行行动时通常会播放动画；我们改为启动一个计时器，以表明所选行动正在进行，借此模拟动画正在播放（附录A，代码片段9）。

Unlike in The Sims all actions in this simulation are individual, there is no chaining of actions nor are there any concurrent interactions. This simplification is what allows us to use a timer for each person taking an action, when the timer is running the “animation” is playing and when the timer completes the character has completed the action and finished its animation. While we do not have proper animations for each sim, when on a timer for an action the sim is moving randomly around the location that they have selected an action at.
与《The Sims》不同，本模拟中的所有行动都各自独立，没有动作链，也没有并发交互。正是这种简化，使我们能够为每个正在采取行动的人使用一个计时器：计时器运行时，“动画”正在播放；计时器结束时，角色便完成了行动，也结束了动画。虽然我们没有为每个模拟市民制作正式动画，但当行动计时器运行时，该模拟市民会在其所选行动的地点附近随机移动。
4.4. Destinations & Unity Interface
4.4. 目的地与Unity接口

For control of character movements, we have a simple interface between the action selection simulation and the Unity code that performs movements. The Simulog code provides a table of people and the destination they are moving to (Appendix A, Code Fragment 7) that the Unity code iterates over each tick to adjust NPC positions. The Unity code in turn provides a function that we can call to ask if someone has arrived at their destination. With this simple interface of action selection assigning destinations to the Unity code and Unity only needing to report back when someone has arrived at the destination, we are able to change out the underlying movement implementation without needing to do any modifications to the action selection algorithm. Currently, the movement is all simple vector addition moving sims at a set speed straight towards their destination.

为了控制角色移动，我们在动作选择模拟与执行移动的Unity代码之间，设置了一个简单接口。Simulog代码提供一个包含人物及其正前往的目的地的表（附录A，代码片段7），Unity代码在每次更新时遍历该表，以调整NPC的位置。Unity代码反过来提供一个可供调用的函数，用以询问某人是否已经到达目的地。通过这个简单接口，动作选择向Unity代码分配目的地，Unity则只需在某人到达目的地时报告回来；这样，我们便能够替换底层移动实现，而无须修改动作选择算法。目前，所有移动都是简单的向量加法，让模拟市民以固定速度，沿直线向目的地移动。

The graph in Figure 2 shows the progression of the simulation over a 25,000-tick run time. The first 5000 ticks spawn one person every tick causing the slow rise in compute time for both the action selection mechanism and the inner-frame updates. For the next 7500 ticks characters begin to arrive at their first destination and need to select their next action, creating a tiered slope in the action selection performance as various numbers of characters need to select an action. From 12500 ticks on we have a steady state where performance is consistent and linear with NPCs now moving around and selecting actions at a rate of 13.7 actions selected on average per tick for our sample with a σ of 3.8 actions.

There is also a baseline cost to running the rest of the declarative simulation when not performing action selection. As can be seen in Figures 2 and 4, the cost of running our declarative simulation on 5000 characters without any action selection takes about 1ms.

5.1. Pushing character counts
5.1. 提高角色数量

The performance shown above is only possible when we first compile our rules down to native C code, the process for which is described in [37], [38], and then we run our compiled code in parallel. The type of parallelism employed is per predicate, not per sim, utilizing the dependency graph for all predicates to spin up tasks that run the compiled rules for a given predicate only when its dependencies have finished. Without these optimizations the maximum character count at nearly the same performance is 2000 NPCs.
要达到上述性能，必须先把规则编译成原生C代码，再并行运行编译后的代码；编译过程见[37], [38]。所用并行方式是按谓词划分，而非按模拟市民划分：利用全部谓词的依赖图启动任务，只有当给定谓词的各项依赖都完成后，才运行该谓词编译后的规则。没有这些优化时，在近似相同的性能下，最多只能运行2000个NPC。

One optimization that could be employed to further stabilize performance (and potentially allow for more NPCs) is to throttle the number of characters that are selecting actions on a given tick. With a limit on the number of characters selecting actions that is slightly higher than the un-limited average number selecting you could effectively cap the cost of doing action selection while still eventually performing the same sets of needs-based calculations. This technique was not employed in this demo but a commercial system that cares more about never dropping below 60fps may want to implement such a throttle.
有一项可采用的优化，能够进一步稳定性能，并有可能支持更多NPC：限制每次更新中选择行动的角色数量。如果把选择行动的角色数上限设为略高于无限制时的平均选择人数，就可以有效限制动作选择的成本，同时最终仍完成相同的那组基于需求的计算。这个演示没有采用此项技术；不过，如果商业系统更看重绝不降至60fps以下，就可能希望实现这样的限流。
6. Conclusion
6. 结论

AI character control based on declarative programming can be surprisingly performant. Through a combination of compilation, parallel evaluation, and careful optimization, thousands of characters can be run at video frame rate. Although this demonstration involves simple needs-based AI, we intend to investigate more complicated techniques in the future.
以声明式编程为基础的人工智能角色控制，其性能可以高得令人意外。通过结合编译、并行求值和仔细优化，可以让数千个角色按视频帧率运行。尽管此次演示涉及的是简单的基于需求的人工智能，我们打算在未来考察更复杂的技术。

Abstract
摘要

Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) are used in a variety of machine learning tasks such as image classification and pattern recognition. Training ANN models on large datasets can be time consuming and require specialized hardware and processing power. Often, the training is performed on powerful systems, and the resultant final trained network can be utilized on small computers and mobile devices to perform tasks instantly. The Nintendo Entertainment System (NES) was released in 1985 and featured a 1.79 MHz CPU and 2 KB of RAM. The original program code for games for the NES fit within 32 KB of ROM on cartridges. In this work, we create an ANN and train it using the EMNIST hand-drawn digit dataset on a desktop computer. This ANN is then ported to the NES utilizing assembly language. The program code and pretrained weights are stored to a game cartridge fitting within the bounds of 32 KB. Additionally, a user interface is provided for drawing and loading test samples and executing the ANN classification of hand drawn digits on a physical NES device from 40 years ago.

人工神经网络（ANN）用于图像分类、模式识别等多种机器学习任务。在大型数据集上训练ANN模型可能耗时较长，并需要专门的硬件和处理能力。训练通常在性能强大的系统上进行，而最终训练好的网络可以用于小型计算机和移动设备，即时执行任务。任天堂娱乐系统（NES）于1985年发布，配有1.79 MHz的CPU和2 KB的RAM。NES游戏最初的程序代码可容纳在卡带32 KB的ROM之内。在本项工作中，我们创建了一个ANN，使用EMNIST手绘数字数据集在台式计算机上对其进行训练，随后用汇编语言将这个ANN移植到NES。程序代码和预训练权重存放在一张游戏卡带中，总容量不超出32 KB。此外，我们提供了一个用户界面，用于绘制和加载测试样本，并在一台40年前的实体NES设备上运行ANN，对手绘数字进行分类。

1. Introduction
1. 引言

Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) are a part of Machine Learning (ML) and are used for several different kinds of tasks such as classification and segmentation [1] as well as prediction [2]. The applications of ANN are numerous and are often used to solve problems in a wide range of fields including science, finance, engineering, agriculture, education, and energy [3].
人工神经网络（ANN）属于机器学习（ML），可用于分类和分割[1]、预测[2]等多种不同任务。ANN的应用很多，经常用于解决科学、金融、工程、农业、教育和能源等众多领域的问题[3]。

A simple architecture for an ANN may involve three layers known as the input, hidden, and output layers [4], though more advanced ANNs like those in Deep Learning (DL) will have several different layers [5]. These layers contain nodes with connections from previous layers, a bias and weights. Data will feed forward through the network producing an output. The learning process involves updating these weights. One of the most common algorithms for this is known as backpropagation [6].
ANN的一种简单架构可以包含输入层、隐藏层和输出层这三层[4]，而深度学习（DL）中的ANN等更先进的网络会有多种不同的层[5]。这些层包含节点，节点具有来自前一层的连接、一个偏置和若干权重。数据沿网络前向传递，产生输出。学习过程涉及更新这些权重。其中一种最常用的算法称为反向传播[6]。

ANNs typically use the IEEE-754 single or double-precision floating-point format [7]. To perform the math required, devices must have a floating-point unit (FPU) along with the usual CPU. Originally used for 2D and 3D graphics acceleration for games, Graphics Processing Units (GPU) are now commonly used for machine learning [8]. In 2015 Google introduced the Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) to increase performance for neural networks and use less power than GPUs [9].
ANN通常使用IEEE-754单精度或双精度浮点格式[7]。为了执行所需的数学运算，设备除了通常的CPU之外，还必须具有浮点运算单元（FPU）。图形处理器（GPU）最初用于游戏的二维和三维图形加速，如今也常用于机器学习[8]。2015年，谷歌推出张量处理单元（TPU），以提高神经网络的性能，并使其功耗低于GPU[9]。

The Nintendo Entertainment System (NES) was originally released in North America in 1985 [10]. The NES featured a Ricoh 2A03 chip that was based on the 8-bit 6502 processor operating at 1.79 MHz [11]. The NES also had only 2 KB of RAM available. The program (game) code is stored within ROM chips on the game cartridges. The original Super Mario Bros. fit within an original restriction of 32 KB of program ROM space [12] before the later creation of memory mapper chips.
任天堂娱乐系统（NES）最初于1985年在北美发布[10]。NES配备Ricoh 2A03芯片，该芯片基于8位6502处理器，工作频率为1.79 MHz[11]。NES可用的RAM也只有2 KB。程序（游戏）代码存储在游戏卡带的ROM芯片中。在后来出现内存映射芯片之前，最初的《Super Mario Bros.》被容纳在最初32 KB程序ROM空间的限制之内[12]。

In this experimental work, we demonstrate that an ANN is capable of running even with severe hardware constraints. We created a simple ANN in the C programming language and trained it on a dataset of small images on a modern computer. The program code for the ANN is ported to 6502 assembly language and includes the pretrained weights from the ANN model. By reducing dimensionality of the images and using a small number of hidden nodes we were able to fit within the 32 KB limit. The program code is placed onto a specialized game cartridge and loaded into the physical NES hardware. We also developed a user interface (UI) which allows the user to draw images as well as load sample dataset images using the NES gamepad. Pressing START executes the ANN and displays its classification of the image.

在这项实验性工作中，我们展示了ANN即使在严格的硬件限制下也能够运行。我们使用C语言创建了一个简单的ANN，并在现代计算机上用一个小图像数据集进行训练。ANN的程序代码被移植到6502汇编语言，并包含ANN模型的预训练权重。通过降低图像维度并使用少量隐藏节点，我们使其容纳在32 KB的限制之内。程序代码被写入一张专用游戏卡带，并加载到实体NES硬件中。我们还开发了一个用户界面（UI），让用户可以使用NES手柄绘制图像，也可以加载数据集中的样本图像。按下START键即可运行ANN，并显示它对图像的分类结果。
2. Materials and Methods
2. 材料与方法
2.1. Dataset
2.1. 数据集

The MNIST dataset [13] consists of hand drawn digit (0 – 9) images and is often referred to as the “hello world” of neural networks and deep learning [14]. The dimensions of the images are 28x28 and contain grayscale values ranging from 0 - 255. Examples of the dataset images can be seen in Figure 1. The training set contains 60,000 images with the testing set having 10,000. These sets are balanced with 6,000 of each digit in the training set and 1,000 of each digit in the testing set. Given we are pretraining the neural network on a modern computer, we opted to use the larger EMNIST dataset [15] which is an extension of MNIST containing four times the number of images of MNIST. This dataset has 240,000 images in the training set and 40,000 in the testing set. These sets are also balanced.

MNIST数据集[13]由手绘数字（0—9）的图像组成，常被称为神经网络和深度学习的“hello world”[14]。图像尺寸为28x28，灰度值范围为0—255。图1展示了数据集图像的例子。训练集包含60,000幅图像，测试集包含10,000幅。两个集合中的类别均衡，训练集中每个数字各有6,000幅图像，测试集中每个数字各有1,000幅。由于我们在现代计算机上预训练神经网络，因此选择使用规模更大的EMNIST数据集[15]；它是MNIST的扩展，图像数量为MNIST的四倍。这个数据集的训练集有240,000幅图像，测试集有40,000幅，两个集合中的类别也都均衡。
Figure 1: Example digit images.
图1：数字图像示例。
2.2. Preparing the Data
2.2. 数据准备

We took multiple steps to reduce the dimensionality of the images to work within memory constraints. First, we changed pixel values from a range of 0 - 255 to be just binary values of 0 or 1. Any pixel value less than 128 was changed to 0 with 128 or greater becoming a 1. Figure 2 shows an image with grayscale values and then changed to binary values. Reducing the values to bits allowed for 8 pixels to be packed into a single byte. This reduced storage requirements by almost ⅛ for our input weight data and loadable test samples.
为了在内存限制内工作，我们采取了多个步骤来降低图像维度。首先，将像素值从0—255的范围改为仅有0或1的二值。任何小于128的像素值都改为0，而大于或等于128的值改为1。图2展示了一幅灰度图像及其转换为二值后的图像。将数值缩减为比特之后，便可以把8个像素打包到一个字节中。对于我们的输入权重数据和可加载测试样本，这使存储需求减少了近⅛。
Figure 2: Left: Original 256 grayscale image. Right: 1-bit binary image.
图2：左：原始的256级灰度图像。右：1位二值图像。

Our goal was to reduce the image resolution to 20×20 with minimal scaling required. Given that the images in the dataset are centered, columns of pixels on the left and right, as well as rows on the top and bottom of the image, can be discarded as they contain no information about the digit. This can be seen in Figure 3. We discarded rows and columns with 2 or fewer pixels of a value of 1.
我们的目标是将图像分辨率降低到20×20，并尽可能减少所需的缩放。由于数据集中的图像居中，图像左右两侧的像素列以及上下两侧的像素行不包含关于数字的信息，因此可以丢弃。图3展示了这一点。我们丢弃了那些值为1的像素数量不超过2个的行和列。
Figure 3: Pixel grid indicating candidate rows/columns to be removed.
图3：标示候选待删除行／列的像素网格。
2.3. Neural Network
2.3. 神经网络

Figure 4 shows the configuration of our ANN. The input layer contains the pixel information of the current image. With our input images having dimensions 20×20, there will be 400 input nodes. As in most neural networks, every input node is connected to every hidden node [16]. Our model uses 16 hidden nodes. Here, we introduce an optimization. Given our pixel input values are either 0 or 1, and these values are multiplied by the weights, input values of 0 can simply be skipped. Additionally, with an input value of 1, we can skip the multiplication and just add the weight to the node’s total. Every hidden node connects to every output node. There are 10 output nodes, one for each digit (0 – 9). All of our nodes also have a bias. Originally, the Sigmoid activation function [17] was popular for neural networks however we opted to use the Leaky ReLU function [18] as it provided better performance.

图4展示了我们ANN的配置。输入层包含当前图像的像素信息。由于输入图像的尺寸为20×20，输入节点将有400个。与大多数神经网络一样，每个输入节点都连接到每个隐藏节点[16]。我们的模型使用16个隐藏节点。在这里，我们引入了一项优化。像素输入值只有0或1，而这些值要与权重相乘，因此可以直接跳过输入值为0的情况。此外，当输入值为1时，可以跳过乘法，直接将权重加到节点的总和中。每个隐藏节点都连接到每个输出节点。输出节点共有10个，分别对应每个数字（0—9）。我们所有的节点也都有一个偏置。Sigmoid激活函数[17]最初曾广泛用于神经网络，不过我们选择使用Leaky ReLU函数[18]，因为它提供了更好的性能。
Figure 4: Diagram of our ANN.
图4：我们的ANN示意图。
Input 1; Input 2; Input 400 Hidden 1; Hidden 16 Output 1; Output 10

With 20×20 input nodes each connected to 16 hidden nodes at 4-bytes per floating-point weight, this would use (20×20×16×4) 25,600 bytes of space. Additionally, the 16 hidden nodes connected to the 10 output nodes is (16×10×4) 640 bytes. Each of the 16 hidden nodes and 10 nodes have a bias input for (16×4 + 10×4) 104 bytes. The stored pretrained weights occupy 26,344 of our total 32,768 program ROM space leaving 6,424 bytes for our code that runs the user interface and executes the ANN to perform the classification.

20×20个输入节点各自连接到16个隐藏节点，每个浮点权重占4字节，这将使用（20×20×16×4）25,600字节的空间。此外，16个隐藏节点与10个输出节点相连，占用（16×10×4）640字节。16个隐藏节点和10个节点各自都有一个偏置输入，共占（16×4＋10×4）104字节。存储的预训练权重占总计32,768字节程序ROM空间中的26,344字节，余下6,424字节留给运行用户界面、执行ANN分类的代码。
2.4. Hardware and Tools
2.4. 硬件与工具

While modern machine learning research is typically developed in the Python programming language using libraries such as PyTorch, Keras, and TensorFlow [19], our ANN is coded from scratch in the C programming language without any of these types of libraries. This allowed for a more direct port to the 6502 assembly language required for developing for the NES. After training, the weights were exported to a format that could be included by a 6502 assembly compiler. Given the NES is an 8-bit processor with no floating point support, in order to port our neural network, we used a floating point library developed by Roy Rankin and Steve Wozniak [20]. To run our program on a physical NES device, we loaded our program onto an SD card and placed it into a Krikzz Everdrive N8 Pro cartridge which can be seen in the left of Figure 5. This cartridge was then placed into an original NES from 1985 seen on the right in Figure 5.

现代机器学习研究通常用Python语言，借助PyTorch、Keras和TensorFlow等库开展[19]；而我们的ANN使用C语言从零编写，没有使用任何这类库。这使它更便于直接移植到开发NES程序所需的6502汇编语言。训练完成后，权重被导出为一种可由6502汇编编译器纳入程序的格式。由于NES使用的是不支持浮点运算的8位处理器，为了移植神经网络，我们采用了Roy Rankin和Steve Wozniak开发的浮点运算库[20]。为了在实体NES设备上运行程序，我们将程序载入一张SD卡，再将其放入Krikzz Everdrive N8 Pro卡带中，如图5左侧所示。随后，将该卡带插入一台1985年的原版NES，如图5右侧所示。

3. Experiments and Discussion
3. 实验与讨论

We trained our ANN on the EMNIST dataset on a desktop computer. We used a learning rate of 0.01, an alpha value of 0.01 for LeakyReLU and 5 epochs. The training completed in 21 seconds. Our simple ANN achieved a 93.11% accuracy on the EMNIST test set. This number could be higher with a larger neural network however for this experiment we needed to stay within the 32 KB limit. 4. Conclusion
4. 结论

In this experimental work, we created a basic ANN image classifier which was trained on a modern computer and then exported the weights from the various layers. We greatly reduced the dimensionality of the input images and used a small set of hidden nodes in order to fit within a 32 KB limit. The ANN was ported to assembly language and using the UI, a user can draw or load testing images and execute the ANN. This demonstrates the 1985 NES is capable of using a basic ANN with pretrained weights to successfully classify digit images.
在这项实验性工作中，我们创建了一个基础的ANN图像分类器，在现代计算机上对其进行训练，随后导出各层的权重。为了容纳在32 KB的限制之内，我们大幅降低了输入图像的维度，并使用了少量隐藏节点。ANN被移植到汇编语言；用户可通过UI绘制或加载测试图像，并运行ANN。这表明，1985年的NES能够利用具有预训练权重的基础ANN，成功对数字图像进行分类。

Future work includes using memory mapper (bank swapping) chips to enable more ROM and therefore larger models to be stored. Additional future work includes building a Reinforcement Learning model that could be used for game AI on the NES.
未来的工作包括使用内存映射（存储体切换）芯片，提供更多ROM空间，从而存储更大的模型。其他未来工作还包括构建一种可用于NES游戏AI的强化学习模型。

Abstract Recent advances in board game agents have led to superhuman performances in various games, but their decision-making processes remain opaque even to experienced players and are not cognitive-plausible from a human perspective. Based on criteria for cognitive-plausible systems, we introduce an approach that emphasizes interpretable knowledge representation through pattern-based and hierarchical structures. Our approach uses Genetic Programming to learn feature programs that capture spatial relationships on the game board. In addition, it utilizes decision trees to model agent behavior based on these feature programs. The result is a hierarchical, pattern-based model for generating post-hoc explanations for board game agents. We show that our method generates comprehensible explanations in Tic-Tac-Toe. We then discuss the current limitations in generalizing the approach to more complex games using Connect 4 as an example.

摘要。棋盘游戏智能体近年的进展，使它们在多种游戏中取得了超越人类的表现；然而，即使对于经验丰富的玩家，它们的决策过程仍然不透明，从人的角度看也不具有认知合理性。依据符合认知合理性的系统应满足的标准，我们提出一种方法，着重通过基于模式和层级的结构，实现可解释的知识表示。该方法用遗传编程学习能够捕捉棋盘空间关系的特征程序，并基于这些特征程序，用决策树建模智能体行为。由此得到一种具有层级、基于模式的模型，为棋盘游戏智能体生成事后解释。我们展示该方法能够在井字棋中生成可理解的解释，随后以四子棋为例，讨论当前将其推广到更复杂游戏时存在的局限。
Keywords Explainable Reinforcement Learning, Genetic Programming, Board Games, Human-like Game Playing
关键词：可解释强化学习，遗传编程，棋盘游戏，类人游戏游玩。
1. Introduction
1 引言

Although board game agents have demonstrated impressive superhuman playing strength in various domains [1, 2], they are not fully comprehensible in terms of why an action is taken, even for professional players. Furthermore, from a cognitive science perspective, the decision-making process of these agents does not resemble the way humans play games [3, 4]. Mándziuk proposes multiple “facets of cognitive-plausible playing systems” about knowledge acquisition and representation [4]. The method we propose addresses both postulates from Mańdziuk [4] concerning knowledge representation: (P1) “Game-related concepts may be effectively represented and processed with the use of pattern-based representation.” (P2) “game-related knowledge should be represented in a hierarchichal structure with various interand intra-level connections.” To that end, we present an approach for explaining board game agents by learning feature programs, i.e., programs that represent single or multiple grid cells and their relation to other cells with Genetic Programming. This is similar to P1 and the work about visual routines – a method to extract spatial information from scenes [5]. In addition, feature programs can represent intra-level connections of P2. By learning a decision tree on the feature activation of these programs, our method can highlight activated features for given state-action pairs, i.e., a hierarchical structure representing the inter-level connections of P2.

尽管棋盘游戏智能体已在多个领域表现出超越人类的棋力[1,2]，但它们为何采取某项行动，即使专业玩家也无法充分理解。此外，从认知科学角度看，这些智能体的决策过程并不像人类下棋的方式[3,4]。Mándziuk针对知识获取与表示，提出了“符合认知合理性的游戏系统”的多个方面[4]。我们的方法回应了Mańdziuk关于知识表示的两条设想[4]：（P1）“借助基于模式的表示，可以有效地表示和处理与游戏有关的概念。”（P2）“与游戏有关的知识，应表示为一种具有多种层间及层内连接的层级结构。”为此，我们提出通过遗传编程学习特征程序，以解释棋盘游戏智能体；这里的程序表示一个或多个网格单元，以及它们与其他单元的关系。这类似于P1，也类似于视觉例程研究——从场景中提取空间信息的一种方法[5]。特征程序还可以表示P2中的层内连接。通过根据这些程序的特征激活情况学习一棵决策树，我们能够针对给定的状态—行动对，突出显示已激活的特征；这一层级结构表示了P2中的层间连接。

An important point worth discussing in advance is whether these postulates are necessary or sufficient for human comprehensibility and cognitive-plausibility. While pattern-based and hierarchical representations may be necessary because they correspond to human perception of recurring structures and the organization of knowledge, they are unlikely to be sufficient [6]. Human comprehensibility also depends on other aspects, such as the abstraction and combination of strategies [7], analogical thinking [8], and the ability to convey explanations in intuitive terms. We will show in our approach that adherence to the postulates contributes to more interpretable models, but a broader spectrum of mechanisms is needed to better approximate cognitive-plausibility [9].

有一点应当事先讨论：这些设想对于人的可理解性和认知合理性，究竟是必要条件还是充分条件？基于模式与层级的表示，或许是必要的，因为它们对应人类对重复结构的感知以及知识的组织方式；但它们不太可能是充分的[6]。人的可理解性还取决于其他方面，例如策略的抽象和组合[7]、类比思维[8]，以及用直观语言传达解释的能力。我们将展示，遵循这些设想有助于得到更可解释的模型，但若要更接近认知合理性，还需要更广泛的一组机制[9]。

We show that the proposed method generates comprehensible explanations for Tic-Tac-Toe. In addition, we present preliminary results for Connect 4 and discuss the limitations that need to be overcome to apply the method to more complex games.
我们展示所提方法能够为井字棋生成可理解的解释；同时给出四子棋的初步结果，并讨论将该方法用于更复杂游戏时，必须克服的局限。
Our contributions are:
我们的贡献如下：
• We present first steps towards a cognitive-plausible approach to explain board game agents.
• 迈出以符合认知合理性的方式解释棋盘游戏智能体的第一步。
• We show a proof of concept for generating explanations using the game Tic-Tac-Toe as an example.
• 以井字棋为例，展示生成解释的概念验证。
• We conduct a case study which outlines the improvements necessary to apply the method on more complex games such as Connect 4.
• 开展一项案例研究，勾勒把该方法应用于四子棋等更复杂游戏所需的改进。

The remainder of the paper is structured as follows: In Section 2 we review related work about genetic programming in the context of board games, as well as program synthesis approaches applied to explainability and interpretability in games. Section 3 introduces the domain-specific language and the representation of programs. The data collection process and methodology are described in Section 4. Subsequently, Section 5 presents and discusses the results of our case studies on Tic-Tac-Toe and Connect 4. Finally, Section 6 summarizes our contributions and outlines directions for future work.
文章其余部分安排如下。第2节回顾棋盘游戏中的遗传编程，以及应用于游戏可解释性与可理解性的程序合成研究。第3节介绍领域专用语言与程序表示。第4节说明数据收集过程和方法。随后，第5节展示并讨论井字棋与四子棋案例的结果。最后，第6节总结贡献并勾勒未来工作方向。
2. Related Work
2 相关工作

The majority of research that uses GP in the context of board games, search for heuristics for evaluating game states. These heuristics are evolved over mathematical functions for games such as Lose Checkers, Reversi, or Seven Wonders [10, 11, 12]. However, searching for heuristics is undesired, as a search algorithm is still necessary. Besides, using heuristics in a search algorithm is not fully explainable, and, in most cases, is cognitively implausible. Nevertheless, heuristics for evaluating game states, are more interpretable than using a combination of deep learning and search algorithms, similar to AlphaZero [1].

在棋盘游戏中使用遗传编程（GP）的研究，多数是在寻找评估游戏状态的启发式函数。这些启发式函数通过对数学函数进行进化而得到，用于求败跳棋、黑白棋或《七大奇迹》等游戏[10,11,12]。然而，寻找启发式函数并不理想，因为仍然需要搜索算法。此外，在搜索算法中使用启发式函数，并不能得到完全的解释，而且大多不符合认知合理性。不过，与AlphaZero[1]那样结合深度学习与搜索算法的方式相比，评估游戏状态的启发式函数仍更容易理解。

Silver et al. learn logical programs which are extracted from decision trees for simple, game-related tasks [13]. In [14], an inductive logic programming algorithm is introduced that finds comprehensible game strategies by providing the game rules as building blocks for logic programs for simple board games. Currently, our method does not use game rules, as they can be derived from the state-action pairs. However, our method is more difficult to learn without game rules.
Silver等人为简单的游戏相关任务，学习从决策树提取的逻辑程序[13]。文献[14]提出一种归纳逻辑编程算法，把游戏规则作为逻辑程序的构建模块，从而为简单棋盘游戏找到可理解的策略。我们的方法目前不使用游戏规则，因为可以从状态—行动对中推导它们；然而，没有游戏规则，我们的方法学习起来也更困难。

The use of programs for explainability in the context of game AI was introduced for a maze-runner agent and two simplified Atari games: Space Invaders and Asterix [15]. In contrast to generating explanations, large language models are used to directly evolve programs as policies for a wide range of digital games, as well as programs as heuristic functions for board games [16].
游戏AI中的程序解释方法，最初用于一个迷宫奔跑智能体，以及两个简化的Atari游戏：《太空侵略者》和Asterix[15]。与生成解释不同，另一项工作用大语言模型直接进化程序：既把程序作为多种数字游戏的策略，也把程序作为棋盘游戏的启发式函数[16]。

The closest work to ours is by Soemers et al. [17], in which game tactics are extracted from linear models trained with self-play and converted into decision and regression trees. To be able to compare game traces collected from human participants with those collected by black-box agents in future work, we decided to generate post-hoc explanations from game traces without using the logits of trained policies, i.e., the raw output predictions of trained machine learning models before turning them into probabilities with the softmax function. Therefore, we only use state-action pairs collected from game agents without logits of a trained oracle.
与我们最接近的是Soemers等人的工作[17]：从通过自我对弈训练的线性模型中提取游戏战术，再转成决策树和回归树。为了在未来比较人类参与者的游戏轨迹与黑箱智能体的轨迹，我们决定直接从游戏轨迹生成事后解释，而不使用已训练策略的logits，即机器学习模型通过softmax函数转为概率之前的原始预测输出。因此，我们只使用从游戏智能体收集的状态—行动对，不使用训练好的预言机模型的logits。
3. Program, Domain-specific Language & Problem Domain
section: 3 程序、领域专用语言与问题域

text: 3 程序、领域专用语言与问题域
section: 3 程序、领域专用语言与问题域

text: Programs are represented by a typed domain-specific language (DSL) which closely resembles the Lisp programming language [18]. The search space is constructed by using a uniformly distributed probabilistic grammar [19] shown in Table 1. Our DSL is inspired by the work about visual routines [5, 13], which uses a fixed set of basic operations to assemble different perception functions to reason about properties of shapes and spatial relations. Since our focus is on board games with a grid-like board and game pieces, the building blocks of our DSL consist of control flow production rules (if clauses and Boolean operators), integers, and methods to get pieces on the board and compare them. The primitive get-board-feature(board, stateObject, object) -> feature, gets one or multiple cells and checks if they are of the same object as the third parameter. If they are the same the feature program is activated. stateObject are always cells of the current state of the board game, while object is always a type provided by the game or environment. The board feature is later able to check if for a specific state this feature program is activated, so board features are actually independent from games and board states and, thus, transferable to other games in the future.
section: 3 程序、领域专用语言与问题域

text: 程序通过一种带类型的领域专用语言（DSL）表示，其形式非常接近Lisp编程语言[18]。搜索空间通过表1所示的均匀分布概率文法构建[19]。我们的DSL受到视觉例程研究[5,13]启发：用固定的一组基本操作，组合出不同的知觉函数，推理形状属性与空间关系。我们关注具有网格状棋盘和棋子的棋盘游戏，因此DSL的构建模块包括控制流产生规则（if条件与布尔运算符）、整数，以及获取和比较棋盘上棋子的方法。原语get-board-feature(board, stateObject, object) -> feature获取一个或多个单元，并检查它们是否与第三个参数属于相同对象；若相同，特征程序就被激活。stateObject始终是棋盘游戏当前状态中的单元，而object始终是游戏或环境提供的一种类型。棋盘特征随后可以检查：对于某个具体状态，这一特征程序是否被激活。因此，棋盘特征实际上独立于游戏和棋盘状态，将来可以迁移到其他游戏。
