text: 1. Introduction
1. 引言

Expressive Range Analysis (ERA) is a method of characterizing the nature and shape of a generative model in terms of its outputs. What sorts of outputs is a generator capable of? What impact does changing inputs of a generator have on its outputs? How do biases manifest in the generative outputs, and how do the inputs influence these biases? ERA is well suited for answering these questions [1]. ERA comes from the domain of Procedural Content Generation (PCG) in video game development: the practice of leveraging algorithmic methods to design and produce artifacts for use in games across a variety of contexts, such as levels or maps [2].
表达范围分析（ERA）是一种依据生成模型的输出，刻画其性质与形态的方法。生成器能够产生哪些类型的输出？改变生成器的输入会怎样影响输出？偏向如何呈现在生成输出中，输入又如何影响这些偏向？ERA很适合回答这些问题[1]。ERA源于电子游戏开发中的程序化内容生成（PCG）领域：利用算法方法设计并产生用于游戏的制品，应用情境包括关卡、地图等[2]。

We recognize common threads between PCG and generative AI (GAI) systems- defined here as the process of using generative technologies such as large language models to produce content, often using natural language prompts as human-provided input- including high-level functionality, motivations, use cases, and shortcomings of both domains (for details, see Section 2). Because of these similarities, we seek to expand and leverage ERA—which has not only proven useful for recognizing bias within, and categorizing generative outputs of PCG systems, but also resembles some existing approaches for GAI analysis [3]—for analysis of GAI system outputs, especially text-to-X, large language model (LLM)-based applications (such as the text-to-text Chat GPT [4], text-to-image Stable Diffusion [5], and text-to-speech ElevenLabs [6]).

我们认识到PCG与生成式人工智能（GAI）系统之间存在共同线索。这里将GAI界定为使用大语言模型等生成技术来产生内容的过程，通常以自然语言提示作为人类提供的输入。这些共同线索包括两个领域的高层功能、动机、使用情境与不足（详见第2节）。基于这些相似之处，我们希望扩展并利用ERA来分析GAI系统的输出，尤其是基于大语言模型（LLM）的“文本到X”应用，例如文本到文本的Chat GPT[4]、文本到图像的Stable Diffusion[5]，以及文本到语音的ElevenLabs[6]。ERA不仅已被证明有助于识别PCG系统的生成输出中的偏向并对这些输出分类，也与GAI分析的一些既有方法相似[3]。

The application of ERA in the domain of GAI is not a one-to-one translation from how the method is used in PCG. Use of GAI tools commonly requires more complicated, varied, and linguistic inputs than PCG, which tends to operate from numerical randomization as a starting point for much of its generation. Because these inputs have a major impact on the outputs of GAI systems [7], selection of these inputs is an important consideration for applying ERA to GAI— e.g. some decision points for input selection could include whether to handcraft inputs or sample the latent space, and whether the inputs should be restricted in a way that targets a specific domain of outputs (i.e. a prompt to output a haiku would be very different from one that might produce a cooking recipe). Furthermore, ERA requires the application of metrics to large quantities of content outputted from the system in question. What metrics are used and how they are determined is a major component of ERA, often directly determining the value provided by the analysis. Because GAI outputs tend to occupy a broad domain of applications and mediums, unique challenges arise when considering these metrics, further complicating the application of ERA in this context.

把ERA用于GAI领域，不能直接照搬它在PCG中的使用方式。与PCG相比，GAI工具通常需要更复杂、更多样且具有语言性质的输入；PCG的大量生成则倾向于以数值随机化为起点。由于这些输入会显著影响GAI系统的输出[7]，输入选择便成为把ERA用于GAI时的重要考虑。例如，选择输入时的一些决策点包括：手工编写输入还是对潜在空间采样，以及是否限制输入，使其针对某个特定输出领域——要求输出俳句的提示，与可能生成食谱的提示会很不一样。此外，ERA需要对所分析系统产生的大量内容应用度量。使用什么度量、怎样确定这些度量，是ERA的重要部分，常常直接决定分析提供的价值。由于GAI输出往往涉及广泛的应用领域和媒介，考虑这些度量时会出现独特挑战，使ERA在这一情境中的应用进一步复杂化。

Responding to 1) these parallels between PCG and GAI, and 2) the massive increase of scope presented by GAI, this paper presents a taxonomy for categorizing approaches to ERA. This taxonomy includes vocabulary to better distinguish examples from existing work in PCG, as well as a compass to guide further exploration of using this method in the rapidly expanding domain of GAI. The goal of this taxonomy is to push the boundaries of what ERA may be used for and how it may be applied.
针对上述两点——1）PCG与GAI之间的相似性，2）GAI带来的范围大幅扩展——本文提出一个对ERA方法进行分类的体系。它既提供词汇，以便更清楚地区分PCG既有研究中的实例，也提供方向，指导人们在迅速扩张的GAI领域进一步探索这种方法。该分类体系旨在拓展ERA可用于什么、以及可以怎样应用的边界。
2. Related Work
2. 相关工作

This work operates in the intersection of procedural content generation and generative AI. Guzdial provides a valuable bridge between these domains with the lens of human-AI interactive generation [8]. While Guzdial uses this lens to frame PCG and GAI as essentially the same process, we view PCG as a broader term describing the process of content generation at its highest level, and GAI as a more descriptive term identifying a subset of generative practices that use specific technologies. Framing GAI as a subset of PCG—or using Guzdial’s lens of human-AI interactive generation [8]—broadens the scope of understanding for both domains and allows the application of evaluation methods of PCG for analysis of GAI systems.

本研究处于程序化内容生成与生成式人工智能的交叉地带。Guzdial以“人机交互生成”的视角，为两个领域搭起了有价值的桥梁[8]。Guzdial借此将PCG与GAI理解为本质上相同的过程；我们则把PCG视为一个更宽泛的术语，在最高层次描述内容生成过程，而把GAI视为一个更具体的术语，指采用特定技术的一部分生成实践。将GAI视作PCG的一个子集，或者采用Guzdial的人机交互生成视角[8]，能够拓宽对两个领域的理解，并使PCG的评估方法可以用于分析GAI系统。

Particularly, we are interested in leveraging expressive range analysis for evaluation of GAI systems [1]. Withington et al. list expressive range analysis as one of 12 "features" used for comparison of PCG systems [9]. We consider ERA a promising method of GAI analysis compared to alternative PCG-evaluation practices due to its flexibility in applying a broad range of analysis metrics to its evaluated systems, particularly highlighting its strength of identifying bias and system tendencies- including as influenced by user input [1]. Withington et al. identifies weaknesses with current evaluation methods for PCG systems, suggesting they could be mitigated by diverse research frameworks and promoting the reuse of methodology where possible [9]. This paper seeks to answer this call by broadening the applicability of ERA.

具体而言，我们希望利用表达范围分析来评估GAI系统[1]。Withington等人把表达范围分析列为比较PCG系统所用的12项“特征”之一[9]。与其他PCG评估实践相比，我们认为ERA是一种有前景的GAI分析方法，因为它可以灵活地对被评估系统应用广泛的分析度量；尤其值得强调的是，它能够识别偏向和系统倾向，包括受用户输入影响的倾向[1]。Withington等人指出了当前PCG系统评估方法的不足，提出可以通过多样化研究框架，并在可能时复用方法来缓解这些不足[9]。本文通过拓宽ERA的适用性，回应这一呼吁。

We seek to do so by presenting a taxonomic framework for categorizing approaches used for ERA, drawing from similar work in PCG such as Togelius et. al. [10] and Smith’s [2] taxonomies of PCG, as well as Withington et al. ’s modern taxonomy of available evaluation approaches [9].
为此，我们提出一个分类框架，对用于ERA的方法进行归类；参考对象包括Togelius等人[10]和Smith[2]对PCG的类似分类研究，以及Withington等人近期对现有评估方法的分类[9]。

Further outlining the connection between GAI and PCG, we consider the motivations and use-cases for such systems. PCG and GAI are both used to automatically generate large amounts of content, and to increase variety of content [11, 12]. PCG is also used for assistive tools, helping with tasks such as level creation [13], and support tools have emerged to make these systems easier to understand [14]. LLM applications like ChatGPT [4] and Stable Diffusion [5] are promoted for their potential to reduce labor costs, enable new business models, and increase access to content creation– Cook claims all of these as common motivations for studying AI in games [15]. We also acknowledge the use of machine learning in PCG [16, 17] as a point that highlights the connection between PCG and GAI.

为了进一步说明GAI与PCG的联系，我们考察这些系统的动机和使用情境。PCG与GAI都用于自动生成大量内容，并增加内容的多样性[11,12]。PCG也用于辅助工具，帮助完成关卡创作等任务[13]；还有支持工具出现，帮助人们更容易理解这些系统[14]。ChatGPT[4]和Stable Diffusion[5]等LLM应用被宣传为能够降低劳动成本、支持新商业模式并扩大内容创作的可及性；Cook认为，这些都是研究游戏AI的常见动机[15]。我们也注意到PCG中机器学习的使用[16,17]，这进一步突出了PCG与GAI之间的联系。

We also recognize parallel claims of GAI and PCG capabilities—and shortcomings thereof—that may provide useful points of interest for continuing this investigation. Developing a useful PCG generator often takes just as much, or more, effort than hand-crafted alternatives [18], despite the allure of rapid content production. Furthermore, the variety content generators are able to produce can be limited, as players are often capable of identifying patterns between generated content [19]. While Generative AI offers potential to expand the type of content that can be generated—such as more complex generative audio and music used to increase variety and interactivity of game music compared to non-generative methods [20], as well as the range of users that can make use of generators—we also view the drawbacks of PCG as rich sites of investigation in GAI. ERA has proven a useful method for identifying such weaknesses in the domain of PCG, and we hope to see its effectiveness applied to GAI as well.

我们也认识到，GAI与PCG的能力宣称及其不足存在相似之处，可以为继续这一研究提供值得关注的问题。尽管快速生产内容很有吸引力，开发一个有用的PCG生成器，常常需要与手工创作替代方案同样多、甚至更多的投入[18]。此外，内容生成器能产生的多样性可能有限，因为玩家通常能够识别生成内容之间的模式[19]。生成式人工智能有望扩展可生成的内容类型，例如，与非生成方法相比，更复杂的生成式音频和音乐可提高游戏音乐的多样性和交互性[20]，也有望扩大能够使用生成器的用户范围；与此同时，我们认为PCG的不足也是GAI中值得深入研究的地方。ERA已被证明有助于在PCG领域识别这类弱点，我们希望它也能有效用于GAI。

GAI technologies have prompted significant concern—i.e. regarding its social and environmental impact, underlying politics of AI design, implementation, and advocacy [21]. Additional concerns include embedded systemic biases, risk of plagiarism and misinformation, and human and environmental costs [22]. Jiang et al. find that artists, in particular, identify harms to professional reputation, intellectual property, and financial risk [23]. Because of GAI’s recognized potential for harm, we value tools and methods for understanding and analyzing these systems and their outputs.
GAI技术已经引起重大关切，例如其社会与环境影响，以及AI设计、实施和倡导背后的政治问题[21]。其他关切包括嵌入其中的系统性偏见、剽窃与错误信息风险，以及人类和环境成本[22]。Jiang等人发现，艺术家尤其指出了对专业声誉、知识产权和财务方面的危害[23]。由于GAI的潜在危害已受到认识，我们重视能够帮助理解和分析这些系统及其输出的工具与方法。
3. The Problem Space
3. 问题空间
Summarizing the process of Expressive Range Analysis, this form of inquiry operates in three steps [1]:
概括而言，表达范围分析这一探究方式分为三个步骤[1]：
• 1) Start with a set of images or similar data (i.e. levels, maps, etc.) produced by the generator being analyzed.
• 1）从被分析生成器产生的一组图像或类似数据（例如关卡、地图等）出发。
• 2) Determine useful metrics for the goal of analysis (i.e. linearity or leniency of a level) and apply them to the data.
• 2）根据分析目标确定有用的度量（例如关卡的线性程度或宽容度），并将其应用于数据。
• 3) Produce a visualization of the metered data space.
• 3）将经过度量的数据空间可视化。

Two challenges arise when considering this method for GAI-generators as opposed to PCG-generators. First, producing a set of data to analyze tends to be more complicated. GAI text-to-X applications require linguistic input, leading to larger variance of the input space in terms of both quantity and meaning. Further complicating the issue, PCG tools are typically custom-made for specific use-cases [18], where GAI tools (such as ChatGPT [4] or Google’s Gemini [24]) are commonly presented as general-purpose—while random inputs could be provided in place of handcrafted ones or the latent space could be randomly sampled, these approaches would provide undesirable outputs, lacking the targeted focus of a particular use-case. The general-purpose nature of GAI systems adds noise to the output space when looking at these tools for specific use-cases, since outputs that don’t fit the specific use-case become irrelevant. Guzdial summarizes this aspect as GAI tool developers seeking to expand the possible valid outputs for a particular tool to include all possible valid outputs for every tool [8]. This noise presents additional challenges: how do you narrow the scope of the output to only match the relevant use-case? What prompts do you provide as an input to produce a suitable set of data to categorize the generator as a whole? Guzdial’s human-centered input alignment [8] may prove a useful attribute of consideration to respond to this challenge.

与PCG生成器相比，把这种方法用于GAI生成器时会出现两个挑战。首先，产生一组待分析数据通常更加复杂。GAI的文本到X应用需要语言输入，因此输入空间在数量和含义两个方面都具有更大的变化。问题还在于，PCG工具通常为特定使用情境定制[18]，而GAI工具，例如ChatGPT[4]或Google的Gemini[24]，通常被呈现为通用工具。虽然可以不用手工输入而提供随机输入，或对潜在空间进行随机采样，但这些方法会产生不理想的输出，缺少某个具体使用情境所需的针对性。面向特定使用情境考察GAI工具时，其通用性会给输出空间增加噪声，因为不适合该情境的输出就变得无关。Guzdial将这一点概括为：GAI工具开发者试图把某个工具可能具有的有效输出扩展为所有工具的一切可能有效输出[8]。这种噪声带来更多挑战：如何缩小输出范围，使其只匹配相关使用情境？应该输入哪些提示，才能得到合适的数据集，据以刻画整个生成器？Guzdial提出的“以人为中心的输入对齐”[8]，可能是回应这一挑战时值得考虑的有用属性。

The second challenge that arises from considering ERA for use in analyzing GAI systems comes from the metrics of analysis. ERA can be used alongside any metrics, depending on what a generative system is being analyzed for. These metrics must be applied to large quantities of data, in some cases encompassing the entire generative output of a system [1]. Furthermore, many examples of ERA employ automatic processing of data, but not all data and research goals benefit from automatable metrics- which tend to be quantitative in nature. The challenge here is twofold: how do you determine semantically meaningful metrics for increasingly variable data? And, accounting for practical workload and feasibility, how do you apply these metrics to increasingly multitudinous data?

考虑将ERA用于GAI系统分析时，第二个挑战来自分析度量。ERA可以配合任何度量使用，具体取决于分析生成系统的目的。这些度量必须应用于大量数据；在某些情况下，数据甚至涵盖系统的全部生成输出[1]。此外，许多ERA实例采用自动化数据处理，但并非所有数据和研究目标都受益于可自动执行的度量——这类度量往往具有定量性质。这里的挑战有两方面：面对日益多变的数据，怎样确定在语义上有意义的度量？在考虑实际工作量与可行性的情况下，又怎样把这些度量应用于日益庞大的数据？

We treat producing an intended result as the motivation behind creating and using generators. While some generators offer promises of increased speed and efficiency, those claims are not always accurate [18]—despite this, generators are valued by many as useful tools. We recognize the purpose of ERA as evaluating the success of that motivation. Using ERA is akin to asking: has this this generator successfully captured what it was designed to capture? With this framing in mind, our motivation for this paper is to facilitate the answering of that question in a greater variety of contexts. The challenge in the case of GAI is, in short: how?
我们把产生预期结果视为创建和使用生成器的动机。虽然有些生成器承诺提高速度和效率，这些宣称并不总是准确[18]；即便如此，许多人仍重视生成器，认为它是有用工具。我们认为，ERA的目的在于评估这一动机是否得到实现。使用ERA相当于询问：这个生成器是否成功捕捉到它原本被设计来捕捉的东西？在这一框架下，本文的动机是帮助人们在更多种情境中回答这个问题。就GAI而言，挑战简言之是：怎样做到？
4. Framework
4. 框架

Here, we present a taxonomy of ERA methods, seeking to provide language and framing to better address the challenges of applying ERA to a greater variety of contexts— especially GAI systems. We have defined five axes for characterizing ERA methodologies: quantitative vs qualitative, product vs process, objective vs subjective, content agnostic vs semantic, and automated vs manual.
这里，我们提出ERA方法的分类体系，提供相应语言与框架，以更好地应对把ERA用于更多情境——特别是GAI系统——的挑战。我们界定了五个刻画ERA方法论的维度：定量与定性、产物与过程、客观与主观、内容无关与语义，以及自动与人工。

We considered three factors as a basis for defining these axes: the origin and definition of ERA, the adopted practice of this method, and its potential for further expansion and refinement. We considered the origin of ERA [1], identifying decision points in how the method may be applied. We also considered how ERA has been adopted in research endeavors and sought to challenge assumptions that have become commonplace. Finally, this taxonomy is also a result of our efforts to address challenges we faced in applying ERA to GAI. We hope to further refine these axes and their definitions in future work.
我们以三个因素作为界定这些维度的基础：ERA的起源与定义、这一方法已被采用的实践，以及进一步扩展和完善的潜力。我们考察ERA的起源[1]，识别应用这一方法时的决策点；也考察研究工作如何采用ERA，并试图质疑那些已经习以为常的假设。最后，这个分类体系也来自我们处理将ERA用于GAI时所遇挑战的尝试。我们希望在未来研究中进一步完善这些维度及其定义。
4.1. Quantitative vs Qualitative
4.1. 定量与定性

The metrics that are applied to the generator-produced data may be quantitative, qualitative, or varying degrees of mixed-method. Many traditional ERA approaches utilize quantitative metrics, as this approach is often more suitable for automatically applying metrics to data and producing a descriptive visualization. Smith and Whitehead use two metrics for applying ERA to Launchpad- linearity and leniency [1]. Both of these metrics are quantitative, because they are described, measured, and depicted numerically. Interestingly, Kreminski et al. [25] identify determining quantitative metrics as an essential step of ERA, which is consistent with the examples of the method’s initial presentation [1]- it is therefore unsurprising that Qualitative metrics are relatively under-utilized in ERA. This taxonomy challenges this assumption—which is present across many ERA-focused research endeavors—instead suggesting an expansion of valid data collection efforts.

应用于生成器所产数据的度量，可以是定量的、定性的，或不同程度混合方法的。许多传统ERA方法使用定量度量，因为它通常更适合自动将度量应用于数据，并生成描述性可视化。Smith与Whitehead将ERA用于Launchpad时采用两个度量：线性程度与宽容度[1]。两者都是定量的，因为它们以数值描述、测量和呈现。值得注意的是，Kreminski等人[25]把确定定量度量视为ERA的必要步骤，这与该方法最初提出时的实例一致[1]；因此，定性度量在ERA中相对较少使用，并不令人意外。本分类体系质疑了这一存在于许多ERA研究中的假设，转而建议扩展有效数据收集工作的范围。

While there is not a strong foundation of qualitative metrics applied to ERA in PCG, some hypothetical qualitative metrics could come from methods like user surveys or interviews, such as those found in play-testing efforts to evaluate elements of a game like challenge or engagement. These metrics could be visually represented with tools such as word clouds, affinity charts, or heat-maps that highlight the frequency of thematic elements within the data, for example.
尽管PCG领域在将定性度量用于ERA方面还没有扎实基础，某些假设性的定性度量可以来自用户调查或访谈等方法，例如游玩测试中用于评估挑战性、投入等游戏要素的方法。这些度量可以借助词云、亲和图，或突出数据中主题要素出现频率的热力图等工具进行可视化呈现。
4.2. Product vs Process
4.2. 产物与过程

Because our goal is to evaluate if a generator is successful in capturing what it was designed to do, it is interesting to consider both the product of a generator and the process of producing that output. The product of a generator is its output- an image, the answer to a question, or a video game level are all examples of this. Analyzing the product is useful for identifying what a generator is capable of- in terms of quality, variety, etc.- and what sort of biases are present in the outputs. Smith and Whitehead [1] present a product-focused approach, as their linearity and leniency metrics consider only the levels produced by the generative system. Withington’s [26] approach is also product-focused, since this work considers the differences between outputs of a generator rather than considering the process of producing those outputs.

由于我们的目标是评估生成器是否成功捕捉到其设计所要求的东西，因此既考察生成器的产物，也考察产生输出的过程，很有意义。生成器的产物就是输出，图像、问题的答案或电子游戏关卡都是例子。分析产物有助于识别生成器在质量、多样性等方面能做到什么，以及输出中存在哪些偏向。Smith与Whitehead[1]采用以产物为中心的方法，因为其线性程度与宽容度度量只考察生成系统产生的关卡。Withington[26]的方法也以产物为中心，因为该研究考察生成器输出之间的差异，而不考察产生这些输出的过程。

The process entails the experience of producing that output. Common narratives of generative systems sell them as faster and more efficient than manual alternatives. Looking at the process allows us to evaluate those claims, using metrics such as the time it takes to get a desirable output or how many iterations of prompts/generations it takes to produce such an output. Kreminski et al. [25] arguably present a process-focused approach, because their motivation for analysis seeks to evaluate the usability experience of a generative system. However, the metrics used are primarily focused on the product of the generator. A more process-centric example would include metrics that evaluate procedural aspects such as the time it takes to generate an output, or the number of generative attempts before a user finds a suitable option.

过程涉及产生输出的经历。有关生成系统的常见叙述，把它们宣传为比人工替代方案更快、更高效。考察过程，可以用获得理想输出所需时间，或产生这一输出需要多少轮提示与生成等度量，评估这些宣称。Kreminski等人[25]可以说提出了一种以过程为中心的方法，因为其分析动机是评估生成系统的可用性体验。然而，所用度量主要集中于生成器的产物。更以过程为中心的例子，会包括评估过程性方面的度量，例如生成一次输出需要的时间，或用户找到合适选项之前需要的生成尝试次数。

Shaker et. al. [11] highlight generator reliability as one important piece of PCG evaluation. Looking at this aspect provides a mixed-method approach that tends to use product to reveal something about the process.
Shaker等人[11]强调，生成器可靠性是PCG评估的重要组成部分。考察这一方面，会提供一种混合方法，往往利用产物揭示过程的某些情况。
4.3. Objective vs Subjective
4.3. 客观与主观

This axis is concerned with the nature of the analysis metric—is a given metric verifiable based on factual evidence, or does it vary with perspective, based in emotion or opinion? Smith and Whitehead’s two metrics for Launchpad again provide a useful example: Linearity, as described in their paper, is an objective metric that describes the factual "profile" of platforming levels (how well the geometry of the level fits a straight line) in the evaluated system [1]. Leniency, however, is identified as a subjective score based on an intuitive sense of how lenient components of a level are towards a player [1]. Subjective metrics are relatively underrepresented in PCG, but may prove useful for evaluating GAI systems– especially as they are applied in creative domains. We consider user experience analysis a useful point of reference for how subjective metrics may be used in data analysis and visualization [27, 28].

这一维度关注分析度量的性质：某一度量能否依据事实证据得到验证，还是会随视角变化，建立在情绪或意见之上？Smith与Whitehead用于Launchpad的两个度量，再次提供了有用例子。按照其论文的描述，线性程度是一项客观度量，用来描述所评估系统中平台跳跃关卡的事实性“轮廓”，即关卡几何形状与直线的拟合程度[1]。宽容度则被确定为主观得分，依据的是对关卡各组成部分对玩家有多宽容的直觉感受[1]。主观度量在PCG中相对较少，但可能有助于评估GAI系统，特别是创作领域中的应用。我们认为，用户体验分析可以为如何在数据分析与可视化中使用主观度量提供有用参照[27,28]。
4.4. Content Agnostic vs Semantic
4.4. 内容无关与语义

This axis is concerned with the data itself and the value sought from analysis. Semantic approaches seek to find meaning within the context of the inputs and outputs of the generator. Smith and Whitehead [1] present a semantic approach, as their metrics are intended to allow comparison of the generated content. Lucas and Volz [29] provide another example of a semantic approach, as theirs is also intended to compare generated content.
这一维度关注数据本身，以及希望从分析中获得的价值。语义方法试图在生成器输入与输出的情境中寻找意义。Smith与Whitehead[1]采用语义方法，因为其度量旨在使生成内容能够相互比较。Lucas与Volz[29]提供了另一个语义方法的例子，其方法同样旨在比较生成内容。

Content agnostic approaches seek to find meaning in the generator, regardless of its inputs or outputs- though the inputs and outputs may be useful for analysis. While Kreminski et al. [25] evaluate the product of the generator, their interests lie in the users of the generative system-answering questions such as how thoroughly they explore the generative range- rather than finding meaning from the generative output itself, making their approach content-agnostic. Withington’s exploration of quality-diversity algorithms [26] presents another content-agnostic example because the focus is not on the details of specific outputs, but rather measuring the differences between them.
内容无关方法试图在生成器中寻找意义，而不依赖其输入或输出，尽管输入和输出可能对分析有用。Kreminski等人[25]虽然评估生成器的产物，但其兴趣在于生成系统的用户，例如回答用户对生成范围探索得有多充分，而不是从生成输出本身寻找意义，因此其方法属于内容无关方法。Withington对质量—多样性算法的研究[26]是另一个内容无关的例子，因为重点并非特定输出的细节，而是测量输出之间的差异。
4.5. Automated vs Manual
4.5. 自动与人工

This axis is concerned with the process of applying metrics to the data. Automated processes are typically conducted computationally, making them especially suitable for quantitative analysis metrics and often desirable for the promise of reduced processing time or effort. Smith and Whitehead [1], Kreminski et al. [25], and Kybartas et al. [30], among others, all present automated approaches for applying ERA metrics to their data.
这一维度关注把度量应用于数据的过程。自动过程通常由计算执行，因此尤其适合定量分析度量；人们也常因其有望减少处理时间或投入而希望采用。Smith与Whitehead[1]、Kreminski等人[25]、Kybartas等人[30]等，都提出了把ERA度量应用于其数据的自动化方法。

Manual processes require human labor for applying analysis metrics to each piece of data—while this tends to be more time-consuming, it also allows closer scrutiny of elements that are difficult to capture without direct human intervention. Manual processes are often unsuitable for the large quantities of data that ERA typically processes, but methods such as crowd sourced photogrammetry—e.g. as used for identifying information about wildlife populations [31]—may hypothetically be leveraged to manually process such data. Human subject experiments, such as those commonly used in narrative generation projects [32], are another example of a manual approach.
人工过程要求人类劳动，将分析度量应用于每一项数据。虽然这往往更耗时，但它也使那些缺少人类直接介入便难以捕捉的要素，能够得到更仔细的审视。人工过程通常不适合ERA一般处理的大量数据，但众包摄影测量等方法，例如用于识别野生动物种群信息的方法[31]，在假设上也许能够被用来人工处理这些数据。叙事生成项目中常见的人类受试者实验[32]，则是人工方法的另一个例子。
5. Discussion
5. 讨论

Framing GAI under the lens of PCG- or both as the same process, e.g. through the lens of human-AI interaction generation [8]- incorporates this new technology into an established domain of research that has ERA as a design-focused method for evaluation. In connecting GAI and PCG, though, we have identified a need for both an improved vocabulary for describing ERA and an expanded potential scope for ERA that challenges existing methods. Thus this taxonomy further expands the potential range of analytical applications for ERA, providing language to better describe and imagine its use-cases and identify its historical gaps. This expansion responds to existing weak-points in PCG evaluation—such as those identified by Withington et al. [9]—by increasing the diversity and re-usability of ERA as a framework for generative analysis.

从PCG的视角理解GAI，或把二者视为同一过程，例如采用人机交互生成的视角[8]，能够将这一新技术纳入一个已有研究领域，而该领域拥有作为设计导向评估方法的ERA。不过，在连接GAI与PCG时，我们发现：既需要改进描述ERA的词汇，也需要扩展ERA的潜在范围，挑战现有方法。因此，这一分类体系进一步扩展了ERA可能的分析应用，为描述和设想其使用情境、识别历史上的空缺提供语言。通过提高ERA作为生成分析框架的多样性与可复用性，这种扩展回应了PCG评估中已有的薄弱环节，例如Withington等人指出的问题[9]。

Further, this taxonomy allows for better description of the flexibility and space occupied by broadly applicable aspects of evaluation, such as those presented in Guzdial’s human-AI interaction generation [8]. For example, Guzdial’s call for human-centered input alignment considers the relationship between valid system inputs and user-preferences regarding those inputs. Using the vocabulary from our taxonomy, this is a process-focused, content-agnostic, subjective approach, because meaning is found according to individual perceptions without concern for the generative output. Such a metric could be applied to data quantitatively or qualitatively, using either an automated or manual approach. Guzdial’s adaptability similarly considers the process of generation and user perceptions [8], and has similar axis placement to human-centered input alignment– though it is objective rather than subjective, since adaptability was a predetermined aspect of the generative process, rather than a variable expressed by human interpretation. Novelty, however, is an objective, product-focused metric because it is based in the observed possible generative outputs.

此外，这一分类体系能够更好地描述那些广泛适用的评估要素的灵活性及其所在位置，例如Guzdial在人机交互生成中提出的要素[8]。以Guzdial倡导的以人为中心的输入对齐为例，它考察有效系统输入与用户对这些输入的偏好之间的关系。使用本分类体系的词汇，这是一种以过程为中心、内容无关且主观的方法，因为它依据个人感知寻找意义，而不关注生成输出。这种度量可以定量或定性地应用于数据，也可以采用自动或人工方法。Guzdial的适应性同样考察生成过程与用户感知[8]，其维度位置与以人为中心的输入对齐相似；但它是客观而非主观的，因为适应性是生成过程中预先确定的方面，而不是由人类解释表达出来的变量。相比之下，新颖性是一项客观、以产物为中心的度量，因为它建立在可观察到的可能生成输出之上。

It is our hope that using the vocabulary of this taxonomy can provide some clarity to the research community on how they are using ERA for evaluation, as well as identify potential new approaches for ERA.
我们希望，使用这一分类体系的词汇，能够帮助研究共同体更清楚地理解自己如何使用ERA进行评估，并识别ERA可能的新方法。
6. Conclusions, Limitations, & Future Work
6. 结论、局限与未来工作

This paper explores an avenue for exploring the intersection of PCG and GAI, using expressive range analysis as a common method for analyzing generative systems and their outputs. We present a taxonomic framework for categorizing existing and imagined ERA inquiries, hoping to allow more effective navigation of this space and leverage PCG tools for study of GAI technologies and systems.
本文探索了一条研究PCG与GAI交叉领域的路径，把表达范围分析作为分析生成系统及其输出的共同方法。我们提出一个分类框架，对既有和设想中的ERA研究进行归类，希望帮助人们更有效地把握这一空间，并利用PCG工具研究GAI技术与系统。

This taxonomy opens interesting possibilities for future applications of ERA. What do qualitative applications of ERA look like? How would manually applying metrics to data compare to more commonly applied automated processes? These are relatively underexplored areas of ERA, and the possibility of applying this method to generative systems makes these questions more compelling.
这一分类体系为ERA的未来应用打开了有趣的可能性。ERA的定性应用会是什么样？与更常用的自动过程相比，人工把度量应用于数据会怎样？这些领域在ERA中相对缺少探索，而将这种方法用于生成系统的可能性，使这些问题更值得追问。

The scope of this paper is limited to theory. This thread of research would benefit from a more complete, systematic review of ERA projects that places existing work on the axes of this taxonomy and further inform the chosen axes. As an extension of this research, we also see value in performing ERA on GAI tools using different combinations of axis placement—especially including qualitative and manual approaches.
本文范围限于理论。对ERA项目进行更完整、系统的综述，将既有研究放到该分类体系的各个维度上，并进一步为所选维度提供依据，会有益于这条研究路线。作为扩展，我们也认为，采用不同维度位置组合，对GAI工具开展ERA具有价值，尤其是纳入定性与人工方法。

Abstract
摘要

Graph grammars are an approach to procedurally generating content for games. However, grammars must often be carefully designed so that generated levels are completable, e.g. keys do not end up behind locks. In this work, we present a graph grammar approach that uses a single unified grammar containing the rules for both generating and playing levels. Such grammars generate not just a level, but an example playthrough of the level. Using a constraint-based application of the grammars can ensure that generated playthrough solves the level. The constraint-based approach is also highly controllable, and can constrain aspects such as the number of times rules are applied, label counts in the generated graph, and matching partial subgraphs. To scale this approach up to larger graphs, we introduce hints into the grammar rules that limit the ranges of variables that can be used for certain nodes and edges. As a motivating example, we reproduce a grammar for generating adventure game missions from Dormans’ previous work, extend it with gameplay rules, and use these for flexible item placement while ensuring completability regarding keys and locks.

图文法是为游戏程序化生成内容的一种方法。不过，通常必须精心设计文法，才能使生成的关卡可以完成，例如避免钥匙最终位于锁后面。在本项工作中，我们提出了一种图文法方法，用一个统一文法同时容纳生成关卡和游玩关卡的规则。这类文法生成的不只是关卡，还包括该关卡的一个通关过程示例。以基于约束的方式应用文法，可以确保生成的通关过程解出关卡。这种基于约束的方法还具有很强的可控性，可以约束规则应用次数、生成图中的标签数量，以及部分子图的匹配等方面。为了将这种方法扩展到更大的图，我们在文法规则中引入提示，限制可用于特定节点和边的变量取值范围。作为动机示例，我们重现了Dormans此前工作中用于生成冒险游戏任务的文法，为其加入玩法规则，并利用这些规则灵活放置物品，同时确保关卡在钥匙与锁方面可以完成。

1. Introduction
1. 引言

Graph grammars are a popular approach to procedural generation of levels for video games [1]. In a graph grammar-based approach, levels are represented as graphs; the grammar provides rules for replacing—or rewriting—certain subgraphs (i.e. arrangements of nodes and edges) with new subgraphs. By repeatedly applying these rules, a graph (and thus level) of the desired complexity can be generated.
图文法是电子游戏关卡程序化生成的一种常见方法[1]。在基于图文法的方法中，关卡被表示为图；文法提供一些规则，用新的子图替换——或重写——特定子图，也就是节点和边的特定排列。通过反复应用这些规则，可以生成具有所需复杂度的图，从而生成相应的关卡。

As is often the case with level generation, it is critical that levels generated by graph grammars are completable—that is, it is possible for a player to complete the level. This means that, e.g. keys should not be behind their associated locks, special items need to defeat a boss should be collectible before getting to that boss, and so on. A number of techniques have been developed to ensure this, including grammars that prevent such situations [2, 3, 4], generate-and-test [5], and constraint-based approaches [6]. However, these previous approaches require either careful manual design of grammars, or implementing a separate system to check or constrain graphs.

与关卡生成中常见的情况一样，确保图文法生成的关卡可以完成至关重要，也就是说，玩家有可能完成关卡。例如，钥匙不应位于与其对应的锁后面；击败某个首领所需的特殊物品，应能在到达该首领之前取得，等等。为确保这一点，研究者已开发了多种技术，包括能防止这类情况的文法[2, 3, 4]、生成后测试[5]以及基于约束的方法[6]。不过，这些既有方法要么要求精心手工设计文法，要么需要另外实现一个系统来检查图或对图施加约束。

Recent work has explored representing the game mechanics themselves as rewrites of subgraphs, essentially a graph grammar [7]. By using a constraint-based framework, this grammar representation of the game mechanics could ensure that the generated graphs were completable. The level itself was generated by constraints learned from example graphs [8], and simultaneously, the game mechanic grammar generated a step-by-step playthrough demonstrating how the level could be completed. This was done by creating a sequence of graphs, with each corresponding to an application of a mechanic rule, and ensuring that the level is solved by the last step.
近期的工作探索了将游戏机制本身表示为子图的重写，这实质上也是一种图文法[7]。利用基于约束的框架，这种对游戏机制的文法表示可以确保生成的图可以完成。关卡本身由从示例图中学得的约束生成[8]；与此同时，游戏机制文法会生成一个逐步展开的通关过程，展示关卡如何被完成。实现方式是创建一个图序列，其中每个图对应一次机制规则的应用，并确保关卡在最后一步得到解决。

In this work, we look at unifying the graph grammar for generating levels and the graph grammar for game mechanics into a single grammar. By unifying these into a single grammar, we can use the previous constraint-based framework to generate graphs that are ensured to be playable in a single constraint problem. We can also use the same representation to describe the rules for generating the graph and ensuring that it is completable.
在本项工作中，我们研究将生成关卡的图文法与游戏机制的图文法统一为一个文法。将两者统一之后，就可以利用既有的约束框架，在一个约束问题中生成保证可玩的图。我们还能够使用同一种表示来描述生成图的规则，并确保图可以完成。

For motivation, we looked to Dormans’ work on graph grammar generation of adventure game missions [2], recreating it in our system, and augmenting it with mechanic rules. Our constraint-based system allows fine-grained control over generated node labels, rule applications, and even entire subgraphs. While the grammar in Dormans’ work was manually constructed to ensure that keys did not end up behind their locks, our system allows flexibility in key and item placement by the generator rules, while relying on the mechanic rules to ensure completability.
作为研究动机，我们参考了Dormans利用图文法生成冒险游戏任务的工作[2]，在我们的系统中将其重现，并为其增加机制规则。我们的约束系统允许细致控制生成的节点标签、规则应用，甚至整个子图。Dormans工作中的文法经过手工构造，以确保钥匙不会最终落在其对应的锁后面；我们的系统则允许生成规则灵活放置钥匙和物品，同时依靠机制规则确保可完成性。

At it core, the system we present is an extension to the previous work [7] in which we include both generator rules and mechanic rules, such that some steps in the graph sequence are generating the level and some are of a playthrough ensuring its completability. However, in order to implement Dormans’ grammar, several pragmatic improvements to the system were needed. Perhaps the most important of these was for performance, to scale up to larger graphs with more steps in their generation. We call these grammar hints, which are additional information about the grammar and individual rules to limit their application and thus the constraint problem to be solved. As one example, since the performance of the constraint satisfaction problem is greatly impacted by the number of potential edges in the graph, each grammar rule can have associated with it an edge hint: information about which edges it is allowed to consider based on node IDs; e.g. instead of a rule having to consider any pair of nodes being connected, it may only have to consider situations where the two nodes have relative ids within a certain range, greatly reducing the space of possibilities. Whereas previous work [7] could set such limitations across the entire graph—referred to as edge setup—in this work it can be set per-rule. We have found grammar hints require additional effort to author, but greatly speed up the generation process.

从核心上看，我们提出的系统是既有工作[7]的扩展：它同时包含生成规则和机制规则，使图序列中的一些步骤用于生成关卡，另一些步骤则构成确保可完成性的通关过程。不过，要实现Dormans的文法，还需要对系统做若干实际改进。其中最重要的或许是性能方面的改进，以扩展到更大的图和更多的生成步骤。我们将这些改进称为文法提示，即关于文法及其各条规则的附加信息，用来限制规则的应用，并由此限制需要求解的约束问题。例如，图中潜在边的数量会极大影响约束满足问题的性能，因此每条文法规则都可以附带一个边提示：它依据节点ID，说明该规则可以考虑哪些边。例如，一条规则不必考虑任意两个节点相连的情况，而可能只需考虑两个节点的相对ID处于特定范围内的情况，从而大幅缩小可能性空间。此前的工作[7]只能在整个图的范围内设定这类限制，称为边设置；本项工作则可以逐条规则设定。我们发现，编写文法提示需要额外工作，但会大幅加快生成过程。

This work contributes a unified graph grammar approach to both generating levels and ensuring their solvability using constraint solving, a demonstration of performance improvements provided by grammar hints, and a demonstration of the controllability of generated graphs afforded by constraint solving.
本项工作的贡献包括：提出一种统一的图文法方法，利用约束求解同时生成关卡并确保其可解；展示文法提示带来的性能改进；展示约束求解为生成图提供的可控性。
2. Related Work
2. 相关工作

Generating completable levels. To ensure that generated levels are completable, there are multiple approaches that are commonly used. One common method is agent-based testing, in which completability is assured by agents attempting to play the levels [9]. Another approach is to add constraints during generation, so that levels always meet some requirements. For example, Nelson and Smith [10] used answer set programming to encode rules about valid paths or item placement. Other systems like Sturgeon combine the rules specified by the designer and learned pattern constraints to guarantee reachability [6]. On the other hand, generate-and-repair techniques have a different approach, in which they ensure completability after the generation process is complete. Autoencoders have been used to automatically fix uncompletable structures by reconstructing levels [11]. More recent methods use explainable AI to detect problematic regions and guide targeted repairs to minimally edit levels until completability is achieved [12].

生成可完成的关卡。为确保生成的关卡可以完成，研究中常用多种方法。一种常见方法是基于智能体的测试，通过让智能体尝试游玩关卡来保证可完成性[9]。另一种方法是在生成过程中加入约束，使关卡始终满足某些要求。例如，Nelson和Smith[10]使用答案集编程，对有效路径或物品放置的规则进行编码。Sturgeon等其他系统则结合设计者指定的规则与学得的模式约束，以保证可达性[6]。另一方面，生成后修复技术采用不同的方法，在生成过程完成后确保可完成性。已有研究用自编码器重构关卡，自动修复不可完成的结构[11]。较新的方法使用可解释AI检测存在问题的区域，并引导针对性修复，以尽可能少地修改关卡，直至实现可完成性[12]。

Generating levels with graph grammars. Graph grammars have been widely explored for level generation. The early work of Adams [13] was one of the earliest works that used a graph grammar (instead of phrase structure grammars) to generate FPS-style dungeons to utilize the power of graphs to represent the complex patterns of connectivity that are found in levels. Following this work, Dormans [2] viewed level design as a sequence of model transformations, and created mission grammars (that included players’ missions and tasks) that get mapped to space graphs (that included spatial layout of levels). Font et al. [4] created a two-stage evolutionary method in which a high-level graph of areas is first evolved, and then expanded into detailed room graphs. They created examples of lock-and-key puzzles that were guaranteed to be completable. Londoño and Missura [14] introduced stochastic graph grammars to learn structural properties from Super Mario Bros levels and generate new levels with similar qualities to expert design. Later review works on graph grammars highlighted that grammars naturally capture high-level structural design patterns [15] and explored expansive examples of level structures and quest generation [16]. Other work has looked at using graph grammars to generate puzzles in educational games [17]. The sophisticated LudoScope level generation system [18, 19] allows a great degree of control over levels generated by graph grammars, for example recipes that can specify the number of times to apply a rule.

用图文法生成关卡。图文法已广泛用于关卡生成。Adams的早期工作[13]是最早使用图文法、而非短语结构文法，来生成FPS风格地下城的工作之一，借助图来表示关卡中复杂的连接模式。随后，Dormans[2]将关卡设计视为一系列模型变换，并创建任务文法，其中包含玩家的任务与目标；这些文法会映射为空间图，后者包含关卡的空间布局。Font等人[4]创建了一种两阶段演化方法，先演化由区域构成的高层图，再将其扩展为详细的房间图。他们生成了保证可以完成的锁与钥匙谜题示例。Londoño和Missura[14]引入随机图文法，从《Super Mario Bros》的关卡中学习结构属性，并生成具有类似专家设计品质的新关卡。后来的图文法综述指出，文法能够自然地捕捉高层结构设计模式[15]，并广泛考察了关卡结构与任务生成的示例[16]。其他工作还研究了用图文法生成教育游戏中的谜题[17]。复杂的LudoScope关卡生成系统[18, 19]允许对图文法生成的关卡进行高度控制，例如用生成配方指定一条规则的应用次数。

3. System Overview
3. 系统概述

For the most part, the core graph grammar system used in this work is similar to that presented in previous work [7], except that some rules conceptually represent graph generation and some represent gameplay mechanics. We briefly describe the previous system, in which rules represented only gameplay mechanics, and were used to ensure that a generated graph could be completed by those mechanics by generating a playthrough. The rules could rewrite the labels on subgraphs: at each step, a subgraph matching the labels on the left-hand side of the rules could be rewritten as the labels on the right-hand side; each node and edge has a static label, which cannot change from step to step, and a dynamic label, which can change from step to step. Visually, each rule is represented as a graph with the left- and right-hand side labels on each node and edge. These rules are incorporated into a constraint satisfaction problem that creates a sequence of graphs, each representing a step in the solution. Roughly speaking, the constraint problem is set up with a (Boolean) variable for each possible label for each possible node and edge, and for dynamic labels, these are for every step. The graphs in the sequence are constrained such that the labels can only change according to the mechanic rules, and the final graph is constrained to be solved; thus, the created sequence of graphs show how the initial graph can be solved by the mechanics as a playthrough. The problem setup must also be provided with a maximum graph size (in terms of nodes) and maximum number of steps, although steps can be marked as terminal, after which no more changes are made.

本项工作所用图文法系统的核心，大体上与既有工作[7]提出的系统相似，区别在于，一些规则在概念上表示图的生成，另一些规则表示玩法机制。下面简述既有系统：其中的规则只表示玩法机制，并通过生成通关过程来确保生成的图可由这些机制完成。规则可以重写子图上的标签：在每一步中，匹配规则左侧标签的子图，都可以被重写为右侧标签。每个节点和每条边都有一个静态标签，不能随步骤变化；还有一个动态标签，可以随步骤变化。在视觉表示上，每条规则是一幅图，其各节点和边同时带有左侧与右侧标签。这些规则被纳入一个约束满足问题，创建图序列，其中每幅图表示求解过程中的一步。大致而言，约束问题为每个可能节点、每条可能边的每种可能标签建立一个布尔变量；对动态标签而言，每一步都要建立这些变量。图序列受到约束，标签只能依照机制规则变化，最终图则必须处于已解决状态。因此，创建出的图序列作为通关过程，展示初始图如何由这些机制解出。问题设置还必须给出图的最大规模，以节点数量计，以及最大步骤数；不过，某些步骤可以标记为终止步骤，此后不再进行任何修改。

As the constraint problem is essentially solving for a label for each node and edge in each timestep, practical considerations about the number of edges that need to be considered can impact performance, as this number grows rapidly as the number of nodes increases. Previously, the number of edges was reduced by an approach called the edge setup. Each node has an ID, from 1...𝑁 , where 𝑁 is the maximum number of nodes in the generated graph. The edge setup globally limited which pairs of nodes could potentially have an edge between them based on ID. Though this is configurable, a straightforward edge setup simply only allows edges from a node ID 𝑖 to nodes up to ID 𝑖 + 𝑛.
由于约束问题实质上是在每个时间步为各节点和边求解标签，需要考虑的边的数量会影响实际性能；随着节点增多，这一数量会迅速增长。此前采用一种称为边设置的方法来减少边数。每个节点都有一个从1...𝑁取值的ID，其中𝑁是生成图的最大节点数。边设置依据ID，在全图范围限制哪些节点对之间可能有边。虽然这一设置可以配置，一种直接的方法是，只允许从ID为𝑖的节点连到ID不超过𝑖+𝑛的节点。

Here now we describe some of the most salient changes from the previous system, updated for this work. As an illustration, we refer to Figure 1, which shows a small set of generator rules and a resulting graph sequence generated by them. In this simple example, the steps only generate a graph in the final step and do not create a playthrough (we use the term graph sequence in general as the steps may be part of generating the graph or part of the playthrough). On the right, there are two generator rules: one that replaces the S node with two others, and then another rule that replaces those two with several other nodes. Constraints are added such that final graph must not have any S, X1 or X2 nodes. On the left the resulting generated graph sequence is shown. Note that the output of the solver is not just the graph from the last step, but the entire sequence of graphs at once.

现在介绍相对于既有系统、本项工作更新的一些主要改动。以图1为例，图中展示了一小组生成规则，以及它们生成的图序列。在这个简单例子中，各步骤只在最后一步生成一幅图，不创建通关过程；我们一般使用“图序列”一词，因为其中的步骤既可能属于图的生成，也可能属于通关过程。右侧有两条生成规则：第一条将S节点替换为另外两个节点，第二条再将这两个节点替换为若干其他节点。我们加入约束，使最终图不得包含任何S、X1或X2节点。左侧展示了生成的图序列。请注意，求解器一次输出的不只是最后一步的图，而是整个图序列。

• Labels. In this work we introduced two special labels: the nil label NIL (shown in figures as ∙), which means that a node or edge is not present, and the start label, S, which represents the start node. To use the existing system, which learned from example training graphs to create the initial graph (the graph in step 0), an example training graph is supplied with a single S node connected to a single NIL node by a NIL edge. The initial graph is constrained to have a single S node, with the rest of the nodes and all edges labeled NIL. Only dynamic labels, that can change from step to step, are used—static labels, though present from the previous system, are set to a fixed value and ignored. So, for example, the first rule in the top-left of Figure 1 can rewrite a S node, along with a non-present NIL edge to a non-present NIL node (the left-hand side of the rule), with a node labeled X1 to a node labeled X2 by and edge labeled labeled (the right-hand side of the rule). This happens in the generated graph sequence in step 2.

• 标签。本项工作引入两个特殊标签：空标签NIL（图中以∙表示），意为某个节点或边不存在；以及起始标签S，表示起始节点。既有系统通过从示例训练图中学习来创建初始图，也就是步骤0的图。为使用该系统，我们提供了一幅示例训练图：一个S节点通过一条NIL边连接一个NIL节点。初始图受到约束，只能有一个S节点，其余节点和全部边都标为NIL。系统仅使用可随步骤变化的动态标签；既有系统中的静态标签仍然存在，但被设为固定值并忽略。例如，图1左上方第一条规则可以将一个S节点，以及一条通向不存在的NIL节点、同样不存在的NIL边（规则左侧），重写成一个标为X1的节点，通过一条标为的边连接一个标为X2的节点（规则右侧）。这发生在生成图序列的步骤2。

• Edge hints. Edge hints can be used to specify on a per-rule basis information about which node IDs should be considered for an edge to connect. These can be relative, meaning they are deltas to the source node ID (shown in figures as +𝑛), or absolute, meaning only a specific node ID can be considered (shown in figures as @𝑛). For example, in the first rule in the top-left of Figure 1, the +7 . . . + 9 means that ID of the node rewritten to X2 must be 7 to 9 greater than the node ID rewritten to X1. This can be used to greatly limit the number of edges in consideration for this rule.
• 边提示。边提示可以逐条规则指定哪些节点ID应当被考虑为边的连接对象。它可以是相对的，表示相对于源节点ID的增量（图中写作+𝑛）；也可以是绝对的，表示只考虑特定节点ID（图中写作@𝑛）。例如，图1左上方第一条规则中的+7…+9表示，被重写为X2的节点，其ID必须比被重写为X1的节点ID大7至9。这可以大幅限制该规则需要考虑的边的数量。
• Node hints. Node hints can be used to specify on which node IDs and in which steps node labels can be present.
• 节点提示。节点提示可用于指定节点标签能够出现在哪些节点ID上，以及哪些步骤中。
• Rule hints. Rule hints can be used to specify in which steps a rule can be applied.
• 规则提示。规则提示可用于指定规则能够在哪些步骤应用。
• Skipped rule application. Whereas in the previous system one rule had to apply each step (until the terminal step), a specific step can allow no rules to be applied.
• 跳过规则应用。既有系统要求每一步都应用一条规则，直到终止步骤；现在可以允许某个特定步骤不应用任何规则。

• Simultaneous rule application. Multiple rules can be allowed to be applied in the same step, as long as they do not involve any of the same nodes or edges. This can allow the number of steps to be reduced, making the problem size smaller.
• 同时应用规则。可以允许多条规则在同一步应用，前提是它们不涉及任何相同的节点或边。这可以减少步骤数，从而缩小问题规模。
• Required rule application. In conjunction with skipped and simultaneous rule application, a step can require all rules that can be applied to be applied.
• 必需的规则应用。结合跳过和同时应用规则的能力，可以要求某一步中所有能够应用的规则都必须被应用。
4. Comparison with Prior Approach
4. 与既有方法的比较

First, we compare the previous graph-global edge setup method the new per-rule edge hints in terms of performance. Using the simple comparison grammar from Figure 1(left), we generated graphs of increasing maximum size allowing 3 steps. Note that the maximum size just sets an upper limit on the number of nodes and edges that can be in the graph and therefore must be considered; however, this simple grammar does not allow anything beyond what is shown in Figure 1(right) to be generated. When generating with edge hints, those in the figure were used. For edge setup, the hints in the figure were not used and a band-9 edge setup was used, where a node ID 𝑖 could connect to node ID up to 𝑖 + 9. Each method was run 25 times, and the time taken to generate graph sequences was averaged. For the constraint solver, we use a portfolio of three instances of PySAT’s [20] gluecard41 SAT solver, in turn based on Glucose [21], MiniCARD [22], and MiniSAT [23].

5. Generating Missions
5. 生成任务

As our motivating example, we sought to recreate Dormans’ [2] adventure game mission grammar in our constraint-based system, and augment it with mechanic rules. As it it quite large, we start with a simplified version, referred to as mini-Dormans, to explain how the new features of the system were used to implement it.
作为动机示例，我们尝试在基于约束的系统中重现Dormans[2]的冒险游戏任务文法，并为其增添机制规则。由于该文法相当庞大，我们先从一个称为mini-Dormans的简化版本入手，说明如何运用系统的新特性来实现它。

The grammar is shown in Figure 2. Edge hints are used throughout; rule hints are used to limit the steps in which rules can apply. Node hints are used to make sure all non-terminal labels are gone by the step the generate rules are done applying. Node hints are used, in conjunction with edge hints to implement an inventory system. Simultaneous rule application is allowed, and skipped/required rule application is used to force the application of rules related to edge traversability. By the end of the graph sequence, the goal node label must be gone (due to the player moving onto it).
文法见图2。整个文法都使用边提示；规则提示用于限制规则可应用的步骤。节点提示用于确保生成规则应用完毕时，全部非终结标签都已消失。节点提示还与边提示结合，用来实现物品栏系统。系统允许同时应用规则，并利用跳过／必需规则应用，强制执行与边的可通行性有关的规则。在图序列结束时，目标节点的标签必须消失，因为玩家已移动到该节点上。

The first generate rule creates two corridors C each followed by a lock l; it can only be used between steps 0 and 1. The next two generate rules can replace these corridors C with slots SL in sequence or parallel, and the next two replace a slot SL with either a key k or nothing n; these can only apply between steps 1 and 3. At this point in the steps the level has been generated. The next rules are meant as a proxy for spatial information in Dormans’ grammar to set up for the mechanic rules: in the original grammar, double edges indicate part of the mission should be spatially behind another when turned into a space. Since we are not generating the space, we instead make all the other edges leading to a node that should be behind a node not travesible. This is accomplished by a required rule application rewriting all incoming single dash - edges to a node with an incoming equal = edge to be an untraversible x between steps 3 and 4, and then marking all the remaining edges as a traversible period . between steps 4 and 5 (the box □ in a node means it that node is ignored in the rule). At this point the playthrough begins: the next rule sets up the player @, with an inventory, which uses node hints and edge hints to use the label at node ID 0 (k:, k:1, k:2) to count the number of keys k the player has collected. The remaining mechanic rules allow the player to move through the graph, collecting keys and using them to open locks, and reach the goal.

第一条生成规则创建两段走廊C，每段后面各有一把锁l；它只可在步骤0与1之间使用。接下来的两条生成规则可用串联或并联的槽位SL替换走廊C，再接下来的两条则将槽位SL替换为钥匙k或空置n；它们只可在步骤1与3之间应用。进行到此，关卡已经生成。接下来的规则代替Dormans文法中的空间信息，为机制规则作准备：在原文法中，双边表示任务的某一部分在转化为空间后，应位于另一部分之后。由于我们不生成空间，因此改为将所有其他通向那个应位于某节点之后的节点的边设为不可通行。具体而言，在步骤3与4之间，利用必需规则应用，将所有进入某节点的单横线-边重写为不可通行的x，条件是该节点另有一条进入它的等号=边；然后在步骤4与5之间，将所有剩余边标为可通行的点号.。节点内的方框□表示该节点在规则中被忽略。此时通关过程开始：下一条规则建立带有物品栏的玩家@；它利用节点提示与边提示，在节点ID 0上使用标签k:、k:1、k:2，记录玩家已收集的钥匙k的数量。余下的机制规则允许玩家在图中移动、收集钥匙并用其开锁，最终抵达目标。

Top control the generated level, constraints are added so that sequence and parallel corridor rules are used once each, and step 3 has 2 keys. The maximum size is 15 nodes and maximum steps is 20. The same solver setup is used as above, and 25 graph sequences were generated.
为控制生成的关卡，我们加入约束：串联走廊规则和并联走廊规则各使用一次，且步骤3中有2把钥匙。最大规模为15个节点，最大步骤数为20。我们使用与上述相同的求解器配置，生成25个图序列。

Figure 3 shows a generated graph sequence using this grammar and hints. The first several steps use generate rules. Step 0 is the initial graph, with just a S node. The next three steps create the graph structure and place the keys. Step 4 marks two edges incoming to the first lock as not traversible, requiring the player to use the remaining edge later, and step 5 marks the rest of the edges as traversible. Step 6 begins the application of the mechanic rules, with the player appearing with an empty inventory. From there the player moves through the graph, picking keys and using them to open locks, and eventually reaching the goal. The player notably does not take the most direct path. Due to unifying the generate rules and mechanic rules into a single grammar, keys are placed in the right locations for the player to open the locks.

We applied the same conceptual approach to Dormans’ full mission grammar [2] to explore the controllability and applications of the unified grammar approach in various configurations. As the grammars and generated graph sequences are quite large, here we describe their setup and summarize their properties, while making more information available at https://osf.io/zxpky/. A partial graph sequence for the most complex, Dormans-slots, is shown in Figure 4.
我们对Dormans完整任务文法[2]采用了同样的概念方法，以考察统一文法方法在不同配置下的可控性与应用。由于文法及生成的图序列相当庞大，这里只说明它们的设置并概述其性质，更多信息见https://osf.io/zxpky/。其中最复杂的Dormans-slots配置的一部分图序列见图4。
• Dormans. This configuration is just generating a Dormans mission graph, with maximum size 45 and maximum 8 steps.
• Dormans。该配置仅生成一个Dormans任务图，最大规模为45，最多8个步骤。
• Dormans-lock-multi. Same as Dormans, but there must be exactly one multi-lock lm node. This could be useful if a designer would like specific nodes present in the generated graph.
• Dormans-lock-multi。与Dormans相同，但必须恰好有一个多重锁lm节点。如果设计者希望生成的图中出现特定节点，这一配置可能有用。

• Dormans-rule-count. Same as Dormans, but the rules for creating a 3 and 5 long linear chain must be used exactly once each. This could be useful if a designer would like specific rules to be used to generate the graph.
• Dormans-rule-count。与Dormans相同，但创建长度为3和5的线性链的规则必须各使用恰好一次。如果设计者希望用特定规则来生成图，这一配置可能有用。

• Dormans-match. Same as Dormans, but a given substructure consisting of 6 nodes and 4 edges must be matched in the final graph. This could be useful if a designer likes part of a generated graph but would like to try variations of the rest of it.
• Dormans-match。与Dormans相同，但最终图必须匹配一个给定子结构，其中含6个节点与4条边。如果设计者喜欢某幅生成图的一部分，但希望尝试其余部分的变体，这一配置可能有用。

• Dormans-slots. Similar to mini-Dormans but with the complete Dormans grammar. Replaces the specific key and item placement rules of the original generate grammar with slot nodes, which can then be filled in with items and keys; augments the generate grammar with a mechanic grammar and uses this to ensure the generated graph is completable. Uses a maximum size of 45 and maximum 35 steps. In the step where the level is generated, there must be 1 quest item, 1 item test, 4 keys, 1 multi-lock, 1 single lock, 1 final key, and 1 final lock.
• Dormans-slots。与mini-Dormans类似，但使用完整的Dormans文法。它用槽位节点替换原始生成文法中特定的钥匙和物品放置规则，再向槽位填入物品与钥匙；同时为生成文法增添机制文法，借此确保生成的图可以完成。最大规模为45，最多35个步骤。在关卡生成完毕的那个步骤中，必须有1件任务物品、1次物品检验、4把钥匙、1个多重锁、1个单锁、1把最终钥匙和1个最终锁。

For each, the same solver setup is used as above, and 25 graph sequences were generated. Summary statistics of timing, sizes, ans steps are given in Table 2. Some observations of note are that to just generate the graphs on this scale takes only a few seconds, and adding in a few additional constraints on the generated graph does appear to increase the time needed much. However, augmenting with mechanics rules greatly increases the time to generate graph sequences, around 2 orders of magnitude on average. This may make it prohibitive still for online or interactive generation.

6. Conclusion
6. 结论

In this work we have presented an approach to generate completable levels using graph grammars. The approach combines rules for generating graphs with rules for running game mechanics on graphs into a single unified grammar. Using a constraint-based system that generates a graph sequence, where the grammar constrains changes between graphs in the sequence and the level must be solved by the final step, the mechanic rule ensure that the level generated by the generate rules can be completed. We describe some practical improvements over the previous system and show their beneficial impact on timing. We also recreate and augment the adventure game mission grammar of Dormans and show how the constraint-based approach can provide controllability of generated graphs.

本项工作提出了一种使用图文法生成可完成关卡的方法。该方法将生成图的规则与在图上运行游戏机制的规则结合为一个统一文法。系统基于约束，生成图序列：文法约束序列中图与图之间的变化，并要求关卡在最后一步得到解决；由此，机制规则确保生成规则创建的关卡可以完成。我们描述了对既有系统的若干实际改进，并展示其对耗时的有利影响。我们还重现并扩展了Dormans的冒险游戏任务文法，展示基于约束的方法如何控制生成的图。

text: Abstract Procedurally generating levels for games often involves writing custom algorithms or providing large amounts of levels to learn from. In this work, we explore an approach to general video game level generation using a game’s source program along with a single level, based on the concept of program inversion. Given the forward program for a game, we produce an inverted program in the same language that essentially runs the game backward. Starting from a solved level (which can be found searching with the forward program on a level), the inverted program can be run to generate variations on the level. We look at simple games written in a domain-specific rewrite-based language for describing tile- and turn-based games, where a single player repeatedly makes deterministic choices until they win. We verify that the level variations created by the inverted program can be solved by the original forward program.

text: 摘要 为游戏程序化生成关卡，往往需要编写定制算法，或提供大量关卡供系统学习。本研究基于程序反演的概念，探索一种利用游戏源程序和单个关卡来进行通用电子游戏关卡生成的方法。给定游戏的正向程序，我们用相同语言产生一个反演程序，它实质上会倒着运行游戏。从一个已解关卡出发——可以使用正向程序在一个关卡上搜索，找到这种状态——运行反演程序，就能生成该关卡的变体。我们考察以一种基于重写的领域专用语言编写的简单游戏；这种语言用于描述图块制、回合制游戏，单个玩家在其中反复作出结果确定的选择，直到获胜。我们验证，反演程序产生的关卡变体能够由原来的正向程序解出。
section: 通过程序反演进行程序化关卡生成

text: Keywords procedural content generation, program inversion, rewrite rules
section: 通过程序反演进行程序化关卡生成

text: 关键词 程序化内容生成；程序反演；重写规则。
section: 通过程序反演进行程序化关卡生成

text: 1. Introduction
1. 引言

Procedural content generation (PCG) for creating game content, such as game levels, has become increasingly popular [1]. There are a wide variety of approaches to PCG, with claimed benefits such as various kinds of replayability and tailoring content to players [2].
利用程序化内容生成（PCG）创作关卡等游戏内容，已经越来越普遍[1]。PCG有多种多样的方法，其宣称的好处包括不同形式的可重玩性，以及针对玩家定制内容等[2]。

However, the majority of PCG techniques require a fair amount of additional work above and beyond the work needed to create a game in the first place. “Classical” rule-, search- and constraint-based approaches require writing custom code just for generating content (e.g., a grammar, a fitness function, or constraints). More recent machine learning and “generative AI” [3] approaches often require large amounts of training data, potentially defeating the purpose of generating content in the first place [4]. If the content being generated is game levels, it is important for them to be completable and solvable by the player, and it is not uncommon to also apply a game-playing agent for testing content (e.g., [5, 6]).
然而，大多数PCG技术都需要在最初制作游戏所需工作之外，再投入相当多的额外劳动。“经典”的基于规则、搜索和约束的方法，需要专门为生成内容编写定制代码，例如语法、适应度函数或约束。较新的机器学习和“生成式AI”方法[3]，往往需要大量训练数据，这可能反而违背最初生成内容的目的[4]。如果生成的是游戏关卡，那么玩家能够完成并解出它们就很重要；人们也常用游戏游玩智能体来测试内容，例如[5,6]。

With the goal of reducing the amount of additional work needed to generate content for a game, in this work we explore an approach to generating content for a game based on things a designer would need to create for the game anyway: the game’s source code, along with at least one level. This can be considered general video game level generation [7]: generating levels for a whole class of games implemented in description language. Our approach is based on the concept of program inversion: the game’s source code is inverted to create a new program, in the original description language, that undoes player moves in the game. The inverted program can then be run on a solved level to generate new starting levels that we know can be solved by the original program. We call this concept procedural level generation via program inversion.

为了减少为游戏生成内容所需的额外工作，本研究探索一种基于设计者无论如何都需要为游戏创建之物的方法：游戏源代码，以及至少一个关卡。这可以视为通用电子游戏关卡生成[7]，即为使用描述语言实现的一整类游戏生成关卡。我们的方法以程序反演概念为基础：将游戏源代码反演，使用原来的描述语言创建一个新程序，用来撤销游戏中玩家的移动。随后可在已解关卡上运行反演程序，生成新的起始关卡；我们知道，这些起始关卡能够由原程序解出。我们将这一概念称为通过程序反演进行程序化关卡生成。

In this work we take an initial step in this direction. We use programs written in a small variant of the domain-specific language Tile Rewrite Rule Behavior Trees (TRRBTs) [8]. In this language, 2D grids of tiles, called boards, are used to represent starting levels as well as the current game configuration, and the logic of a game’s program is represented using a behavior-tree like structure, called a tree. Leaf nodes of the tree can change the board by rewriting one pattern of tiles (the left-hand side) with another (the right-hand side), or check for the existence of a pattern of tiles on the board by matching it. We chose this language as inverting the changes to board configuration based on rewrites is straightforward: swap the left and right hand sides of the rule. Additionally, the modularity of the language allows us to limit the structure of supported games, and we do not use the full range of tree and node structures that TRRBTs can support. We limit to games with a simple tree structure: those where a single player repeatedly makes a choice with deterministic consequences until they win.

本研究向这一方向迈出了初步一步。我们使用领域专用语言“图块重写规则行为树”（Tile Rewrite Rule Behavior Trees，TRRBTs）[8]的一个小型变体来编写程序。在这种语言中，由图块构成的二维网格称为棋盘，用于表示起始关卡及当前游戏配置；游戏程序的逻辑则用一种类似行为树的结构表示，称为树。树的叶节点可以把一种图块模式，即左侧，重写为另一种模式，即右侧，从而改变棋盘；也可以通过匹配，检查棋盘上是否存在某种图块模式。我们选择这种语言，是因为反演基于重写的棋盘配置变化很直接：交换规则的左右两侧即可。此外，语言的模块性使我们能够限制所支持游戏的结构；我们并未使用TRRBTs可以支持的全部树和节点结构。我们只处理具有简单树结构的游戏：单个玩家反复作出具有确定后果的选择，直到获胜。

To generate levels for a game, given the game’s TRRBT code tree and a board, we use the tree to solve the board (if needed — an already solved board can be provided), then invert the tree and run the inverted tree on the solved board to generate new boards. These boards are variations on the original board. These variations maintain certain features from the initial input board as there are elements of the boards that cannot be changed by rewrites (e.g., walls or the dimensions of the board). However, this approach is effective in generating interesting and solvable level variations. While the result of a program inversion with one starting board will have some underlying constants between all levels, these level variations have advantages from requiring many more steps to solve to having more interactive pieces on the board, depending on the game.

给定游戏的TRRBT代码树与一个棋盘，要为它生成关卡，我们先用树解出棋盘——如果需要的话，也可以直接提供一个已解棋盘——再反演树，在已解棋盘上运行反演树，生成新棋盘。这些棋盘是原棋盘的变体。由于棋盘上有些要素不能通过重写改变，例如墙壁或棋盘尺寸，这些变体会保留初始输入棋盘的某些特征。不过，这一方法能够有效生成有趣且可解的关卡变体。虽然从一个起始棋盘进行程序反演，所得全部关卡之间会存在一些底层不变量，但视游戏而定，这些关卡变体可以带来不同优势，例如需要更多解题步数，或在棋盘上具有更多可交互棋子。

We present the program inversion approach we used for TRRBTs having this structure, and implemented four games: Peg Solitaire (jumping pegs to remove them), Merge (merging neighboring numbers into higher numbers), Sokoban (pushing crates onto targets), and TwoDoor (a simple lock-and-key dungeon). We show empirically that the inverted trees only generate solvable boards, by enumerating them and checking their solvability. We also show that generating boards using an inverted tree compares favorably to a similar approach using only the original (forward) tree.
我们介绍用于这种结构的TRRBTs的程序反演方法，并实现四种游戏：Peg Solitaire（跳过棋子并将其移除）、Merge（把相邻数字合并为更大的数字）、Sokoban（把箱子推到目标位置），以及TwoDoor（简单的锁钥地牢）。我们通过枚举棋盘并检查其可解性，从经验上表明反演树只生成可解棋盘；也表明，使用反演树生成棋盘，与仅使用原始正向树的类似方法相比具有优势。

This work contributes the general concept of program inversion as an approach to generating content for games from a game’s source code, as well as an exploration of this concept in a domain-specific language, generating levels across several games.
本研究的贡献，是提出把程序反演作为一种从游戏源代码生成游戏内容的方法的一般概念，并在一种领域专用语言中探索这一概念，为多个游戏生成关卡。
2. Related Work
2. 相关工作

Procedural Content Generation. A variety of approaches have been developed for procedural content in games [1]. These range from “classic” techniques, such as constructive- or rule- based (e.g., [9, 10]), to search-based (e.g., [11, 12]), and constraint-based (e.g., [13, 14]) methods. Such approaches generally require implementing a generator in addition to implementing the game itself.
程序化内容生成。游戏程序化内容生成已有多种方法[1]，从构造式、基于规则等“经典”技术，例如[9,10]，到基于搜索，例如[11,12]，以及基于约束的方法，例如[13,14]。这些方法通常要求在实现游戏之外，再实现一个生成器。

Recently, machine learning approaches that can learn from example content have been developed in the area of PCGML [3], as well as “generative AI” [15]. Such approaches can require large amounts of data for training or pre-training, and may not guarantee solvability of generated levels (sometimes relying on an agent test or repair step). Some learning approaches, however, can learn from a single example level (e.g., WaveFunctionCollapse [16] or Sturgeon [17]). These approaches could thus potentially require only the game’s code and an example level to work, as they could learn to generate levels from the example level, and then use the code to check solvability, in a generate-and test framework. Comparing that to our program inversion approach would be interesting future work.

近年来，PCGML[3]及“生成式AI”[15]领域发展了能够从内容示例学习的机器学习方法。这类方法可能需要大量数据进行训练或预训练，也可能无法保证生成关卡的可解性，有时需要智能体测试或修复步骤。不过，一些学习方法能够从单个示例关卡学习，例如WaveFunctionCollapse[16]或Sturgeon[17]。因此，这些方法也可能只需游戏代码和一个示例关卡便可工作：先从示例关卡学习生成关卡，再在生成—测试框架中使用游戏代码检查可解性。将其与我们的程序反演方法比较，会是有趣的未来工作。

In this work we enumerate all the possible boards found by the inverted tree. This is essentially a form of Exhaustive PCG [18]; however, we do this mainly to confirm the levels’ solvability. Some work has looked at interactively visualizing and filtering such large datasets of generated levels [19].
本研究枚举反演树找到的全部可能棋盘。这实质上是穷尽式PCG[18]的一种形式；不过，我们这样做主要是为了确认关卡可解性。已有研究探索了对这种大型生成关卡数据集进行交互式可视化与筛选[19]。

General Video Game Level Generation and Game DSLs. A number of domain-specific languages have been developed over the years for describing both board and video games, such as Ludii [20], Game Description Language [21], Video Game Description Language [22], Ceptre [23], and PuzzleScript [24]. Some have been used as targets for general video game level generation: that is, given a game’s code in some description language along with a player agent, generate levels for the game [7].
通用电子游戏关卡生成与游戏DSL。多年来，人们开发了多种描述棋盘游戏和电子游戏的领域专用语言，例如Ludii[20]、游戏描述语言[21]、电子游戏描述语言[22]、Ceptre[23]和PuzzleScript[24]。其中一些已被用作通用电子游戏关卡生成的目标语言：给定以某种描述语言编写的游戏代码及一个玩家智能体，为该游戏生成关卡[7]。

One approach in this area approached generating levels for games written in VGDL by translating it into Answer Set Programming [25]. This approach also applied an evolutionary process with agents verifying that levels are solvable. Other work developed a framework for evaluating general VGDL level generators [7]. VGDL has also been used for evaluating general level generators [26].
这一领域的一种方法，把VGDL游戏翻译为回答集程序设计，以生成关卡[25]。该方法还采用进化过程，并由智能体验证关卡可解性。另一项研究开发了评估通用VGDL关卡生成器的框架[7]。VGDL也被用于评估通用关卡生成器[26]。
Figure 1: Generic approach to TRRBT program inversion. Forward tree on the left and inverted tree on the right.

图1：TRRBT程序反演的一般方法。左侧为正向树，右侧为反演树。 图内文字汉译：Program: forward，程序：正向；Program: inverted，程序：反演；loop-until-all，循环直至一轮中全部子节点失败；win:1，玩家1获胜；lose:1，玩家1失败；player:1，玩家1；rewrite，重写；match-times:T，模式出现T次；END，终局模式；LEFT与RIGHT，规则左侧与右侧。下标与规则箭头按原图保留。

PuzzleScript has also been a target for general level generation. For example, one approach has used constructive and search based techniques based on an analysis of a game’s rules [27]. While most prior work in general video game level generation creates levels, our work aims to create a level generator in the original language. Notably, earlier work in TRRBTs [8] generated randomly shuffled levels using the player’s moves from within the tree, but only if the individual moves themselves were reversible.
PuzzleScript也被用作通用关卡生成的目标。例如，一种方法基于游戏规则分析，采用构造式和基于搜索的技术[27]。多数既有通用电子游戏关卡生成研究直接创建关卡；我们的目标则是用原语言创建一个关卡生成器。值得注意的是，早期TRRBTs研究[8]利用树内部的玩家移动，生成随机打乱的关卡，但仅在各次移动本身可逆时才这样做。

Game Mechanic Inversion. Some previous work has looked at inverting moves or mechanics in specific games as a way to ensure the solvability of generated levels. This is a not uncommon approach to generating Sokoban [28] levels, by letting the character pull rather than push crates from a solved configuration (e.g., [29, 30, 31]), as well as similar specific games. A similar approach, that of undoing moves, has also been applied to generating Sudoku number puzzles [32]. Some work on Sokoban has also looked at using reversed moves to solve puzzles, starting from the solution and searching backwards to the start [33]. While usually these works look at specific games, we are looking at a more general technique for a whole category of games.

游戏机制反演。一些既有研究把特定游戏中的移动或机制反演，用来保证生成关卡的可解性。在生成Sokoban[28]及类似特定游戏的关卡时，这是一种并不少见的方法：从已解配置出发，让角色拉箱子，而不是推箱子，例如[29,30,31]。类似的撤销移动方法，也曾用于生成数独谜题[32]。一些Sokoban研究还用反向移动来求解谜题，从解开始向起点逆向搜索[33]。这些工作通常研究特定游戏；我们则研究面向一整类游戏的更通用技术。

Program Inversion. The general concept of program inversion [34], roughly speaking, is to derive a program that does the opposite of some given program, mapping outputs back to inputs. A number of approaches to program inversion focus on theoretical proofs of the correctness of the inversion [35], for example of tree traversals [36, 37] or certain types of matrix multiplication [38]. The program inversion concept is promising for programs that naturally pair in this way, such as compression/decompression programs [39].
程序反演。粗略地说，程序反演的一般概念[34]，是导出一个与给定程序作用相反的程序，把输出映射回输入。一些程序反演方法关注反演正确性的理论证明[35]，例如树遍历[36,37]或某些矩阵乘法[38]。对于压缩／解压缩这类天然成对的程序[39]，程序反演概念很有前景。

In some cases a non-deterministic mapping from outputs back to inputs may be acceptable [40] or even desirable. A similar approach to ours, for example, has been used to generate TIFF images for testing implementations of image clients [41]. They use a normalization program to create a normalized representation of an image, and then invert that program and use the inverse program to generate test images. This can be seen as analogous to our approach of using the original (forward) program to solve a level and then the inverse program to generate new levels from that.
在某些情况下，从输出回到输入的非确定性映射也许可以接受[40]，甚至是所希望的。例如，一种与我们类似的方法曾用于生成TIFF图像，以测试图像客户端的实现[41]。它先用归一化程序创建图像的归一化表征，再反演这一程序，利用逆程序生成测试图像。这可以类比于我们先用原始正向程序解出关卡，再用逆程序据此生成新关卡的方法。
3. System Overview
3. 系统概述
Here we describe the approach we take to generating levels based on a game’s source code.
这里介绍我们依据游戏源代码生成关卡的方法。

Game Representation. Our inversion method for level generation uses Tile Rewrite Rule Behavior Trees (TRRBTs) as the underlying game representation [8], although we only support a very specific type of game, and not the full range of games that TRRBTs allow. Games consist of a board and a tree. The board is a 2D array of tiles — strings of characters — that represent the current configuration of a game. A board can have multiple named layers of tiles that are stacked on top of each other. This makes it easier for something like foreground tiles to move over background tiles (e.g. pushing crates over targets in Sokoban, discussed below). Terminology-wise, “board” can be considered the term for a “level” in TRRBTs. A layered 2D array of tiles that does not represent the game board is also called a pattern. A board can also have a result associated with it, either win or lose if the game has ended in one of those outcomes, stalemate if the game has ended without an explicit outcome, or nil if the game is still running.

游戏表征。我们的关卡生成反演方法以图块重写规则行为树（TRRBTs）作为底层游戏表征[8]，但只支持很特定的一类游戏，而非TRRBTs允许的全部游戏。游戏由棋盘和树组成。棋盘是图块，即字符串，构成的二维数组，表示游戏当前配置。一个棋盘可以具有多个相互叠放、各有名称的图块层。这使前景图块越过背景图块等操作更容易实现，例如下文Sokoban中把箱子推过目标位置。在术语上，可以把“棋盘”看作TRRBTs中“关卡”的称谓。不代表游戏棋盘的分层二维图块数组，也称为模式。棋盘还可以带有结果值：若游戏已按相应结果结束，则为win或lose；若游戏结束但没有明确结果，则为stalemate；若游戏仍在进行，则为nil。

The tree determines the logic of the game and makes changes to the board. The tree is run as a behavior tree, with nodes succeeding or failing based on specific conditions for their node type, and returning that information to their parent node, which adjusts its behavior based on its children.
树决定游戏逻辑，并修改棋盘。树按照行为树方式运行：节点根据所属类型的特定条件成功或失败，把这一信息返回父节点；父节点再根据子节点调整行为。
Figure 2: Inversion of tree for Peg Solitaire. Forward tree on the left and inverted tree on the right.

图2：Peg Solitaire的树反演。左侧为正向树，右侧为反演树。 图内文字汉译：Peg Solitaire，单人跳棋；forward，正向；inverted，反演；loop-until-all，循环直至一轮中全部子节点失败；win:1，玩家1获胜；lose:1，玩家1失败；player:1，玩家1；rewrite，重写；match-times:1，模式出现1次。棋子、空格与重写方向按原图保留。
Figure 3: Forward trees for other games used. For space, rewrite nodes that are rotations of others are omitted.

图3：所用其他游戏的正向树。受篇幅限制，作为其他节点旋转形式的rewrite节点予以省略。 图内文字汉译：Merge，合并；Sokoban，推箱子；TwoDoor，双门；forward，正向；loop-until-all，循环直至一轮中全部子节点失败；win:1，玩家1获胜；player:1，玩家1；rewrite，重写；match-times:0／1，模式出现0／1次；main，主层；trgt，目标层。图中的字符图块、数字与箭头保留原样。

Both a board and a tree are required for a game to be played. Although in previous work boards were included directly in the tree through a set-board node, in our method, we separated the board from the tree so that we could more easily invert the tree and and allow for different starting boards to be passed into the same tree.
要进行游戏，棋盘和树两者缺一不可。虽然早期工作通过set-board节点把棋盘直接纳入树中，我们的方法将棋盘与树分开，以便更容易反演树，并使不同起始棋盘能够传入同一棵树。
Supported Tree Structure and Inversion. In this work we use only a few node types and require them to be in a particular arrangement. The node types are:
所支持的树结构及其反演。本研究只使用少量节点类型，并要求它们按特定方式排列。节点类型如下：
• loop-until-all: Iteratively runs children in order until all children fail on one iteration. Succeeds if any child succeeds, otherwise fails.
• loop-until-all：按顺序反复运行子节点，直到某一轮中全部子节点都失败。如果任何子节点成功，则成功；否则失败。
• win and lose: Runs children in order. If any child succeeds, immediately ends the game with the respective result for its associated player; otherwise fails.
• win和lose：按顺序运行子节点。如果任何子节点成功，立即以该节点对应玩家的相应结果结束游戏；否则失败。

• player: All children of a player node must be rewrite nodes. If any LEFT pattern of a child is present in the current board, the player can chose one LEFT to be replace with its associated RIGHT and the player node succeeds. Fails if there are no LEFT patterns present.
• player：player节点的全部子节点都必须是rewrite节点。如果任一子节点的LEFT模式出现在当前棋盘上，玩家可以选择一个LEFT，用其对应的RIGHT替换，此时player节点成功。若不存在任何LEFT模式，则失败。
• rewrite: Contain the rewrites, where the associated LEFT can be replaced with the associated RIGHT. In this work, these are always the child of a player node and so not run directly.
• rewrite：包含重写操作，可用对应的RIGHT替换LEFT。本研究中，这些节点始终是player节点的子节点，因此不会被直接运行。
• match-times: Succeeds if its pattern is present in the current board its associated number of times, otherwise fails.
• match-times：如果其模式在当前棋盘中出现的次数符合节点所关联的次数，则成功；否则失败。

Our program inversion approach takes a tree representing a game’s (forward) logic as an input. These trees are required to fit the specific tree structure shown in Figure 1(left). This structure essentially represents a game loop that alternates checking for a win and the player making a move. The root is a loop-until-all node with two children. The first child of this loop is a win node that has a child match-times node that succeeds if a pattern END is matched on the board T times. The second child of loop-until-all is required to be the player node with a series of N rewrite nodes with patterns LEFTi and RIGHTi, 1 ≤ i ≤ N as children. Note that in this structure, checking for a win before the player moves allows starting from a board that is already solved.

我们的程序反演方法以表示游戏正向逻辑的树作为输入。这些树必须符合图1左侧所示的特定结构。该结构实质上表示一个游戏循环：交替检查是否获胜和让玩家移动。根节点是一个具有两个子节点的loop-until-all节点。该循环的第一个子节点是win节点，它又有一个match-times子节点；当模式END在棋盘上匹配T次时，这个子节点成功。loop-until-all的第二个子节点必须是player节点，其子节点是一系列共N个rewrite节点，具有模式LEFTi与RIGHTi，其中1≤i≤N。请注意，在这种结构中，先检查获胜再让玩家移动，因此允许从一个已经解出的棋盘开始。

text 正向枚举 输入：tree：（正向）游戏树 board：起始棋盘 输出：boardsGen：生成的棋盘 boardsEnum ← enumerate(tree, board) boardsGen ← {b ∈ boardsEnum | bresult = nil ∧ solve(tree, board) ≠ nil} 算法2：正向枚举棋盘。

The inverted version of such a tree is shown in Figure 1(right). The root remains a loop-until-all node, with the order of the children reversed. First is the player node, with the order of its rewrite children reversed, and the sides if these individual rewrite nodes reversed, and so that RIGHTi is on the left and LEFTi is on the right. This allows individual rewrites to be done backward. Second is a lose node, taking the place of the win node and its match-times child and associated END. A lose node is used so that the inverted game won’t output a board that is already winning. Note that here losing is checked for after making a move, as the inverted tree presumes that it is starting from a board that won from the forward tree.

这种树的反演版本见图1右侧。根节点仍为loop-until-all，但其子节点顺序颠倒。首先是player节点，其rewrite子节点的顺序也颠倒；各个rewrite节点的两侧同样颠倒，使RIGHTi位于左侧，LEFTi位于右侧。这样就可以反向执行各次重写。其次是lose节点，它取代win节点，同时承接其match-times子节点及关联的END。使用lose节点，是为了避免反演游戏输出一个已经获胜的棋盘。注意，这里是在移动之后检查失败，因为反演树预设自己从一个在正向树中已经获胜的棋盘开始。

The resulting inverted tree can be run on a solved board, and each board that would be presented to the player will be a solvable starting board for the game. This can be used to generate new levels that are variations on the same underlying level structure.
所得反演树可以在已解棋盘上运行，而每个将被呈现给玩家的棋盘，都会成为该游戏的一个可解起始棋盘。这可用于生成新关卡，它们是同一底层关卡结构的变体。
4. Evaluation
4. 评估
Here we describe evaluations of the program inversion approach. Game trees and enumerated boards from the evaluation can be found at https://osf.io/er5wh/.
这里介绍对程序反演方法的评估。评估所用游戏树和枚举棋盘可在https://osf.io/er5wh/获取。

Inverted Enumeration of Boards. To empirically verify that the inverted trees generate only boards that can be solved, and to gather descriptive information on the generated boards, we enumerate all boards that are produced by an inverted tree, starting from a solved board.
棋盘的逆向枚举。为了从经验上验证反演树只生成可解棋盘，并收集生成棋盘的描述性信息，我们从已解棋盘出发，枚举反演树产生的全部棋盘。

The overall approach is shown in Algorithm 1. It starts by taking the (forward) tree for a game in the structure described above and a solvable starting board for the game. The function solve runs a breath-first search with the forward tree until it reaches a solved board that wins the game; this also associates the number of steps it took to solve with the board. Then invert produces the inverted tree as described above. Next, enumerate finds all boards reachable by the inverted tree, starting from the solved board; each enumerated board also gets associated with the number of steps it took to reach. From these enumerated boards, we keep only those that took at least one step to reach (so they are not the solved board from which inverted enumeration began) and either have not ended or ended in a stalemate. These enumerated boards are checked by asserting that it is possible to win each of then using the forward tree.

总体方法见算法1。首先取得符合上述结构的游戏正向树，以及该游戏的一个可解起始棋盘。solve函数用正向树进行广度优先搜索，直到到达一个获胜的已解棋盘；同时把求解所需步数与该棋盘关联。随后，invert按前述方法产生反演树。接着，enumerate从已解棋盘出发，找出反演树能够到达的全部棋盘，并把到达各棋盘所需的步数与其关联。从这些枚举棋盘中，我们只保留至少经过一步才能到达的棋盘——因此不包括逆向枚举开始时的已解棋盘——而且它们要么尚未结束，要么以僵局结束。最后，通过断言每一个枚举棋盘都可以利用正向树获胜，检查这些棋盘。

This game makes use of TRRBT’s layers to have a separate layer for the targets under the main layer so the player and crates can move over them. The use of layers can be seen in the tree for Sokoban in Figure 3; the match-times node ensures there are no crates on the main layer that don’t line up with the targets on the target layer.
• Sokoban：基于解谜游戏Sokoban[28]，玩家角色P可以在地面上推动箱子O，目标是把所有箱子放到目标位置上。该游戏使用TRRBT的分层，在主层下方为目标设置单独一层，使玩家和箱子可以从目标上经过。Sokoban的树见图3，其中可以看到分层的使用；match-times节点确保主层上不存在未与目标层目标位置对齐的箱子。
