5. Discussion
5. 讨论

Checking that all the boards enumerated by the inverted tree when starting from a solved board are themselves solvable shows, empirically in the cases that were tried, that running the inverted tree will always result in a solvable board that could thus be used in a game.
检查从已解棋盘出发由反演树枚举出的全部棋盘，确认它们自身都可解，这在所尝试的情形中从经验上表明：运行反演树总会产生一个可解棋盘，因此可以用于游戏。

One potentially useful feature of the approach is that it works from a solved board or a starting board. This provides flexibility, as a designer can either use a starting board (which they may already have if they are working on a game) and get variations on that board, or start from a desired solution and generate boards directly from that.
这一方法一个可能有用的特点，是既可从已解棋盘，也可从起始棋盘工作。这带来了灵活性：设计者可以使用一个起始棋盘——如果正在制作游戏，他们可能已经有这样的棋盘——获得其变体；也可以从期望的解出发，直接生成棋盘。

We also found that, in comparison to just forward enumeration from a solvable board, inverse enumeration find more boards. When starting from a solved board there are, unsurprisingly, no new boards to be found. But even in the games starting from unsolved boards, inverted enumeration is able to find a larger number of boards with higher average and maximum solution lengths.
我们还发现，与从可解棋盘仅做正向枚举相比，逆向枚举能找到更多棋盘。从已解棋盘开始时，正向方法找不到新棋盘，这并不意外。但即使对于从未解棋盘开始的游戏，逆向枚举仍能找到更多棋盘，而且它们的平均和最大解步长度都更高。

We also think, subjectively, inverse enumeration finds some interesting levels. For example, the generated Sokoban boards appear to include the provided starting board as a step along the solution path. The generated TwoDoor boards involve backtracking a bit after collecting a key: one to collect the other key behind a door, and one just to use up a key in a door as the player can only exit without a key.
我们还主观地认为，逆向枚举找到了一些有趣关卡。例如，生成的Sokoban棋盘似乎把提供的起始棋盘包含为解题路径中的一步。生成的TwoDoor棋盘则涉及拿到钥匙之后略作折返：一个是去取得门后的另一把钥匙，另一个则只是在门上用掉钥匙，因为玩家只有不携带钥匙时才能退出。
6. Conclusion
6. 结论

In this work we have presented the concept of program inversion for procedural content generation. Although other work has applied inverted mechanics to content generation in specific games, we show an implementation of that concept using a small version of the Tile Rewrite Rule Behavior Trees domain-specific language that captures a class of simple games. This allows new boards to be generated for these games directly from their source code and a single example board.
本研究提出了将程序反演用于程序化内容生成的概念。虽然已有工作把反演机制用于特定游戏的内容生成，我们展示了这一概念的一种实现：使用图块重写规则行为树这一领域专用语言的小型版本，覆盖一类简单游戏。由此，可以直接依据这些游戏的源代码和单个示例棋盘，为它们生成新棋盘。

In the future we are interested in expanding the approach to larger, more complex games that use more of the TRRBT language, or other other existing languages such as Ludii or PuzzleScript; also developing approaches to generating levels based just on the game’s code without a provided starting level. By creating a level generator in the same language as the original game, there is the possibility of integrating the two and adding a runtime level generator back into the original game (perhaps as a language feature in a TRRBT transform node). Since the inverted programs are themselves games, it may be possible to play them to generate levels for the original game.

未来，我们希望把这一方法扩展到更大、更复杂的游戏，使其使用更多TRRBT语言功能，或Ludii、PuzzleScript等其他现有语言；也希望发展只依靠游戏代码、不需要给定起始关卡的关卡生成方法。由于关卡生成器使用与原游戏相同的语言，二者有可能整合，把运行时关卡生成器加入原游戏，例如作为TRRBT transform节点中的一种语言功能。由于反演程序本身也是游戏，也许还可以通过游玩这些反演程序，为原游戏生成关卡。

We would also like to perform a user study of game designers to see how useful this approach is to them. We are also interested in methods to verify inversion works for generating solvable levels theoretically rather than empirically. Finally, program inversion may be useful for generating other types of content.
我们也希望开展面向游戏设计者的用户研究，考察这一方法对他们有多大帮助。此外，我们还对验证反演能够生成可解关卡的理论方法感兴趣，而不只是进行经验验证。最后，程序反演也可能有助于生成其他类型的内容。

论文利用游戏自身的源程序和一个棋盘，通过反演图块重写规则，从已解状态生成新的可解起始关卡。作者限定了所支持的行为树结构，在Peg Solitaire、Merge、Sokoban与TwoDoor四种游戏中枚举并核查关卡，再与正向枚举比较。论文同时保留这一方法对语言与棋盘结构的限制，并把更复杂游戏、设计者研究和理论正确性证明列为未来方向。 原文由Harper Noteboom, Kalyani Nair, Seth Cooper署名，载于CEUR Workshop Proceedings《CEUR工作坊论文集》第4090卷。原文依CC BY 4.0许可使用；本页汉译与排版转换属于对原作的改编，原作者署名、版权及原许可保留。

text: THE TOYS TO HAVE
应备的玩具

The jolliest indoor games for boys and girls demand a floor, and the home that has no floor upon which games may be played falls so far short of happiness. It must be a floor covered with linoleum or cork carpet, so that toy soldiers and such-like will stand up upon it, and of a color and surface that will take and show chalk marks; the common green-colored cork carpet without a pattern is the best of all. It must be no highway to other rooms, and well lit and airy. Occasionally, alas! it must be scrubbed—and then a truce to Floor Games. Upon such a floor may be made an infinitude of imaginative games, not only keeping boys and girls happy for days together, but building up a framework of spacious and inspiring ideas in them for after life. The men of to-morrow will gain new strength from nursery floors. I am going to tell of some of these games and what is most needed to play them; I have tried them all and a score of others like them with my sons, and all of the games here illustrated have been set out by us. I am going to tell of them here because I think what we have done will interest other fathers and mothers, and perhaps be of use to them (and to uncles and such-like tributary subspecies of humanity) in buying presents for their own and other people's children.

男孩女孩们玩得最开心的室内游戏，都少不了一块地板；家里若没有可供游戏的地板，幸福也就大打折扣。这块地板须铺上油毡或软木地毯，让玩具兵之类的东西站得稳；它的颜色和表面，还得容得下粉笔的印迹，并使它们显现出来。最普通的绿色软木地毯，不带任何花纹，就是最好的选择。这里不能是通往其他房间的必经之路，还要光线充足、空气流通。唉，偶尔它总得擦洗一下——地板游戏便只好暂时停战。在这样的地板上，可以开展无穷无尽的想象游戏；它们不但让男孩女孩们一连几天快快乐乐，还为他们日后的生活搭起一个宽广而富于启发的观念框架。明日的人们，将从儿童房的地板上获得新的力量。我准备讲讲其中的一些游戏，以及玩这些游戏时最需要的东西。我和儿子们试过这里的每一种游戏，还试过二十来种同类游戏；本书图示的各个场景，也都由我们亲手布置。我之所以要在这里讲述，是因为我觉得，我们做过的事情会使别的父母感兴趣；当他们为自己的孩子或别人的孩子买礼物时，或许也能派上用场——对叔叔舅舅这类人类的附属亚种，也一样。

Now, the toys we play with time after time, and in a thousand permutations and combinations, belong to four main groups. We have (1) Soldiers, and with these I class sailors, railway porters, civilians, and the lower animals generally, such as I will presently describe in greater detail; (2) Bricks; (3) Boards and Planks; and (4) a lot of Clockwork Railway Rolling-Stock and Rails. Also there are certain minor objects—tin ships, Easter eggs, and the like—of which I shall make incidental mention, that like the kiwi and the duck-billed platypus refuse to be classified.
说起来，那些让我们一玩再玩、做出上千种排列组合的玩具，可以分成四大类。我们有：（1）玩具兵；水兵、铁路搬运工、平民，以及通常所谓的低等动物，我也都归在这一类，稍后还要说得更细些；（2）积木；（3）木板和木条；（4）一大批发条铁路的车辆和轨道。此外还有若干小东西，譬如铁皮船、复活节彩蛋之类，我会顺便提到。它们就像几维鸟和鸭嘴兽，偏偏不肯归入任何一类。

These we arrange and rearrange in various ways upon our floor, making a world of them. In doing so we have found out all sorts of pleasant facts, and also many undesirable possibilities; and very probably our experience will help a reader here and there to the former and save him from the latter.
我们在地板上用种种办法把它们摆了又摆，组成一个世界。这样做，让我们发现了各式各样令人愉快的事情，也发现了不少不大可取的可能性。我们的经验，很可能帮助这里的一些读者享受到前者，同时免去后者的麻烦。

For instance, our planks and boards, and what one can do with them, have been a great discovery. Lots of boys and girls seem to be quite without planks and boards at all, and there is no regular trade in them. The toyshops, we found, did not keep anything of the kind we wanted, and our boards, which we had to get made by a carpenter, are the basis of half the games we play. The planks and boards we have are of various sizes. We began with three of two yards by one; they were made with cross pieces like small doors; but these we found unnecessarily large, and we would not get them now after our present experience. The best thickness, we think, is an inch for the larger sizes and three-quarters and a half inch for the smaller; and the best sizes are a yard square, thirty inches square, two feet, and eighteen inches square—one or two of each, and a greater number of smaller ones, 18 × 9, 9 × 9, and 9 × 4½. With the larger ones we make islands and archipelagos on our floor while the floor is a sea, or we make a large island or a couple on the Venice pattern, or we pile the smaller on the larger to make hills when the floor is a level plain, or they roof in railway stations or serve as bridges, in such manner as I will presently illustrate. And these boards of ours pass into our next most important possession, which is our box of bricks.

比如说，我们的木条和木板，以及用它们能够做的事情，就是一项大发现。许多男孩女孩似乎根本没有木条和木板，也似乎没有专门经营它们的生意。我们发现，玩具店里没有我们想要的这类东西。那些不得不请木匠专门做的木板，却成了我们一半游戏的根基。我们的木条和木板有各种尺寸。最初买了三块，长两码、宽一码，装着横档，活像几扇小门；后来却发现，它们大得没有必要。有了如今的经验，我们不会再买那样的板子了。我们觉得，较大的板子以一英寸厚为最好，较小的则用四分之三英寸和半英寸两种厚度；大小则以一码见方、三十英寸见方、两英尺见方和十八英寸见方为好——每种一两块，另备更多小块，尺寸为18×9、9×9、9×4½英寸。地板当海时，我们就用大木板做出岛屿和群岛；也可以照威尼斯的样子，做成一座大岛或相连的两座岛。地板当平原时，就把小板叠在大板上，造出山丘。它们还可以给火车站做屋顶，或者搭成桥梁；这些用法，我马上会配图说明。谈完木板，自然就接到我们下一件最重要的家当：一箱积木。

(But I was nearly forgetting to tell this, that all the thicker and larger of these boards have holes bored through them. At about every four inches is a hole, a little larger than an ordinary gimlet hole. These holes have their uses, as I will tell later, but now let me get on to the box of bricks.)
（不过我差点忘记说，所有较厚、较大的木板上都钻了孔。大约每隔四英寸便有一孔，比普通手钻钻出的孔稍大些。这些孔自有用途，稍后我会讲到；眼下还是先接着说那箱积木。）

This, again, wasn't a toyshop acquisition. It came to us by gift from two generous friends, unhappily growing up and very tall at that; and they had it from parents who were one of several families who shared in the benefit of a Good Uncle. I know nothing certainly of this man except that he was a Radford of Plymouth. I have never learned nor cared to learn of his commoner occupations, but certainly he was one of those shining and distinguished uncles that tower up at times above the common levels of humanity. At times, when we consider our derived and undeserved share of his inheritance and count the joys it gives us, we have projected half in jest and half in earnest the putting together of a little exemplary book upon the subject of such exceptional men: Celebrated Uncles, it should be called; and it should stir up all who read it to some striving at least towards the glories of the avuncular crown. What this great benefactor did was to engage a deserving unemployed carpenter through an entire winter making big boxes of wooden bricks for the almost innumerable nephews and nieces with which an appreciative circle of brothers and sisters had blessed him. There are whole bricks 4½ inches × 2¼ × 1⅛; there are half bricks 2¼ × 2¼ × 1⅛; and there are quarters—called by those previous owners (who have now ascended to, we hope but scarcely believe, a happier life near the ceiling) "piggys." You note how these sizes fit into the sizes of our boards, and of each size—we have never counted them, but we must have hundreds. We can pave a dozen square yards of floor with them.

这同样不是从玩具店买来的。它是两位慷慨的朋友送给我们的；可惜他们已长大，个子还长得很高。他们又是从父母那里得到的，而他们父母的一家，则是蒙一位“好叔叔”施惠的几个家庭之一。关于这位先生，我只确知他是普利茅斯Radford家族的一员。我从未打听、也不在意他平日里做些什么；但他无疑属于那种光彩夺目、卓尔不群的叔叔——这样的人，偶尔会在人类的平常水准之上高高耸起。有时，我们想到辗转继承来、本不配享有的这份遗产，细数它带给我们的欢乐，便半开玩笑、半当真地筹划，要为这些非凡人物编一本可作榜样的小书，题名就叫《著名的叔叔们》。它该使每一个读到它的人，至少也努力向那顶叔辈桂冠的荣光靠近一些。这位大恩人做过的事，是雇用一名值得帮助的失业木匠，让他用整整一个冬天，为几乎数不清的侄儿侄女制作一大箱一大箱的木积木；这些孩子，正是他那一圈心怀感激的兄弟姐妹赐给他的。整块积木的尺寸是4½×2¼×1⅛英寸；半块是2¼×2¼×1⅛英寸；还有四分之一块。先前的主人把后者叫做“小猪”——那些主人如今已经长到更靠近天花板的地方，过起一种但愿更幸福的生活，虽然我们希望如此，却很难真心相信。你会发现，这些尺寸恰好与我们木板的尺寸相配。每一种我们都有好几百块吧，虽然从未真正数过。它们足以在地板上铺满十二平方码。

How utterly we despise the silly little bricks of the toy-shops! They are too small to make a decent home for even the poorest lead soldiers, even if there were hundreds of them, and there are never enough, never nearly enough; even if you take one at a time and lay it down and say, "This is a house," even then there are not enough. We see rich people, rich people out of motor cars, rich people beyond the dreams of avarice, going into toyshops and buying these skimpy, sickly, ridiculous pseudo-boxes of bricklets, because they do not know what to ask for, and the toyshops are just the merciless mercenary enemies of youth and happiness—so far, that is, as bricks are concerned. Their unfortunate under-parented offspring mess about with these gifts, and don't make very much of them, and put them away; and you see their consequences in after life in the weakly-conceived villas and silly suburbs that people have built all round big cities. Such poor under-nourished nurseries must needs fall back upon the Encyclopædia Britannica, and even that is becoming flexible on India paper! But our box of bricks almost satisfies. With our box of bricks we can scheme and build, all three of us, for the best part of the hour, and still have more bricks in the box.

我们多么看不起玩具店里那些愚蠢的小积木！它们太小，就算有好几百块，也不足以给最穷的铅制玩具兵盖一所像样的房子。何况数量从来不够，远远不够；即便你一次拿一块放下，说“这算是一所房子”，它们也还是不够。我们看见有钱人，从汽车里走下来的有钱人，富得连贪心鬼都做梦也想不到的有钱人，走进玩具店，买下那些少得可怜、病恹恹、可笑得简直配不上积木箱之名的小木块盒子，只因为他们不知道该要什么。至于玩具店，就积木而言，实在是青春和幸福那毫不留情、唯利是图的敌人。他们那些可怜的、没得到父母得当照顾的孩子，拿着礼物胡乱摆弄一番，没弄出什么名堂，便收了起来。你会在日后的生活中看到这种后果：大城市四周，那些构想软弱的别墅和傻乎乎的郊区，就是人们这样造出来的。如此可怜、养料不足的儿童房，不免只好求助于《大英百科全书》；可是连它如今也用印度纸印得软绵绵了！不过，我们这箱积木已差不多令人满意。我们三个人可以一起设计、搭建上大半个钟头，箱子里还留着更多积木。

So much now for the bricks. I will tell later how we use cartridge paper and cardboard and other things to help in our building, and of the decorative use we make of plasticine. Of course, it goes without saying that we despise those foolish, expensive, made-up wooden and pasteboard castles that are sold in shops—playing with them is like playing with somebody else's dead game in a state of rigor mortis. Let me now say a little about toy soldiers and the world to which they belong. Toy soldiers used to be flat, small creatures in my own boyhood, in comparison with the magnificent beings one can buy to-day. There has been an enormous improvement in our national physique in this respect. Now they stand nearly two inches high and look you broadly in the face, and they have the movable arms and alert intelligence of scientifically exercised men. You get five of them mounted or nine afoot in a box for a small price. We three like those of British manufacture best; other makes are of incompatible sizes, and we have a rule that saves much trouble, that all red coats belong to G. P. W., and all other colored coats to F. R. W., all gifts, bequests, and accidents notwithstanding. Also we have sailors; but, since there are no red-coated sailors, blue counts as red.

积木先说到这里。稍后我会讲，我们怎样用厚绘图纸、纸板和其他东西辅助搭建，又怎样发挥橡皮泥的装饰作用。不言而喻，我们也瞧不起商店里出售的那些愚蠢、昂贵、事先搭好的木头或硬纸板城堡——玩那些东西，就像在玩别人已经死去、陷入尸僵的游戏。现在，再说说玩具兵和它们所属的世界吧。与今天可以买到的那些气派家伙相比，我小时候的玩具兵又扁又小。从这个角度看，我们国民的体格实在有了巨大的进步。如今它们高近两英寸，大大方方地正视着你；手臂可以活动，神气机敏，就像受过科学锻炼的人。一盒五个骑兵或九个步兵，花不多的钱便买得到。我们三个人最喜欢英国制造的；别处制造的尺寸不相配。我们还有一条省掉许多麻烦的规矩：红制服一概归G. P. W.，其他颜色的制服一概归F. R. W.，不论礼物、遗赠或偶然情况如何，都是如此。我们也有水兵；不过水兵没有穿红制服的，所以蓝色就算红色。
[图中文字：ENCYCLOPÆDIA／BRITANNICA]
[图内译释：《大英百科全书》]
[图中文字：MADE／IN／GERMANY；ENGLISH／MAKE]
[图内译释：德国制造；英国制造]

Then we have "beefeaters," [1 The warders in the Tower of London are called "beefeaters"; the origin of the term is obscure.] Indians, Zulus, for whom there are special rules. We find we can buy lead dogs, cats, lions, tigers, horses, camels, cattle, and elephants of a reasonably corresponding size, and we have also several boxes of railway porters, and some soldiers we bought in Hesse-Darmstadt that we pass off on an unsuspecting home world as policemen. But we want civilians very badly. We found a box of German civilians once in a shop, the right size but rather heavy, and running to nearly five cents apiece (which is too dear), gentlemen in tweed suits carrying bags, a top-hatted gentleman, ladies in gray and white, two children, and a dog, and so on, but we have never been able to find any more. They do not seem to be made at all—will toy manufacturers please note? I write now as if I were Consul-General in Toyland, noting new opportunities for trade. Consequent upon this dearth, our little world suffers from an exaggerated curse of militarism, and even the grocer wears epaulettes. This might please Lord Roberts and Mr. Leo Maxse, but it certainly does not please us. I wish, indeed, that we could buy boxes of tradesmen: a blue butcher, a white baker with a loaf of standard bread, a merchant or so; boxes of servants, boxes of street traffic, smart sets, and so forth. We could do with a judge and lawyers, or a box of vestrymen. It is true that we can buy Salvation Army lasses and football players, but we are cold to both of these. We have, of course, boy scouts. With such boxes of civilians we could have much more fun than with the running, marching, swashbuckling soldiery that pervades us. They drive us to reviews; and it is only emperors, kings, and very silly small boys who can take an undying interest in uniforms and reviews.

此外，我们还有“食牛肉者”[1 伦敦塔的守卫被称为“食牛肉者”；这一称呼的由来不明。]、印第安人和祖鲁人，它们另有特别的规则。我们发现，铅制的狗、猫、狮子、老虎、马、骆驼、牛和大象，也可以买到大小大致相称的。我们还有几盒铁路搬运工，以及在黑森-达姆施塔特买的一些玩具兵；在家里这个毫无戒心的世界中，我们就把后者冒充警察。不过，我们极缺平民。有一次，我们在一家商店里找到过一盒德国平民，大小合适，只是略重，每个又要将近五美分，太贵了。有穿粗花呢衣服、提着包的先生，戴高顶礼帽的先生，穿灰衣服或白衣服的女士，两个孩子，一条狗，等等；可我们再也没找到过更多。它们似乎压根就没人生产——请玩具制造商们留意一下，好吗？我现在写着写着，仿佛成了玩具国的总领事，正在记录新的贸易机会。由于这种匮乏，我们的小世界蒙受着一种过分严重的军国主义诅咒，连杂货商都戴着肩章。罗伯茨勋爵和Leo Maxse先生也许会喜欢这一点，可我们实在不喜欢。我真希望能买到一盒盒手艺人和店主：穿蓝衣的肉贩，穿白衣、拿着一条标准面包的面包师，再有一两个商人；还有一盒盒仆人、一盒盒街头行人车辆、时髦人士，等等。来一位法官和一些律师，或者一盒教区理事，我们也用得上。确实，救世军的姑娘和足球运动员是买得到的，可我们对这两种都不感兴趣。当然，我们也有童子军。如果有这样的一盒盒平民，我们能够得到的乐趣，会比那些到处都是、跑步行军、舞刀弄枪的兵士多得多。它们逼得我们只好举行阅兵；而对制服和阅兵能够永远兴致不减的，也只有皇帝、国王，以及非常愚蠢的小男孩。
[图中文字：TEA；JAM；JA…；TRY ·／OUR／HAM／NOW ·；DOG／BISCUIT；POTATOE…]
[图内译释：茶；果酱；另一罐标签仅局部可见，不补写遮挡字母；现在尝尝我们的火腿；狗饼干；马铃薯]

And lastly, of our railways, let me merely remark here that we have always insisted upon one uniform gauge and everything we buy fits into and develops our existing railway system. Nothing is more indicative of the wambling sort of parent and a coterie of witless, worthless uncles than a heap of railway toys of different gauges and natures in the children's playroom.
最后，再说我们的铁路。我在这里只提醒一句：我们始终坚持统一轨距，买来的每一样东西，都要能接入我们已有的铁路系统，并使它发展。儿童游戏室里，一堆轨距不同、式样不一的铁路玩具，最能说明父母办事漫无章法，周围还围着一群没头脑、不中用的叔叔舅舅。

And so, having told you of the material we have, let me now tell you of one or two games (out of the innumerable many) that we have played. Of course, in this I have to be a little artificial. Actual games of the kind I am illustrating here have been played by us, many and many a time, with joy and happy invention and no thought of publication. They have gone now, those games, into that vaguely luminous and iridescent world of memories into which all love-engendering happiness must go. But we have tried our best to set them out again and recall the good points in them here.
既然已经交代了我们手头的材料，现在就讲讲我们玩过的一两个游戏吧——它们只是无数游戏中的几个。当然，在这里，我不得不稍稍作一点人为的安排。本书图示的这类游戏，我们其实已玩过许多许多回，充满欢乐和快乐的发明，从未想到要把它们发表出来。如今那些游戏早已过去，进入了朦胧发亮、流光溢彩的记忆世界；一切唤起爱的幸福，终究都要到那里去。不过，我们还是尽力重新摆出它们，在这里追忆其中的妙处。

text: THE GAME OF THE WONDERFUL ISLANDS
奇妙群岛的游戏

In this game the floor is the sea. Half—rather the larger half because of some instinctive right of primogeniture—is assigned to the elder of my two sons (he is, as it were, its Olympian), and the other half goes to his brother. We distribute our boards about the sea in an archipelagic manner. We then dress our islands, objecting strongly to too close a scrutiny of our proceedings until we have done. Here, in the illustration, is such an archipelago ready for its explorers, or rather on the verge of exploration. There are altogether four islands, two to the reader's right and two to the left, and the nearer ones are the more northerly; it is as many as we could get into the camera. The northern island to the right is most advanced in civilization, and is chiefly temple. That temple has a flat roof, diversified by domes made of half Easter eggs and cardboard cones. These are surmounted by decorative work of a flamboyant character in plasticine, designed by G. P. W. An oriental population crowds the courtyard and pours out upon the roadway. Note the grotesque plasticine monsters who guard the portals, also by G. P. W., who had a free hand with the architecture of this remarkable specimen of eastern religiosity. They are nothing, you may be sure, to the gigantic idols inside, out of the reach of the sacrilegious camera. To the right is a tropical thatched hut. The thatched roof is really that nice ribbed paper that comes round bottles—a priceless boon to these games. All that comes into the house is saved for us. The owner of the hut lounges outside the door. He is a dismounted cavalry-corps man, and he owns one cow. His fence, I may note, belonged to a little wooden farm we bought in Switzerland. Its human inhabitants are scattered; its beasts follow a precarious living as wild guinea-pigs on the islands to the south.

在这个游戏里，地板就是大海。其中一半分给我的长子——凭着某种本能的长子继承权，这一半还要稍大些；他仿佛就是这片海域的奥林匹斯神。另一半则归他的弟弟。我们把木板分散放在海上，摆成群岛的样子。然后，各自装点自己的岛屿；没有做完以前，若有人凑得太近来细看我们的制作，我们是大不乐意的。图上就是这样一片等待探险者到来的群岛，或者说，探险正要开始。岛共有四个，读者的右手边两个、左手边两个；靠近读者的两个，位置也较偏北。照相机所能容纳的，最多就是这些岛。右侧北边那座岛的文明最为发达，主要由一座神庙构成。神庙的屋顶是平的，上面用半个复活节彩蛋和纸板圆锥做成圆顶，使它有些变化。圆顶上又装着G. P. W.设计的华丽橡皮泥装饰。东方的居民挤满庭院，又涌到道路上。请看守在门口的那些怪诞橡皮泥怪兽，也出自G. P. W.之手；这座非凡的东方宗教建筑，完全放手由他来设计。你尽可相信，与里面那些巨大的神像相比，它们还算不了什么；那些神像，在这架亵渎神圣的照相机拍不到的地方。右边是一间热带茅草屋。那茅草屋顶，其实就是包在瓶子外面、带着楞纹的好纸——对于这些游戏，它可是无价之宝。凡是进了家门的这种纸，全都替我们留着。屋主正懒洋洋地待在门外。他原是个下了马的骑兵，养着一头牛。顺带说，他的篱笆来自我们在瑞士买过的一座小木农场。农场的人类居民如今已经四散；它的动物们，则到南边的岛上，当起生活不安稳的野豚鼠来。
[图中文字：TANDSTICOR／SAFETY]
[图内译释：火柴／安全]
[图中文字：TO THE FARM]
[图内译释：往农场]

Your attention is particularly directed to the trees about and behind the temple, which thicken to a forest on the further island to the right. These trees we make of twigs taken from trees and bushes in the garden, and stuck into holes in our boards. Formerly we lived in a house with a little wood close by, and our forests were wonderful. Now we are restricted to our garden, and we could get nothing for this set out but jasmine and pear. Both have wilted a little, and are not nearly such spirited trees as you can make out of fir trees, for instance. It is for these woods chiefly that we have our planks perforated with little holes. No tin trees can ever be so plausible and various and jolly as these. With a good garden to draw upon one can make terrific sombre woods, and then lie down and look through them at lonely horsemen or wandering beasts.

尤其请注意神庙四周和后面的树木：到了右侧较远的那座岛上，它们便密集成了森林。这些树，是我们从花园的树木和灌丛上取来枝条，插进木板上的孔里做成的。从前我们住的房子附近有一小片树林，那时我们的森林可真好。如今只能从自家花园取材，这次布置，能找到的也只有素馨枝和梨树枝。两种枝条都已有些萎蔫，远不如用冷杉之类的树木做出来的那样有精神。我们在木板上钻小孔，主要就是为了这些树林。任何铁皮树，都不可能像它们这样逼真、多变而有趣。有一座好花园可供取材，就能造出幽暗得惊人的树林；再趴到地板上，透过树林，去看那些孤独的骑手或四处游荡的野兽。
[图中文字：BEWARE／OF · WILD／CAMELS／ETC ·]
[图内译释：当心野骆驼等（图中为玩具象，照录图中文字）]

That further island on the right is a less settled country than the island of the temple. Camels, you note, run wild there; there is a sort of dwarf elephant, similar to the now extinct kind of which one finds skeletons in Malta, pigs, a red parrot, and other such creatures, of lead and wood. The pear-trees are fine. It is those which have attracted white settlers (I suppose they are), whose thatched huts are to be seen both upon the beach and inland. By the huts on the beach lie a number of pear-tree logs; but a raid of negroid savages from the adjacent island to the left is in progress, and the only settler clearly visible is the man in a rifleman's uniform running inland for help. Beyond, peeping out among the trees, are the supports he seeks.

右侧较远的那座岛，比神庙岛更少有人定居。你看，骆驼在那里野生野长；还有一种侏儒象，像马耳他发现过骨架的那种已经灭绝的小象。此外还有猪、一只红鹦鹉，以及其他铅制或木制的同类生物。那些梨树长得很好。正是它们招来了白人移民——我想，那些人应该是白人吧——他们的茅草屋，在海滩上和内陆都看得见。海滩边的屋子旁，放着一些梨树原木；但左侧邻岛的黑种野蛮人正在发动袭击，惟一看得分明的移民，是那个穿着步枪兵制服、正往内陆奔去求援的人。他所寻找的援兵，就在更远的树林间隐约露出身影。

These same negroid savages are as bold as they are ferocious. They cross arms of the sea upon their rude canoes, made simply of a strip of cardboard. Their own island, the one to the south-left, is a rocky wilderness containing caves. Their chief food is the wild-goat, but in pursuit of these creatures you will also sometimes find the brown bear, who sits—he is small but perceptible to the careful student—in the mouth of his cave. Here, too, you will distinguish small guinea-pig-like creatures of wood, in happier days the inhabitants of that Swiss farm. Sunken rocks off this island are indicated by a white foam which takes the form of letters, and you will also note a whirlpool between the two islands to the right.

这些黑种野蛮人既凶猛，又大胆。他们用简陋的独木舟横渡海汊；说是独木舟，其实不过是一条纸板。他们自己的岛，也就是左边偏南的那座，是一片有洞穴的荒凉岩地。他们的主食是野山羊；不过，追寻这些动物时，你有时也会找到棕熊。它正坐在洞口——个子虽小，仔细观察还是看得见的。在这里，你也能辨认出那些像小豚鼠的木制动物；在更幸福的往日，它们还住在那座瑞士小农场里。岛外的暗礁，用白色泡沫标出；这泡沫恰好长成字母的形状。你还会注意到，右边两个岛之间有一道旋涡。
[图中文字：CHOCOLATE]
[图内译释：巧克力]
[图中文字：SUNKEN／ROCKS；WHIRLPOOL／NO SHIP ESCAPES]
[图内译释：水下礁石；漩涡／船只无一能脱逃]
A view showing the raid of the Negroid savages upon the white settlers of Pear Tree Island
黑种野蛮人袭击梨树岛白人移民的一景。

Finally comes the island nearest to the reader on the left. This also is wild and rocky, inhabited not by negroid blacks, but by Indians, whose tents, made by F. R. W. out of ordinary brown paper and adorned with chalk totems of a rude and characteristic kind, pour forth their fierce and well-armed inhabitants at the intimation of an invader. The rocks on this island, let me remark, have great mineral wealth. Among them are to be found not only sheets and veins of silver paper, but great nuggets of metal, obtained by the melting down of hopelessly broken soldiers in an iron spoon. Note, too, the peculiar and romantic shell beach of this country. It is an island of exceptional interest to the geologist and scientific explorer. The Indians, you observe, have domesticated one leaden and one wooden cow.

最后是左边最靠近读者的那座岛。这里也荒凉、多岩石，不过，住的不是黑种人，而是印第安人。他们的帐篷，是F. R. W.用普通牛皮纸做的，上面用粉笔画着粗朴而别具特色的图腾。只消传来入侵者的风声，凶悍而武装齐全的居民就会从帐篷里涌出。顺便说，这座岛的岩石蕴藏着丰富的矿产：不但能找到成片的银色箔纸和银箔矿脉，还有一大块一大块的金属矿块；它们是把损坏得无法挽救的玩具兵放在铁勺里熔化得来的。也请留意这个国家奇特而浪漫的贝壳海滩。对地质学家和科学探险者而言，这是一座格外有趣的岛。你看，印第安人已经驯养了一头铅牛和一头木牛。
[图中文字：ANY PERSON／WORRYING THIS／LION WILL／BE SCALPED.]
[图内译释：任何逗扰这只狮子的人都将被剥头皮。]

This is how the game would be set out. Then we build ships and explore these islands, but in these pictures the ships are represented as already arriving. The ships are built out of our wooden bricks on flat keels made of two wooden pieces of 9 x 4½ inches, which are very convenient to push about over the floor. Captain G. P. W. is steaming into the bay between the eastern and western islands. He carries heavy guns, his ship bristles with an extremely aggressive soldiery, who appear to be blazing away for the mere love of the thing. (I suspect him of Imperialist intentions.) Captain F. R. W. is apparently at anchor between his northern and southern islands. His ship is of a slightly more pacific type. I note on his deck a lady and a gentleman (of German origin) with a bag, two of our all too rare civilians. No doubt the bag contains samples and a small conversation dictionary in the negroid dialects. (I think F. R. W. may turn out to be a Liberal.) Perhaps he will sail on and rescue the raided huts, perhaps he will land and build a jetty, and begin mining among the rocks to fill his hold with silver. Perhaps the natives will kill and eat the gentleman with the bag. All that is for Captain F. R. W. to decide.

游戏的场景就是这样布置的。接下来，我们造船，探索这些岛屿；不过，在这些照片里，船已被摆成正在到达的样子。船用我们的木积木搭建，平底龙骨则由两块9×4½英寸的木片做成，在地板上推来推去十分方便。G. P. W.船长正驾着汽船，驶入东、西岛屿之间的海湾。他载着重炮，船上到处站着极富侵略性的兵士；他们似乎只是为了开火本身的乐趣，就不停地开火。（我怀疑他有帝国主义的企图。）F. R. W.船长则似乎正在自己的南北两岛之间停泊。他的船，属于稍稍和平一些的类型。我注意到，他的甲板上有一位女士和一位提包的先生（德国来的），是我们那些少得可怜的平民中的两位。不消说，包里装着货样和一本黑种人方言的小会话词典。（我觉得F. R. W.将来或许会成为一位自由党人。）也许他会继续航行，去解救那些遭到袭击的小屋；也许他会登陆，搭起码头，在岩石间开矿，用银子装满货舱。也许土著会杀掉并吃掉那位提包的先生。这些，全由F. R. W.船长自己决定。
[图内译释：舰上小牌字迹模糊，无法可靠辨读。]

You see how the game goes on. We land and alter things, and build and rearrange, and hoist paper flags on pins, and subjugate populations, and confer all the blessings of civilization upon these lands. We keep them going for days. And at last, as we begin to tire of them, comes the scrubbing brush, and we must burn our trees and dismantle our islands, and put our soldiers in the little nests of drawers, and stand the island boards up against the wall, and put everything away. Then perhaps, after a few days, we begin upon some other such game, just as we feel disposed. But it is never quite the same game, never. Another time it may be wildernesses for example, and the boards are hills, and never a drop of water is to be found except for the lakes and rivers we may mark out in chalk. But after one example others are easy, and next I will tell you of our way of making towns.

你看，游戏就是这样进行下去的。我们登陆，改变事物，搭建，重新布置，把纸旗升上大头针，征服居民，将文明的一切福祉赐给这些土地。我们让这些活动持续好几天。最后，等我们开始玩腻了，刷地板的刷子便到来了；我们只得烧掉我们的树，拆散岛屿，把玩具兵放回一个个小抽屉，把岛屿木板靠墙竖起，将一切收好。也许过了几天，我们就又随心所欲，开始另一场同类游戏。但它从来不会是完全相同的游戏，从来不会。例如，下次也许是一片荒野，木板就是山丘；除了用粉笔画出的湖泊和河流，再也找不到一滴水。不过，有了一个例子，其他玩法便容易想出来。接着，我就讲讲我们怎样建造城镇。
[图中文字：VOTES／FOR／WOM／EN；24 A／PENY]
[图内译释：妇女选举权；一便士24个]

text: OF THE BUILDING OF CITIES
论城市的建造
[图中文字：BLUE END；BOUNDARY／LINE]
[图内译释：蓝端；边界线]

We always build twin cities, like London and Westminster, or Buda-Pesth, because two of us always want, both of them, to be mayors and municipal councils, and it makes for local freedom and happiness to arrange it so; but when steam railways or street railways are involved we have our rails in common, and we have an excellent law that rails must be laid down and switches kept open in such a manner that anyone feeling so disposed may send a through train from their own station back to their own station again without needless negotiation or the personal invasion of anybody else's administrative area. It is an undesirable thing to have other people bulging over one's houses, standing in one's open spaces, and, in extreme cases, knocking down and even treading on one's citizens. It leads at times to explanations that are afterwards regretted.

我们总是建造一对双子城，像伦敦与威斯敏斯特，或布达与佩斯，因为我们中间总有两个人，个个都想当市长，又兼任整个市议会；这样安排有助于地方的自由与幸福。不过，凡是涉及蒸汽铁路或有轨电车，我们的轨道就共同使用。我们还有一条极好的法律：铺设轨道与开放道岔时，必须保证任何有此兴致的人，都能让一列直通列车从自己的车站出发，再回到自己的车站，不必进行多余的交涉，也不必亲自侵入别人管辖的区域。让别人整个身子探在自己的房屋上面，站在自己的空地上，严重时还撞倒、甚至踩着自己的市民，这都是令人不快的事。有时会因此说出一些事后懊悔的话。
[图中文字：CROSS BY／BRIDGE／ONLY · · ·]
[图内译释：只能由桥通行……]
[图中文字：VOTE FOR／ME；POLLING／BOOTH]
[图内译释：投我一票；投票站]

We always have twin cities, or at the utmost stage of coalescence a city with two wards, Red End and Blue End; we mark the boundaries very carefully, and our citizens have so much local patriotism (Mr. Chesterton will learn with pleasure) that they stray but rarely over that thin little streak of white that bounds their municipal allegiance. Sometimes we have an election for mayor; it is like a census but very abusive, and Red always wins. Only citizens with two legs and at least one arm and capable of standing up may vote, and voters may poll on horseback; boy scouts and women and children do not vote, though there is a vigorous agitation to remove these disabilities. Zulus and foreign-looking persons, such as East Indian cavalry and American Indians, are also disfranchised. So are riderless horses and camels; but the elephant has never attempted to vote on any occasion, and does not seem to desire the privilege. It influences public opinion quite sufficiently as it is by nodding its head.

我们总有一对双子城，最多合并成一座分为红端与蓝端两区的城市。我们把界线划得十分仔细；我们的市民又有那么强的地方爱国心（切斯特顿先生听了一定高兴），很少越过那条划定他们效忠哪个市政当局的细细白线。有时我们举行市长选举；这有点像人口普查，只是充斥着谩骂，而且总是红方获胜。只有具备两条腿和至少一条胳膊、能够站立的市民才有选举权，投票人可以骑在马上投票。童子军、妇女和儿童都没有选举权，尽管争取取消这些资格限制的运动正进行得轰轰烈烈。祖鲁人，以及东印度骑兵、美洲印第安人这类外貌像外国人的人，也被剥夺了选举权。没有骑手的马和骆驼同样如此。不过，大象从未试图在任何一次选举中投票，似乎也不想获得这种特权。它只须点一点头，就已经足够影响舆论了。

We have set out and I have photographed one of our cities to illustrate more clearly the amusement of the game. Red End is to the reader's right, and includes most of the hill on which the town stands, a shady zoological garden, the town hall, a railway tunnel through the hill, a museum (away in the extreme right-hand corner), a church, a rifle range, and a shop. Blue End has the railway station, four or five shops, several homes, a hotel, and a farm-house, close to the railway station. The boundary drawn by me as overlord (who also made the hills and tunnels and appointed the trees to grow) runs irregularly between the two shops nearest the cathedral, over the shoulder in front of the town hall, and between the farm and the rifle range.

我们布置好了一座城市，我又拍了照片，以便更清楚地说明这个游戏的乐趣。红端在读者的右手边，包括城市所在山丘的大部分、一座绿荫掩映的动物园、市政厅、一条穿山铁路隧道、一座博物馆（远在最右边的角落）、一座教堂、一处步枪靶场和一家商店。蓝端有火车站、四五家商店、几处住宅、一家旅馆，以及紧挨火车站的一座农舍。身为最高领主的我（山丘和隧道也由我建造，树木亦奉我的命令生长）划出的界线，从最靠近主教座堂的两家商店之间，越过市政厅前的山肩，再从农场和靶场之间曲曲折折地穿过。

The nature of the hills I have already explained, and this time we have had no lakes or ornamental water. These are very easily made out of a piece of glass—the glass lid of a box for example—laid upon silver paper. Such water becomes very readily populated by those celluloid seals and swans and ducks that are now so common. Paper fish appear below the surface and may be peered at by the curious. But on this occasion we have nothing of the kind, nor have we made use of a green-colored tablecloth we sometimes use to drape our hills. Of course, a large part of the fun of this game lies in the witty incorporation of all sorts of extraneous objects. But the incorporation must be witty, or you may soon convert the whole thing into an incoherent muddle of half-good ideas.

山丘是怎么回事，我已经解释过。这一回我们没有设置湖泊或观赏水景。这样的水面非常容易做，只要在银纸上铺一块玻璃——比如盒子的玻璃盖——就行。如今十分常见的赛璐珞海豹、天鹅和鸭子，很容易就使这种水面热闹起来。纸鱼在水面下游弋，好奇的人可以往里窥看。不过，这一次我们什么也没做，也没用那块有时拿来披在山上的绿色桌布。当然，这个游戏的很大一部分乐趣，在于把各色各样的外来物件巧妙地纳入其中。但这种纳入一定要巧妙，否则很快就会把整个东西弄成一团互不相干、半好不坏的点子。
[图中文字：HEAR!／HEAR!]
[图内译释：说得好！说得好！]
[图中文字：IT IS DANGEROUS／TO FEED THE／DUCKS WITH／LIGHTED／MATCHES!]
[图内译释：用点燃的火柴喂鸭子很危险！]

I have taken two photographs, one to the right and one to the left of this agreeable place. I may perhaps adopt a kind of guide-book style in reviewing its principal features: I begin at the railway station. I have made a rather nearer and larger photograph of the railway station, which presents a diversified and entertaining scene to the incoming visitor. Porters (out of a box of porters) career here and there with the trucks and light baggage. Quite a number of our all-too-rare civilians parade the platform: two gentlemen, a lady, and a small but evil-looking child are particularly noticeable; and there is a wooden sailor with jointed legs, in a state of intoxication as reprehensible as it is nowadays happily rare. Two virtuous dogs regard his abandon with quiet scorn. The seat on which he sprawls is a broken piece of some toy whose nature I have long forgotten, the station clock is a similar fragment, and so is the metallic pillar which bears the name of the station. So many toys, we find, only become serviceable with a little smashing. There is an allegory in this—as Hawthorne used to write in his diary.

我给这个宜人的地方拍了两张照片，一张拍右边，一张拍左边。介绍这里的主要特色时，我或许可以采用一种旅游指南的笔调：先从火车站说起。我另拍了一张火车站的近景大照片；初到此地的游客会看到一派丰富多彩、趣味盎然的景象。搬运工（来自一盒搬运工玩具）推着行李车、带着轻便行李四下奔走。我们那些总嫌太少的平民，也有好些正在站台上散步。其中尤其引人注目的，是两位绅士、一位女士，以及一个个头虽小、却一脸坏相的孩子。还有一个双腿带关节的木头水手，醉得不成样子；这样可耻的醉态，如今幸而已很少见了。两只品行端正的狗，安静而轻蔑地看着他这副放纵模样。他瘫坐的长椅，是某件玩具的断片，那玩具本来是什么，我早已忘记。车站的钟也是类似的残件，那根挂着站名的金属柱也一样。我们发现，好多玩具都得先砸坏一点才有用。这其中是有寓意的——霍桑从前在日记里就常这样写。
[图中文字：JABZ／HAIR／TONIC；G.P.W.；TICKETS／HERE；HUM]
[图内译释：JABZ生发水；G.P.W.；在此购票；HUM（帽带字样，不擅自展开船名）]
("What is he doing, the great god Pan, Down in the reeds by the river?")
（“伟大的潘神，他在做什么， 在河边的芦苇丛里？”）

The fences at the ends of the platforms are pieces of wood belonging to the game of Matador—that splendid and very educational construction game, hailing, I believe, from Hungary. There is also, I regret to say, a blatant advertisement of Jab's "Hair Color," showing the hair. (In the photograph the hair does not come out very plainly.) This is by G. P. W., who seems marked out by destiny to be the advertisement-writer of the next generation. He spends much of his scanty leisure inventing and drawing advertisements of imaginary commodities. Oblivious to many happy, beautiful, and noble things in life, he goes about studying and imitating the literature of the billboards. He and his brother write newspapers almost entirely devoted to these annoying appeals. You will note, too, the placard at the mouth of the railway tunnel urging the existence of Jinks' Soap upon the passing traveller. The oblong object on the placard represents, no doubt, a cake of this offensive and aggressive commodity. The zoological garden flaunts a placard, "Zoo, two cents pay," and the grocer's picture of a cabbage with "Get Them" is not to be ignored. F. R. W. is more like the London County Council in this respect, and prefers bare walls.

站台两端的围栏，是“Matador”游戏里的木制零件——那是一种出色而且非常有教育意义的建造游戏，我记得是从匈牙利来的。此外，很遗憾还得说，这里有一幅扎眼的Jab牌“染发剂”广告，上面画着头发。（照片里头发显得不太清楚。）这是G. P. W.的作品；他仿佛命中注定，要成为下一代的广告撰稿人。他把自己本已不多的闲暇，大半用来为想象中的商品编画广告。他对生活中许多快乐、美好和高尚的事物视而不见，却四处研究、模仿广告牌上的文辞。他和弟弟编的报纸，几乎全是这些恼人的招徕。你还会注意到铁路隧道口的招贴，正向过路旅客极力宣告Jinks肥皂的存在。招贴上的长方形物体，无疑代表一块这种惹人讨厌、咄咄逼人的商品。动物园招摇地挂着一块牌子：“动物园，入场付两美分。”杂货商画的一棵卷心菜，配上“快来买”的字样，也不容忽视。F. R. W.在这一点上更像伦敦郡议会，宁愿墙上光秃秃的。

The railway station at Blue End
蓝端的火车站

"Returning from the station," as the guide-books say, and "giving one more glance" at the passengers who are waiting for the privilege of going round the circle in open cars and returning in a prostrated condition to the station again, and "observing" what admirable platforms are made by our 9 by 4½ pieces, we pass out to the left into the village street. A motor omnibus (a one-horse hospital cart in less progressive days) stands waiting for passengers; and, on our way to the Cherry Tree Inn, we remark two nurses, one in charge of a child with a plasticine head. The landlord of the inn is a small grotesque figure of plaster; his sign is fastened on by a pin. No doubt the refreshment supplied here has an enviable reputation, to judge by the alacrity with which a number of riflemen move towards the door. The inn, by the by, like the station and some private houses, is roofed with stiff paper.

“从车站折返”——旅游指南会这样说——“再看一眼”那些等着获准乘坐敞车绕行一圈、最后筋疲力尽地回到车站的旅客，再“留意一下”我们九英寸乘四英寸半的木板能搭出多么出色的站台，我们便向左走出去，来到村街上。一辆机动公共汽车（在从前不那么进步的日子里，它是一辆单马拉的救护车）正停着等候乘客。在前往樱桃树旅店的路上，我们看到两位保姆，其中一位看管着一个脑袋是橡皮泥做的孩子。旅店老板是个模样古怪的小石膏人，招牌用一根大头针别着。看好几名步枪兵兴冲冲地奔向店门的样子，就知道这里供应的酒食一定名声远扬。顺便说一句，这家旅店同车站及某些私宅一样，都用硬纸作屋顶。
[图中文字：SCURSION ·／TRAIN]
[图内译释：游览列车]
[图中文字：INN]
[图内译释：客栈]

These stiff-paper roofs are one of our great inventions. We get thick, stiff paper and cut it to the sizes we need. After the game is over, we put these roofs inside one another and stick them into the bookshelves. The roof one folds and puts away will live to roof another day.
这些硬纸屋顶是我们的一大发明。找来厚而硬的纸，按所需尺寸裁剪即可。游戏结束后，我们把屋顶套叠在一起，插进书架。屋顶折好、收起，留得下回再来盖屋顶。
[图中文字：TRY／WODDY’S／HOME／MADE／HAMS]
[图内译释：尝尝Woddy自制的火腿]
[图中文字：JOKIL CO／SHOPMEN；BUY／OUR／GRAPES／BEWARE／OF／SUBSTIT／UTES；TEA；DON’T／LOSE／HEART／BUY／OUR／CABBA／GES]
[图内译释：JOKIL公司商人；购买我们的葡萄；谨防冒牌货；茶；不要灰心；购买我们的卷心菜]

Proceeding on our way past the Cherry Tree, and resisting the cosy invitation of its portals, we come to the shopping quarter of the town. The stock in the windows is made by hand out of plasticine. We note the meat and hams of "Mr. Woddy," the cabbages and carrots of "Tod & Brothers," the general activities of the "Jokil Co." shopmen. It is de rigueur with our shop assistants that they should wear white helmets. In the street, boy scouts go to and fro, a wagon clatters by; most of the adult population is about its business, and a red-coated band plays along the roadway. Contrast this animated scene with the mysteries of sea and forest, rock and whirlpool, in our previous game. Further on is the big church or cathedral.

我们继续赶路，经过樱桃树旅店，抵住门口那温馨的邀约，便来到城里的商业区。橱窗里的货品都是用橡皮泥手工捏成的。我们看到“Woddy先生”店里的肉和火腿、“Tod兄弟”店里的卷心菜和胡萝卜，以及“Jokil公司”店员们的各项忙碌。我们的店员一律须戴白色头盔。街上，童子军来来往往，一辆货车辘辘驶过；大多数成年居民都在忙自己的事，一支穿红外套的乐队沿街演奏。把这生气勃勃的景象，同前一个游戏里大海与森林、岩石与旋涡的神秘景象对照一下吧。再往前就是大教堂，或说主教座堂。
[图中文字：SILENCE；KEEP TO THE RIGHT；THE REST／OF THIS／ANIMAL／IS NOW／EXTINCT；DO NOT TOUCH；DO NOT TOUCH；ANTIENT／POT]
[图内译释：肃静；靠右行；这只动物的其余部分现已灭绝；请勿触摸（台座正面）；请勿触摸（台座侧面）；古代陶罐]

It is built in an extremely debased Gothic style; it reminds us most of a church we once surveyed during a brief visit to Rotterdam on our way up the Rhine. A solitary boy scout, mindful of the views of Lord Haldane, enters its high portal. Passing the cathedral, we continue to the museum. This museum is no empty boast; it contains mineral specimens, shells—such great shells as were found on the beaches of our previous game,—the Titanic skulls of extinct rabbits and cats, and other such wonders. The slender curious may lie down on the floor and peep in at the windows.

它采用一种退化得极厉害的哥特式风格，让我们最先想到的，是有一回沿莱茵河溯流而上、短暂停留鹿特丹时看过的一座教堂。一个落单的童子军，牢记Haldane勋爵的主张，走进那高高的门洞。经过主教座堂，我们继续前往博物馆。这座博物馆可不是空口吹嘘：里面有矿物标本、贝壳——就是前一个游戏的海滩上找到的那些巨型贝壳——还有已经灭绝的兔子和猫那硕大无比的头骨，以及诸如此类的奇物。身材纤细的好奇者，可以趴在地板上从窗口往里看。
[图中文字：THE／PLASTICINORUS ·；DO·NOT·TOUCH DO·NOT…]
[图内译释：橡皮泥兽（图中戏拟名称PLASTICINORUS）；勿触摸；勿……（句子沿台座延伸）]

"We now," says the guidebook, "retrace our steps to the shops, and then, turning to the left, ascend under the trees up the terraced hill on which stands the Town Hall. This magnificent building is surmounted by a colossal statue of a chamois, the work of a Wengen artist; it is in two stories, with a battlemented roof, and a crypt (entrance to right of steps) used for the incarceration of offenders. It is occupied by the town guard, who wear 'beefeater' costumes of ancient origin."
“现在，”旅游指南说，“我们原路返回商店，再向左转，沿着树下的小路，登上市政厅所在的梯状山丘。这座宏伟建筑的顶端，矗立着一尊巨大的岩羚像，是文根一位艺术家的作品。建筑共两层，屋顶设有雉堞，另有一间用来关押犯人的地下室（入口在台阶右侧）。驻守这里的城市卫队，身穿古老的‘食牛肉者’式服装。”
[图中文字：BLUE END／MINERAL]
[图内译释：蓝端矿物（展品标牌）]

Note the red parrot perched on the battlements; it lives tame in the zoölogical gardens, and is of the same species as one we formerly observed in our archipelago. Note, too, the brisk cat-and-dog encounter below. Steps descend in wide flights down the hillside into Blue End. The two couchant lions on either side of the steps are in plasticine, and were executed by that versatile artist, who is also mayor of Red End, G. P. W. He is present. Our photographer has hit upon a happy moment in the history of this town, and a conversation of the two mayors is going on upon the terrace before the palace. F. R. W., mayor of Blue End, stands on the steps in the costume of an admiral; G. P. W. is on horseback (his habits are equestrian) on the terrace. The town guard parades in their honor, and up the hill a number of blue-clad musicians (a little hidden by trees) ride on gray horses towards them.

留意那只栖在雉堞上的红鹦鹉：它养熟在动物园里，和我们先前在群岛上见过的那只属于同一种类。也留意一下下方那场热闹的猫狗交锋。宽阔的台阶一层层顺着山坡通往蓝端。台阶两侧的两只卧狮，用橡皮泥做成，出自那位多才多艺、同时兼任红端市长的艺术家G. P. W.之手。他本人也在场。我们的摄影师捕捉到了这座城市历史上的一个愉快时刻，两位市长正在宫殿前的平台上交谈。蓝端市长F. R. W.身穿海军将领的服装，站在台阶上；G. P. W.骑马立在平台上（他素来有骑马的习惯）。城市卫队正为他们列队致敬，山坡上一队穿蓝衣的乐手（稍稍被树遮住）骑着灰马向他们走来。
[图中文字：TOWN／HALL]
[图内译释：市政厅]
[图中文字：THE／ZOO；1ᴰ；PAY；PUSH]
[图内译释：动物园；一便士；付款；推]

Passing in front of the town hall, and turning to the right, we approach the zoölogical gardens. Here we pass two of our civilians: a gentleman in black, a lady, and a large boy scout, presumably their son. We enter the gardens, which are protected by a bearded janitor, and remark at once a band of three performing dogs, who are, as the guide-book would say, "discoursing sweet music." In neither ward of the city does there seem to be the slightest restraint upon the use of musical instruments.
从市政厅前经过，再向右拐，我们来到动物园附近。在这里，我们从两位平民身旁走过：一位黑衣绅士、一位女士，还有一个大个头童子军，想必是他们的儿子。我们进入由一名蓄着胡须的门房守卫的园子，立刻发现一个由三只会表演的狗组成的乐队，正用旅游指南的话来说，“奏出甜美的音乐”。城里两个区，似乎都丝毫不限制乐器的使用。
It is no place for neurotic people.
这里可不是神经衰弱的人待的地方。

The gardens contain the inevitable elephants, camels (which we breed, and which are therefore in considerable numbers), a sitting bear, brought from last game's caves, goats from the same region, tamed and now running loose in the gardens, dwarf elephants, wooden nondescripts, and other rare creatures. The keepers wear a uniform not unlike that of railway guards and porters. We wander through the gardens, return, descend the hill by the school of musketry, where soldiers are to be seen shooting at the butts, pass through the paddock of the old farm, and so return to the railway station, extremely gratified by all we have seen, and almost equally divided in our minds between the merits and attractiveness of either ward. A clockwork train comes clattering into the station, we take our places, somebody hoots or whistles for the engine (which can't), the signal is knocked over in the excitement of the moment, the train starts, and we "wave a long, regretful farewell to the salubrious cheerfulness of Chamois City." . . .

园里少不了大象，还有骆驼（我们自己繁殖，因此数目相当可观）、一头从上个游戏的洞穴里带来的坐熊、几只来自同一地方的山羊——如今已经驯服，在园里自由跑动——还有侏儒象、说不上名目的木头动物，以及其他珍奇生物。饲养员的制服，同列车乘务员和搬运工的服装颇为相像。我们在园里漫步，然后折返，沿着射击学校旁的路下山，可以看见士兵们正在向靶垛射击；再穿过老农场的围场，回到火车站。眼前的一切让我们心满意足，两个区各有长处、各有魅力，几乎难分高下。一列发条火车哐当哐当地进站了，我们各就各位，有人替机车鸣笛或吹哨（因为它自己不会）；一时兴奋，信号机被碰倒了，火车开动，我们“久久挥手，依依不舍地告别岩羚城健康宜人的欢快气氛”。……
[图中文字：BLUE／END；…W.R.]
[图内译释：蓝端；货车侧面铁路缩写，首部字母不清，不展开机构名]
The terraced hill on which stands the Town Hall. Behind can be seen the Zoölogical Gardens
市政厅所在的梯状山丘，后方可见动物园

You see now how we set out and the spirit in which we set out our towns. It demands but the slightest exercise of the imagination to devise a hundred additions and variations of the scheme. You can make picture-galleries—great fun for small boys who can draw; you can make factories; you can plan out flower-gardens—which appeals very strongly to intelligent little girls; your town hall may become a fortified castle; or you may put the whole town on boards and make a Venice of it, with ships and boats upon its canals, and bridges across them. We used to have some very serviceable ships of cardboard, with flat bottoms; and then we used to have a harbor, and the ships used to sail away to distant rooms, and even into the garden, and return with the most remarkable cargoes, loads of nasturtium-stem logs, for example. We had sacks then, made of glove-fingers, and several toy cranes. I suppose we could find most of these again if we hunted for them. Once, with this game fresh in our minds, we went to see the docks, which struck us as just our old harbor game magnified.

现在你已经看到，我们如何布置城镇，又怀着怎样的兴致来布置。只须稍稍发挥想象力，就能给这个方案想出上百种增添和变化。你可以造画廊——这对会画画的小男孩尤其有趣；可以造工厂；可以规划花园——这对聪明的小女孩尤其有吸引力；市政厅可以变成设防的城堡；或者，把整座城镇放到木板上，让它成为一座威尼斯，运河上有船，河道上架着桥。我们过去有些平底硬纸板船，很是好用；那时也有一座港口，船从那里出航，驶向遥远的房间，甚至花园，再载着稀奇古怪的货物回来，比如一船船旱金莲茎秆做的原木。我们那时还用手套的指头做了麻袋，并且有几架玩具起重机。我想，只要找一找，大部分东西应该还能找到。有一回，脑子里还留着这个游戏的鲜明印象，我们去参观码头，觉得那不过是把我们从前的港口游戏放大了。

[图内译释：试试我们的周末游览：最好，走得最远；午夜快车；BER；鸡蛋；GPW；FRW；HGW]
[图中文字：DOGS／MUST BE／ON LEAD；SILENCE；PICTURES／FOR SALE／2ᴰ EACH；CAT；DUKE；…OTHER／AND CHIL…；THE／STORM；MONARCH／OF THE／GLEN；DERBY；CHARITY；BABY；PORTRAIT]
[图内译释：犬只必须牵引；肃静；绘画出售，每幅二便士；猫（画名）；公爵（画名）；……／与孩子……（题名被前景人物遮挡，不补不可见字）；暴风雨（画名）；山谷之王（画名）；德比赛马（画名）；慈善（画名）；婴儿（画名）；肖像（画名）]

"I say, Daddy," said one of us in a quiet corner, wistfully, as one who speaks knowingly against the probabilities of the case, and yet with a faint, thin hope, "couldn't we play just for a little with these sacks . . . until somebody comes?"
“我说，爸爸，”我们中的一个在僻静角落里满怀向往地说；他明知事情大概不会有指望，却仍抱着一丝微弱的希望，“这些麻袋，能不能让我们就玩一小会儿……等有人来再说？”

Of course the setting-out of the city is half the game. Then you devise incidents. As I wanted to photograph the particular set-out for the purpose of illustrating this account, I took a larger share in the arrangement than I usually do-It was necessary to get everything into the picture, to ensure a light background that would throw up some of the trees, prevent too much overlapping, and things like that. When the photographing was over, matters became more normal. I left the schoolroom, and when I returned I found that the group of riflemen which had been converging on the public-house had been sharply recalled to duty, and were trotting in a disciplined, cheerless way towards the railway station. The elephant had escaped from the zoo into the Blue Ward, and was being marched along by a military patrol. The originally scattered boy scouts were being paraded. G. P. W. had demolished the shop of the Jokil Company, and was building a Red End station near the bend. The stock of the Jokil Company had passed into the hands of the adjacent storekeepers. Then the town hall ceremonies came to an end and the guard marched off. Then G. P. W. demolished the rifle-range, and ran a small branch of the urban railway uphill to the town hall door, and on into the zoological gardens. This was only the beginning of a period of enterprise in transit, a small railway boom. A number of halts of simple construction sprang up. There was much making of railway tickets, of a size that enabled passengers to stick their heads through the middle and wear them as a Mexican does his blanket. Then a battery of artillery turned up in the High Street and there was talk of fortifications. Suppose wild Indians were to turn up across the plains to the left and attack the town! Fate still has toy drawers untouched. . . .

当然，布置城市只是游戏的一半。接下来还要想出各种事件。因为我想把这一次的布置拍下来，给这篇说明配图，所以在安排上比平时多插了些手。必须让所有东西都进入镜头，保证背景足够明亮，能够衬出某些树木，避免过多遮挡，诸如此类。照片拍完，一切又比较正常了。我离开教室，再回来时，发现那队原本正向酒馆聚拢的步枪兵，已经被严令召回执勤，正纪律严明、垂头丧气地小跑着去火车站。大象从动物园逃进蓝区，正由一队巡逻士兵押送着。原先散在各处的童子军也列起了队。G. P. W.拆掉了Jokil公司的商店，正在铁道转弯处附近建一座红端车站。Jokil公司的存货，已落入邻近店主手中。接着，市政厅的典礼结束了，卫队开走。随后，G. P. W.又拆掉靶场，让市内铁路的一条小支线沿山坡铺到市政厅门前，再一直伸进动物园。这只是一段交通事业兴盛期的开端，是一次小小的铁路热潮。几个构造简单的停靠站冒了出来。大家忙着制作车票，票大到足以让乘客把头从中间穿过去，像墨西哥人披毯子那样套在身上。接着，一连炮兵出现在大街上，大家又议论起了修筑工事的事。要是野蛮的印第安人从左边的平原那头冒出来，攻打这座城镇，可怎么办！命运手里还有尚未打开的玩具抽屉呢。……
[图中文字：TICKET；1ᴰ；OFFICERS／FREE／PASS]
[图内译释：票；一便士；军官免费通行证]

So things will go on till putting-away night on Friday. Then we shall pick up the roofs and shove them away among the books, return the clockwork engines very carefully to their boxes, for engines are fragile things, stow the soldiers and civilians and animals in their nests of drawers, burn the trees again—this time they are sweet-bay; and all the joys and sorrows and rivalries and successes of Blue End and Red End will pass, and follow Carthage and Nineveh, the empire of Aztec and Roman, the arts of Etruria and the palaces of Crete, and the plannings and contrivings of innumerable myriads of children, into the limbo of games exhausted . . . it may be, leaving some profit, in thoughts widened, in strengthened apprehensions; it may be, leaving nothing but a memory that dies.

事情就会这样发展下去，直到星期五晚上收拾玩具的时候。那时，我们会拿起屋顶，塞到书本之间，把发条机车小心翼翼地放回盒子——机车可是脆弱的东西——再把士兵、平民和动物放回它们那一层层的抽屉窝里，又一次烧掉树木——这一回用的是月桂树。于是，蓝端和红端的一切欢乐、悲伤、竞争与成功，都将消逝，追随迦太基与尼尼微、阿兹特克与罗马的帝国、伊特鲁里亚的艺术与克里特的宫殿，以及无数亿万儿童的筹划与巧思，一同进入那些已玩尽兴致的游戏的幽冥……或许留下某些收获：思路更开阔，理解力更强；也或许，除了一段终将消散的记忆，什么都没有留下。

text: I have now given two general types of floor game; but these are only just two samples of delightful and imagination-stirring variations that can be contrived out of the toys I have described. I will now glance rather more shortly at some other very good uses of the floor, the boards, the bricks, the soldiers, and the railway system—that pentagram for exorcising the evil spirit of dulness from the lives of little boys and girls. And first, there is a kind of lark we call Funiculars. There are times when islands cease somehow to dazzle, and towns and cities are too orderly and uneventful and cramped for us, and we want something—something to whizz. Then we say: "Let us make a funicular. Let us make a funicular more than we have ever done. Let us make one to reach up to the table."
section: 缆索铁路、弹珠塔、城堡与战争游戏，不过战争游戏只谈一点点

text: 我已经介绍了两种基本的地板游戏；但利用前面那些玩具，可以想出许多令人愉快、激发想象的变化，这不过是其中两个例子。现在，我要稍微简略一些，再谈谈地板、木板、积木、士兵和铁路系统的其他几种妙用——这五样东西，便是驱逐小男孩和小女孩生活中无聊恶魔的五芒星。首先，有一种嬉戏，我们叫它“缆索铁路”。有些时候，不知怎么，岛屿不再让人眼花缭乱，城镇对我们来说又太规矩、太平静、太局促了；我们想要点什么——什么能嗖嗖飞驰的东西。于是我们说：“来造一条缆索铁路吧。造一条比以前所有的都更了不起的。造一条能一直通到桌上的吧。”
section: 缆索铁路、弹珠塔、城堡与战争游戏，不过战争游戏只谈一点点

text: We dispute whether it isn't a mountain railway we are after. The bare name is refreshing; it takes us back to that unforgettable time when we all went to Wengen, winding in and out and up and up the mountain side—from slush, to such snow and sunlight as we had never seen before. And we make a mountain railway. So far, we have never got it up to the table, but some day we will. Then we will have a station there on the flat, and another station on the floor, with shunts and sidings to each.
section: 缆索铁路、弹珠塔、城堡与战争游戏，不过战争游戏只谈一点点

text: 我们争论，自己想造的会不会其实是一条山地铁路。光是这个名字就叫人精神一振，让我们回到全家去文根的那段难忘时光：沿山腰蜿蜒进出，不断向上、再向上，从泥泞的雪水，一路来到从未见过的那般白雪与阳光之中。于是，我们造一条山地铁路。到目前为止，还没能让它通到桌上，不过总有一天会做到的。到时候，在上面那块平地上设一座车站，地板上再设一座，两座都配上调车线和侧线。
section: 缆索铁路、弹珠塔、城堡与战争游戏，不过战争游戏只谈一点点

text: The peculiar joy of the mountain railway is that, if it is properly made, a loaded car—not a toy engine; it is too rough a game for delicate, respectable engines—will career from top to bottom of the system, and go this way and that as your cunningly-arranged switches determine; and afterwards—and this is a wonderful and distinctive discovery—you can send it back by 'lectric.
section: 缆索铁路、弹珠塔、城堡与战争游戏，不过战争游戏只谈一点点

text: 山地铁路特有的乐趣在于，只要造得合适，一辆装满东西的车——不能用玩具机车；这玩法太粗野，不适合精细而体面的机车——就能从整个系统的最高处冲到最低处，随着你巧妙安排的道岔，忽而向这边，忽而向那边。然后——这是个奇妙而独特的发现——你可以用“电车”把它送回去。
section: 缆索铁路、弹珠塔、城堡与战争游戏，不过战争游戏只谈一点点

text: What is a 'lectric? You may well ask. 'Lectrics were invented almost by accident, by one of us, to whom also the name is due. It came out of an accident to a toy engine; a toy engine that seemed done for, and that was yet full of life.
section: 缆索铁路、弹珠塔、城堡与战争游戏，不过战争游戏只谈一点点

text: 什么是“电车”？你大可以这样问。“电车”几乎是一次意外的发明，发明者是我们中的一个，名字也出自他。这事起于一辆玩具机车的意外：那辆机车看起来已经报废了，却仍充满活力。
section: 缆索铁路、弹珠塔、城堡与战争游戏，不过战争游戏只谈一点点

text: You know, perhaps, what a toy engine is like. It has the general appearance of a railway engine; funnels, buffers, cab, and so forth. All these are very elegant things, no doubt; but they do not make for lightness, they do not facilitate hill-climbing. Now, sometimes an engine gets its clockwork out of order, and then it is over and done for; but sometimes it is merely the outer semblance that is injured—the funnel bent, the body twisted. You remove the things and, behold! you have bare clock-work on wheels, an apparatus of almost malignant energy, soul without body, a kind of metallic rage. This it was that our junior member instantly knew for a 'lectric, and loved from the moment of its stripping.
section: 缆索铁路、弹珠塔、城堡与战争游戏，不过战争游戏只谈一点点

text: 你也许知道，玩具机车是什么样子。它大体上有一辆火车头的模样：烟囱、缓冲器、驾驶室，等等。这些东西无疑都很雅致，但并不能减轻重量，也不利于爬坡。有时，机车的发条出了故障，那就彻底完了；但有时受损的只是外表——烟囱弯了，车身歪了。把这些东西卸掉，瞧！你就得到一套装在轮子上的裸露发条机构，一部精力充沛得近乎凶恶的装置，一个没有肉身的灵魂，一团金属的狂怒。我们最年幼的成员立刻认定，这就是“电车”，而且从它被剥去外壳的那一刻起就爱上了它。
section: 缆索铁路、弹珠塔、城堡与战争游戏，不过战争游戏只谈一点点

text: (I have, by the by, known a very serviceable little road 'lectric made out of a clock-work mouse.)
section: 缆索铁路、弹珠塔、城堡与战争游戏，不过战争游戏只谈一点点

text: （顺便说一句，我还知道，有人用一只发条老鼠做成过一辆很好用的小型公路“电车”。）
section: 缆索铁路、弹珠塔、城堡与战争游戏，不过战争游戏只谈一点点

text: Well, when we have got chairs and boxes and bricks, and graded our line skilfully and well, easing the descent, and being very careful of the joining at the bends for fear that the descending trucks and cars will jump the rails, we send down first an empty truck, then trucks loaded with bricks and lead soldiers, and then the 'lectric; and then afterwards the sturdy 'lectric shoves up the trucks again to the top, with a kind of savagery of purpose and a whizz that is extremely gratifying to us. We make switches in these lines; we make them have level-crossings, at which collisions are always being just averted; the lines go over and under each other, and in and out of tunnels. . . .
section: 缆索铁路、弹珠塔、城堡与战争游戏，不过战争游戏只谈一点点

text: 好，等我们找来了椅子、箱子和积木，巧妙妥当地调好了线路坡度，使下坡平缓一些，又仔细处理好弯道接缝，以免下行的货车和车厢脱轨，就先放一辆空货车下去，再放装满积木和铅制士兵的货车，最后放“电车”。随后，结实的“电车”又把货车一路推回顶端，带着一股近乎凶猛的执着，嗖嗖作响，让我们心满意足。我们在线路上设置道岔；设置平交道口，碰撞总是在千钧一发时得以避免；线路彼此上下交越，又从隧道里钻进钻出。……
section: 缆索铁路、弹珠塔、城堡与战争游戏，不过战争游戏只谈一点点

text: The marble tower, again, is a great building, on which we devise devious slanting ways down which marbles run. I do not know why it is amusing to make a marble run down a long intricate path, and dollop down steps, and come almost but not quite to a stop, and rush out of dark places and across little bridges of card: it is, and we often do it.
section: 缆索铁路、弹珠塔、城堡与战争游戏，不过战争游戏只谈一点点

text: 弹珠塔则是一座大建筑，我们在上面安排曲折的斜坡通道，让弹珠沿路滚下。我不知道，为什么让一颗弹珠滚过一条漫长复杂的路径，咚咚地跌下台阶，差一点停住却又没有停住，从暗处冲出来，再越过小小的纸板桥，会这么有趣；但它就是有趣，我们也常常这样玩。
section: 缆索铁路、弹珠塔、城堡与战争游戏，不过战争游戏只谈一点点

text: Castles are done with bricks and cardboard turrets and a portcullis of card, and draw-bridge and moats; they are a mere special sort of city-building, done because we have a box of men in armor. We could reconstruct all sorts of historical periods if the toy-soldier makers would provide us with people. But at present, as I have already complained, they make scarcely anything but contemporary fighting men. And of the war game I must either write volumes or nothing. For the present let it be nothing. Some day, perhaps, I will write a great book about the war game and tell of battles and campaigns and strategy and tactics. But this time I set out merely to tell of the ordinary joys of playing with the floor, and to gird improvingly and usefully at toymakers. So much, I think, I have done. If one parent or one uncle buys the wiselier for me, I shall not altogether have lived in vain.
section: 缆索铁路、弹珠塔、城堡与战争游戏，不过战争游戏只谈一点点

text: 城堡用积木来搭，配上硬纸板角楼、纸板升降闸门，还有吊桥和护城河；这不过是一种特别的造城游戏，之所以这样造，是因为我们有一盒披甲武士。只要玩具士兵制造商肯供应人物，各个历史时期我们都能重建。可正如我已经抱怨过的，他们眼下除了当代军人，几乎什么也不做。至于战争游戏，我要么写上好几大卷，要么一个字也不写。眼下就一字不写吧。或许有一天，我会写一本谈战争游戏的大书，讲述战斗、战役、战略和战术。但这一次，我原本只想讲讲在地板上玩耍的寻常乐趣，顺带给玩具制造商一些有益、促人改进的讥评。我想，这些我已经做到了。只要有一位父亲、母亲或叔伯，因为读了我的话而更明智地买玩具，我这一辈子就不算全然白活。
section: 缆索铁路、弹珠塔、城堡与战争游戏，不过战争游戏只谈一点点

text: 地板游戏 Floor Games 地板游戏 H. G. Wells 赫伯特·乔治·威尔斯 1911 2026

威尔斯把家里的地板变成海洋、群岛和两座相邻的城市。木板叠成山丘，花园里的枝条插进小孔成为树林，积木、铅制人物与发条火车组成可以不断改造的世界。书先讲材料和尺寸，再展示探索群岛、营造城镇、搭山地铁路与弹珠塔的具体玩法；照片和页边插画记录了这些布置，也延续着他对玩具商、城市生活与成人权威的调侃。 这些游戏允许布置、故事和规则一起生长。两个孩子各有自己的辖区，共享铁道，举行市长选举，也会在大人离开后拆掉商店、另建车站，让原先的安排转向新的事件。威尔斯由此讨论成品玩具的局限、材料能否反复组合，以及儿童从造世界的过程中获得怎样的想象空间。最后一节简短谈到战争游戏，把更系统的战斗规则留给另一部书。

I. Of the Legendary Past
I. 传说中的往昔

“Little Wars” is the game of kings—for players in an inferior social position. It can be played by boys of every age from twelve to one hundred and fifty—and even later if the limbs remain sufficiently supple,—by girls of the better sort, and by a few rare and gifted women. This is to be a full History of Little Wars from its recorded and authenticated beginning until the present time, an account of how to make little warfare, and hints of the most priceless sort for the recumbent strategist. …
《小战争》是供社会地位稍逊的人玩的王者游戏。十二岁到一百五十岁之间任何年龄的男孩都能玩——只要四肢还足够灵活，更老一点也行——较出色的女孩也能玩，还有少数罕见而天资出众的女人。这将是一部完整的《小战争》史，从有据可查、得到证实的起源，一直讲到当下；既介绍怎样打小战争，也为卧地运筹的战略家提供无比珍贵的诀窍。……

But first let it be noted in passing that there were prehistoric “Little Wars.” This is no new thing, no crude novelty; but a thing tested by time, ancient and ripe in its essentials for all its perennial freshness—like spring. There was a Someone who fought Little Wars in the days of Queen Anne; a garden Napoleon. His game was inaccurately observed and insufficiently recorded by Laurence Sterne. It is clear that Uncle Toby and Corporal Trim were playing Little Wars on a scale and with an elaboration exceeding even the richness and beauty of the contemporary game. But the curtain is drawn back only to tantalise us. It is scarcely conceivable that anywhere now on earth the Shandean Rules remain on record. Perhaps they were never committed to paper. …

不过，先顺便说明，史前就有过“小战争”。这不是新事物，不是什么粗陋的新奇玩意；它已经受过时间的检验，根本上古老而成熟，却又永远鲜活，正如春天。安妮女王时代，就有某个人打过小战争：一位花园里的拿破仑。劳伦斯·斯特恩对他的游戏观察得不准确，记录得也不充分。显然，托比叔叔和特里姆下士玩的小战争，规模与精细程度，甚至超过当代游戏的丰富与美观。然而，帷幕只被掀开一点，徒然吊起我们的胃口。很难想象，今天世上还有哪里保存着那套“尚迪式规则”。也许它们从来就没有落到纸上。……

And in all ages a certain barbaric warfare has been waged with soldiers of tin and lead and wood, with the weapons of the wild, with the catapult, the elastic circular garter, the peashooter, the rubber ball, and such-like appliances—a mere setting up and knocking down of men. Tin murder. The advance of civilisation has swept such rude contests altogether from the playroom. We know them no more. …
而且，历朝历代都有一种野蛮战争，用锡、铅、木头做的士兵，拿原始武器作战：弹弓、有弹性的环形袜带、吹豆筒、橡皮球，以及诸如此类的器具——不过是把兵人摆好，再把它们打倒。对锡兵的谋杀。文明的进步，早已将这些粗野的较量从游戏室一扫而空。我们再也不知道这种东西了。……

text: The beginning of the game of Little War, as we know it, became possible with the invention of the spring breechloader gun. This priceless gift to boyhood appeared somewhen towards the end of the last century, a gun capable of hitting a toy soldier nine times out of ten at a distance of nine yards. It has completely superseded all the spiral-spring and other makes of gun hitherto used in playroom warfare. These spring breechloaders are made in various sizes and patterns, but the one used in our game is that known in England as the four-point-seven gun. It fires a wooden cylinder about an inch long, and has a screw adjustment for elevation and depression. It is an altogether elegant weapon.

text: 我们所知的小战争游戏，之所以能够诞生，是因为弹簧后膛炮的发明。这份给少年时代的无价礼物，大约出现在上个世纪末：在九码距离外，它十发有九发能击中一个玩具士兵。它已经彻底取代此前游戏室战争里使用的各种螺旋弹簧炮和其他炮型。这些弹簧后膛炮有不同尺寸和式样，我们游戏所用的，是在英国称为“四点七炮”的那一种。它发射一枚大约一英寸长的木制圆柱，并用螺丝调节仰角和俯角。总之，是一件精巧优雅的武器。

text: He fired that day a shot that still echoes round the world. An affair—let us parallel the Cannonade of Valmy and call it the Cannonade of Sandgate—occurred, a shooting between opposed ranks of soldiers, a shooting not very different in spirit—but how different in results!—from the prehistoric warfare of catapult and garter. “But suppose,” said his antagonists; “suppose somehow one could move the men!” and therewith opened a new world of belligerence.

text: But the writer had in those days a very dear friend, a man too ill for long excursions or vigorous sports [he has been dead now these six years], of a very sweet companionable disposition, a hearty jester and full of the spirit of play. To him the idea was broached more fruitfully. We got two forces of toy soldiers, set out a lumpish Encyclopædic land upon the carpet, and began to play. We arranged to move in alternate moves: first one moved all his force and then the other; an infantry-man could move one foot at each move, a cavalry-man two, a gun two, and it might fire six shots; and if a man was moved up to touch another man, then we tossed up and decided which man was dead. So we made a game, which was not a good game, but which was very amusing once or twice. The men were packed under the lee of fat volumes, while the guns, animated by a spirit of their own, banged away at any exposed head, or prowled about in search of a shot. Occasionally men came into contact, with remarkable results. Rash is the man who trusts his life to the spin of a coin. One impossible paladin slew in succession nine men and turned defeat to victory, to the extreme exasperation of the strategist who had led those victims to their doom. This inordinate factor of chance eliminated play; the individual freedom of guns turned battles into scandals of crouching concealment; there was too much cover afforded by the books and vast intervals of waiting while the players took aim. And yet there was something about it. … It was a game crying aloud for improvement.
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: 不过，笔者那时有一位非常亲爱的朋友。他病得很重，不能远足，也不能参加剧烈运动[如今他已经去世六年了]；他性情温厚，极好相处，爱说笑，满怀游戏精神。向他提起这个想法，就有成果得多。我们弄来两支玩具士兵部队，用百科全书在地毯上摆出一片笨重的地形，开始玩起来。我们约定轮流行动：先由一方移动他的全部兵力，再轮到另一方；每回合，步兵能走一英尺，骑兵两英尺，炮两英尺，而且炮能打六发；如果一个兵人移到与另一个兵人相接触的位置，就掷硬币决定谁死。于是，我们做成了一种游戏，虽说不是好游戏，但玩上一两次还是非常有趣的。士兵密集地挤在厚书背后，炮却像有自己的意志一样，向任何露出的脑袋砰砰开火，或者四处游荡，寻找射击机会。偶尔，兵人彼此接触，结果非同寻常。拿自己的性命赌硬币正反的人，实在鲁莽。有一位不可思议的勇士，竟一连斩杀九人，反败为胜；把那些牺牲者带上绝路的战略家，为此恼火到了极点。如此过分的偶然因素，消解了游戏；炮的自主行动，把战斗变成了蹲伏躲藏的丑剧；书本提供的掩护太多，玩家瞄准时，等待又太久。然而，它终究有点什么。……这是一种大声呼唤改进的游戏。

text: Improvement came almost simultaneously in several directions. First there was the development of the Country. The soldiers did not stand well on an ordinary carpet, the Encyclo pædia made clumsy cliff-like “cover,” and more particularly the room in which the game had its beginnings was subject to the invasion of callers, alien souls, trampling skirt-swishers, chatterers, creatures unfavourably impressed by the spectacle of two middle-aged men playing with “toy soldiers” on the floor, and very heated and excited about it. Overhead was the day nursery, with a wide extent of smooth cork carpet (the natural terrain of toy soldiers), a large box of bricks—such as I have described in Floor Games,—and certain large inch-thick boards.

text: 改进几乎同时在几个方向上出现了。首先，是地形的发展。士兵在普通地毯上站不稳，《百科全书》又构成笨拙的、悬崖般的“掩体”；尤其是，游戏诞生的那个房间，总会遭到来客侵入：异类灵魂、拖着沙沙裙摆到处踩踏的人、喋喋不休的人；他们看见两个中年男人坐在地板上玩“玩具士兵”，而且还热火朝天、兴奋不已，便心生反感。楼上是白天使用的儿童室，有大片平滑的软木地毯——玩具士兵的天然地形——有一大箱积木，就是我在《地板游戏》中介绍过的那种，还有几块一英寸厚的大木板。

text: It was an easy task for the head of the household to evict his offspring, annex these advantages, and set about planning a more realistic country. (I forget what became of the children.) The thick boards were piled up one upon another to form hills; holes were bored in them, into which twigs of various shrubs were stuck to represent trees; houses and sheds (solid and compact piles of from three to six or seven inches high, and broad in proportion) and walls were made with the bricks; ponds and swamps and rivers, with fords and so forth indicated, were chalked out on the floor, garden stones were brought in to represent great rocks, and the “Country” at least of our perfected war game was in existence. We discovered it was easy to cut out and bend and gum together paper and cardboard walls, into which our toy bricks could be packed, and on which we could paint doors and windows, creepers and rain-water pipes, and so forth, to repre sent houses, castles, and churches in a more realistic manner, and, growing skilful, we made various bridges and so forth of card. Every boy who has ever put together model villages knows how to do these things, and the attentive reader will find them edifyingly represented in our photographic illustrations.

text: 一家之主很容易就能把子女赶出去，兼并这些有利条件，着手规划更逼真的地形。（我忘了孩子们后来怎么样了。）厚木板一层层叠起来，形成山丘；在木板上钻孔，插入各种灌木的小枝，代表树木；用积木搭起房屋、棚舍和围墙，房屋棚舍是结实紧凑的积木堆，高三英寸到六七英寸不等，宽度也按比例；在地板上用粉笔画出池塘、沼泽和河流，标明涉渡点等等；再搬来花园里的石头，代表巨岩。至此，我们完善后的战争游戏，至少已有了它的“地形”。我们发现，用纸和纸板剪出墙壁，再弯折、粘合，里面塞进玩具积木，就能轻易造出更逼真的房屋、城堡和教堂；墙面上可以画门窗、攀缘植物、落水管等等，用以表现这些建筑。技术熟练后，我们又用卡纸做了各种桥梁之类。凡是拼搭过模型村庄的男孩，都知道怎样做这些东西；细心的读者，也能从我们的照片插图中看到颇有启发的示范。

text: There has been little development since that time in the Country. Our illustrations show the methods of arrangement, and the reader will see how easily and readily the utmost variety of battlefields can be made. (It is merely to be remarked that a too crowded Country makes the guns ineffective and leads to a mere tree to tree and house to house scramble, and that large open spaces along the middle, or rivers without frequent fords and bridges, lead to ineffective cannonades, because of the danger of any advance. On the whole, too much cover is better than too little.) We decided that one player should plan and lay out the Country, and the other player choose from which side he would come. And to-day we play over such landscapes in a cork-carpeted schoolroom, from which the proper occupants are no longer evicted but remain to take an increasingly responsible and less and less audible and distressing share in the operations.

text: 自那以后，地形没有多少发展。插图显示了布置方法，读者会看到，多种多样的战场，制作起来何其容易便捷。（只须指出，地形过于拥挤，会使炮失效，战斗沦为从树到树、从房到房的混乱争夺；而中央大片开阔地，或者缺少足够涉渡点和桥梁的河流，会因任何推进都很危险，而导致毫无成效的炮战。总体而言，掩护太多，胜过太少。）我们决定，由一位玩家规划布置地形，再由另一位选择从哪一边进入。今天，我们就在一间铺着软木地毯的教室里，使用这类景观进行游戏；房间原本的主人不再被赶出去，而是留下来参加作战，承担的责任越来越大，声音却越来越小，造成的苦恼也越来越少。

text: 我们发现，有必要制定一些通则。房屋和棚舍必须用实心的积木堆构成，不能做成能把士兵放进去的空心房子，否则就会产生混乱局面。而且，显然还须规定：在木板和房屋所放置的地板或木板上，用粉笔描出它们的轮廓，以便把意外移位的东西放回原处。

text: And while we thus perfected the Country, we were also eliminating all sorts of tediums, disputable possibilities, and deadlocks from the game. We decided that every man should be as brave and skilful as every other man, and that when two men of opposite sides came into contact they would inevitably kill each other. This restored strategy to its predominance over chance.
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: 在这样完善地形的同时，我们也从游戏中消除各种乏味、可能引起争议的情形，以及僵局。我们决定，每个士兵都应当与其他所有士兵一样勇敢、一样熟练；敌对双方的两名士兵一旦接触，就必然同归于尽。这让战略重新取得了对偶然性的支配地位。
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: We then began to humanise that wild and fearful fowl, the gun. We decided that a gun could not be fired if there were not six—afterwards we re duced the number to four—men within six inches of it. And we ruled that a gun could not both fire and move in the same general move: it could either be fired or moved (or left alone). If there were less than six men within six inches of a gun, then we tried letting it fire as many shots as there were men, and we permitted a single man to move a gun, and move with it as far as he could go by the rules—a foot, that is, if he was an infantry-man, and two feet if he was a cavalry-man. We abolished altogether that magical freedom of an unassisted gun to move two feet. And on such rules as these we fought a number of battles. They were interesting, but not entirely satisfactory. We took no prisoners—a feature at once barbaric and unconvincing. The battles lingered on a long time, because we shot with extreme care and deliberation, and they were hard to bring to a decisive finish. The guns were altogether too predominant. They prevented attacks getting home, and they made it possible for a timid player to put all his soldiers out of sight behind hills and houses, and bang away if his opponent showed as much as the tip of a bayonet. Monsieur Bloch seemed vindicated, and Little War had become impossible. And there was something a little absurd, too, in the spectacle of a solitary drummer-boy, for example, marching off with a gun.
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: 随后，我们开始驯化那种野蛮而可怕的飞禽：炮。我们决定，一门炮周围六英寸内，如果没有六个士兵——后来我们把这个数目降为四个——就不能开火。我们还规定，在同一个总回合内，炮不能既开火又移动：它可以开火，或移动，或什么也不做。如果炮周围六英寸内不足六人，我们就试着让它按人数发射同样数量的炮弹；并允许一个人拖动炮，按照规则能走多远，就带着炮走多远：步兵一英尺，骑兵两英尺。我们彻底取消了炮在无人协助下还能自行移动两英尺的魔法自由。按照这些规则，我们打了好几场仗。有趣，但并不完全令人满意。我们不俘虏任何人，这一点既野蛮，又不可信。战斗延续很久，因为我们射击得极其小心、极其从容，难以打出决定性的结局。炮的优势太大。它们使进攻难以冲到跟前，也让胆小的玩家能够把全部士兵藏到山丘和房屋后面；对手只要露出一个刺刀尖，就会挨炮。布洛赫先生似乎得到了证明，小战争已经不可能进行了。而且，比如一个孤零零的鼓手小孩，拖着一门炮离开的景象，也确实有点荒唐。
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: But as there was nevertheless much that seemed to us extremely pretty and picturesque about the game, we set to work—and here a certain Mr M. with his brother, Captain M., hot from the Great War in South Africa, came in most helpfully—to quicken it. Manifestly the guns had to be reduced to manageable terms. We cut down the number of shots per move to four, and we required that four men should be within six inches of a gun for it to be in action at all. Without four men it could neither fire nor move—it was out of action; and if it moved, the four men had to go with it. Moreover, to put an end to that little resistant body of men behind a house, we required that after a gun had been fired it should remain, without alteration of the elevation, pointing in the direction of its last shot, and have two men placed one on either side of the end of its trail. This secured a certain exposure on the part of concealed and sheltered gunners. It was no longer possible to go on shooting out of a perfect security for ever. All this favoured the attack and led to a livelier game.
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: 不过，这个游戏仍有许多在我们看来极其美好、极富画意的地方，所以我们便着手加快它的节奏；这时，某位M.先生和他的兄弟M.上尉——刚从南非大战回来——给予了极大的帮助。显然，必须把炮限制在可以控制的范围内。我们将每回合的射击数削减为四发，并规定：一门炮周围六英寸以内，必须有四个士兵，才能处于可作战状态。没有四个人，它既不能开火，也不能移动：它失去了作战能力；如果炮移动，这四个人也必须同行。此外，为了解决藏在房屋后面、顽抗不退的那一小撮人，我们规定，炮开过火后，仰角不得改变，必须继续指向最后一发的射击方向；炮架尾端两侧，各须放一名士兵。这就让躲藏着、有掩护的炮手，也必须作出一定的暴露。此后，再也不能永远躲在绝对安全的位置不断射击了。所有这些，都有利于进攻，使游戏更为活跃。
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: Our next step was to abolish the tedium due to the elaborate aiming of the guns, by fixing a time limit for every move. We made this an outside limit at first, ten minutes, but afterwards we discovered that it made the game much more warlike to cut the time down to a length that would barely permit a slow-moving player to fire all his guns and move all his men. This led to small bodies of men lagging and “getting left,” to careless exposures, to rapid, less accurate shooting, and just that eventfulness one would expect in the hurry and passion of real fighting. It also made the game brisker. We have since also made a limit, sometimes of four minutes, sometimes of five minutes, to the interval for adjustment and deliberation after one move is finished and before the next move begins. This further removes the game from the chess category, and approximates it to the likeness of active service. Most of a general's decisions, once a fight has begun, must be made in such brief intervals of time. (But we leave unlimited time at the outset for the planning.)
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: 下一步，是给每回合规定时限，消除仔细瞄炮造成的冗长乏味。起先，我们定了一个宽松的上限：十分钟。后来却发现，把时间缩短到只能勉强让行动较慢的玩家打完所有炮、移动完全部士兵，游戏就会更像战争。于是，一小群士兵会落后、会“被丢下”，会出现疏忽造成的暴露，射击变得匆忙、较不准确；总之，就出现了人们在真实战斗的忙乱与激情中可以预料的种种变故。游戏也因此更明快。后来，我们又给一回合结束到下一回合开始之间，用于调整和思考的间隔规定了时限：有时四分钟，有时五分钟。这使游戏进一步脱离棋类范畴，更接近实际服役作战的样貌。战斗一旦开始，将军的大多数决断，就必须在这样短促的时间间隔内作出。（不过，开局时的筹划，我们不限制时间。）
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: As to our time-keeping, we catch a visitor with a stop-watch if we can, and if we cannot, we use a fair-sized clock with a second-hand: the player not moving says “Go,” and warns at the last two minutes, last minute, and last thirty seconds. But I think it would not be difficult to procure a cheap clock— because, of course, no one wants a very accurate agreement with Greenwich as to the length of a second—that would have minutes instead of hours and seconds instead of minutes, and that would ping at the end of every minute and discharge an alarm note at the end of the move. That would abolish the rather boring strain of time-keeping. One could just watch the fighting.
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: 至于计时，如果能抓住一位带秒表的来客，就让他负责；找不到，就用一座大小适中、带秒针的钟。不行动的玩家喊“开始”，并在还剩两分钟、一分钟、三十秒时提醒。但我想，要弄一只便宜的钟并不困难——因为，当然，谁也不需要它对一秒有多长，与格林尼治保持极其精确的一致——让表盘用分钟取代小时，用秒取代分钟；每过一分钟叮一声，回合结束时再响一次警报。那样，就能免去计时这种颇为无聊的紧张劳动，只管看战斗就行了。
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: Moreover, in our desire to bring the game to a climax, we decided that instead of a fight to a finish we would fight to some determined point, and we found very good sport in supposing that the arrival of three men of one force upon the back line of the opponent's side of the country was of such strategic importance as to determine the battle. But this form of battle we have since largely abandoned in favour of the old fight to a finish again. We found it led to one type of battle only, a massed rush at the antagonist's line, and that our arrangements of time-limits and capture and so forth had eliminated most of the concluding drag upon the game.
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: 此外，我们为了让游戏达到高潮，决定不再打到最后，而是打到某个预定的节点。我们发现，不妨假设：一支部队有三个人到达对手一侧地形的后边线，就具有足以决定战斗的战略重要性；这样玩颇有趣味。但这种战斗形式，后来又大体被我们放弃，重新采用原来打到最后的方式。因为它只会导向一种战斗：集结全军，猛冲对手的线；而我们关于时限、俘虏等等的安排，已经消除了游戏结尾大部分拖沓之处。
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: Our game was now very much in its present form. We considered at various times the possibility of introducing some complication due to the bringing up of ammunition or supplies generally, and we decided that it would add little to the interest or reality of the game. Our battles are little brisk fights in which one may suppose that all the ammunition and food needed are carried by the men themselves.
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: 我们的游戏这时已经很接近今天的样子。我们曾数次考虑，是否加入运输弹药或一般补给造成的复杂情况；最后决定，那对游戏的趣味或逼真程度都增加不了多少。我们的战斗是些短促明快的小规模战斗，完全可以假定，所需的全部弹药和食物，都由士兵自己携带。
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: But our latest development has been in the direction of killing hand to hand or taking prisoners. We found it necessary to distinguish between an isolated force and a force that was merely a projecting part of a larger force. We made a definition of isolation. After a considerable amount of trials we decided that a man or a detachment shall be considered to be isolated when there is less than half its number of its own side within a move of it. Now, in actual civilised warfare small detached bodies do not sell their lives dearly; a considerably larger force is able to make them prisoners without difficulty. Accordingly we decided that if a blue force, for example, has one or more men isolated, and a red force of at least double the strength of this isolated detachment moves up to contact with it, the blue men will be considered to be prisoners.
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: 而我们最新的发展，是在近身杀敌或俘虏方面。我们发现，必须区分孤立的部队，和只是从大部队中突出一部分的部队。因此，我们定义了“孤立”。经过相当多的试验后，我们决定：如果一个兵人或一支分队，在距其一回合行程以内，本方人数不足它自身人数的一半，就视为孤立。如今，在实际的文明战争中，脱离主力的小分队不会拼命卖出自己的性命；兵力多得多的部队，可以轻易将其俘虏。因此我们决定：例如，蓝方有一个或多个士兵孤立，而至少有这支孤立分队两倍兵力的红方部队，推进到与它接触时，这些蓝方士兵便视为俘虏。
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: That seemed fair; but so desperate is the courage and devotion of lead soldiers, that it came to this, that any small force that got or seemed likely to get isolated and caught by a superior force instead of waiting to be taken prisoners, dashed at its possible captors and slew them man for man. It was manifestly unreasonable to permit this. And in considering how best to prevent such inhuman heroisms, we were reminded of another frequent incident in our battles that also erred towards the incredible and vitiated our strategy. That was the charging of one or two isolated horse-men at a gun in order to disable it. Let me illustrate this by an incident. A force consisting of ten infantry and five cavalry with a gun are retreating across an exposed space, and a gun with thirty men, cavalry and infantry, in support comes out upon a crest into a position to fire within two feet of the retreating cavalry. The attacking player puts eight men within six inches of his gun and pushes the rest of his men a little forward to the right or left in pursuit of his enemy. In the real thing, the retreating horsemen would go off to cover with the gun, “hell for leather,” while the infantry would open out and retreat, firing. But see what happened in our imperfect form of Little War! The move of the retreating player began. Instead of retreating his whole force, he charged home with his mounted desperadoes, killed five of the eight men about the gun, and so by the rule silenced it, enabling the rest of his little body to get clean away to cover at the leisurely pace of one foot a move. This was not like any sort of warfare. In real life cavalry cannot pick out and kill its equivalent in cavalry while that equivalent is closely supported by other cavalry or infantry; a handful of troopers cannot gallop past well and abundantly manned guns in action, cut down the gunners and interrupt the fire. And yet for a time we found it a little difficult to frame simple rules to meet these two bad cases and prevent such scandalous possibilities. We did at last contrive to do so; we invented what we call the mêlée, and our revised rules in the event of a mêlée will be found set out upon a later page. They do really permit something like an actual result to hand-to-hand encounters. They abolish Horatius Cocles.
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: 这看起来很公平。然而，铅兵的勇气与献身精神实在惊人，事情就成了这样：一支小部队一旦陷入孤立，或者看来可能被优势兵力孤立并抓住，就不肯等待被俘，而会冲向可能俘虏自己的敌人，一命换一命，把他们杀掉。允许这样做，显然不合理。在考虑怎样最好地防止这种超人的英勇时，我们又想起战斗中经常发生的另一种情况，同样难以置信，也同样损害了战略：一两个孤立的骑兵，冲向一门炮，令它失去作战能力。我用一件事来说明。一支由十名步兵、五名骑兵和一门炮组成的部队，正撤过一片开阔地；对面一门炮，在三十名骑兵和步兵支援下，越过山脊，进入可以开火的位置，离撤退中的骑兵不到两英尺。进攻的玩家，把八个人放在本方炮周围六英寸以内，其余人稍稍向左或向右前进，追击敌人。若是真打，撤退的骑兵会拖着炮，拼命疾驰，逃入掩护；步兵则会散开，边打边撤。可看看我们这套不完善的小战争里发生了什么！撤退一方的回合开始了。他没有让全军后撤，而是让那些亡命骑兵冲到炮前，杀死炮旁八人中的五人，于是按规则使炮哑火，让自己那支小部队的其余人员，能以每回合一英尺的悠闲步调，从容逃入掩护。这不像任何一种战争。在现实中，骑兵不能挑出并杀死与自己人数相当的敌方骑兵，同时无视那些敌方骑兵正得到其他骑兵或步兵的密切支援；一小撮骑兵，也不可能从人员充足、运转良好的炮旁飞驰而过，砍倒炮手，打断射击。然而，我们有一段时间，确实很难制定简单规则，来处理这两种恶劣情况，防止如此荒唐的可能。最终，我们想出了办法：发明了所谓“混战”；修订后的混战规则，后文将会列出。它们确实能够让近身相遇得到某种类似实际情况的结果。它们废除了霍拉提乌斯·科克莱斯。
