text: We also found difficulties about the capturing of guns. At first we had merely provided that a gun was captured when it was out of action and four men of the opposite force were within six inches of it, but we found a number of cases for which this rule was too vague. A gun, for example, would be disabled and left with only three men within six inches; the enemy would then come up eight or ten strong within six inches on the other side, but not really reaching the gun. At the next move the original possessor of the gun would bring up half a dozen men within six inches. To whom did the gun belong? By the original wording of our rule, it might be supposed to belong to the attack which had never really touched the gun yet, and they could claim to turn it upon its original side. We had to meet a number of such cases. We met them by requiring the capturing force—or, to be precise, four men of it—actually to pass the axle of the gun before it could be taken.
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: 我们也在夺炮方面遇到了困难。起先，我们只规定：一门炮失去作战能力，而且敌方四个人在它六英寸以内时，它就被夺取了。但许多情况下，这条规则过于含混。例如，一门炮失去了作战能力，六英寸内只剩三个人；敌方随即有八到十人进入另一侧六英寸以内，却没有真正抵达炮的位置。下一回合，炮原本的主人，又调来六个人进入六英寸范围。这门炮归谁？按原规则的措辞，它似乎应当归属于那些连炮都还没有真正碰到的进攻者；他们可以宣称，要把它掉过头，向原来的本方开火。我们必须处理好几种这样的情况。解决办法，是要求夺炮部队——准确地说，其中四个人——必须实际越过炮轴，才能把炮夺走。
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: All sorts of odd little difficulties arose too, connected with the use of the guns as a shelter from fire, and very exact rules had to be made to avoid tilting the nose and raising the breech of a gun in order to use it as cover. …
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: 另外，还有各种古怪的小困难，与把炮本身当作躲避火力的掩体有关；于是，必须制定十分精确的规则，防止玩家压低炮口、抬高炮膛尾部，把炮当掩护。……
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: We still found it difficult to introduce any imitation into our game of either retreat or the surrender of men not actually taken prisoners in a mêlée. Both things were possible by the rules, but nobody did them because there was no inducement to do them. Games were apt to end obstinately with the death or capture of the last man. An inducement was needed. This we contrived by playing not for the game but for points, scoring the result of each game and counting the points towards the decision of a campaign. Our campaign was to our single game what a rubber is to a game of whist. We made the end of a war 200, 300, or 400 or more points up, according to the number of games we wanted to play, and we scored a hundred for each battle won, and in addition 1 for each infantry-man, 1½ for each cavalry-man, 10 for each gun, ½ for each man held prisoner by the enemy, and ½ for each prisoner held at the end of the game, subtracting what the antagonist scored by the same scale. Thus, when he felt the battle was hopelessly lost, he had a direct inducement to retreat any guns he could still save and surrender any men who were under the fire of the victors' guns and likely to be slaughtered, in order to minimise the score against him. And an interest was given to a skilful retreat, in which the loser not only saved points for himself but inflicted losses upon the pursuing enemy.
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: 我们仍然觉得，很难在游戏里引入任何类似撤退的行为，或让没有在混战中实际被俘的人员投降。这两件事按规则都允许，但谁也不做，因为没有动机让他们这样做。游戏往往顽固地延续到最后一人死亡或被俘。必须给人一个动机。我们的办法，是不再单纯争一局胜负，而是争积分；把每局结果计分，再用积分决定一场战役。战役与单局的关系，类似惠斯特牌的一组比赛与其中一局的关系。我们根据想打多少局，将一场战争的终点定为领先200、300、400或更多分；每赢一场战斗，记一百分，另外每名步兵记1分，每名骑兵记1½分，每门炮记10分，每个落在敌人手里的本方俘虏记½分，游戏结束时，每名自己掌握的俘虏也记½分，再减去对手按同样标准所得的分数。这样，一旦觉得战斗已经无可挽回地输了，玩家就有直接的动机，撤出还能保住的炮，让处在胜利者炮火之下、很可能被屠杀的人投降，以尽量减少净失分。高明的撤退也因而变得有意思：败方不仅为自己保存分数，还能让追击的敌人蒙受损失。

text: At first we played the game from the outset, with each player's force within sight of his antagonist; then we found it possible to hang a double curtain of casement cloth from a string stretched across the middle of the field, and we drew this back only after both sides had set out their men. Without these curtains we found the first player was at a heavy disadvantage, because he displayed all his dispositions before his opponent set down his men.
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: 起初，我们从开局就让双方兵力彼此可见；后来发现，可以在横穿战场中部的一根绳上，挂起两片窗帘布，等双方都把士兵摆好以后再拉开。没有帘子，先摆的一方就处于很不利的地位，因为对手尚未放下自己的士兵，他已经暴露了全部部署。
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: And at last our rules have reached stability, and we regard them now with the virtuous pride of men who have persisted in a great undertaking and arrived at precision after much tribulation. There is not a piece of constructive legislation in the world, not a solitary attempt to meet a complicated problem, that we do not now regard the more charitably for our efforts to get a right result from this apparently easy and puerile business of fighting with tin soldiers on the floor.
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: 终于，我们的规则稳定了。如今，我们像那些坚持完成了一项伟大事业、历尽磨难后终于达到精确的人一样，带着道德高尚的自豪看待它们。世界上无论哪一项建设性的立法，无论哪一次解决复杂问题的尝试，在我们费尽力气、要把“在地板上用锡兵打仗”这件看似轻易、孩子气的事情做好以后，都会得到我们更多的宽厚理解。
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: And so our laws all made, battles have been fought, the mere beginnings, we feel, of vast campaigns. The game has become in a dozen aspects extra ordinarily like a small real battle. The plans are made, the Country hastily surveyed, and then the curtains are closed, and the antagonists make their opening dispositions. Then the curtains are drawn back and the hostile forces come within sight of each other; the little companies and squadrons and batteries appear hurrying to their positions, the infantry deploying into long open lines, the cavalry sheltering in reserve, or galloping with the guns to favourable advance positions. In two or three moves the guns are flickering into action, a cavalry mêlée may be in progress, the plans of the attack are more or less apparent, here are men pouring out from the shelter of a wood to secure some point of vantage, and here are troops massing among farm buildings for a vigorous attack. The combat grows hot round some vital point. Move follows move in swift succession. One realises with a sickening sense of error that one is outnumbered and hard pressed here and uselessly cut off there, that one's guns are ill-placed, that one's wings are spread too widely, and that help can come only over some deadly zone of fire.
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: 就这样，我们的法则全都制定完毕，战斗也一场场打过了；在我们看来，这还不过是庞大战役的开头。这游戏在十几个方面，已异乎寻常地像一场真正的小战斗。计划做好，匆匆勘察地形，随后合上帘子，对手们各自展开初始部署。再拉开帘子，敌对部队便进入彼此视野；一支支小连队、骑兵中队、炮兵连，匆忙赶往阵位：步兵展开成长长的散兵线，骑兵藏作预备队，或与炮一同疾驰，抢占有利的前进阵位。两三个回合内，炮火就开始闪动，也许骑兵混战已经展开；进攻计划已多少显露，这里有人从树林掩护中涌出，抢占要点，那里又有部队在农场建筑间集结，准备猛攻。围绕某个要害，战况转为激烈。一回合紧接一回合，迅速推进。你会带着一种因犯错而恶心的感觉发现：此处兵力不足，受到压迫；彼处却白白被切断；炮位放错了，两翼拉得过宽，援军只能穿越某片致命的火力地带，才能赶到。
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: So the fight wears on. Guns are lost or won, hills or villages stormed or held; suddenly it grows clear that the scales are tilting beyond recovery, and the loser has nothing left but to contrive how he may get to the back line and safety with the vestiges of his command. …
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: 战斗于是继续。炮被夺走，或被夺回；山丘和村庄被攻下，或守住。忽然，你看清天平已经倾斜，再也无法挽回；败者所剩的，只有设法带着残部退到后边线，逃到安全地带。……
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: But let me, before I go on to tell of actual battles and campaigns, give here a summary of our essential rules.
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: 不过，在继续讲实际的战斗和战役之前，我先在这里归纳一下我们的基本规则。
section: II. 现代小战争的开端

text: III. The Rules
III. 规则
Here, then, are the rules of the perfect battle-game as we play it in an ordinary room.
下面，就是我们在普通房间里玩的、完善的战斗游戏的规则。
The Country
地形
(1) The Country must be arranged by one player, who, failing any other agreement, shall be selected by the toss of a coin.
（1）地形须由一名玩家布置；如无其他约定，就以掷硬币决定由谁布置。
(2) The other player shall then choose which side of the field he will fight from.
（2）然后，由另一名玩家选择从战场的哪一侧作战。

(3) The Country must be disturbed as little as possible in each move: Nothing in the Country shall be moved or set aside deliberately to facilitate the firing of guns. A player must not lie across the Country so as to crush or disturb the Country if his opponent objects. Whatever is moved by accident shall be replaced after the end of the move.
（3）每回合对地形的扰动，应尽可能少。不得为了便于开炮，而故意移动或移开地形中的任何东西。如果对手反对，玩家不得横卧在地形上，压坏或扰乱地形。任何意外移动的东西，都应在回合结束后放回原处。
The Move
回合
(1) After the Country is made and the sides chosen, then (and not until then) the players shall toss for the first move.
（1）地形布置好、双方选定以后，玩家才可以掷硬币，决定谁先行动；在这之前不行。

(2) If there is no curtain, the player winning the toss, hereafter called the First Player, shall next arrange his men along his back line, as he chooses. Any men he may place behind or in front of his back line shall count in the subsequent move as if they touched the back line at its nearest point. The Second Player shall then do the same. But if a curtain is available both first and second player may put down their men at the same time. Both players may take unlimited time for the putting down of their men; if there is a curtain it is drawn back when they are ready, and the game then begins.
（2）如果没有帘子，掷币获胜的玩家，以下称为先手玩家，应当接着按自己的意愿，沿本方后边线布置士兵。他放在后边线前面或后面的士兵，在随后回合里，都视为接触着后边线上距自己最近的一点。然后，后手玩家照做。如果有帘子，先后手双方则可以同时放置士兵。双方布置士兵的时间都不受限制；如有帘子，待双方准备妥当后拉开，游戏随即开始。

(3) The subsequent moves after the putting down are timed. The length of time given for each move is determined by the size of the forces engaged. About a minute should be allowed for moving 30 men and a minute for each gun. Thus for a force of 110 men and 3 guns, moved by one player, seven minutes is an ample allowance. As the battle progresses and the men are killed off, the allowance is reduced as the players may agree. The player about to move stands at attention a yard behind his back line until the timekeeper says “Go.” He then proceeds to make his move until time is up. He must instantly stop at the cry of “Time.” Warning should be given by the timekeeper two minutes, one minute, and thirty seconds before time is up. There will be an interval before the next move, during which any disturbance of the Country can be rearranged and men accidentally overturned replaced in a proper attitude. This interval must not exceed five or four minutes, as may be agreed upon.

（3）布置完成后的各回合，都要计时。每回合给予的时间，取决于参战兵力的大小。移动30人应当给大约一分钟，每门炮另给一分钟。因此，一位玩家指挥110人、3门炮，七分钟就十分充裕。随着战斗进行、人员阵亡，可按双方约定缩短时限。即将行动的玩家，须在本方后边线后一码处立正，等计时员喊“开始”。随后，他便行动，直到时限到达；一听“时间到”，必须立刻停止。计时员应在结束前两分钟、一分钟和三十秒分别提醒。下一回合开始前，应有一段间隔，供人恢复受扰动的地形，把意外翻倒的士兵重新放正。这一间隔不得超过双方约定的五分钟或四分钟。

(4) Guns must not be fired before the second move of the first player—not counting the “putting down” as a move. Thus the first player puts down, then the second player, the first player moves, then the second player, and the two forces are then supposed to come into effective range of each other and the first player may open fire if he wishes to do so.
（4）先手玩家的第二回合以前，不得开炮；“布置士兵”不算一回合。因此，先手先布置，后手再布置；先手行动，后手再行动；这时，双方才视为进入彼此的有效射程，先手如愿意，就可以开火。
(5) In making his move a player must move or fire his guns if he wants to do so, before moving his men. To this rule of “Guns First” there is to be no exception.
（5）玩家行动时，若要移动炮或用炮射击，必须先做这些，再移动士兵。“炮先行动”这条规则，不容例外。
(6) Every soldier may be moved and every gun moved or fired at each move, subject to the following rules:
（6）每回合，每个士兵都可以移动，每门炮都可以移动或射击，但须遵守以下规则：
Mobility of the Various Arms
各兵种的机动能力
(Each player must be provided with two pieces of string, one two feet in length and the other six inches.)
（每位玩家必须备有两根绳子，一根长两英尺，另一根长六英寸。）
(1) An infantry-man may be moved a foot or any less distance at each move.
（1）每回合，一名步兵可以移动一英尺，或者任何小于一英尺的距离。
(2) A cavalry-man may be moved two feet or any less distance at each move.
（2）每回合，一名骑兵可以移动两英尺，或者任何小于两英尺的距离。
(3) A gun is in action if there are at least four men of its own side within six inches of it. If there are not at least four men within that distance, it can neither be moved nor fired.
（3）一门炮周围六英寸内，至少有四名本方士兵，才处于可作战状态。如果这一距离内不足四人，它既不能移动，也不能开火。

(4) If a gun is in action it can either be moved or fired at each move, but not both. If it is fired, it may fire as many as four shots in each move. It may be swung round on its axis (the middle point of its wheel axle) to take aim, provided the Country about it permits; it may be elevated or depressed, and the soldiers about it may, at the discretion of the firer, be made to lie down in their places to facilitate its handling. Moreover, soldiers who have got in front of the fire of their own guns may lie down while the guns fire over them. At the end of the move the gun must be left without altering its elevation and pointing in the direction of the last shot. And after firing, two men must be placed exactly at the end of the trail of the gun, one on either side in a line directly behind the wheels. So much for firing. If the gun is moved and not fired, then at least four men who are with the gun must move up with it to its new position, and be placed within six inches of it in its new position. The gun itself must be placed trail forward and the muzzle pointing back in the direction from which it came, and so it must remain until it is swung round on its axis to fire. Obviously the distance which a gun can move will be determined by the men it is with; if there are at least four cavalry-men with it, they can take the gun two feet, but if there are fewer cavalry-men than four and the rest infantry, or no cavalry and all infantry, the gun will be movable only one foot.

（4）处于可作战状态的炮，每回合可以移动或射击，但不能两者兼做。如果射击，每回合最多可打四发。在周围地形允许的情况下，可以绕炮的轴心，也就是轮轴中点，转动炮来瞄准；可以调整仰角和俯角；为便于操作，开炮的人还可自行决定，让炮周围的士兵在原地卧倒。此外，处于本方炮火前方的士兵，也可以卧倒，让炮弹从头顶飞过。回合结束时，炮的仰角不得改变，必须仍指向最后一发的射击方向。射击后，还必须在炮架尾端的准确位置放两名士兵，两侧各一，位于炮轮正后方的一条线上。关于射击，规定如此。如果炮移动而不射击，则伴随该炮的至少四名士兵，必须与炮一起前进到新位置，并被放在炮的新位置六英寸以内。炮本身必须炮架尾端向前，炮口向后，指向来时的方向；在下次绕轴转向开火以前，必须保持这种姿态。显然，一门炮能移动多远，取决于伴随它的士兵：如果至少有四名骑兵，他们能带着炮走两英尺；若骑兵不足四名、其余是步兵，或者完全没有骑兵、全是步兵，那么炮只能移动一英尺。

(5) Every man must be placed fairly clear of hills, buildings, trees, guns, etc. He must not be jammed into interstices, and either player may insist upon a clear distance between any man and any gun or other object of at least one-sixteenth of an inch. Nor must men be packed in contact with men. A space of one-sixteenth of an inch should be kept between them.
（5）每个士兵都必须与山丘、建筑、树木、炮等保持明确的空隙。不得将士兵挤塞在缝隙里；任何一位玩家，都可以要求任何士兵与任何炮或其他物体之间，至少留出十六分之一英寸的净距离。士兵也不得互相紧贴，彼此应当保持十六分之一英寸的间隔。

(6) When men are knocked over by a shot they are dead, and as many men are dead as a shot knocks over or causes to fall or to lean so that they would fall if unsupported. But if a shot strikes a man but does not knock him over, he is dead, provided the shot has not already killed a man. But a shot cannot kill more than one man without knocking him over, and if it touches several without oversetting them, only the first touched is dead and the others are not incapacitated. A shot that rebounds from or glances off any object and touches a man, kills him; it kills him even if it simply rolls to his feet, subject to what has been said in the previous sentence.

（6）被一发炮弹击倒的士兵，算作死亡。一发炮弹打倒多少人，使多少人跌落，或倾斜到失去支撑就会倒下的程度，就算杀死多少人。但是，炮弹击中一个士兵却没把他打倒，他也算死亡，条件是这一发尚未杀死过其他人。不过，一发炮弹在没有把人打倒的情况下，不能杀死一个以上的士兵；如果它碰到几个人，却没把他们掀倒，那么只有第一个被碰到的人死亡，其余人并未失去行动能力。炮弹从任何物体上弹回或擦过，再碰到士兵，也会杀死他；即使只是滚到他的脚边，也能杀死他，但须受前一句所述限制。
Hand-to-Hand Fighting and Capturing
近身战斗与俘虏

(1) A man or a body of men which has less than half its own number of men on its own side within a move of it, is said to be isolated. But if there is at least half its number of men of its own side within a move of it, it is not isolated; it is supported.
（1）一个士兵或一支部队，如果在距离自己一回合行程内，本方人数不足自身人数的一半，就称为“孤立”。但是，如果这一范围内的本方人数至少达到自身人数的一半，就“不孤立”，而是“有支援”。
(2) Men may be moved up into virtual contact (one-eighth of an inch or closer) with men of the opposite side. They must then be left until the end of the move.
（2）士兵可以被移动到与敌方士兵近乎接触的位置，即相距八分之一英寸或更近。此后，必须让他们留在原处，直到回合结束。

(3) At the end of the move, if there are men of the side that has just moved in contact with any men of the other side, they constitute a mêlée. All the men in contact, and any other men within six inches of the men in contact, measuring from any point of their persons, weapons, or horses, are supposed to take part in the mêlée. At the end of the move the two players examine the mêlée and dispose of the men concerned according to the following rules:—
（3）回合结束时，如果刚刚行动的一方，有士兵与另一方的任何士兵接触，他们就构成一场“混战”。所有相互接触的士兵，以及距这些接触者六英寸以内的其他士兵，都视为参加混战；距离可从兵人的身体、武器或马匹的任何一点量起。回合结束后，双方玩家检查混战，并按以下规则处理相关士兵：

Either the numbers taking part in the mêlée on each side are equal or unequal.
参加混战的双方人数，要么相等，要么不等。
(a) If they are equal, all the men on both sides are killed.
（a）如果人数相等，双方所有参加者一律死亡。
(b) If they are unequal, then the inferior force is either isolated or (measuring from the points of contact) not isolated.
（b）如果人数不等，人数较少的一方，要么是孤立的，要么从接触点量起并不孤立。

(b1) If it is isolated (see 1 above), then as many men become prisoners as the inferior force is less in numbers than the superior force, and the rest kill each a man and are killed. Thus nine against eleven have two taken prisoners, and each side seven men dead. Four of the eleven remain with two prisoners. One may put this in another way by saying that the two forces kill each other off, man for man, until one force is double the other, which is then taken prisoner. Seven men kill seven men, and then four are left with two.
（b1）如果人数较少的一方是孤立的（见上文第1条），那么，双方人数相差多少，较少的一方就有多少人被俘；其余人员各杀死一人，同时自己也被杀死。例如，九人对十一人，九人一方有两人被俘，双方各死七人；十一人中，剩下四人，带着两名俘虏。也可以换一种说法：双方一人换一人地互相杀死，直到一方人数达到另一方两倍，后者便被俘。七个人杀死七个人，最后剩下四人对两人。
(b2) But if the inferior force is not isolated (see 1 above), then each man of the inferior force kills a man of the superior force and is himself killed.
（b2）但如果人数较少的一方并不孤立（见上文第1条），那么，该方每人杀死人数较多一方的一人，同时自己也被杀死。

And the player who has just completed the move, the one who has charged, decides, when there is any choice, which men in the mêlée, both of his own and of his antagonist, shall die and which shall be prisoners or captors.
如果存在选择，刚完成这一回合、也就是发起冲锋的玩家，可以决定混战中本方与敌方的哪些人死亡，哪些人成为俘虏或俘获者。

All these arrangements are made after the move is over, in the interval between the moves, and the time taken for the adjustment does not count as part of the usual interval for consideration. It is extra time.
以上一切处理，都在回合结束后、两回合之间的间隔内完成；用于这种调整的时间，不计入通常留给思考的间隔，而是额外时间。

The player next moving may, if he has taken prisoners, move these prisoners. Prisoners may be sent under escort to the rear or wherever the capturer directs, and one man within six inches of any number of prisoners up to seven can escort these prisoners and go with them. Prisoners are liberated by the death of any escort there may be within six inches of them, but they may not be moved by the player of their own side until the move following that in which the escort is killed. Directly prisoners are taken they are supposed to be disarmed, and if they are liberated they cannot fight until they are rearmed. In order to be rearmed they must re turn to the back line of their own side. An escort having conducted prisoners to the back line, and so beyond the reach of liberation, may then return into the fighting line.

接下来行动的玩家，如已抓到俘虏，可以移动这些俘虏。俘虏可以由人押送到后方，或押往俘获者指定的任何地方；一个士兵，只要在俘虏六英寸以内，就可以押送任意不超过七名俘虏，并与他们同行。如果距俘虏六英寸内的押送者被杀，俘虏就被解放；但本方玩家，要到押送者被杀的下一回合，才能移动他们。士兵一被俘，就视为已被缴械；即使获释，在重新武装以前，也不能战斗。要重新武装，就必须返回本方后边线。押送者将俘虏带到后边线，使他们脱离可能被解救的范围后，就可以回到战斗线上。

Prisoners once made cannot fight until they have returned to their back line. It follows, therefore, that if after the adjudication of a mêlée a player moves up more men into touch with the survivors of this first mêlée, and so constitutes a second mêlée, any prisoners made in the first mêlée will not count as combatants in the second mêlée. Thus if A moves up nineteen men into a mêlée with thirteen of B's—B having only five in support,—A makes six prisoners, kills seven men, and has seven of his own killed. If, now, B can move up fourteen men into mêlée with A's victorious survivors, which he may be able to do by bringing the five into contact, and getting nine others within six inches of them, no count is made of the six of B's men who are prisoners in the hands of A. They are disarmed. B, therefore, has fourteen men in the second mêlée and A twelve, B makes two prisoners, kills ten of A's men, and has ten of his own killed. But now the six prisoners originally made by A are left without an escort, and are therefore recaptured by B. But they must go to B's back line and return before they can fight again. So, as the outcome of these two mêlées, there are six of B's men going as released prisoners to his back line whence they may return into the battle, two of A's men prisoners in the hands of B, one of B's staying with them as escort, and three of B's men still actively free for action. A, at a cost of nineteen men, has disposed of seventeen of B's men for good, and of six or seven, according to whether B keeps his prisoners in his fighting line or not, temporarily.

士兵一旦被俘，在返回本方后边线之前，就不能战斗。因此，如果在裁定一场混战之后，某位玩家再调来人员，与第一次混战的幸存者接触，从而构成第二次混战，那么，第一次混战中的俘虏，不算第二次混战的战斗人员。例如，A调来十九人与B的十三人混战，而B只有五人支援，A就抓六个俘虏，杀七人，本方也死七人。这时，如果B能够调来十四人，与A的获胜幸存者再打一场混战——他或许可以让那五人上前接触，再把另外九人调到他们六英寸以内——则已经落在A手中、成为俘虏的B方六人，不计入兵力。他们已被缴械。因此，第二场混战中，B有十四人，A有十二人；B俘虏两人，杀死A方十人，自己也死十人。但这时，原先被A俘虏的六人，身旁已没有押送者，所以被B解救。不过，在重新战斗之前，他们必须先回B的后边线，再回来。于是，两场混战的结果如下：B有六人作为获释俘虏，前往本方后边线，此后可以返回战斗；A有两人成为B方俘虏，B有一人留下押送他们，另有三人仍可自由作战。A以十九人的代价，永久清除了B的十七人，另暂时清除了六人或七人，具体取决于B是否把俘虏留在战斗线上。

(4) Any isolated body may hoist the white flag and surrender at any time.
（4）任何孤立部队，都可以随时举白旗投降。

(5) A gun is captured when there is no man whatever of its original side within six inches of it, and when at least four men of the antagonist side have moved up to it and have passed its wheel axis going in the direction of their attack. This latter point is important. An antagonist's gun may be out of action, and you may have a score of men coming up to it and within six inches of it, but it is not yet captured; and you may have brought up a dozen men all round the hostile gun, but if there is still one enemy just out of their reach and within six inches of the end of the trail of the gun, that gun is not captured: it is still in dispute and out of action, and you may not fire it or move it at the next move. But once a gun is fully captured, it follows all the rules of your own guns.

（5）一门炮在以下条件下被夺取：原属一方在炮六英寸内，已一个人也没有；敌方至少四人已来到炮旁，并沿进攻方向越过炮的轮轴。后一点很重要。一门敌炮也许已经失去作战能力，你也许已有二十个人接近它，进入六英寸以内，但它尚未被夺取；即使你把十二个人带到敌炮周围，只要仍有一个敌人在他们够不到的地方，同时处于炮架尾端六英寸以内，那门炮就没有被夺取：归属仍有争议，而且无法作战；下一回合，你不能用它开火，也不能移动它。但是，炮一旦完全被夺取，就按本方炮的全部规则行动。
Varieties of the Battle-Game
战斗游戏的几种类型
You may play various types of game.
你可以玩不同类型的游戏。

(1) One is the Fight to the Finish. You move in from any points you like on the back line and try to kill, capture, or drive over his back line the whole of the enemy's force. You play the game for points; you score 100 for the victory, and 10 for every gun you hold or are in a position to take, 1½ for every cavalry-man, 1 for every infantry-man still alive and uncaptured, ½ for every man of yours prisoner in the hands of the enemy, and ½ for every prisoner you have taken. If the battle is still undecided when both forces are reduced below fifteen men, the battle is drawn and the 100 points for victory are divided.

（1）一种是“决战到底”。你可以从本方后边线上任何喜欢的位置进入，努力把敌军全部杀死、俘虏，或赶过敌方自己的后边线。这种游戏按积分计算：获胜得100分；每门掌握在你手中、或你处于能够夺取它的位置的炮，得10分；每名骑兵得1½分；每名仍活着、未被俘的步兵得1分；每名落在敌人手里的本方俘虏得½分；每名你抓获的俘虏，也得½分。如果双方兵力都已降到十五人以下，战斗仍未决出胜负，就算平局，胜利的100分由双方平分。
Text in the original image (transcription) A DRAW
图内文字汉译 平局
Note.—This game can be fought with any sized force, but if it is fought with less than 50 a side, the minimum must be 10 a side.
注：这种游戏可以使用任何规模的兵力，但如果每方不到50人，每方最低兵力就必须是10人。

(2) The Blow at the Rear game is decided when at least three men of one force reach any point in the back line of their antagonist. He is then supposed to have suffered a strategic defeat, and he must retreat his entire force over the back line in six moves, i.e. six of his moves. Anything left on the field after six moves capitulates to the victor. Points count as in the preceding game, but this lasts a shorter time and is better adapted to a cramped country with a short back line. With a long rear line the game is simply a rush at some weak point in the first player's line by the entire cavalry brigade of the second player. Instead of making the whole back line available for the Blow at the Rear, the middle or either half may be taken.

（2）“直击后方”游戏，在一方至少三人到达敌方后边线任意一点时，就分出胜负。此时，敌方视为遭受战略失败，必须在六回合内，也就是本方的六个回合内，将全部兵力撤过后边线。六回合后，任何还留在战场上的人员和装备，都向胜者投降。计分与前一种游戏相同；但这种玩法历时更短，更适合地形狭窄、后边线较短的场地。如果后边线很长，游戏就只是后手玩家将整个骑兵旅，向先手玩家阵线的某个薄弱点猛冲。供“直击后方”使用的后边线，也可以不是整条，而只取中央部分，或取其中任意一半。

(3) In the Defensive Game, a force, the defenders, two-thirds as strong as its antagonist, tries to prevent the latter arriving, while still a quarter of its ori ginal strength, upon the defender's back line. The Country must be made by one or both of the players before it is determined which shall be defender. The players then toss for choice of sides, and the winner of the toss becomes the defender. He puts out his force over the field on his own side, anywhere up to the distance of one move off the middle line—that is to say, he must not put any man within one move of the middle line, but he may do so anywhere on his own side of that limit,—and then the loser of the toss becomes first player, and sets out his men a move from his back line. The defender may open fire forthwith; he need not wait until after the second move of the first player, as the second player has to do.

（3）在“防御战”中，防守方的兵力是对手的三分之二；他们试图阻止对方在仍保有原始兵力四分之一时，到达防守方的后边线。在决定谁防守之前，必须先由一位或两位玩家布置地形。然后，双方掷币选择阵营，掷币获胜者成为防守方。他可以将兵力部署在本方一侧的战场上，直到距中线一回合行程的位置；也就是说，任何士兵都不得放在距中线一回合行程以内，但在这一限制之外、本方一侧的任意位置都可以部署。然后，掷币输的一方成为先手，把士兵布置在距本方后边线一回合行程的位置。防守方可以立刻开火，无须像通常的后手玩家一样，等到先手第二回合之后。
Composition of Forces
兵力组成

Except in the above cases, or when otherwise agreed upon, the forces engaged shall be equal in number and similar in composition. The methods of handicapping are obvious. A slight inequality (chances of war) may be arranged between equal players by leaving out 12 men on each side and tossing with a pair of dice to see how many each player shall take of these. The best arrangement and proportion of the forces is in small bodies of about 20 to 25 infantry-men and 12 to 15 cavalry to a gun. Such a force can manœuvre comfortably on a front of 4 or 5 feet. Most of our games have been played with about 80 infantry, 50 cavalry, 3 or 4 naval guns, and a field gun on either side, or with smaller proportional forces. We have played excellent games on an eighteen-foot battlefield with over two hundred men and six guns a side. A player may, of course, rearrange his forces to suit his own convenience; brigade all or most of his cavalry into a powerful striking force, or what not. But more guns proportionally lead to their being put out of action too early for want of men; a larger proportion of infantry makes the game sluggish, and more cavalry—because of the difficulty of keeping large bodies of this force under cover—leads simply to early heavy losses by gunfire and violent and disastrous charging. The composition of a force may, of course, be varied considerably. One good Fight to a Finish game we tried as follows: We made the Country, tossed for choice, and then drew curtains across the middle of the field. Each player then selected his force from the available soldiers in this way: he counted infantry as 1 each, cavalry as 1½, and a gun as 10, and, taking whatever he liked in whatever position he liked, he made up a total of 150. He could, for instance, choose 100 infantry and 5 guns, or 100 cavalry and no guns, or 60 infantry, 40 cavalry, and 3 guns. In the result, a Boer-like cavalry force of 80 with 3 guns suffered defeat at the hands of 110 infantry with 4.

除上述情况，或另有约定外，参战双方的人数应相等，组成应相似。让子的办法显而易见。水平相同的玩家，也可以各留下12人，再掷两枚骰子，看每位玩家能从这12人中取多少，以安排一点轻微的不平等，模拟战争的偶然。最佳编组和比例，是每门炮配一个小队，约有20至25名步兵、12至15名骑兵。这样一支部队，能够在4或5英尺宽的正面上从容机动。我们的大多数游戏，每方约用80名步兵、50名骑兵、3或4门舰炮，以及一门野战炮；或者，按相同比例使用较小兵力。我们曾在十八英尺的战场上，以每方两百余人、六门炮，玩出极好的游戏。玩家当然可以按自己的便利重新编组：把全部或大部分骑兵合编为一支强大突击队，或者采取别的办法。但是，炮的比例过高，会因人员不足，而使它们过早失去作战能力；步兵比例更高，会让游戏迟缓；更多骑兵，则因为大部队骑兵难以保持隐蔽，只会导致较早遭受炮火重创，发动猛烈而灾难性的冲锋。当然，部队组成可以有相当大的变化。我们试过一种很好的“决战到底”玩法：先布置地形，掷币选边，再沿战场中线拉起帘子。接着，每位玩家用如下方法，从现有玩具士兵中选取兵力：每个步兵算1，每个骑兵算1½，一门炮算10；可以任意选择兵种，放在任何喜欢的位置，凑到总数150。例如，他可以选100名步兵、5门炮，或100名骑兵、不配炮，或60名步兵、40名骑兵、3门炮。结果，一支布尔人式的80骑兵、3门炮的部队，被110步兵、4门炮击败了。
Size of the Soldiers
士兵的尺寸

The soldiers used should be all of one size. The best British makers have standardised sizes, and sell infantry and cavalry in exactly proportioned dimensions; the infantry being nearly two inches tall. There is a lighter, cheaper make of perhaps an inch and a half high that is also available. Foreign-made soldiers are of variable sizes.
所用士兵，尺寸应当一致。英国最好的制造商已经统一了尺寸，出售的步兵和骑兵，比例完全相称；步兵高近两英寸。另外，也有一种更轻、更便宜、高约一英寸半的兵人可以使用。外国制造的士兵，尺寸则各不相同。

IV. The Battle of Hook's Farm
IV. 胡克农场之战

And now, having given all the exact science of our war game, having told something of the development of this warfare, let me here set out the particulars of an exemplary game. And suddenly your author changes. He changes into what perhaps he might have been—under different circumstances. His inky fingers become large, manly hands, his drooping scholastic back stiffens, his elbows go out, his etiolated complexion corrugates and darkens, his moustaches increase and grow and spread, and curl up horribly; a large, red scar, a sabre cut, grows lurid over one eye. He expands—all over he expands. He clears his throat startlingly, lugs at the still growing ends of his moustache, and says, with just a faint and fading doubt in his voice as to whether he can do it, “Yas, Sir!”

现在，我们的战争游戏的全部精确科学已经交代过，这种作战方式的发展，也说了一些；让我接着列出一局示范游戏的具体经过。突然，你的作者变了。他变成了另一种境遇下，他本可能成为的那个人。他沾着墨水的手指，变成又大又有男子气概的手；学究式的佝偻后背挺直了，双肘向外张开；原本苍白的面色，皱起来、黑下去；胡须增多、增长、扩展开，凶恶地翘起；一道大大的、红色的刀疤，在一只眼睛上方显得分外狰狞。他膨胀起来，全身都膨胀起来。他令人一惊地清了清嗓子，拉扯着还在不断生长的胡须梢；声音里，只有一丝微弱而渐渐消失的疑虑，怀疑自己能不能做得到。他说道：“是，先生！”

Now for a while you listen to General H. G. W., of the Blue Army. You hear tales of victory. The photographs of the battlefields are by a woman war-correspondent, A. C. W., a daring ornament of her sex. I vanish. I vanish, but I will return. Here, then, is the story of the battle of Hook's Farm.
现在，请暂且听蓝军H. G. W.将军讲话。你将听到胜利的故事。战场照片，是一位女战地记者A. C. W.拍摄的，她是一位大胆、为女性增光的人物。我消失了。我消失了，但会回来。下面，就是胡克农场战斗的故事。

“The affair of Hook's Farm was one of those brisk little things that did so much to build up my early reputation. I did remarkably well, though perhaps it is not my function to say so. The enemy was slightly stronger, both in cavalry and infantry, than myself[]; he had the choice of position, and opened the ball. Nevertheless I routed him. I had with me a compact little force of 3 guns, 48 infantry, and 25 horse. My instructions were to clear up the country to the east of Firely Church.
“胡克农场一役，是那种干脆利落的小战斗，正是它们，为我早年的声誉奠定了重要基础。我干得非常出色，虽然这或许不该由我自己来说。敌方的骑兵和步兵，都比我略多一些[]；他有选阵地之权，又先开了场。尽管如此，我还是把他打得大败。我手下是一支紧凑的小部队：3门炮，48名步兵，25名骑兵。我的命令，是肃清Firely教堂以东的地带。
[ A slight but pardonable error on the part of the gallant gentleman. The forces were exactly equal.]
[ 这位英勇的绅士，犯了一个轻微却可以原谅的错误。双方兵力完全相等。]

“We came very speedily into touch. I discovered the enemy advancing upon Hook's Farm and Firely Church, evidently with the intention of holding those two positions and giving me a warm welcome. I have by me a photograph or so of the battlefield and also a little sketch I used upon the field. They will give the intelligent reader a far better idea of the encounter than any so-called ‘fine writing’ can do.
“我们很快就接触上了。我发现敌人正向胡克农场和Firely教堂推进，显然打算占据这两处，热烈地欢迎我。我这里留有一两张战场照片，还有一幅当时在战场上用过的略图。聪明的读者，从这些东西里，会比从任何所谓的‘华丽文笔’中，更清楚地了解这一遭遇。

“The original advance of the enemy was through the open country behind Firely Church and Hook's Farm; I sighted him between the points marked A A and B B, and his force was divided into two columns, with very little cover or possibility of communication between them if once the intervening ground was under fire. I reckoned about 22 to his left and 50 or 60 to his right.[] Evidently he meant to seize both Firely Church and Hook's Farm, get his guns into action, and pound my little force to pieces while it was still practically in the open. He could reach both these admirable positions before I could hope to get a man there. There was no effective cover whatever upon my right that would have permitted an advance up to the church, and so I decided to concentrate my whole force in a rush upon Hook's Farm, while I staved off his left with gun fire. I do not believe any strategist whatever could have bettered that scheme. My guns were at the points marked D C E, each with five horsemen, and I deployed my infantry in a line between D and E. The rest of my cavalry I ordered to advance on Hook's Farm from C. I have shown by arrows on the sketch the course I proposed for my guns. The gun E was to go straight for its assigned position, and get into action at once. C was not to risk capture or being put out of action; its exact position was to be determined by Red's rapidity in getting up to the farm, and it was to halt and get to work directly it saw any chance of effective fire.

“敌人最初穿过Firely教堂和胡克农场后方的开阔地前进；我在标记为A A和B B的点之间发现了他。他的兵力分为两列；一旦中间地带受到火力控制，两列之间就几乎没有掩护，也很难联络。我估计，他左边约22人，右边50或60人。[]他显然想同时夺取Firely教堂和胡克农场，把炮投入战斗，趁我的小部队还几乎完全暴露时，将它轰成碎片。他能抢在我有望把一人派到那里之前，抵达这两处极好的阵地。我的右翼完全没有足以掩护向教堂推进的有效遮蔽物，所以我决定，集中全部兵力猛扑胡克农场，同时用炮火挡住他的左翼。我不相信任何战略家，能拟出比这更好的方案。我的炮分别位于D、C、E各点，每门配五名骑兵；步兵则展开在D、E两点之间。我命令其余骑兵从C向胡克农场推进。我在略图上用箭头画出了各门炮预定的路线。E炮应直赴指定位置，立刻投入战斗。C炮不可冒着被夺取或丧失作战能力的风险前进；它的确切阵位，要看红方抵近农场的速度，一看到有效射击机会，就应停下开火。
[ Here again the gallant gentleman errs; this time he magnifies.]
[ 这位英勇的绅士，又弄错了；这一次，他夸大了。]

“Red had now sighted us. Throughout the affair he showed a remarkably poor stomach for gun-fire, and this was his undoing. Moreover, he was tempted by the poorness of our cover on our right to attempt to outflank and enfilade us there. Accordingly, partly to get cover from our two central guns and partly to outflank us, he sent the whole of his left wing to the left of Firely Church, where, except for the gun, it became almost a negligible quantity. The gun came out between the church and the wood into a position from which it did a considerable amount of mischief to the infantry on our right, and nearly drove our rightmost gun in upon its supports. Meanwhile, Red's two guns on his right came forward to Hook's Farm, rather badly supported by his infantry.

“此时，红方也看见我们了。整个战斗中，他对炮火都表现出惊人的畏缩，正是这一点毁了他。此外，他看到我们右翼掩护薄弱，便受了引诱，企图从那里迂回，沿纵向扫射我军。因此，一方面为了躲开我们中央两门炮，另一方面为了迂回，他把整个左翼派到Firely教堂左边；除那门炮以外，这支兵力几乎变得无足轻重。那门炮从教堂与树林之间出来，进入一个能够重创我们右翼步兵的位置，差点把我们最右边的炮，逼回后方的支援部队当中。与此同时，红方右翼的两门炮向胡克农场前进，他的步兵给予的支援却相当糟糕。

“Once they got into position there I perceived that we should be done for, and accordingly I rushed every available man forward in a vigorous counter attack, and my own two guns came lumbering up to the farmhouse corners, and got into the wedge of shelter close behind the house before his could open fire. His fire met my advance, littering the gentle grass slope with dead, and then, hot behind the storm of shell, and even as my cavalry gathered to charge his guns, he charged mine. I was amazed beyond measure at that rush, knowing his sabres to be slightly outnumbered by mine. In another moment all the level space round the farmhouse was a whirling storm of slashing cavalry, and then we found ourselves still holding on, with half a dozen prisoners, and the farmyard a perfect shambles of horses and men. The mêlée was over. His charge had failed, and, after a brief breathing-space for my shot-torn infantry to come up, I led on the counter attack. It was brilliantly successful; a hard five minutes with bayonet and sabre, and his right gun was in our hands and his central one in jeopardy.

“我看出，一旦他们在那里占好阵位，我们就完了。因此，我让所有可用人员，在一次猛烈的反击中冲上前去；本方另外两门炮，也隆隆地挪到农舍墙角，在他的炮来得及开火以前，钻进房屋紧后方那一楔形的掩护区。他的炮火迎击我的推进，让平缓草坡上布满死者；紧接炮弹风暴，在我的骑兵正集结、准备冲击他的炮时，他却冲向了我的炮。那一冲，令我惊讶万分，因为我知道，他的马刀比我的略少。转眼间，农舍四周的平地，就成了骑兵挥刀厮杀、旋转翻腾的风暴；随后，我们发现，自己仍守住阵地，抓了六个左右的俘虏，而农场院子，已成为人马横尸的屠场。混战结束了。他的冲锋失败；我稍歇片刻，等被炮火打得七零八落的步兵跟上，就率军反击。反击极为成功：刺刀与马刀艰苦拼杀五分钟，他右翼的炮，便落入我们手中，中央那门也岌岌可危。

“And now Red was seized with that most fatal disease of generals, indecision. He would neither abandon his lost gun nor adequately attack it. He sent forward a feeble little infantry attack, that we cut up with the utmost ease, taking several prisoners, made a disastrous demonstration from the church, and then fell back altogether from the gentle hill on which Hook Farm is situated to a position beside and behind an exposed cottage on the level. I at once opened out into a long crescent, with a gun at either horn, whose crossfire completely destroyed his chances of retreat from this ill-chosen last stand, and there presently we disabled his second gun. I now turned my attention to his still largely unbroken right, from which a gun had maintained a galling fire on us throughout the fight. I might still have had some stiff work getting an attack home to the church, but Red had had enough of it, and now decided to relieve me of any further exertion by a precipitate retreat. My gun to the right of Hook's Farm killed three of his flying men, but my cavalry were too badly cut up for an effective pursuit, and he got away to the extreme left of his original positions with about 6 infantry-men, 4 cavalry, and 1 gun. He went none too soon. Had he stayed, it would have been only a question of time before we shot him to pieces and finished him altogether.”

“这时，红方染上了将军们最致命的疾病：犹豫不决。他既不放弃已经丢掉的炮，也不充分进攻它。他派出一小股软弱的步兵进攻，我们轻而易举地将其打垮，抓了几个俘虏；他又从教堂方向作了一次灾难性的佯动，随后便从胡克农场所在的缓坡上全面退却，退到平地上一间暴露的小屋旁边和后面。我立即展开为一个长长的新月形，两尖各有一门炮，交叉火力彻底断绝了他从这处选错的最后阵地撤退的可能。不久，我们就使他的第二门炮失去作战能力。随后，我把注意力转向他那仍大体完整的右翼；整场战斗中，那里的炮一直用恼人的火力袭扰我们。要把进攻推进到教堂跟前，也许还得费些力气；不过，红方已经受够了，决定仓皇撤退，免得我再费力。胡克农场右边的那门本方炮，杀死了他逃跑中的三人；但我的骑兵已被打得太惨，无法有效追击。他带着约6名步兵、4名骑兵、1门炮，逃到自己原阵地最左端。他走得并不算早。倘若留下，我们迟早会将他轰碎，彻底消灭。”
