So far, and a little vaingloriously, the general. Let me now shrug my shoulders and shake him off, and go over this battle he describes a little more exactly with the help of the photographs. The battle is a small, compact game of the Fight-to-a-Finish type, and it was arranged as simply as possible in order to permit of a full and exact explanation.
以上，就是将军那略带虚荣的叙述。现在，让我耸耸肩，把他甩掉，借助照片，更精确地回看他描述的这场战斗。这是一局规模小而紧凑的“决战到底”游戏；为了能够作出完整、准确的说明，布置得尽可能简单。
Fig. 6b.—BATTLE OF HOOK’S FARM. Position of armies at end of Blue’s third move. (See page 81.)
图6b——胡克农场之战。蓝方第三回合结束时双方的位置。（见第81页。）
Fig. 7.—BATTLE OF HOOK’S FARM. Showing the frantic rush of Red’s left wing across the open to join the main body. (See page 82.)
图7——胡克农场之战。红方左翼疯狂冲过开阔地，试图与主力会合。（见第82页。）

Figure 1 shows the country of the battlefield put out; on the right is the church, on the left (near the centre of the plate) is the farm. In the hollow between the two is a small outbuilding. Directly behind the farm in the line of vision is another outbuilding. This is more distinctly seen in other photographs. Behind, the chalk back line is clear. Red has won the toss, both for the choice of a side and, after making that choice, for first move, and his force is already put out upon the back line. For the sake of picturesqueness, the men are not put exactly on the line, but each will have his next move measured from that line. Red has broken his force into two, a fatal error, as we shall see, in view of the wide space of open ground between the farm and the church. He has 1 gun, 5 cavalry, and 13 infantry on his left, who are evidently to take up a strong position by the church and enfilade Blue's position; Red's right, of 2 guns, 20 cavalry, and 37 infantry aim at the seizure of the farm.

图1显示了布置好的战场地形：右边是教堂，左边、靠近图版中央的位置，是农场。两者之间的洼地，有一间小附屋。沿视线看，在农场正后方，还有另一间附屋；它在其他照片中更清楚。后方，可以清楚看见粉笔画出的后边线。红方掷币获胜，既选了边，又在选边后赢得先手；他的兵力，已沿后边线布置。为求画面好看，兵人没有恰好放在线上，但下一回合，每人的移动距离，仍须从该线量起。红方把兵力分成两部分；考虑到农场与教堂之间大片开阔地，这将是一个致命错误，我们马上就会看到。他左翼有1门炮、5名骑兵、13名步兵，显然打算在教堂旁占据坚固阵地，纵射蓝方阵地；红方右翼的2门炮、20名骑兵和37名步兵，则以夺取农场为目标。

Figure 2 is a near view of Blue's side, with his force put down. He has grasped the strategic mistake of Red, and is going to fling every man at the farm. His right, of 5 cavalry and 16 infantry, will get up as soon as possible to the woods near the centre of the field (whence the fire of their gun will be able to cut off the two portions of Red's force from each other), and then, leaving the gun there with sufficient men to serve it, the rest of this party will push on to co-operate with the main force of their comrades in the inevitable scrimmage for the farm.
图2是蓝方一侧部署完成后的近景。他已看清红方的战略错误，准备把每个人都投入农场方向。他的右翼，即5名骑兵和16名步兵，将尽快抵达战场中央附近的树林；那里的炮火，可以切断红方两部分兵力之间的联系。随后，他会把炮和足以操作它的人留在那里，其余人员继续前进，与主力同伴协作，参加那场不可避免的农场争夺战。

Figure 3 shows the fight after Red and Blue have both made their first move. It is taken from Red's side. Red has not as yet realised the danger of his position. His left gun struggles into position to the left of the church, his centre and right push for the farm. Blue's five cavalry on his left have already galloped forward into a favourable position to open fire at the next move—they are a little hidden in the picture by the church; the sixteen infantry follow hard, and his main force makes straight for the farm.
图3显示双方各完成第一回合后的战况，照片从红方一侧拍摄。红方尚未意识到自身处境的危险。他的左炮，正吃力地进入教堂左侧阵位；中央和右翼则向农场推进。蓝方左翼的五名骑兵，已经疾驰到有利阵位，准备下一回合开炮；画面中，他们部分被教堂挡住。十六名步兵紧紧跟随，主力则直奔农场。

Figure 4 shows the affair developing rapidly. Red's cavalry on his right have taken his two guns well forward into a position to sweep either side of the farm, and his left gun is now well placed to pound Blue's infantry centre. His infantry continue to press forward, but Blue, for his second move, has already opened fire from the woods with his right gun, and killed three of Red's men. His infantry have now come up to serve this gun, and the cavalry who brought it into position at the first move have now left it to them in order to gallop over to join the force attacking the farm. Undismayed by Red's guns, Blue has brought his other two guns and his men as close to the farm as they can go. His leftmost gun stares Red's in the face, and prevents any effective fire, his middle gun faces Red's middle gun. Some of his cavalry are exposed to the right of the farm, but most are completely covered now by the farm from Red's fire. Red has now to move. The nature of his position is becoming apparent to him. His right gun is ineffective, his left and his centre guns cannot kill more than seven or eight men between them; and at the next move, unless he can silence them, Blue's guns will be mowing his exposed cavalry down from the security of the farm. He is in a fix. How is he to get out of it? His cavalry are slightly outnumbered, but he decides to do as much execution as he can with his own guns, charge the Blue guns before him, and then bring up his infantry to save the situation.

图4显示，战事正在迅速发展。红方右翼骑兵，将两门炮带到很靠前的位置，能够扫射农场两侧；左炮也已就位，足以轰击蓝方步兵中央。他的步兵继续压上，但蓝方在第二回合，已用右炮从树林里开火，杀死红方三人。蓝方步兵这时赶到，可以操作这门炮；第一回合把炮运到阵位的骑兵，便把炮交给他们，驰去加入进攻农场的部队。蓝方毫不畏惧红方炮火，把另外两门炮和人员，尽可能靠近农场。他最左边的炮，与红方的炮迎面对峙，阻止了任何有效射击；中央炮，则面对红方中央炮。有些蓝方骑兵暴露在农场右侧，但大多数人，此时已有农场完全挡住红方火力。现在轮到红方行动。他逐渐看清自己的处境：右炮不起作用，左炮和中央炮合起来，也杀不了七八人以上；下一回合，除非他能让蓝方炮哑火，否则，蓝方便会躲在农场的安全掩护里，用炮扫倒他暴露的骑兵。他陷入困境了。怎么脱身？他的骑兵略处人数劣势，但仍决定，先用自己的炮尽可能杀伤，再冲向面前的蓝方炮，随后调上步兵，挽救局面。

Figure 5a shows the result of Red's move. His two effective guns have between them bowled over two cavalry and six infantry in the gap between the farm and Blue's right gun; and then, following up the effect of his gunfire, his cavalry charges home over the Blue guns. One oversight he makes, to which Blue at once calls his attention at the end of his move. Red has reckoned on twenty cavalry for his charge, forgetting that by the rules he must put two men at the tail of his middle gun. His infantry are just not able to come up for this duty, and consequently two cavalry-men have to be set there. The game then pauses while the players work out the cavalry mêlée. Red has brought up eighteen men to this; in touch or within six inches of touch there are twenty-one Blue cavalry. Red's force is isolated, for only two of his men are within a move, and to support eighteen he would have to have nine. By the rules this gives fifteen men dead on either side and three Red prisoners to Blue. By the rules also it rests with Red to indicate the survivors within the limits of the mêlée as he chooses. He takes very good care there are not four men within six inches of either Blue gun, and both these are out of action therefore for Blue's next move. Of course Red would have done far better to have charged home with thirteen men only, leaving seven in support, but he was flurried by his comparatively unsuccessful shooting—he had wanted to hit more cavalry—and by the gun-trail mistake. Moreover, he had counted his antagonist wrongly, and thought he could arrange a mêlée of twenty against twenty.

图5a显示红方这一回合的结果。他两门有效的炮，在农场与蓝方右炮之间的空隙里，共打倒两名骑兵和六名步兵；然后，骑兵乘着炮击的效果，一直冲到蓝方炮上。他犯了一个疏忽；回合一结束，蓝方便立刻指出：红方按二十名骑兵来计划冲锋，却忘了规则要求，中央炮的炮架尾端必须留两人。他的步兵恰好来不及赶上执行这项任务，所以必须放两名骑兵在那里。随后，游戏暂停，双方计算骑兵混战的结果。红方投入十八人；直接接触、或在接触点六英寸内的蓝方骑兵，则有二十一人。红方这支部队是孤立的，因为距他们一回合行程内，只有两名本方人员；而要支援十八人，就必须有九人。按规则，双方各死十五人，蓝方俘虏三名红方人员。规则还规定，红方可以在混战范围内，按自己的选择指定幸存者。他十分小心，确保两门蓝方炮各自六英寸内，都不足四人，因此，下一回合，蓝方的这两门炮，都无法作战。当然，红方如果只用十三人冲锋，留下七人支援，会好得多；但射击不太成功——他本想打中更多骑兵——以及炮架尾端的错误，令他慌了手脚。此外，他把对手人数算错了，以为可以安排一场二十对二十的混战。

Figure 5b shows the game at the same stage as 5a, immediately after the adjudication of the mêlée. The dead have been picked up, the three prisoners, by a slight deflection of the rules in the direction of the picturesque, turn their faces towards captivity, and the rest of the picture is exactly in the position of 5a.
图5b显示的，是与5a相同阶段的游戏：混战刚刚裁定结束。死者已经拾起；稍稍偏离规则、为画面好看起见，三名俘虏已转过身，朝向被押走的方向。画面其余部分，与5a的位置完全相同。

It is now Blue's turn to move, and figure 6a shows the result of his move. He fires his rightmost gun (the nose of it is just visible to the right) and kills one infantry-man and one cavalry-man (at the tail of Red's central gun), brings up his surviving eight cavalry into convenient positions for the service of his temporarily silenced guns, and hurries his infantry forward to the farm, recklessly exposing them in the thin wood between the farm and his right gun. The attentive reader will be able to trace all this in figure 6a, and he will also note the three Red cavalry prisoners going to the rear under the escort of one Khaki infantry man.
现在轮到蓝方行动，图6a显示其行动结果。他发射最右边的炮，炮口在右侧刚好可见，杀死一名步兵和一名骑兵，后者在红方中央炮的尾架旁；他把剩下的八名骑兵，调到便于操作暂时哑火的各门炮的位置，又催促步兵前进到农场，鲁莽地让他们暴露在农场与右炮之间的稀疏树林里。细心的读者，可以在图6a中逐一追踪这些变化；还会注意到，三名被俘的红方骑兵，正由一名穿卡其色制服的步兵押往后方。

Figure 6b shows exactly the same stage as figure 6a, that is to say, the end of Blue's third move. A cavalry-man lies dead at the tail of Red's middle gun, an infantry-man a little behind it. His rightmost gun is abandoned and partly masked, but not hidden, from the observer, by a tree to the side of the farmhouse.
图6b显示的，与6a完全是同一阶段，即蓝方第三回合结束之时。一名骑兵死在红方中央炮的尾架旁，稍后方还有一名死去的步兵。红方最右边的炮已被放弃；从观察者的角度看，农舍旁的一棵树，挡住它一部分，但并未把它完全遮住。
And now, what is Red to do?
现在，红方该怎么办？

The reader will probably have his own ideas, as I have mine. What Red did do in the actual game was to lose his head, and when at the end of four minutes' deliberation he had to move, he blundered desperately. He opened fire on Blue's exposed centre and killed eight men. (Their bodies litter the ground in figure 7, which gives a complete bird's-eye view of the battle.) He then sent forward and isolated six or seven men in a wild attempt to recapture his lost gun, massed his other men behind the inadequate cover of his central gun, and sent the detachment of infantry that had hitherto lurked uselessly behind the church, in a frantic and hopeless rush across the open to join them. (The one surviving cavalry-man on his right wing will be seen taking refuge behind the cottage.) There can be little question of the entire unsoundness of all these movements. Red was at a disadvantage, he had failed to capture the farm, and his business now was manifestly to save his men as much as possible, make a defensive fight of it, inflict as much damage as possible with his leftmost gun on Blue's advance, get the remnants of his right across to the church—the cottage in the centre and their own gun would have given them a certain amount of cover,—and build up a new position about that building as a pivot. With two guns right and left of the church he might conceivably have saved the rest of the fight.

读者也许有自己的想法，我也有我的。红方在实际游戏中真正做的，却是乱了方寸；四分钟考虑结束、轮到他行动时，他犯下了严重错误。他向蓝方暴露的中央开火，杀死八人。（他们的尸体散落在图7地面上，这幅照片完整俯瞰了整个战场。）然后，他派出六七个人，使他们陷入孤立，疯狂地企图夺回丢失的炮；把其他人聚集在中央炮不足以遮护他们的掩体后；又把一直无用地躲在教堂后方的那支步兵分队派出来，疯狂而毫无希望地冲过开阔地，与他们汇合。（可以看见，他右翼唯一幸存的骑兵，正在小屋后避难。）这一切行动完全不妥当，几乎毫无疑问。红方处于劣势，没有夺下农场，显然应当尽可能保全人员，打一场防御战：用最左边的炮，尽量杀伤蓝方推进的部队；把右翼残余转移到教堂去，中间的小屋和他们自己的炮，可以提供一定掩护；再以教堂为枢纽，建立新阵地。教堂左右各放一门炮，也许还能挽回余下的战斗。

That, however, is theory; let us return to fact. Figure 8 gives the disastrous consequences of Red's last move. Blue has moved, his guns have slaughtered ten of Red's wretched foot, and a rush of nine Blue cavalry and infantry mingles with Red's six surviving infantry about the disputed gun. These infantry by the definition are isolated; there are not three other Reds within a move of them. The view in this photograph also is an extensive one, and the reader will note, as a painful accessory, the sad spectacle of three Red prisoners receding to the right. The mêlée about Red's lost gun works out, of course, at three dead on each side, and three more Red prisoners.

不过，这只是理论；让我们回到事实。图8显示了红方上回合所造成的灾难性后果。蓝方已经行动，他的炮杀死了红方十名倒霉的步兵；九名蓝方骑兵与步兵，又冲进那门归属未定的炮周围，与红方六名幸存步兵混在一起。按定义，这些步兵是孤立的：距他们一回合行程以内，没有另外三名红方人员。这张照片的视野也很开阔；读者还会注意到一个令人痛心的陪衬：三名红方俘虏，正向右方渐渐远去。围绕红方失炮的混战，结果当然是双方各死三人，再添三名红方俘虏。

Henceforth the battle moves swiftly to complete the disaster of Red. Shaken and demoralised, that unfortunate general is now only for retreat. His next move, of which I have no picture, is to retreat the infantry he has so wantonly exposed back to the shelter of the church, to withdraw the wreckage of his right into the cover of the cottage, and—one last gleam of enterprise—to throw forward his left gun into a position commanding Blue's right.
此后，战斗迅速向红方的彻底灾难发展。这位不幸的将军，受到震动，士气瓦解，一心只想退却。他的下一回合，我没有照片：他把刚才肆意暴露的步兵，撤回教堂掩护下，把右翼残部撤进小屋的掩护，并且——这是最后一线进取精神——把左炮向前推出，进入能够控制蓝方右翼的位置。
Fig. 8.—BATTLE OF HOOK’S FARM. The Red Army suffers heavy losses. (See page 83.)
图8——胡克农场之战。红军遭受重大损失。（见第83页。）
Fig. 9.—BATTLE OF HOOK’S FARM. Complete victory of the Blue Army. (See page 85.)
图9——胡克农场之战。蓝军完全获胜。（见第85页。）

Blue then pounds Red's right with his gun to the right of the farm and kills three men. He extends his other gun to the left of the farm, right out among the trees, so as to get an effective fire next time upon the tail of Red's gun. He also moves up sufficient men to take possession of Red's lost gun. On the right Blue's gun engages Red's and kills one man. All this the reader will see clearly in figure 9, and he will also note a second batch of Red prisoners—this time they are infantry, going rearward. Figure 9 is the last picture that is needed to tell the story of the battle. Red's position is altogether hopeless. He has four men left alive by his rightmost gun, and their only chance is to attempt to save that by retreating with it. If they fire it, one or other will certainly be killed at its tail in Blue's subsequent move, and then the gun will be neither movable nor fireable. Red's left gun, with four men only, is also in extreme peril, and will be immovable and helpless if it loses another man.

随后，蓝方用农场右侧的炮，轰击红方右翼，杀死三人。他把另一门炮，移到农场左边，深入树林，以便下一次有效射击红方炮的尾架。他还调上足够人员，接管红方丢掉的炮。在右翼，蓝方炮与红方炮交火，杀死一人。读者在图9中，会清楚看见这一切；还会注意到，第二批红方俘虏正在往后走，这次是步兵。要讲清这场战斗，图9就是最后需要的一张照片。红方处境完全绝望。最右炮旁，只有四人活着；他们唯一的机会，是拖着炮后撤，设法把它保住。如果开火，蓝方下一回合，一定会有人死在炮尾架旁；到那时，炮既不能移动，也不能射击。红方左炮同样只有四人，也处于极度危险之中；再损失一人，就会动弹不得、毫无办法。
Text in the original image (transcription) HOOKS FARM
图内文字汉译 胡克农场。
Text in the original image (transcription) WHITE FLAG
图内文字汉译 白旗。

Very properly Red decided upon retreat. His second gun had to be abandoned after one move, but two of the men with it escaped over his back line. Five of the infantry behind the church escaped, and his third gun and its four cavalry got away on the extreme left-hand corner of Red's position. Blue remained on the field, completely victorious, with two captured guns and six prisoners.
红方十分明智地决定撤退。他的第二门炮，在一回合后就不得不放弃，但炮旁两人逃过了本方后边线。教堂后面的五名步兵逃了出来；第三门炮及其四名骑兵，也从红方阵地最左端撤走。蓝方留在战场，取得完全胜利：夺炮两门，俘虏六人。
There you have a scientific record of the worthy general's little affair.
这就是那位可敬将军的小小战斗的科学记录。
V. Extensions and Amplifications of Little War
section: V. 小战争的扩展与增补

text: V. 小战争的扩展与增补
section: V. 小战争的扩展与增补

text: Now that battle of Hook's Farm is, as I have explained, a simplification of the game, set out entirely to illustrate the method of playing; there is scarcely a battle that will not prove more elaborate (and eventful) than this little encounter. If a number of players and a sufficiently large room can be got, there is no reason why armies of many hundreds of soldiers should not fight over many square yards of model country. So long as each player has about a hundred men and three guns there is no need to lengthen the duration of a game on that account. But it is too laborious and confusing for a single player to handle more than that number of men.
section: V. 小战争的扩展与增补

text: 正如我解释过的，胡克农场之战是游戏的简化，完全为了说明玩法而安排。几乎任何一场战斗，都会比这个小遭遇更复杂，变故也更多。如果能找到一批玩家，以及足够大的房间，许多百人的军队，完全可以在许多平方码的模型地形上交战。只要每位玩家大约掌握一百人和三门炮，就无须因此延长游戏时间。但对单一玩家来说，操作超过这个数量的人员，就过于费力，也过于混乱。
section: V. 小战争的扩展与增补

text: Moreover, on a big floor with an extensive country it is possible to begin moving with moves double or treble the length here specified, and to come down to moves of the ordinary lengths when the troops are within fifteen or twelve or ten feet of each other. To players with the time and space available I would suggest using a quite large country, beginning with treble moves, and, with the exception of a select number of cavalry scouts, keeping the soldiers in their boxes with the lids on, and moving the boxes as units. (This boxing idea is a new one, and affords a very good substitute for the curtain; I have tried it twice for games in the open air where the curtain was not available.) Neither side would, of course, know what the other had in its boxes; they might be packed regiments or a mere skeleton force. Each side would advance on the other by double or treble moves behind a screen of cavalry scouts, until a scout was within ten feet of a box on the opposite side. Then the contents of that particular box would have to be disclosed and the men stood out. Troops without any enemy within twenty feet could be returned to their boxes for facility in moving. Playing on such a scale would admit also of the introduction of the problem of provisions and supplies. Little toy Army Service waggons can be bought, and it could be ruled that troops must have one such waggon for every fifty men within at least six moves. Moreover, ammunition carts may be got, and it may be ruled that one must be within two moves of a gun before the latter can be fired. All these are complications of the War Game, and so far I have not been able to get together sufficient experienced players to play on this larger, more elaborate scale. It is only after the smaller simpler war game here described has been played a number of times, and its little dodges mastered completely, that such more warlike devices become practicable.
section: V. 小战争的扩展与增补

text: 此外，在地板很大、地形广阔的情况下，起初可以按这里规定距离的两倍或三倍行动；等双方距离缩短到十五、十二或十英尺，再恢复通常的移动距离。对于有时间、有场地的玩家，我建议使用相当大的地形，从三倍移动距离开始；除少数选出的骑兵侦察兵外，其余士兵都放在盖好盖子的盒子里，把盒子作为整体移动。（装盒的想法是新近提出的，能够很好地代替帘子；我已经试过两次，都是在没法挂帘子的户外游戏中。）当然，双方都不知道对手盒子里是什么：可能是满编团，也可能只是空架子部队。双方在骑兵侦察幕掩护下，以两倍或三倍移动距离相向推进；直到一名侦察兵，来到敌方某个盒子十英尺以内，那个盒子的内容才须公开，把士兵摆出来。二十英尺内没有敌人的部队，可以重新装盒，方便移动。采用这样的规模，还可以加入给养与补给问题。市面上可以买到小型玩具军需车；可以规定，每五十人，必须有一辆这样的车，位于至少六回合可达的范围内。另外，还可以买到弹药车，并规定：一门炮要开火，必须有一辆弹药车在它两回合行程以内。所有这些，都使战争游戏更复杂；迄今为止，我还未能凑齐足够多有经验的玩家，来进行这种规模更大、更为复杂的游戏。只有将这里描述的较小、较简单的战争游戏玩过多次，彻底掌握其中的小窍门以后，这些更像战争的办法，才会变得切实可行。
section: V. 小战争的扩展与增补

text: But obviously with a team of players and an extensive country, one could have a general controlling the whole campaign, divisional commanders, batteries of guns, specialised brigades, and a quite military movement of the whole affair. I have (as several illustrations show) tried Little Wars in the open air. The toy soldiers stand quite well on closely mown grass, but the long-range gun-fire becomes a little uncertain if there is any breeze. It gives a greater freedom of movement and allows the players to lie down more comfortably when firing, to increase, and even double, the moves of the indoor game. One can mark out high roads and streams with an ordinary lawn-tennis marker, mountains and rocks of stones, and woods and forests of twigs are easily arranged. But if the game is to be left out all night and continued next day (a thing I have as yet had no time to try), the houses must be of some more solid material than paper. I would suggest painted blocks of wood. On a large lawn, a wide country-side may be easily represented. The players may begin with a game exactly like the ordinary Kriegspiel, with scouts and boxed soldiers, which will develop into such battles as are here described, as the troops come into contact. It would be easy to give the roads a real significance by permitting a move half as long again as in the open country for waggons or boxed troops along a road. There is a possibility of having a toy railway, with stations or rolling stock into which troops might be put, on such a giant war map. One would allow a move for entraining and another for detraining, requiring the troops to be massed alongside the train at the beginning and end of each journey, and the train might move at four or five times the cavalry rate. One would use open trucks and put in a specified number of men—say twelve infantry or five cavalry or half a gun per truck,—and permit an engine to draw seven or eight trucks, or move at a reduced speed with more. One could also rule that four men—the same four men—remaining on a line during two moves, could tear up a rail, and eight men in three moves replace it.
section: V. 小战争的扩展与增补

text: 不过，显而易见，有一组玩家和广阔地形，就可以设一名将军控制整场战役，再有师级指挥官、炮兵连、专门化的旅，整场行动也就颇有军事作战的样子。我曾在户外试过小战争，几幅插图已经显示这一点。玩具士兵，在修剪得很短的草地上站得相当稳；不过，只要有一点风，远距离炮火就稍有些不可靠。户外游戏让移动更自由，也让玩家开炮时躺得更舒服；室内游戏的移动距离，还可以增大，甚至加倍。可以用普通草地网球场划线器，标出大路和溪流；用石头堆出山和岩石，用枝条布置树林与森林，都很容易。但如果游戏要在外面放一整夜，次日继续——这件事我迄今还没有时间尝试——房屋就必须用比纸更结实的材料做。我建议用涂漆的木块。一片大草坪，很容易就能表现广阔乡野。玩家可以从与普通兵棋完全一样的游戏开始，用侦察兵和装盒士兵；随着部队相遇，再发展成这里所描述的战斗。若允许车辆或装盒部队沿道路移动时，比在野地中多走一半距离，道路便很容易获得实际意义。在这样一张巨型战争地图上，也可能设置玩具铁路、车站，以及可以装入士兵的车辆。可以规定，登车用一回合，下车再用一回合；并要求每次旅程开始和结束时，部队都必须集中在列车旁。列车移动速度，可以是骑兵的四倍或五倍。可以用敞篷货车，每节装规定数量的士兵，比如十二名步兵、五名骑兵，或半门炮；允许一台机车牵引七八节车厢，车厢更多则降低速度。还可以规定：四个人，而且必须是同样四个人，在铁路线旁停留两个回合，就能拆掉一段铁轨；八个人，用三个回合，可以把它修复。
section: V. 小战争的扩展与增补

text: I will confess I have never yet tried over these more elaborate developments of Little Wars, partly because of the limited time at my disposal, and partly because they all demand a number of players who are well acquainted with the game on each side if they are not to last interminably. The Battle of Hook's Farm (one player a side) took a whole afternoon, and most of my battles have lasted the better part of a day.
section: V. 小战争的扩展与增补

text: 我得承认，这些更复杂的小战争扩展，我还从来没有实际试过；一部分因为我的时间有限，另一部分因为，如果不想让游戏没完没了，它们就需要双方各有若干名十分熟悉游戏的玩家。胡克农场之战，每方只有一人，也花了整整一个下午；我的大多数战斗，都延续了大半天。
section: V. 小战争的扩展与增补

text: VI. Ending With a Sort of Challenge
VI. 以一种挑战结束

I could go on now and tell of battles, copiously. In the memory of the one skirmish I have given I do but taste blood. I would like to go on, to a large, thick book. It would be an agreeable task. Since I am the chief inventor and practiser (so far) of Little Wars, there has fallen to me a disproportionate share of victories. But let me not boast. For the present, I have done all that I meant to do in this matter. It is for you, dear reader, now to get a floor, a friend, some soldiers and some guns, and show by a grovel ling devotion your appreciation of this noble and beautiful gift of a limitless game that I have given you.

现在，我本可以继续讲战斗，滔滔不绝地讲。回味刚才那场小冲突，不过让我尝到一点血腥味。我倒想继续写下去，写成一部又大又厚的书，那将是一件愉快的工作。由于迄今为止，我是小战争的主要发明者和实践者，胜利也不成比例地落在了我这一边。不过，还是不要自夸了。关于此事，我目前已把原来打算做的事情都做完了。亲爱的读者，现在轮到你去找一块地板、一位朋友、一些士兵和几门炮，用匍匐在地的虔诚，表明你对我赠予你的这份高贵、美好、无穷尽的游戏礼物的欣赏。
Text in the original image (transcription) LITTLE WARS
图内文字汉译 小战争。

And if I might for a moment trumpet! How much better is this amiable miniature than the Real Thing! Here is a homeopathic remedy for the imaginative strategist. Here is the premeditation, the thrill, the strain of accumulating victory or disaster—and no smashed nor sanguinary bodies, no shattered fine buildings nor devastated country sides, no petty cruelties, none of that awful universal boredom and embitterment, that tiresome delay or stoppage or embarrassment of every gracious, bold, sweet, and charming thing, that we who are old enough to remember a real modern war know to be the reality of belligerence. This world is for ample living; we want security and freedom; all of us in every country, except a few dull-witted, energetic bores, want to see the manhood of the world at something better than apeing the little lead toys our children buy in boxes. We want fine things made for mankind—splendid cities, open ways, more knowledge and power, and more and more and more,—and so I offer my game, for a particular as well as a general end; and let us put this prancing monarch and that silly scare-monger, and these excitable “patriots,” and those adventurers, and all the practitioners of Welt Politik, into one vast Temple of War, with cork carpets everywhere, and plenty of little trees and little houses to knock down, and cities and fortresses, and unlimited soldiers—tons, cellars-full,—and let them lead their own lives there away from us.

容我鼓吹片刻！这友善的小模型，比真实的东西好多少啊！它给富于想象力的战略家，提供了一剂顺势疗法。在这里，有预谋，有惊险，有胜利或灾难逐渐积累的紧张；却没有破碎、流血的身体，没有被摧毁的优美建筑和遭蹂躏的乡野，没有卑小的残酷，没有那种可怕、普遍的无聊与怨毒；也没有对一切优雅、勇敢、甜美、迷人的事物，那种令人厌烦的拖延、中断或阻挠。我们这些年纪足以记得一场真正现代战争的人，都知道，那才是好战的现实。这个世界是为了让人充分生活的；我们要安全与自由。每个国家的所有人，除了少数头脑迟钝、精力旺盛的讨厌鬼，都希望看见世界上的壮年男子，做些比模仿孩子们整盒买来的小铅玩具更好的事。我们要为人类造出美好事物：辉煌的城市，通畅的道路，更多知识与力量，越来越多，越来越多。所以，我把这游戏拿出来，既为了一个具体目的，也为了一个一般目的：让我们把这个耀武扬威的君主、那个愚蠢的恐慌煽动者、这些易激动的“爱国者”、那些冒险家，还有所有世界政治的实践者，都送进一座巨大的战争神殿；里面到处铺软木地毯，有许多可供推倒的小树、小房子，还有城市、要塞，以及无穷无尽的士兵，几吨几吨、几地窖几地窖的士兵；让他们远离我们，在里面过自己的日子。

My game is just as good as their game, and saner by reason of its size. Here is War, done down to rational proportions, and yet out of the way of mankind, even as our fathers turned human sacrifices into the eating of little images and symbolic mouthfuls. For my own part, I am prepared. I have nearly five hundred men, more than a score of guns, and I twirl my moustache and hurl defiance eastward from my home in Essex across the narrow seas. Not only eastward. I would conclude this little discourse with one other disconcerting and exasperating sentence for the admirers and practitioners of Big War. I have never yet met in little battle any military gentleman, any captain, major, colonel, general, or eminent commander, who did not presently get into difficulties and confusions among even the elementary rules of the Battle. You have only to play at Little Wars three or four times to realise just what a blundering thing Great War must be.

我的游戏，和他们的游戏一样好，而且因为规模适当，更为理智。这里有战争，但已缩小到合理的比例，并且不再妨碍人类；正如我们的祖先，把人祭变成吃下小小的人像和象征性的一口食物。至于我自己，已经准备好了。我有将近五百人、二十多门炮；我捻着胡须，从埃塞克斯的家中，越过狭窄海峡，向东方发出挑战。不只是东方。我还想用另一句话，结束这篇小小议论；它会使大战的爱好者与实践者，感到不安和恼怒。迄今为止，我在小战斗中遇到的军人，无论上尉、少校、上校、将军，还是著名统帅，没有一个不在不久之后，就被战斗中哪怕最基本的规则，弄得困难重重、混乱不堪。你只须玩过三四次小战争，就能明白，真正的大战一定是何等笨拙的东西。

Great War is at present, I am convinced, not only the most expensive game in the universe, but it is a game out of all proportion. Not only are the masses of men and material and suffering and inconvenience too monstrously big for reason, but—the available heads we have for it, are too small. That, I think, is the most pacific realisation conceivable, and Little War brings you to it as nothing else but Great War can do.
我确信，当下的大战，不仅是宇宙中最昂贵的游戏，而且是一个规模完全失衡的游戏。不仅人员、物资、苦难和不便的数量，大到令人无法理喻；而且，我们手头可用来驾驭它的脑袋，又实在太小。我想，这是人能设想的最有利于和平的领悟；除了大战本身，只有小战争，能以这样的方式，把你带到这一认识。
APPENDIX. Little Wars and Kriegspiel
附录：小战争与兵棋

This little book has, I hope, been perfectly frank about its intentions. It is not a book upon Kriegspiel. It gives merely a game that may be played by two or four or six amateurish persons in an afternoon and evening with toy soldiers. But it has a very distinct relation to Kriegspiel; and since the main portion of it was written and published in a magazine, I have had quite a considerable correspondence with military people who have been interested by it, and who have shown a very friendly spirit towards it—in spite of the pacific outbreak in its concluding section. They tell me—what I already a little suspected—that Kriegspiel, as it is played by the British Army, is a very dull and unsatisfactory exercise, lacking in realism, in stir and the unexpected, obsessed by the umpire at every turn, and of very doubtful value in waking up the imagination, which should be its chief function. I am particularly indebted to Colonel Mark Sykes for advice and information in this matter. He has pointed out to me the possibility of developing Little Wars into a vivid and inspiring Kriegspiel, in which the element of the umpire would be reduced to a minimum; and it would be ungrateful to him, and a waste of an interesting opportunity, if I did not add this Appendix, pointing out how a Kriegspiel of real educational value for junior officers may be developed out of the amusing methods of Little War. If Great War is to be played at all, the better it is played the more humanely it will be done. I see no inconsistency in deploring the practice while perfecting the method. But I am a civilian, and Kriegspiel is not my proper business. I am deeply preoccupied with a novel I am writing, and so I think the best thing I can do is just to set down here all the ideas that have cropped up in my mind, in the footsteps, so to speak, of Colonel Sykes, and leave it to the military expert, if he cares to take the matter up, to reduce my scattered suggestions to a system.

我希望，这本小书已把自己的意图交代得十分坦率。它不是一本论兵棋的书。它只是提供一种游戏，让两人、四人或六个业余爱好者，用玩具士兵，玩上一个下午加一个晚上。但它与兵棋确有十分明确的关系；自从其主体部分写出、在杂志发表后，我便与许多对此感兴趣的军界人士，有了相当多通信。他们表现出十分友好的态度，尽管本书结尾有一场和平主义的爆发。他们告诉我一些我原已有所怀疑的事：英国陆军所玩的兵棋，是一种十分枯燥、令人不满的练习，缺少真实感、活力和意外，每一步都摆脱不了裁判；它能否唤醒想象力，非常可疑，而这本应是它的主要功能。在这件事上，我特别感谢马克·赛克斯上校，给我意见和信息。他向我指出，把小战争发展成一种生动而鼓舞人的兵棋的可能；在这种兵棋中，裁判的作用会降到最低。如果我不加上这篇附录，说明如何从小战争的有趣办法中，发展出一种真正有助于初级军官教育的兵棋，既是辜负他，也浪费了一个有意思的机会。倘若大战终究要打，打得越好，就能打得越人道。我看不出，谴责这种实践，同时完善它的方法，有何矛盾。不过，我是平民，兵棋并非我的本行。我正全神贯注于一部正在写的小说，所以，我想自己能做的最好事情，就是把脑中涌出的想法全都写在这里；可以说，它们沿着赛克斯上校的足迹而来。至于把这些零散建议整理成体系，就留给有兴趣接手的军事专家吧。

Now, first, it is manifest that in Little Wars there is no equivalent for rifle-fire, and that the effect of the gun-fire has no resemblance to the effect of shell. That may be altered very simply. Let the rules as to gun-fire be as they are now, but let a different projectile be used—a projectile that will drop down and stay where it falls. I find that one can buy in ironmongers' shops small brass screws of various sizes and weights, but all capable of being put in the muzzle of the 4·7 guns without slipping down the barrel. If, with such a screw in the muzzle, the gun is loaded and fired, the wooden bolt remains in the gun and the screw flies and drops and stays near where it falls—its range being determined by the size and weight of screw selected by the gunner. Let us assume this is a shell, and it is quite easy to make a rule that will give the effect of its explosion. Half, or, in the case of an odd number, one more than half, of the men within three inches of this shell are dead, and if there is a gun completely within the circle of three inches radius from the shell, it is destroyed. If it is not completely within the circle, it is disabled for two moves. A supply waggon is completely destroyed if it falls wholly or partially within the radius. But if there is a wall, house, or entrenchment between any men and the shell, they are uninjured—they do not count in the reckoning of the effect of the shell.

首先，显而易见，小战争中没有与步枪火力相当的东西，炮火的效果，也不像炮弹爆炸的效果。这可以很简单地改变。让开炮规则维持现状，但换一种弹射物，一种落下后会停留在落点的弹射物。我发现，五金店里有各种尺寸和重量的小黄铜螺丝，都能放进四点七炮的炮口，而不滑入炮管。如果炮口里放这样一枚螺丝，再装填、开火，木弹柱会留在炮内，螺丝飞出、落下，停在落点附近；射程取决于炮手选用的螺丝尺寸与重量。假定它是一枚炮弹，就很容易制定规则，给出爆炸效果：距这枚炮弹三英寸以内的人，一半死亡；若人数为奇数，则为比半数多一人。如果一门炮完全位于以炮弹为中心、半径三英寸的圆内，它便被摧毁；如果没有完全位于圆内，就失去作战能力两个回合。补给车只要全部或部分进入这一半径，就完全被毁。但若某些人员与炮弹之间有墙、房屋或战壕，他们便不受伤害，也不计入炮弹效果的计算。

I think one can get a practical imitation of the effect of rifle-fire by deciding that for every five infantry-men who are roughly in a line, and who do not move in any particular move, there may be one (ordinary) shot taken with a 4·7 gun. It may be fired from any convenient position behind the row of five men, so long as the shot passes roughly over the head of the middle man of the five.
我认为，可以用下述办法，实际模拟步枪火力的效果：每五名大致排成一线、在某个回合没有移动的步兵，允许用四点七炮，作一次普通射击。炮可以放在这五个人后方任何合适的位置，只须让弹丸大致从五人中央那人的头顶经过。

Of course, while in Little Wars there are only three or four players, in any proper Kriegspiel the game will go on over a larger area—in a drill-hall or some such place,—and each arm and service will be entrusted to a particular player. This permits all sorts of complicated imitations of reality that are impossible to our parlour and playroom Little Wars. We can consider transport, supply, ammunition, and the moral effect of cavalry impact, and of uphill and downhill movements. We can also bring in the spade and entrenchment, and give scope to the Royal Engineers. But before I write anything of Colonel Sykes' suggestions about these, let me say a word or two about Kriegspiel “country.”
当然，小战争只有三四个玩家，任何像样的兵棋，却要在更大空间里进行，比如操练大厅之类；每个兵种与勤务部门，都交给一名专门玩家。这样就能对现实作各种复杂模仿，而这些在我们客厅和游戏室里的小战争中，是不可能的。我们可以考虑运输、补给、弹药、骑兵冲击对士气的作用，以及上坡和下坡移动；还可以加入铁锹与掘壕，让皇家工兵发挥作用。不过，在写赛克斯上校对这些问题的建议之前，先让我就兵棋的“地形”，说上一两句话。

The country for Kriegspiel should be made up, I think, of heavy blocks or boxes of wood about 3 × 3 × ½ feet, and curved pieces (with a rounded outline and a chord of three feet, or shaped like right-angled triangles with an incurved hypotenuse and two straight sides of 3 feet) can easily be contrived to round off corners and salient angles. These blocks can be bored to take trees, etc., exactly as the boards in Little Wars are bored, and with them a very passable model of any particular country can be built up from a contoured Ordnance map. Houses may be made very cheaply by shaping a long piece of wood into a house-like section and sawing it up. There will always be someone who will touch up and paint and stick windows on to and generally adorn and individualise such houses, which are, of course, the stabler the heavier the wood used. The rest of the country as in Little Wars.

我认为，兵棋地形，应由约3 × 3 × ½英尺的厚重木块或木箱构成；再很容易地制作一些弧形部件，用来磨圆角落和突出的棱角：其轮廓可以是一段弧，弦长三英尺；也可以像直角三角形，斜边向内凹，两条直边各长3英尺。可以像小战争的木板那样，在这些木块上钻孔，插树等等；参照有等高线的军用测绘地图，就能搭出任何特定地形的相当像样的模型。把一根长木料，削成房屋形的截面，再锯成一段段，就能非常便宜地做出房子。总会有人愿意，为这些房子修饰、上漆、贴窗户，装饰它们，让它们各具特色；当然，所用木料越重，房屋就越稳。其余地形，与小战争相同。

Upon such a country a Kriegspiel could be played with rules upon the lines of the following sketch rules, which are the result of a discussion between Colonel Sykes and myself, and in which most of the new ideas are to be ascribed to Colonel Sykes. We proffer them, not as a finished set of rules, but as material for anyone who chooses to work over them, in the elaboration of what we believe will be a far more exciting and edifying Kriegspiel than any that exists at the present time. The game may be played by any number of players, according to the forces engaged and the size of the country available. Each side will be under the supreme command of a General, who will be represented by a cavalry soldier. The player who is General must stand at or behind his representative image and within six feet of it. His signalling will be supposed to be perfect, and he will communicate with his subordinates by shout, whisper, or note, as he thinks fit. I suggest he should be considered invulnerable, but Colonel Sykes has proposed arrangements for his disablement. He would have it that if the General falls within the zone of destruction of a shell he must go out of the room for three moves (injured); and that if he is hit by rifle-fire or captured he shall quit the game, and be succeeded by his next subordinate.

在这样的地形上，可以采用类似以下草拟规则的办法，玩一场兵棋。这些规则，是赛克斯上校与我讨论的结果，其中大部分新想法，应归功于赛克斯上校。我们提出它们，并非把它们当作一套完成的规则，而是作为材料，供愿意进一步加工的人，发展出一种兵棋；我们相信，它会远比当下任何已有的兵棋更刺激、更有启发。根据参战兵力和可用地形大小，游戏可以由任意数量的玩家参加。每方均由一名将军最高统率，以一个骑兵兵人代表。扮演将军的玩家，必须站在代表自己的兵人所在位置，或它的后方，且与它相距不超过六英尺。他的信号传达，视为完美无误；可以按意愿，对部下大喊、低声说话或传递纸条。我建议，将军应视为不会受伤；但赛克斯上校提出了一套令他失去行动能力的安排：如果将军落入一枚炮弹的杀伤区，就必须离开房间三个回合，表示受伤；如果被步枪火力击中，或被俘，就须退出游戏，由下一级部属接任。
Now as to the Moves.
现在，说说移动。
It is suggested that:
建议如下：
Infantry shall move one foot.
步兵移动一英尺。
Cavalry shall move three feet.
骑兵移动三英尺。
The above moves are increased by one half for troops in twos or fours on a road.
以二人或四人纵队沿道路行进的部队，上述移动距离增加一半。
Royal Engineers shall move two feet.
皇家工兵移动两英尺。
Royal Artillery shall move two feet.
皇家炮兵移动两英尺。
Transport and Supply shall move one foot on roads, half foot across country.
运输与补给部队，在道路上移动一英尺，在野地移动半英尺。
The General shall move six feet (per motor), three feet across country.
将军乘汽车移动六英尺，在野地移动三英尺。
Boats shall move one foot.
船只移动一英尺。

In moving uphill, one contour counts as one foot; downhill, two contours count as one foot. Where there are four contours to one foot vertical the hill is impassable for wheels unless there is a road.
上坡移动时，越过一条等高线，算一英尺；下坡时，两条等高线算一英尺。如果每垂直上升一英尺，就有四条等高线，轮式车辆便无法通过该山坡，除非有道路。
Infantry.
步兵。
To pass a fordable river = one move.
渡过可涉渡的河流 = 一个回合。
To change from fours to two ranks = half a move.
由四人纵队变为两列横队 = 半个回合。
To change from two ranks to extension = half a move.
由两列横队展开为散兵队形 = 半个回合。
To embark into boats = two moves for every twenty men embarked at any point.
登船 = 在任意一点，每二十人，两个回合。
To disembark = one move for every twenty men.
下船 = 每二十人，一个回合。
Cavalry.
骑兵。
To pass a fordable river = one move.
渡过可涉渡的河流 = 一个回合。
To change formation = half a move.
改变队形 = 半个回合。
To mount = one move.
上马 = 一个回合。
To dismount = one move.
下马 = 一个回合。
Artillery.
炮兵。
To unlimber guns = half a move.
将炮从前车解脱，展开炮位 = 半个回合。
To limber up guns = half a move.
将炮挂接前车，准备行进 = 半个回合。
Rivers are impassable to guns.
炮不能通过河流。
Neither Infantry, Cavalry, nor Artillery can Fire and Move in One Move.
步兵、骑兵、炮兵，都不能在同一回合内，既射击又移动。
Royal Engineers.
皇家工兵。
No repairs can be commenced, no destructions can be begun, during a move in which R.E. have changed position.
皇家工兵在某回合改变了位置，该回合便不能开始任何修理或破坏。
Rivers impassable.
不能通过河流。
Transport and Supply.
运输与补给。
No supplies or stores can be delivered during a move if T. and S. have moved.
运输与补给部队若在某回合移动，该回合便不能交付任何补给品或物资。
Rivers impassable.
不能通过河流。
Next as to Supply in the Field:
接着，说说野战补给：

All troops must be kept supplied with food, ammunition, and forage. The players must give up, every six moves, one packet of food per thirty men; one packet of forage per six horses; one packet of ammunition per thirty infantry which fire for six consecutive moves.
所有部队，都必须持续获得食物、弹药和饲料供应。每六回合，玩家必须交出：每三十人一包食物；每六匹马一包饲料；每三十名连续开火六回合的步兵，一包弹药。
These supplies, at the time when they are given up, must be within six feet of the infantry they belong to and eighteen feet of the cavalry.
交出这些补给时，它们必须位于所属步兵六英尺以内，以及所属骑兵十八英尺以内。

Isolated bodies of less than thirty infantry require no supplies—a body is isolated if it is more than twelve feet off another body. In calculating supplies for infantry the fractions either count as thirty if fifteen or over, or as nothing if less than fifteen. Thus forty-six infantry require two packets of food or ammunition; forty-four infantry require one packet of food.
不足三十名步兵的孤立部队，无须补给；一支部队距另一支超过十二英尺，就算孤立。计算步兵补给时，不足一个三十人整组的余数，若为十五或更多，就算三十；若不到十五，就不计。因此，四十六名步兵，需要两包食物或弹药；四十四名步兵，只需要一包食物。
N.B.—Supplies are not effective if enemy is between supplies and troops they belong to.
注意：如果敌人处于补给品与其所属部队之间，补给便不生效。
Men surrounded and besieged must be victualled at the following rate:—
被包围、被围困的人员，须按以下比例供给：
One packet food for every thirty men for every six moves.
每三十人，每六回合，一包食物。
One packet forage every six horses for every six moves.
每六匹马，每六回合，一包饲料。
In the event of supplies failing, horses may take the place of food, but not of course of forage; one horse to equal one packet.
补给断绝时，马可以代替食物；当然，不能代替饲料。一匹马相当于一包食物。
In the event of supplies failing, the following consequences ensue:—
补给断绝时，会产生以下后果：
Infantry without ammunition cannot fire (guns are supposed to have unlimited ammunition with them).
步兵没有弹药，便不能射击；炮则视为自带无限弹药。
Infantry, cavalry, R.A., and R.E. cannot move without supply—if supplies are not provided within six consecutive moves, they are out of action.
步兵、骑兵、皇家炮兵和皇家工兵，没有补给，便不能移动；如果连续六回合都没有获得补给，就失去作战能力。
A force surrounded must surrender four moves after eating its last horse.
一支被包围的部队，吃掉最后一匹马后，再过四回合，就必须投降。
Now as to Destructions:
现在，说说破坏：
To destroy a railway bridge R.E. take two moves; to repair, R.E. take ten moves.
皇家工兵破坏一座铁路桥，需要两回合；修复，需要十回合。
To destroy a railway culvert R.E. take one move; to repair R.E. take five moves.
皇家工兵破坏一处铁路涵洞，需要一回合；修复，需要五回合。
To destroy a river road bridge R.E. take one move; to repair R.E. take five moves.
皇家工兵破坏一座跨河公路桥，需要一回合；修复，需要五回合。
A supply depot can be destroyed by one man in two moves, no matter how large (by fire).
无论补给仓库多大，一个人都能在两回合内，以纵火将其摧毁。
Four men can destroy the contents of six waggons in one move.
四个人，可以在一回合内，毁掉六辆车上的物资。
A contact mine can be placed on a road or in any place by two men in six moves; it will be exploded by the first pieces passing over it, and will destroy everything within six inches radius.[]
两个人，用六回合，可以在道路或任何地方放置一枚触发雷；第一批经过它的棋子，会将它引爆，半径六英寸以内的一切，都会被摧毁。[]
Next as to Constructions:
接着，说说构筑：
Entrenchments can be made by infantry in four moves.[] They are to be strips of wood two inches high tacked to the country, or wooden bricks two inches high. Two men may make an inch of entrenchment.
步兵可在四回合内筑起战壕。[]战壕用两英寸高的木条，钉在地形上，或者用两英寸高的木积木表示。两个人，可以构筑一英寸长的战壕。
Epaulements for guns may be constructed at the rate of six men to one epaulement in four moves.[]
六个人，四回合，可以为一门炮构筑一道炮位胸墙。[]

[ Notice to be given to umpire of commencement of any work or the placing of a mine. In event of no umpire being available, a folded note must be put on the mantelpiece when entrenchment is commenced, and opponent asked to open it when the trench is completed or the mine exploded.]
[ 任何工程开始，或放置地雷时，都须通知裁判。如果没有裁判，则在开始掘壕时，必须把一张折好的纸条放在壁炉架上；等战壕完工，或地雷爆炸时，再请对手打开。]
Rules as to Cavalry Charging:
关于骑兵冲锋的规则：
No body of less than eight cavalry may charge, and they must charge in proper formation.
少于八名骑兵的部队，不得冲锋；冲锋时，必须保持适当队形。
If cavalry charges infantry in extended order:—
如果骑兵冲击散开队形的步兵：
If the charge starts at a distance of more than two feet, the cavalry loses one man for every five infantry-men charged, and the infantry loses one man for each sabre charging.
若冲锋从两英尺以外开始，每五名被冲击的步兵，使骑兵损失一人；每名冲锋的骑兵，使步兵损失一人。
At less than two feet and more than one foot, the cavalry loses one man for every ten charged, and the infantry two men for each sabre charging.
距离小于两英尺、大于一英尺时，每十名被冲击的步兵，使骑兵损失一人；每名冲锋的骑兵，使步兵损失两人。
At less than one foot, the cavalry loses one man for every fifteen charged, and the infantry three men for each sabre charging.
距离小于一英尺时，每十五名被冲击的步兵，使骑兵损失一人；每名冲锋的骑兵，使步兵损失三人。
If cavalry charges infantry in close order, the result is reversed.
如果骑兵冲击密集队形的步兵，结果则反过来。
Thus at more than two feet one infantry-man kills three cavalry-men, and fifteen cavalry-men one infantry-man.
因此，两英尺以外，一名步兵杀死三名骑兵，十五名骑兵杀死一名步兵。
At more than one foot one infantry-man kills two cavalry, and ten cavalry one infantry.
一英尺以外，一名步兵杀死两名骑兵，十名骑兵杀死一名步兵。
At less than one foot one infantry-man kills one cavalry, and five cavalry one infantry.
一英尺以内，一名步兵杀死一名骑兵，五名骑兵杀死一名步兵。
However, infantry that have been charged in close order are immobile for the subsequent move.
不过，以密集队形受到冲击的步兵，下一回合不能移动。
Infantry charged in extended order must on the next move retire one foot; they can be charged again.
以散开队形受到冲击的步兵，下一回合必须后退一英尺；他们还可以再次遭到冲击。
If cavalry charges cavalry:—
如果骑兵冲击骑兵：

If cavalry is within charging distance of the enemy's cavalry at the end of the enemy's move, it must do one of three things—dismount, charge, or retire. If it remains stationary and mounted and the enemy charges, one charging sabre will kill five stationary sabres and put fifteen others three feet to the rear.
若敌方回合结束时，本方骑兵已在敌方骑兵的冲锋距离内，就必须从三件事中选择一件：下马、冲锋或退却。如果他们不动，继续骑在马上，而敌人发动冲锋，那么每名冲锋骑兵，便能杀死五名静止骑兵，并把另外十五名逼退三英尺。
Dismounted cavalry charged is equivalent to infantry in extended order.
下马骑兵遭到冲击，等同于散开队形的步兵。

If cavalry charges cavalry and the numbers are equal and the ground level, the result must be decided by the toss of a coin; the loser losing three-quarters of his men and obliged to retire, the winner losing one-quarter of his men.
如果骑兵冲击骑兵，双方人数相等，地面平坦，则必须掷硬币决定结果：输方损失四分之三人员，并被迫退却；赢方损失四分之一人员。
If the numbers are unequal, the mêlée rules for Little Wars obtain if the ground is level.
如果人数不等，地面平坦，则适用小战争的混战规则。

If the ground slopes, the cavalry charging downhill will be multiplied according to the number of contours crossed. If it is one contour, it must be multiplied by two; two contours, multiplied by three; three contours, multiplied by four.
如果地面有坡度，向下坡冲锋的骑兵，将按越过的等高线数量倍增。越过一条，乘二；两条，乘三；三条，乘四。

If cavalry retires before cavalry instead of accepting a charge, it must continue to retire so long as it is pursued—the pursuers can only be arrested by fresh cavalry or by infantry or artillery fire.
如果骑兵面对骑兵，不接受冲锋，而选择退却，只要仍被追击，就必须不断后退；追击者只能被新的骑兵，或步兵、炮兵的火力阻止。
If driven off the field or into an unfordable river, the retreating body is destroyed.
如果被赶出战场，或赶进不能涉渡的河流，退却部队便被消灭。

If infantry find hostile cavalry within charging distance at the end of the enemy's move, and this infantry retires and yet is still within charging distance, it will receive double losses if in extended order if charged; and if in two ranks or in fours, will lose at three feet two men for each charging sabre; at two feet, three men for each charging sabre. The cavalry in these circumstances will lose nothing. The infantry will have to continue to retire until their tormentors have exterminated them or been driven off by someone else.
若敌方回合结束时，步兵发现敌方骑兵已在冲锋距离以内，而步兵虽然后退，却仍处于这一距离内，那么，如果以散开队形受到冲击，就承受双倍损失；如果排成两列横队或四人纵队，则在三英尺距离，每名冲锋骑兵杀死两人；两英尺距离，每名冲锋骑兵杀死三人。在这些情况下，骑兵没有损失。步兵必须继续后退，直到这些折磨他们的敌人，将他们杀光，或被别人赶走。

If cavalry charges artillery and is not dealt with by other forces, one gun is captured with a loss to the cavalry of four men per gun for a charge at three feet, three men at two feet, and one man at one foot.
如果骑兵冲击炮兵，而且未被其他部队拦住，那么，每夺取一门炮，在三英尺距离发动冲锋，骑兵损失四人；两英尺，损失三人；一英尺，损失一人。
If artillery retires before cavalry when cavalry is within charging distance, it must continue to retire so long as the cavalry pursues.
如果炮兵在骑兵已进入冲锋距离时，面对骑兵后撤，只要骑兵继续追击，就必须不断后撤。

The introduction of toy railway trains, moving, let us say, eight feet per move, upon toy rails, needs rules as to entraining and detraining and so forth, that will be quite easily worked out upon the model of boat embarkation here given. An engine or truck within the circle of destruction of a shell will be of course destroyed.
引入沿玩具铁轨行驶的玩具火车，比如每回合移动八英尺，就需要制定登车、下车等规则；依照这里给出的登船办法，很容易制定出来。机车或货车车厢，如果处于炮弹的杀伤圈内，当然会被摧毁。

The toy soldiers used in this Kriegspiel should not be the large soldiers used in Little Wars. The British manufacturers who turn out these also make a smaller, cheaper type of man—the infantry about an inch high—which is better adapted to Kriegspiel purposes.
这套兵棋所用的玩具士兵，不应是小战争里使用的那种大兵人。生产大兵人的英国厂商，也生产一种更小、更便宜的兵人：步兵约高一英寸，更适合兵棋用途。

We hope, if these suggestions “catch on,” to induce them to manufacture a type of soldier more exactly suited to the needs of the game, including tray carriers for troops in formation and (what is at present not attainable) dismountable cavalry that will stand.
我们希望，如果这些建议“流行起来”，就能促使他们生产一种更切合游戏需要的士兵，包括承载队列部队的托盘，以及目前还买不到的、可以下马而且能够站立的骑兵。

We place this rough sketch of a Kriegspiel entirely at the disposal of any military men whose needs and opportunities enable them to work it out and make it into an exacter and more realistic game. In doing so, we think they will find it advisable to do their utmost to make the game work itself, and to keep the need for umpire's decisions at a minimum. Whenever possible, death should be by actual gun- and rifle-fire and not by computation. Things should happen, and not be decided. We would also like to insist upon the absolute need of an official upon either side, simply to watch and measure the moves taken, and to collect and check the amounts of supply and ammunition given up. This is a game like real war, played against time, and played under circumstances of considerable excitement, and it is remarkable how elastic the measurements of quite honest and honourable men can become.

我们把这套兵棋的粗略草案，完全交由任何有需要、也有机会的军界人士使用，请他们进一步加工，做成一种更精确、更逼真的游戏。这样做时，我们认为，他们会发现，最好竭力让游戏自行运转，把需要裁判裁决的情况降到最低。只要可能，死亡就应当由实际的炮火与步枪火力造成，而不是计算出来。事情应当发生，而不是由人判定。我们还要坚持，双方各有一名工作人员，是绝对必要的；他们只负责观察、测量已采取的移动，收取并核对交出的补给与弹药数量。这游戏像真实战争一样，必须与时间赛跑，而且是在相当兴奋的情况下进行；十分诚实、体面的人，其测量尺度，竟能变得多么有弹性，实在值得注意。

We believe that the nearer that Kriegspiel approaches to an actual small model of war, not only in its appearance but in its emotional and intellectual tests, the better it will serve its purpose of trial and education.
我们相信，兵棋越接近真实战争的小型模型，不仅外观如此，而且在情感和智力考验上也如此，它就越能发挥检验与教育的作用。

《小战争》从玩具弹簧炮和家庭地板上的试玩出发，追踪一套微缩战争游戏如何形成。威尔斯把射击、移动、近身混战、俘虏、积分与撤退逐步组织成规则，再用胡克农场一役展示具体后果；后续章节讨论装盒侦察、多人指挥、户外场地、运输与铁路，并以对现实战争规模及代价的批评收束。兵棋附录把后勤、工兵、骑兵冲锋与指挥限制引入更复杂的训练模型，同时明确这些只是有待完善的规则草案。 规则不是一次写定的：怎样限制炮手伸手，骑兵能走多远，混战时怎样计算支援，都来自反复试玩和争论。威尔斯也不断比较地板战争与真实战争的差别，希望把竞争留在可收拾的微缩世界里；书末却又尝试把这套玩法扩展为军用兵棋。家庭游戏、设计试验和战争批评由此交织在一起。

PREFACE
序

The increasing popularity of Croquet, and the deficiencies of the existing manuals of the game, have encouraged me to give this little book to the public. The treatise of Captain Mayne Reid, to which the introduction of croquet in this country is mainly due, is deficient in system and arrangement, and affords no intelligible determination to many of the cases I have instanced in illustration of the rules of the game. The manuals published in this country are still more faulty. The rules afford no solution to half of the ambiguous cases that arise in ordinary play; and some are guilty of the strange error of allowing the "Roquet Croquet" to every ball—a liberty totally at variance with the fundamental principles of the game, and which in the hands of strong players would prolong the contest indefinitely, make victory depend upon a single chance hit, and reduce the opportunities for generalship and combination to a minimum. I have dwelt at some length upon the "right of declining," and the "theory of double points;" principles which, though hinted at by Captain Reid, are left rather obscure in his book. Players will find that this power of economizing privileges adds greatly to the interest of the game, and renders many a cunning plot and counter-plot necessary.

槌球日益流行，现有游戏手册又存在种种不足，因此我决定将这本小书公诸于世。Mayne Reid 上尉的论著，对于槌球传入我国居功至伟，却缺少系统和条理；我为说明游戏规则列举的许多案例，在他的书中也找不到明白的裁断。本国出版的手册，缺点更多。日常游戏中出现的疑难情形，至少有一半无法从这些规则中得到解决；有些手册甚至犯了一个奇怪错误，准许所有球使用“无足击送”。这种自由完全违背游戏的基本原则，落到高手手中，会使比赛无限拖延，使 胜负取决于一次偶然命中，把运筹与配合的机会压到最低。我用了相当篇幅讨论“放弃的权利”和“一击双得分的理论”；Reid 上尉虽曾提到这些原则，在书中却讲得相当含糊。玩家会发现，节省特权的这种能力，大大增加了游戏的趣味，也使巧妙布局及其反制成为必要。

The origin of this game is unknown. No man invented whist or chess, and croquet like them seems to have been evolved by some process of nature, as a crystal forms or a flower grows—perfect, in accordance with eternal laws. There is in all these games a certain theory which furnishes interpretations for all cases that arise in actual play. The rules are grouped about a central principle. The mimic battles have a unity, and are homogeneous in all their parts. If the rules are indefinite or contradictory the game loses its distinctive character. If the rules are accurate and rigidly enforced, croquet is a game of the highest interest. I am informed by a scientific billiard player that though croquet is inferior to billiards in affording opportunities for delicate manipulation and manual dexterity, that it far excels that elegant game in the field it opens for the exercise of the higher qualities of combination and foresight. Whist exercises the memory and the power of calculating probabilities; chess the imagination and the faculty of abstract reasoning; but croquet, though it taxes these mental qualities less, combines them with the delights of out-door exercise and social enjoyment, fresh air and friendship—two things which are of all others most effective in promoting happiness. Those who have been in the habit of regarding croquet as a game for children may, perhaps, smile at my enthusiasm; but let them procure a perfect ground, balls and mallets, play half a dozen four-ball games in strict accordance with the rules, and when they can claim to have mastered the game, they will acknowledge themselves converts.

这项游戏的起源无人知晓。惠斯特牌和国际象棋都不是由某一个人发明的；槌球也仿佛像它们一样，经由某种自然过程演化而成，如晶体凝结、花朵生长，依照永恒法则，完美地形成。所有这些游戏都各有一种理论，可为实际游戏中出现的一切情形提供解释。规则围绕一个核心原则组织起来。这些模拟战斗具有统一性，所有部分相互协调。如果规则含糊或自相矛盾，游戏就失去其独特性质。如果规则准确并得到严格执行，槌球便极富趣味。一位精通台球的球手告诉我，槌球虽然在提 供精细操控和手上技巧的机会方面不及台球，在为配合与预见这些更高能力提供施展空间方面，却远远胜过那项优雅的游戏。惠斯特牌锻炼记忆与计算概率的能力；国际象棋锻炼想象与抽象推理能力；槌球对这些心智能力的要求虽较低，却把它们与户外运动、社交的乐趣结合起来，带来新鲜空气与友谊——这两样东西，比其他事物更能增进幸福。习惯把槌球当作儿童游戏的人，也许会笑我热情过头；但只要他们备好上佳的场地、球和球槌，严格依照规则，打上半打四球比赛，等到能够声称掌握这项游戏时，就会承认自己已经信服。

I have adopted the plan of giving first definitions, then rules, then cases adjudged under the rules; as the common law consists of the definitions of legal terms, the statement of legal maxims or principles, and the reports of litigated causes. The laws are in substance those adopted by the "Newport Croquet Club," and many of the cases given actually occurred in play, and were settled in full bench after long and animated discussion. I think the laws will not conflict with those of Captain Reid, while I hope that they will be found more full and accurate, and of more exact application. I cannot flatter myself that I have provided for every possible ambiguous case; still, I hope that I have indicated the solution to most of the questions that are likely to arise in the course of a game.

我采用的编排方式，是先给出定义，再列规则，最后列出依据规则裁决的案例；正如普通法由法律术语的定义、法律格言或原则的陈述，以及争讼案件的报告构成。这些规则实质上就是“纽波特槌球俱乐部”采用的规则；而且 所列许多案例确实发生在比赛中，经过长时间而热烈的讨论，由全体在场裁议者共同裁定。我想，这些规则不会与 Reid 上尉的规则冲突，也希望它们更完整、更准确，应用起来更为精确。我不敢自夸已为一切可能的疑难情形作出规定，但仍希望，游戏过程中可能出现的多数问题，我都已指明解决之道。
I shall be very happy to receive suggestions from any lovers of the game who may discover errors or imperfections; for why should not croquet as well as chess have its literature.
若有喜爱这项游戏的人发现错误或缺漏，我非常乐于收到建议；槌球为什么不能像国际象棋一样，也拥有自己的文献呢？
Newport, R.I., July 7th, 1865.
罗得岛州纽波特，1865 年 7 月 7 日。

CHAPTER I
第一章
DEFINITIONS
定义
Arena.—The space included by the boundaries of the croquet ground, within which a ball driven out of it is entitled to be placed.
场内区域（Arena）——槌球场边界所围成的空间。被击出这一区域的球，有权移回其中放置。
Blow.—The stroke of the mallet. A blow opposed to a push.
击打（Blow）——球槌的一次击球；与推球相区别。
Booby.—A ball that fails to run the first bridge.
未过门球（Booby）——未能通过第一道球门的球。
Bridged Ball.—A ball that has run the first bridge.
已过门球（Bridged Ball）——已通过第一道球门的球。
Central Bridges.—Those in a line between the stakes.
中线球门（Central Bridges）——位于两桩之间同一直线上的球门。
Chiefs.—The leaders of the sides, who strike for the first choice.
领队（Chiefs）——双方的带队者，通过击球争取先选权。
Concussion.—The displacement of a ball by another ball.
碰撞移位（Concussion）——一个球被另一个球碰撞而发生移位。

Croquet.—The title of the game. A privilege gained by making "roquet." It consists in placing the playing ball in contact with the roqueted ball, and on any side of it; holding it there with the foot, and striking it with the mallet, by which means the other is driven in any required direction.
槌球；贴球击送（Croquet）——游戏的名称；也是通过“有效撞球”取得的一项特权。其做法是：把本方正在打的球放到被撞球旁，使两球接触，可以选择其任意一侧；用脚把本球 压在原位，再以球槌击打本球，从而把另一球送往所需方向。
Croqueterie.—The implements of the game—namely, balls, mallets, stakes and bridges.
槌球器具（Croqueterie）——游戏所用的器具，即球、球槌、球桩和球门。
Dead Ball.—A rover struck against the starting stake, and thereby struck out of the game.
死球（Dead Ball）——游走球撞到起点桩，从而退出游戏的球。
Double Point.—Two points made on the same blow.
一击双得分（Double Point）——同一次击打取得两个得分。
Enemy.—A player on the opposite side.
敌方（Enemy）——对方阵营的一名玩家。
Flank Bridges.—Those on the right and left of a line between the stakes.
侧翼球门（Flank Bridges）——位于两桩连线左右两侧的球门。
Flinch.—When in executing the "croquet" the playing ball escapes from under the foot, it is said to "flinch."
脱脚（Flinch）——执行“贴球击送”时，本球从脚下逸出，便称为“脱脚”。
Front of a Bridge.—That side from which a ball must proceed in running it; the side toward the starting stake for the first half round; the side towards the turning stake for the last half round.
球门的迎面侧（Front of a Bridge）——球过门时必须从这一侧进入；前半程是朝向起点桩的一侧，后半程则是朝向折返桩的一侧。
Friends.—Players on the same side.
同伴（Friends）——同一方的玩家。

Grand Round.—The grand round consists in running all the bridges, (the central ones in both directions,) and tolling the turning stake, in proper order; after completing which the ball becomes a rover.
全程（Grand Round）——按规定顺序通过全部球门（中线球门须从两个方向分别通过），并撞到折返桩。完成全程后，该球成为游走球。

Half Round.—The first half round includes running the central bridges and those on the left flank, and is to be made before tolling the stake; the second half round includes the central bridges and those on the left flank which are to be run in the reverse order between tolling and striking out.
半程（Half Round）——前半程包括通过中线球门及左侧翼球门，须在撞折返桩之前完成；后半程包括中线球门及左侧翼球门，须在撞折返桩之后、撞桩退场之前，按相反顺序通过。
Misplay.—Playing out of proper tour; playing the ball of another player, or continuing the tour after failing to make a point.
错打（Misplay）——不按应有回合出手；打了别人的球；或未能得分后仍继续本回合。
Oblique Bridge.—A bridge accidentally out of perpendicular, either to the horizon or to the line joining the stakes.
偏斜球门（Oblique Bridge）——因意外而偏离垂直方向的球门；这里既指不再垂直于水平面，也指不再垂直于两桩连线。
Overrunning a Bridge.—A ball overruns its proper bridge when, in attempting to run it, it passes it on one side.
偏越球门（Overrunning a Bridge）——尝试通过应过球门时，从其一侧越过，称为偏越球门。
Placing a Ball.—Bringing it within the arena when driven out of it, or removing a ball from a fixed obstacle.
放置球（Placing a Ball）——把被击出场内区域的球移回其中，或把球从固定障碍物旁移开。
Point.—A blow by which a step on the round or a roquet is made, thereby entitling the player to continuance of tour—that is, to another blow.
得分（Point）——一次完成行程步骤或有效撞球的击打，使玩家有权继续本回合，也就是再击一次。

Position.—A ball is in position when it is in front of its proper bridge, with a reasonable probability of running it on the next blow. The position is good or bad according to the ease or difficulty of the run.
进门位置（Position）——球处在应过球门的迎面侧，而且下一击有合理机会过门，便算处于进门位置。位置的好坏，取决于过门的难易程度。
Proper Bridge.—The next "step on the round," the making of which constitutes a point.
应过球门（Proper Bridge）——行程中下一项应完成的步骤；完成它便构成一次得分。
Push.—Shoving the ball with the mallet, allowed on some croquet-grounds instead of a blow.
推球（Push）——用球槌推送球；有些槌球场准许用这种方式代替击打。
Re-roquet.—After roquetting a ball to roquet it again during the same tour, a right acquired only by making a step on the round.
再撞（Re-roquet）——对某球作过有效撞球后，在同一回合中再次对它作有效撞球；只有完成一项行程步骤，才能取得这一权利。
Ricochet.—Two or more roquets made on the same blow.
连撞（Ricochet）——同一次击打取得两次或更多次有效撞球。

Roquet.—The contact of the playing ball with another ball under such circumstances as to constitute a point; that is, provided both balls are bridged balls at the time of contact, and roquet has not been made on the same ball before in the same tour since the right to re-roquet has been acquired.
有效撞球（Roquet）——本球与另一球接触，且符合构成得分的条件：两球在接触时都必须已过第一门；自取得再撞权以来，本球尚未在同一回合中对该球作过有效撞球。

Roquet-Croquet; Croquet sans pied.—The privilege of the rover. It differs from croquet in that the playing ball is not held with the foot, so that when struck it follows the croquetted ball or diverges in another direction.
无足击送（Roquet-Croquet；Croquet sans pied）——游走球的特权。它与贴球击送的区别，在于不用脚压住本球；因而击打时，本球会跟随被击送的球，或向另一方向分开。
Rover.—A ball that has made the grand round, but not struck out.
游走球（Rover）——已经完成全程，却尚未撞桩退场的球。
Running a Bridge.—Passing through the proper bridge from the front, or completing such passage, one of the steps on the round, a "point," if made by a blow of the mallet.
过门（Running a Bridge）——从迎面侧通过应过球门，或完成 这一穿越过程。这是行程中的一项步骤；如果由球槌击打完成，就构成“得分”。
Side.—One of the two parties of players, of which the members play alternately.
一方（Side）——玩家分成的两个阵营之一；两方成员交替出手。
Spot.—A point between the starting stake and the first bridge, one mallet's length from the former; from which the play commences.
开球点（Spot）——起点桩与第一道球门之间，距起点桩一槌长的位置；游戏由此开始。
Starting Stake.—That near which the play commences, and the striking of which by a rover puts it out.
起点桩（Starting Stake）——游戏从其附近开始；游走球撞到它，便退出游戏。
Step on the Round.—Running the proper bridge, or tolling the stake at the proper time, which advances a ball on the grand round, and gives the right to re-roquet.
行程步骤（Step on the Round）——通过应过球门，或在适当时机撞折返桩；它推进球的全程，并赋予再撞权。

Striking for First Choice.—The usual method of deciding the first choice, in making up the sides and the first play. Each chief places a ball under the arch of the first bridge and plays at the stake. The ball lying nearest the stake entitles the chief playing it to the first choice of friends and the option of the first or second play.
击球争先选权（Striking for First Choice）——组队和决定谁先开球时，通常用这一方式决定先选权。双方领队各把一个球放在第一道球门拱下，朝球桩击球。谁的球最后离桩最近，谁就有权先选同伴，并可选择第一或第二个出手。
Striking Out.—Hitting the starting stake when a rover, putting a ball out, and if the last of the side constituting the victory.
撞桩退场（Striking Out）——游走球击中起点桩，使该球退出游戏；如果它是本方最后一球，也就意味着本方获胜。
Tolling the Stake.—Hitting the turning stake at the proper time; one of the steps on the grand round.
撞折返桩（Tolling the Stake）——在适当时机击中折返桩；这是全程中的一项步骤。
Tour of Play.—The tour of a player or right to play, following the order of the colors on the stake, and continuing as long as he makes a point.
击球回合（Tour of Play）——玩家的回合或击球权，按照球桩上的颜色顺序轮转；只要继续得分，这一回合就继续。
Turning Stake.—The stake to be tolled, opposite to the starting stake.
折返桩（Turning Stake）——须撞到的球桩，位于起点桩对面。
CHAPTER II
第二章
THE GROUND AND CROQUETERIE
场地与槌球器具

The most important requisite for a croquet ground is smoothness of surface. Very good sport may be had on a ground slightly inclined; indeed a little practice will enable the players to make allowance for the inclination, so as to play with as much accuracy as if the surface were horizontal. But if the turf presents small inequalities, the direction and force of the stroke can never be accurately estimated. If the stroke is gentle, the ball may fall short or be turned aside. If the stroke is forcible, the ball will bound along the ground, and may jump entirely over another ball which it was intended to roquet. A croquet ground can always be brought to the requisite degree of smoothness by having the surface beaten with a spade after a rain; or, better still, thoroughly rammed with a paver's mallet. Rolling is not so effective, unless the ground is very soft or the roller very heavy. The size and shape of the ground is a matter of much less importance. The boundaries within which a ball can be placed should be traced or agreed upon; still better permanently defined by a ditch or slight embankment; and should, if possible, form a parallelogram of eighty feet by fifty. The turf within them should be kept as short as possible. The best arrangement of bridges for the four-ball game is that given in Figure I. For the six or eight-ball game Figure II. is preferable. A ball meets with two kinds of obstructions in making the "grand round"—it is obliged to pass through all the bridges, and again it may be croquetted and driven out of its course by an enemy. In the six or eight ball game, the dangers being much increased, it is well to diminish the difficulties, or the contest may be tediously protracted. This is accomplished by removing the central bridge and straightening the course. The channel is less tortuous, but "roving" privateers, clothed with "belligerent rights," are more frequently met, and the risks and excitement of the passage are equalized in both cases.

槌球场最重要的条件，是地面平整。略有坡度的场地也能玩得很好；实际上，只须稍加练习，玩家就能把坡度计入判断，使击球像在水平地面上一样准确。但若草皮有细小起伏，就永远无法准确估计击球方向和力度。轻击时，球可能停得过近，或偏向一旁；重击时，球会在地上跳动，甚至从本来想有效撞击的另一个球上方整个跃过。雨后用铁锹拍打地面，总能使槌球场达到所需的平整程度；更好的办法，是用铺路工的夯槌彻底夯实。除非地面很软或压辊很重，滚压并不那么有 效。场地的大小与形状，重要性低得多。应把球可以移回放置的区域边界划出，或预先约定；更好的是用浅沟或低土埂永久标定。条件许可时，应划成长八十英尺、宽五十英尺的平行四边形。区内草皮应尽可能剪短。四球比赛最好的球门布局见图一；六球或八球比赛则以图二为宜。球完成“全程”时，会遇到两类阻碍：一是必须通过全部球门，二是可能被敌方贴球击送而偏离路线。六球或八球比赛中的危险大增，宜适当降低困难，否则比赛可能拖得令人厌烦。办法是移去中央球门，使路线更直。航道虽然少了曲折，享有“交战权”的“游走”私掠船却更常出现；两种玩法中，通行的风险与刺激因此得以平衡。

The balls should be perfect spheres, about three inches in diameter, the size depending upon the weight of the wood from which they are made. Maple or beech is a very good material, but the best are made from the buttonwood or American sycamore. They should be boiled in linseed oil to give them the requisite weight and firmness. If boiled too long, however, they will become too heavy. Six ounces is about the proper weight, and a light ball is infinitely preferable to a heavy one for accurate play at long distances. Eight balls constitute a full set. They must be painted different colors, as the individuality of each ball is an important element in the game. As there is no necessity for the exercise of great strength in croquet, a set of balls made from seasoned wood and prepared as I have described ought to last a generation.

球应当是直径约三英寸的正球体，具体大小取决于所用木材的重量。枫木或山毛榉都是很好的材料，但最好的球以美洲悬铃木制成。应放入亚麻籽油中煮过，使球具有所需的重量和坚实程度；但若煮得太久，又会过重。约六盎司是合适重量；长距离准确击球时，轻球远胜重球。八个球构成一整套。各球须涂不同颜色，因为每个球的独立身份是游戏的重要因素。槌球并不需要使很大的力气，因此，以充分干燥的木材制球，再按我所述方式处理，一套球理应能用上一代人的时间。

A variety of mallets should be provided, as different players prefer different sizes. One of the surest hitters I have ever known uses a mallet about fourteen inches long with a heavy head. The wood of the apple tree is the best material for the heads, and straight-grained ash for the handles. The standard handle is thirty-two inches long, one inch in diameter at the upper end, and five-eighths of an inch at the lower, tapering gradually. The head should be a cylinder about two inches in diameter and four inches long. It is best to make the faces square; for if they are convex, it renders it necessary to strike the ball exactly with the centre of the mallet head to insure an accurate stroke.
应备有多种球槌，因为不同玩家偏好不同大小。我认识的一位击球极准的球手，使用一把长约十四英寸、槌头很重的球槌。制作槌头最好的 材料是苹果木，槌柄则宜用纹理直的白蜡木。标准槌柄长三十二英寸，上端直径一英寸，下端直径八分之五英寸，逐渐收细。槌头应为直径约两英寸、长四英寸的圆柱体。击球端面最好做成平正的；若端面凸起，要击得准确，就必须以槌头端面的正中心击中球。

The stakes should be about two feet long, and one and one-half inches in diameter. At least one of them should have rings painted on it corresponding to the colors of the balls. This is merely to aid in recollecting the order of play.
球桩应长约两英尺、直径一又二分之一英寸。至少一根桩上应画有与各球颜色相应的色环。这只是为了帮助记住出手顺序。

Nine bridges are required in the four-ball arrangement, ten in the other. Firkin hoops, or hickory withs, about as large as the ramrod of a rifle, will answer the purpose very well. If soaked a day or two they can easily be bent into the required shape. The best, however, are made of three-eighths round iron. The span of the bridges should be rather less than three times the diameter of a ball. Eight inches is enough. If the ground is small so as to necessitate placing the bridges closer than in the standard arrangement, the span should be narrowed, and "vice versa," on the principle that too much difficulty protracts the game, too little renders it devoid of interest. The height and form of the arch is immaterial, but the pier or side of the bridge should be straight for at least three inches from the ground, and the centre of the arch from seven to nine inches high. The bridges should be driven firmly into the ground, in a plane perpendicular to the horizon and to the line joining the stakes. An inspection of the diagrams will furnish all needful information as to position.

四球布局需要九道球门，另一种布局需要十道。桶箍，或粗细约如步枪通条的山核桃木条，都很合用；浸泡一两天后，就能轻易弯成所需形状。不过，最好的球门用直径八分之三英寸的圆铁条制成。球门跨度应略小于球直径的三倍，八英寸已经足够。如果场地较小，以 致球门间距不得不小于标准布局，就应缩小跨度；反之亦然。原则是：太难会拖长游戏，太容易又使游戏失去趣味。拱门的高度与形状无关紧要，但两侧门柱从地面起至少三英寸应保持笔直，拱顶中央高七至九英寸。球门须牢固插入地中，其所在平面应垂直于水平面，也垂直于两桩连线。查看示意图，就能得到位置方面所需的一切信息。
CHAPTER III
第三章
MANNER OF PLAYING THE GAME
游戏玩法

The game of croquet may be played by any number of players up to eight. If eight enter the game, each player must be provided with a mallet, and each will play one ball. If a less number of persons play, eight balls may still be used, one or more of the players playing two balls. In all cases there should be two sides, or parties, each of course having the same number of balls; and the balls, whether played by the same or different persons, having their turns always in the same prescribed order. An eight-ball or even a six-ball game is apt to be tedious, and skilful players invariably give the preference to the four-ball game, which may therefore be considered croquet par eminence. With more than four balls the element of chance enters too largely, and the combinations become too intricate, to be foreseen with any degree of certainty. The true lover of croquet will no more be tempted into an eight-ball game than a scientific chess-player will indulge in that abnormal monstrosity "four-handed chess." Played with two balls only, the game degenerates into a mere race. The four-ball game with two players is preferred by many, though lacking the sociality which is one of the charms of croquet. As the rules are the same in all cases, I shall hereafter, for convenience of illustration, take it for granted that there are four balls and four players. If the sides are not otherwise made up, two of the players are selected as chiefs. They strike for the first choice, (see definition); the one who wins it chooses a friend, then the other, and so on till the sides are made up. The winning chief plays first if he chooses, or, if not, the other chief leads, and the winning chief plays second; then one of the friends of the first player, and so on, the members of the two sides playing alternately. The first player uses the ball the color of which is highest on the stake, and the next takes the color immediately below. It is usual to have the rings on the stake alternately some light and dark color, so that the light colors form one side and the dark the other. After leading, the function of the chief ceases, except in match games, when he is allowed to direct the play of his side. At the commencement of the game the first player places his ball upon the spot, and strikes it with his mallet in the direction of the first bridge. If it run the bridge—that is, pass completely through it, he has the right to another blow; if not it is called a booby, and he must wait till the others have played and his turn comes round again. Suppose, however, that he has run the first bridge, and on his second blow runs the second bridge, he thus takes another step on the "grand round," or makes another point, which entitles him to still another blow. As it is generally impossible to run the third bridge on the third blow, he now tries to get "position" for his ball in front of the third bridge; but as he does not make a point on this last blow, he is not entitled to continuance of tour. He therefore stops, and the first player of the other side begins by placing his ball upon the spot and attempting to run the first bridge. If he runs it he has a little more latitude in his play, for he may now make a point in two ways—either by hitting the other ball, provided it is not a booby, or running his next bridge. Suppose he chooses to play for the second bridge, and, having run it, plays at the other ball already in position for the third bridge. If he succeeds in hitting it, he is said to have roqueted it, and having thus made a point, may play again and attempt the third bridge. But he has still another privilege; he may take his ball up, place it by the side of the other ball, and croquet it; after which he proceeds to play his ball from the position in which he placed it, having retained it there by his foot during the croquet. He will probably be in position for the third bridge. If he runs it his tour still continues, and he may play for the next bridge, or roquet the other ball again, which he may previously have croqueted, into the proper position. His tour continues till he fails to make a point, when the next player on the other side begins. After running the first bridge, he acquires, of course, the right of roqueting the other two balls. If he roquets an enemy's ball, he croquets it, if he wishes, into a disadvantageous position. If he roquets a friend, he croquets his ball into better position, or perhaps through its proper bridge. This will constitute a step on the grand round for the friend's ball, and will advance it as much as if it were driven through the bridge by the mallet of its proper player. After roqueting a ball, however, a player cannot roquet the same ball again until his own ball has made a step on the grand round. He may drive his own ball against it, and perhaps displace it by the concussion; but the hit does not constitute a roquet, does not entitle to croquet, or to continuance of tour. After making a step on the grand round, however, all his privileges are revived. After all the players have had their tours in the order of the colors on the stake, the first player takes his second tour, and so on. At the beginning of each new tour the grand round is taken up again, and the ball may make a point by making the "proper step on the round"—that is, the one next in order to that last made—whether made by a stroke of the mallet, by "concussion," or by croquet. Or it may make a point by roqueting any of the other balls. In the last case it may play again, either from the spot to which it has rolled or from the side of the roqueted ball; or it may croquet it and then play, attempting the proper step on the round, or roqueting another ball. If it has roqueted all the balls, it can make a point only by running its bridge, or tolling the stake, whichever may be the proper step; after which, as said before, all its privileges are renewed.

槌球可由不超过八人的任意人数参与。八人参赛时，每人必须有一把球槌，各打一球。人数较少时，仍可使用八球，由一名或多名玩家各打两球。无论何种情况，都应分成两方，每方球数当然相同；各球无论由同一人还是不同人操控，都始终按同一规定顺序轮流出手。八球乃至六球比赛都容易冗长，熟练玩家一贯更喜欢四球玩法，因此四球可视为最典型的槌球。超过四球，偶然因素就过多，各种配合也复杂得无法作出较可靠的预见。真正 热爱槌球的人，不会被八球玩法吸引，正如精通国际象棋的人不会沉迷那种畸形怪物“四人国际象棋”。只用两球，游戏又退化成单纯的竞速。许多人喜欢两人各打两球的四球玩法，尽管它少了槌球的一项魅力：社交。各种玩法规则相同，为便于举例，下文都假定有四球、四名玩家。如果双方尚未以其他方式分好，就选两人作领队。他们击球争先选权（见定义）；获胜者先选一名同伴，然后另一方选择，如此继续，直到组队完成。赢得先选权的领队若愿意，便先开球；否则由另一领队先打，赢得先选权者第二个打。然后轮到先打者的一名同伴，如此类推，双方成员交替出手。先打者使用球桩上最上方色环对应的球，下一人取紧接其下的颜色。桩上色环通常深浅交替，因此浅色球组成一方，深色球组成另一方。领队完成开 球后，其职能便终止；但正式对抗赛例外，领队可以指导本方的打法。游戏开始，第一名玩家把球放在开球点上，朝第一门方向击球。如果过门，即完全通过该门，他便有权再击一次；如果未过，就称为未过门球，必须等其他人都打过，自己的回合再次到来。假设他已通过第一门，第二击又通过第二门，便又完成一项“全程”步骤，即又得一分，有权继续再击。第三击通常不可能通过第三门，因此他会尝试把球放到第三门前的“进门位置”；但最后这一击没有得分，所以无权继续本回合。他于是停下，由另一方的第一名玩家把球放到开球点上，尝试通过第一门。如果通过，他就有更多选择，因为这时有两种得分方式：击中另一球——前提是对方不是未过门球——或通过自己的下一门。假设 他选择通过第二门，过门后，再朝已经处于第三门进门位置的另一球击打。如果成功击中，便称为作了有效撞球；既然得分，就可以再击，尝试通过第三门。但他还有另一项特权：可以拿起本球，放在另一球旁，执行贴球击送；随后从放置本球的位置继续打，因为击送时已用脚把球留在原地。他这时很可能已处于第三门的进门位置。如果过门，回合仍继续，可以朝下一门打，或再次有效撞击那只球；此前也许已经把它贴球击送到了合适的位置。只要未能得分，回合才告结束，接着由另一方的下一名玩家开始。通过第一门后，他当然取得有效撞击另外两球的权利。如果撞的是敌球，只要愿意，就可把它击送到不利位置；如果撞的是同伴的球，就把它击送到更好的位置，甚至送过其应过球门。这为同伴的球完成了一项全程步骤，其行程进展 与由该球自己的玩家用槌击打过门完全相同。不过，有效撞击某球之后，必须先让本球完成一项全程步骤，才能在同一回合中再次有效撞击同一球。仍可把本球击向它，也许通过碰撞使它移位；但这次接触不构成有效撞球，不赋予贴球击送权，也不能据以继续回合。一旦完成一项全程步骤，所有这些特权又都恢复。全部玩家按照球桩颜色顺序完成各自回合后，第一个玩家开始第二回合，如此类推。每个新回合开始时，继续此前的全程；球可以完成“应做的行程步骤”而得分，即按顺序完成上一项之后的下一项，无论上一项是由球槌击打、碰撞还是贴球击送完成的。也可以通过有效撞击其他任何一球得分。后一种情况下，可以从本球滚停的位置继续打，或从被撞球旁继续；也可以先贴球击送，再击球尝试完成应做的行程步骤，或有效撞击另一球。如果所有球都已撞过，就只能通过应过球门、或撞折返 桩来得分，取决于哪一项是应做的步骤；完成后，如前所述，一切特权便又恢复。

Thus the game continues until one of the balls completes the grand round, as explained in the diagrams. The last step is running the first bridge in the reverse direction. The player making this takes up his ball, unless he has been so unfortunate as to strike out on the same blow; and places it on the spot whence he continues his tour as a rover, namely, that of croqueting without the foot, or roquet-croqueting after making a roquet. By this means he not only drives off the roqueted ball but follows it with his own, or forces them in divergent directions. If he is skillful, he may leave his own ball near one of the other balls, which he may then proceed to roquet, and succeeding in this, to croquet, or to roquet-croquet, whichever may be most advantageous. As he has no bridges to run he can never re-roquet, and hence after he has roqueted and croqueted all the other balls his tour terminates at the next blow.

游戏如此继续，直到某球完成图示的全程。最后一步，是反向通过第一门。完成这一步的玩家，应拿起球，放到开球点上，从那里以游走球身份继续本回合；除非倒霉到在同一击中已经撞桩退场。游走球的特权，就是完成有效撞球后，可以不用脚进行击送，亦即无足击送。这样，它不仅把被撞球送走，本球也能跟随，或把两球送向不同方向。球手若熟练，可以把本球留在另一球附近，接着尝试有效撞击它；成功后，再按哪种方式更有利，选择贴球击送或无足击送。由于已无球门要过，游走球永远不能取得再撞权；因此，对其他所有球都作过有效撞球并击送之后，再打一击，本回合便告结束。

As soon as a rover touches the starting stake it becomes a dead ball and must be removed from the field. It makes no difference whether it strike out by its own act, or is struck out by its partner, or by one of the enemy. The latter catastrophe will be of frequent occurrence unless perpetually guarded against, for the partner or partners are thereby left to fight against superior numbers. When all the balls of a side succeed in striking the stake the game is over, and the side has won the victory.
游走球一接触起点桩，就成为死球，必须移出场地。它是 自己撞桩退场，还是被同伴或敌方撞出，都没有区别。如果不时刻防备，后一种灾难就会经常发生，使剩下的同伴不得不以少敌多。当一方所有球都成功击中球桩时，游戏结束，该方获胜。
With this brief outline of the game, the reader is referred for details to the chapter on the rules.
