CHAPTER IV
第四章
THE RULES
规则
1. Each ball must first be placed upon the spot and played from thence.
1. 每个球最初都必须放在开球点上，从那里打出。

A booby does not return to the spot, but continues to play as a booby, without the right to roquet or be roquetted until it is bridged. Hence a booby has but one blow unless that blow bridge it. It may hit another ball and be hit, but the contact never constitutes a point.
未过门球不回到开球点，而是继续以未过门球身份打；在通过第一门以前，既无权有效撞击他球，也不能成为他球有效撞球的对象。因此，未过门球每回合只有一击，除非这一击使它过门。它可以击中其他球，也可以被击中，但这种接触绝不构成得分。
2. The mallet must be used with one hand, and the stroke must be a blow.
2. 球槌必须单手使用，而且出手必须是击打。

With balls and mallets of the standard size, there is no necessity for using both hands. It is difficult to draw the precise line between a legitimate blow and a push. In every blow the mallet follows the ball a little, for it takes a small interval of time for the momentum of the mallet to transfer itself to the ball; but in the push a new impulse is given to the ball every instant, and this may act unfairly; for instance, a ball is to be roqueted at a distance of six inches or a foot. If the playing ball is pushed until it reach the other ball, the latter is virtually moved by the mallet as much as in the roquet-croquet, instead of being moved by concussion merely. This would be inconsistent with the theory of the game. Again, a ball is in contact with the pier of its proper bridge so that it cannot run it by a blow. If a push be allowed, it might be pushed into position, and then pushed through by slightly changing the direction of the mallet. It would thus be played in a curved line. It may be objected to this rule that the vicinity of the stake or the piers of a bridge may render a blow impossible; but a little attention will obviate the necessity of playing in constrained positions.

使用标准大小的球与球槌，没有必要双手持槌。合法击打与推球之间，很难划出精确界线。每次击打，球槌都会稍稍跟随球一段，因为球槌的动量传给球，需要很短的一段时间；但推球时，球在每 一瞬间都受到新的推动力，可能因此产生不公平效果。例如，要有效撞击六英寸或一英尺外的一球，如果一直推着本球，直到它碰到另一球，后者实际上就像在无足击送中一样受到球槌推动，而不只是因碰撞而移动。这与游戏的理论不符。再如，本球正贴着应过球门的门柱，无法以击打过门。如果准许推球，就能先把它推到进门位置，再略改球槌方向，将它推过球门；球便能沿曲线被操纵。有人可能反对，认为球靠近球桩或门柱时，击打也许根本不可能；但只要稍加留意，就可避免不得不从受限位置击球。
3. The stroke is delivered when an audible sound is made or the ball moved.
3. 只要发出可听见的声响，或使球移动，便算已经出手。

The habit of giving the ball a little preparatory tap should be avoided. It is allowed to strike the pier of a bridge or the stake with the view of moving the ball by concussion; but if the ball do not move the blow is complete, and the error in judgment cannot be rectified.
应避免先轻轻敲球一下作准备的习惯。准许击打球门门柱或球桩，意图凭碰撞使球移动；但即使球未动，这一击也已完成，不能再补救自己的判断错误。
4. The tour of a ball continues as long as it makes a point, and terminates with the first blow on which no point is made.
4. 只要球继续得分，它的回合就继续；第一记未能得分的击打，使该回合结束。
5. To make a point a ball must either make a step on the grand round or roquet another ball.
5. 球要得分，必须完成全程中的一项步骤，或有效撞击另一球。
Croquet is not considered a point, because it is not a play of the player's own ball but a privilege, after which the tour is continued by virtue of the roquet.
贴球击送不算得分，因为它并非对玩家本球的一次普通击球，而是一项特权；执行后，回合依据此前的有效撞球而继续。
6. Each ball before striking out must make every step on the grand round in the prescribed order, either directly by a blow of the mallet, or indirectly by concussion or croquet.
6. 每个球在撞桩退场之前，都必须依规定顺序完成全程的每一项步骤；既可由球槌直接击打完成，也可通过碰撞或贴球击送间接完成。

"Directly by a blow of the mallet"—that is, during the ball's own tour, whether proceeding from the mallet immediately, or by rebound from a fixed object or the person of an enemy. "Indirectly," not during its own tour, when moved by another ball or accidentally.
“由球槌直接击打”，是指在该球自己的回合内，无论球直接受球槌推动，还是从固定物体或敌方玩家身上反弹。“间接”则指在自己的回合之外，被另一球推动，或因意外而移动。
7. Making the proper step on the round, but no other, constitutes a point, or entitles to continuance of tour.
7. 只有完成应做的行程步骤，才构成得分或有权继续回合；其他步骤都不构成得分。
A step made indirectly is no point either for the playing ball or the other, though the latter is advanced on its round.
间接完成的步骤，对正在打的球和另一球都不算得分，尽管另一球的行程确实得到了推进。
8. The bridges must be run from the front—that is, from the side towards the starting stake for the first half-round, and from the other side for the second half-round.
8. 球门必须从迎面侧通过：前半程从朝向起点桩的一侧进入，后半程则从另一侧进入。
9. A bridge is not run unless the ball pass completely through it.
9. 只有整个球完全穿过球门，才算过门。

To decide this in a doubtful case, place the mallet handle against the piers in front; if any part of the ball project beyond the plane of the bridge it will become evident. The ball is then said to rest under the arch of the bridge.
有疑问时，可把槌柄从迎面侧靠在两根门柱上；若球有任何部分突出于球门所在平面，就能看出来。此时称球停在球门拱下。
10. A ball resting under the arch of a bridge and having come from the front makes no point, but is in position to run the bridge.
10. 从迎面侧进入、停在球门拱下的球，不算得分，但已处于通过该门的进门位置。
The run may now be completed by concussion, or, if the ball remain till next tour, by a blow of the mallet.
此后可以通过碰撞完成过门；如果球一直留到下一回合，也可用球槌击打完成。
11. A ball resting under the arch of a bridge, and having come from the reverse side, is not in position to run it.
11. 从背面一侧进入、停在球门拱下的球，不算处于通过该门的进门位置。
To decide a doubtful case, place the mallet handle against the piers on the reverse side.
有疑问时，把槌柄从背面一侧靠在两根门柱上，即可判断。

Case.—A ball was in position under the arch of a bridge but is driven back, and afterwards gains the same position from the reverse side. Is it in position, since it once reached that point from the front? No. The run of the bridge must be continuous, though not necessarily at one blow.
判例——一球原先在门拱下处于进门位置，后来被击退，又从背面一侧回到同一位置。既然它曾从迎面侧到达此处，现在是否仍算处于进门位置？不算。过门过程必须连续，虽然未必由同一次击打完成。
12. If a ball pass completely through a bridge and rebound or roll back, the run remains good.
12. 球若完全过门，随后反弹或滚回，过门仍然有效。
13. If a ball pass completely through a bridge in the reverse direction, and rebound or roll back under the arch, it is in position.
13. 球若反向完全穿过球门，然后反弹或滚回拱下，就算处于进门位置。
14. If a bridge be oblique any player may adjust it, unless a ball be under the arch.
14. 如果球门偏斜，任何玩家都可以调整，除非有球停在拱下。
That is, it must first be decided whether the ball has run the bridge or is in position.
也就是说，必须先判定球是否已经过门，或是否处于进门位置。
15. The stake may be tolled from any direction and by the slightest perceptible touch.
15. 可以从任何方向撞折返桩；只要是能辨察的最轻微接触，也算撞到。
An audible sound will be evidence of the tolling; but when it is so near that the sound cannot be distinguished from that of the mallet, it must be seen to change its direction.
听见响声，可以证明球已触桩；但球离桩很近，触桩声与槌击声分不清时，就必须看见球改变方向。

16. A ball roquets another when it comes in contact with it from a blow of the mallet; provided both balls are bridged at the time of contact, and the playing ball has not roqueted the other ball before during the same tour since making a step on the round.
16. 本球因球槌击打而接触另一球，就构成对该球的有效撞球，条件是：接触时，两球都已通过第一门；而且自完成一项行程步骤之后，本球尚未在同一回合中对该球作过有效撞球。
Case.—A booby hits a booby and both pass through the first bridge; can it croquet? No. It is not a roquet unless they remain in contact after passing through the bridge. It must roquet again.
判例——一个未过门球击中另一个未过门球，两球都通过第一门；它能否贴球击送？不能。除非两球过门后仍保持接触，否则不构成有效撞球，必须重新有效撞击一次。
17. A ball already in contact with another ball does not roquet unless it move it perceptibly.
17. 已经与另一球接触的球，必须使另一球发生可辨察的移动，才构成有效撞球。
To do this it must, of course, play in a direction less than ninety degrees from a line joining the centres of the balls.
要做到这一点，击球方向与两球球心连线的夹角，当然必须小于九十度。
18. A ball can acquire the right to re-roquet—that is, to roquet the same ball again during the same tour—only by making a step on the round.
18. 球只有完成一项行程步骤，才能取得再撞权，即在同一回合内再次有效撞击同一球的权利。

A ball may hit another ball twice or more during the same tour, and between two consecutive bridges, or between the bridge and the turning stake, and move it, each time by concussion; but only one (not necessarily the first) contact is a valid roquet.
在同一回合中、两道连续球门之间，或球门与折返桩之间，一球可以两次乃至多次击中另一球，每次都通过碰撞使它移动；但只有一次接触算作有效撞球，而且未必是第一次。
19. A roquet, but no hit which does not fulfil all the conditions of a roquet, constitutes a point, and entitles to continuance of tour.
19. 有效撞球构成得分，并赋予继续回合的权利；不具备有效撞球全部条件的接触，都不算得分。
20. A roquet, but no other hit, entitles to the privileges of croquet.
20. 只有有效撞球才赋予贴球击送的特权；其他接触都不能。
21. The croquet may be declined, and the tour continued from the spot to which the player's ball has rolled, or from the side of the roqueted ball.
21. 可以放弃贴球击送，从本球滚停的位置，或从被有效撞击的球旁，继续本回合。

The privilege of the croquet thus consists of two parts. First, the option between the final position of the playing ball and a new position in contact with the roqueted ball, and on any side of it. Second, the croquet proper. The second only, or both parts of this privilege may be declined; but this must be distinguished from "declining roquet" afterward mentioned.
因此，贴球击送特权包含两部分。第一，可以选择让本球留在最后停下的位置，或把它移到与被撞球接触的新位置，放在其任 意一侧。第二，是贴球击送本身。可以只放弃第二部分，也可以两部分都放弃；但必须与下文所说的“放弃有效撞球”区分。

Case.—A ball not a rover having roqueted another ball, is placed in contact with it, and, without using the foot, the player drives them both in any direction, as in roquet-croquet. Is this allowed? Yes. The croquet was declined and the stroke was a common blow; but the other ball, being merely moved by concussion, (since it was previously roqueted,) the tour cannot be continued unless a point was made at the same time.
判例——一只尚未成为游走球的球，有效撞击另一球后，被放到与它接触的位置；玩家不用脚，同时把两球打向任意方向，像无足击送那样。这是否允许？允许。玩家放弃了贴球击送，这一击是普通击打；但另一球此前已被有效撞击过，此时只是因碰撞而移动，所以除非这一击同时取得其他得分，否则本回合不能继续。
22. If after a roquet the playing ball be taken up or moved from its place, it must continue its tour from the side of the roqueted ball.
22. 有效撞球之后，如果本球被拿起或挪离原处，就必须从被撞球旁继续本回合。

Case.—A ball roquets another ball, driving the latter by concussion through the playing ball's proper bridge; remaining, however, in position to run the bridge. The player begins to move the ball, but on second thought concludes to run the bridge. Can he claim to have moved it by accident? No, even if it was not taken up from the ground; for it may be presumed that it was done with the intention to croquet. Whether he croquet or not he must take position by the side of the other, and has lost his opportunity to run the bridge. So, too, if he takes position under the arch of the bridge he is not in position to run it, for the space over which the ball is carried is no part of its course.
判例——一球有效撞击另一球，使后者因碰撞穿过本球的应过球门；本球却仍留在可以过门的位置。玩家开始挪动本球，随后改变主意，决定过门。他能否声称这是意外挪动？不能，即使球尚未被提离地面，也不行，因为可以推定挪球是为了贴球击送。不管是否执行击送，他都必须 在另一球旁就位，已经失去这次过门机会。同样，把球放到门拱下执行击送，也不算处于进门位置；因为球被拿着移过的空间，不属于它的行进路线。
23. The croquet must be executed before continuance of tour.
23. 必须先执行贴球击送，才能继续本回合。

Case.—A ball roquets another and on the same blow runs its bridge; the croquet is then executed. Does the run hold good. Yes, at the player's option. Case.—Under the same circumstances the playing ball is taken to the side of the roqueted ball. Can it re-roquet it on the ground that it has run a bridge since the roquet? No. The right to re-roquet must be acquired after croqueting or moving the playing ball. But the playing ball might have re-roqueted from its final position, declining the first croquet.
判例——一球在同一击中，先有效撞击另一球，又通过本球的球门；随后执行贴球击送。过门还算有效吗？算，由玩家自行选择。判例——同样情况下，本球被拿到被撞球旁。能否以有效撞球之后已过一道球门为由，再撞同一球？不能。再撞权必须在执行贴球击送或挪动本球之后取得。但玩家本来可以放弃第一次贴球击送，从本球最后停下的位置，再撞那一球。
24. The croquet is completed when the mallet makes a perceptible blow against the croqueting ball; but if the mallet altogether miss it, the blow may be repeated.
24. 只要球槌对执行击送的本球作出可辨察的击打，贴球击送便算完成；但若球槌完全没有碰到本球，就可以重击。
The blow is perceptible if an audible sound is made, whether the croqueted ball move or not.
只要发出了听得见的响声，便属可辨察的击打，无论被击送的另一球是否移动。

Case.—A player in croqueting claims to have hit his foot; the croqueted ball, however, has moved from its place. Can he restore it and repeat the blow? No. The claim should not be allowed, for it is impossible to tell in such cases whether the ball was hit or only the foot. If it be necessary to get the other ball out of the way, he must drive it by concussion with his own.
判例——玩家在贴球击送时，声称自己打中了脚，但被击送球已经离开原位。他能否把球放回，再击一次？不能。不应准许这一主张，因为此类情况下无法判断究竟打中了球，还是只打中了脚。如果必须把另一球从路线上移走，他就只能用本球通过碰撞把它打走。
25. If the player's ball flinch in executing the croquet he forfeits the remainder of his tour, and no point made by a flinching ball is valid.
25. 贴球击送时，本球若脱脚，玩家就丧失该回合余下的击球权；脱脚球取得的任何得分都无效。

Case.—A flinching ball rests under the arch of its proper bridge, having come from the front. Is it in position? No. If the complete run is illegal, the partial run is also, as in the case of moving a ball to croquet.
判例——脱脚球从迎面侧进入，停在应过球门的拱下。它算处于进门位置吗？不算。既然完整过门都不合法，部分过门也不合法；与把球挪去贴球击送的情形相同。
26. If a ball be driven out of the arena, it must be brought within it, and placed one foot from the boundary at the nearest point.
26. 球被击出场内区域时，必须移回区域内，在离边界最近的地方，距边界一英尺处放置。

This rule is on the supposition that the arena is of the standard dimensions or something near it. If from the imperfections of the ground the boundaries at any place approach too near the stakes or bridges, this rule must be modified so that a ball shall not materially alter its position with reference to the bridges, stakes, or other balls. Under the same limitations it may be removed one foot from a tree or other obstacle. The ball should be placed immediately.
这条规则以场内区域具有标准或接近标准尺寸为前提。如果由于场地不完善，有些地方的边界太靠近球桩或球门，就必须调整这条规则，使球相对于球门、 球桩或其他球的位置，不发生实质改变。在同样限制下，也可把球从树或其他障碍物旁移开一英尺。应当立即放置球。

Case.—A's ball is played against a tree. If B roquet it he cannot croquet it, or play his ball afterwards to advantage. Can he compel A to place his ball? Yes; but not so that B's position after the roquet shall be improved. If this were not so ruled, an obstacle would often be made a refuge. Cases of this kind often arise on imperfect grounds. They must be settled like cases in equity; as fairly as possible for each side, and so that neither can take advantage of technicalities.
判例——A 的球打到一棵树旁。B 若有效撞击它，就既不能贴球击送，也无法在随后有利地打本球。他能否要求 A 放置其球？可以，但不能因此改善 B 在有效撞球后的位置。若不这样裁定，障碍物便常会变成避难所。这类情形在不完善的场地经常出现，必须像衡平法案件一样处理，尽可能公平照顾双方，使任何一方都不能利用技术细节取巧。

27. If a player misplay, and the enemy challenge him before allowing the play of another ball, they have the option of replacing the misplaying ball and any which may have been moved in their former positions, or allowing any or all of them to remain in the positions to which they have rolled. And no point made by a misplaying ball, if properly challenged, is valid, except at their option.
27. 玩家错打时，如果敌方在允许另一球出手之前提出异议，敌方可以选择把错打球及任何被移动的球放回原位，也可以允许其中任意球或全部球留在滚停的位置。对于被及时提出异议的错打球，它取得的任何得分，除非敌方选择认可，否则均无效。

The option belongs to the enemy of the players and not of the ball. If the challenge be made as soon as possible, though another ball is played at the same time, the requirements of the rule are satisfied.
选择权属于错打玩家的敌方，而不是所打那只球的敌方。只要已尽早提出异议，即使另一 球恰好同时出手，也满足本规则要求。

Case.—A misplaying ball runs a bridge after croqueting its partner through his proper bridge. The enemy challenge and elect to leave both balls in their final position. Can they compel them to renew their bridges? The ball of the misplayer must re-run its bridge; but any other ball has made the step unless it is restored to its former position. The latter is regarded as accidentally displaced, and follows the rule provided for that case. If the misplay consist of illegal continuance of tour, of course the penalty does not extend to the correct play which preceded it.
判例——一只错打球先把同伴的球贴球击送过其应过球门，随后本球也过了一门。敌方提出异议，选择让两球都留在最终位置。能否强迫两球重新过门？错打球必须重新过门；其他球则已经完成该步骤，除非被放回原位。后者被视为意外移位，适用为这种情形制定的规则。如果错打仅在于不合法地继续回合，处罚当然不追溯到此前合法的击球。
28. If a player misplay, whether with his own or another ball, he forfeits his next tour.
28. 玩家错打时，无论打的是本球还是他球，都丧失自己的下一回合。

When a misplay is detected the play is stopped, and the damages under the preceding rules taken, and the player who should have played takes his tour, and so on, omitting the misplayer's next tour. Thus if A play in his partner C's tour, the order will be C, D, B, C, etc. If A play without right to continuance of tour, the order will be B, C, D, B, C, etc.
发现错打，应立即停下，依前述规则处理造成的损害，由本来应该出手的玩家开始回合，如此继续，并跳过错打者的下一回合。例如 A 在同伴 C 的回合出手，接下来的顺序应为 C、D、B、C，等等。如果 A 在无权继续回合时继续击球，接下来的顺序便为 B、C、D、B、C，等等。
29. If a misplay is not challenged until the play of another ball has commenced, the play stands, but the misplayer loses his first tour after the discovery.
29. 如果到另一球已开始出手后，才对错打提出异议，已发生的击球照算，但错打者丧失被发现后的第一个回合。

Case.—D plays after A and is challenged, but shows that A misplayed in his partner's tour. Has D misplayed? No. He played in his proper tour. C has lost his tour through neglect, and A has anticipated a tour, while the other side has lost the right to exact the penalty for A's misplay, the order of play is B, A, D, B, C, etc.
判例——D 在 A 之后出手，遭到异议，但指出 A 是在其同伴的回合中错打。D 是否也错打？没有；D 是在自己的正确回合出手。C 因疏忽丧失一个回合，A 则提前用了一个回合；另一方也已失去要求处罚 A 错打的权利。接下来的出手顺序为 B、A、D、B、C，等等。

Case.—While B is playing it is discovered that A misplayed. Is B's play correct? Yes. B naturally plays after A. B finishes his play, and the order of play is B, A, B, C, D, B, etc. Here A's tour is merely transposed, and B gains an extra tour, so that in both cases the misplaying side loses one tour. If a player misplays in the tour of an enemy and is not challenged in time, the misplayer and the neglectful party will each lose a tour. Thus if D omit his tour the order will be C, A, B, C, D, B, etc. If A play without right to continuance of tour, so as in effect to take two tours, and it is discovered after B begins to play, A merely anticipates his next turn, and the order is A, A, B, C, D, B, etc.

判例——B 击球过程中，才发现 A 曾错打。B 的击球是否正确？正确，B 自然在 A 之后出手。B 完成击球后，顺序为 B、A、B、C、D、B，等等。这里 A 的回合只是被调换位置，B 则多得一个回合，所以两种情形中，错打的一方都损失一个回合。如果有人在敌方回合错打，却未及时受到异议，那么错打者和疏忽的一方，各损失一个回合。例如 D 漏打自己的回合，顺序便为 C、A、B、C、D、B，等等。如果 A 在没有继续回合权利的情况下出手，实际上占用了两个回合，直到 B 开始击球后才被发现，那么 A 只是预用了下一回合，顺序为 A、A、B、C、D、B，等等。

30. If a misplay has taken place so that the balls are playing in a wrong order, but the original misplayer cannot be discovered, the playing ball must finish its tour and the right order be taken up.
30. 如果发生过错打，以致各球按错误顺序出手，但无法找出最初的错打者，则正在打的球应完成本回合，随后恢复正确顺序。

A case of frequent occurrence in the four-ball game. The sides are still playing alternately, but in an inverted order, A, D, C, B. A misplay has evidently been made, but none of the subsequent players can be convicted, because each has followed his partner after the proper interval; hence no penalty can be exacted on either side. If two partners are playing in succession, the last always misplays; and, if detected before the next play, must suffer the full penalty, and any previous player in the same circumstances loses his next turn.
这在四球比赛中经常发生。双方仍交替出手，但次序颠倒，成为 A、D、C、B。显然曾有人错打，但后续任何玩家都无法被判定有错，因为每人都是在同伴之后，间隔了正确的轮次才出手；因此双方都不能被处以处罚。如果同伴两人接连出手，后打者总是错打；若在下一次出手前被发现，必须承受全部处罚；此前有同样情形的玩家，则各失去自己的下一回合。

31. If a ball be played before the preceding ball has finished or abandoned its tour, the enemy have the option of replacing the ball to take its tour after the other has finished, or letting the play stand as the player's next tour.
31. 如果前一球尚未完成或放弃回合，后一球便出手，敌方可以选择把该球放回，等前一球打完后再开始它的回合；也可以让这次击球照算，作为该玩家的下一回合。

This case is excluded from the definition of misplay, and the penalty exacted is less. As will be seen by the next rule, the ball prematurely played will have had but one blow. If it was a good one the enemy will have the ball replaced; if a poor one they will let it stand; and if an easy point has been made, the player loses the rest of his tour, as in misplay, except that if a step on the round is made it is valid.
这种情形不包括在错打的定义内，处罚也较轻。由下一条可知，提前出手的球，此时只会已打过一击。如果那一击打得好，敌方就会要求 放回；如果打得不好，则让它照算。如果那一击轻易得分，玩家也像错打一律失去该回合余下的击球权；区别只在于：如果完成了一项行程步骤，该步骤有效。
32. A player abandons his tour if he allows the next player to make two blows before challenging him, or make use of words or actions implying that he has finished his tour.
32. 玩家若在下一人已击两次之后才提出异议，或以言语、行动表示本回合已经结束，就算放弃本回合。
As calling the name of a player or color of the ball. Of course it is implied that a tour abandoned cannot be resumed.
例如叫出下一名玩家的姓名，或其球的颜色。这里当然也意味着，已经放弃的回合不能恢复。

Case.—A seems to abandon his tour, B begins to play, and C reminds A of his right to continuance of tour. Has A abandoned his tour? Yes, if he had not intended to play until he was reminded, or acted so as to convey such an impression.
判例——A 看起来放弃了本回合，B 开始击球，C 却提醒 A 仍有权继续。A 是否已经放弃？如果在受到提醒之前，他本来不准备再击，或其举动使人产生这种印象，就算放弃。
33. A ball accidentally displaced may be replaced, or allowed to remain, at the option of the enemy of the player who caused the accident.
33. 球意外移位时，造成意外的玩家之敌方，有权选择把球放回，或让它留在现处。
A ball moved under the foot in croqueting, but not flinching, is accidentally displaced.
贴球击送时，球在脚下挪动，却没有脱脚，算作意外移位。
34. If a ball accidentally displaced make a step on the round, the step is valid unless the ball be replaced.
34. 意外移位的球若完成一项行程步骤，除非将球放回，否则该步骤有效。
In the same case the position is good if it pass under the arch of a bridge from the front.
同样情况下，若球从迎面侧进入门拱下，也算处于进门位置。

35. If a ball in motion be interrupted by one of the players, it may rest at the point of interruption, or be carried to the most distant part of the arena in the direction in which it was moving, at the option of the enemy of the player causing the interruption.
35. 如果有玩家拦住正在运动的球，造成阻拦者的敌方，可以选择让球停在受阻处，或沿其原运动方向，把球移至场内区域的最远处。
If a croqueted ball is interrupted, the croquet may be repeated.
如果被拦住的是正被贴球击送的球，可以重新执行击送。
36. A player may decline any point made by himself, and play precisely as if the point had not been made.
36. 玩家可以放弃自己取得的任何得分，此后完全按照该得分未曾发生的情况继续打。

Of course if no other point is made on the same blow the tour is finished. The application of the principle is connected with double points. If a single roquet is declined, the effect is the same as if the croquet and continuance of tour were declined; but if a step on the round is declined, it remains the proper step and must be made again, and the tour ceases. If the player wishes to adopt this course he must signify that he declines the run or toll, or he will be presumed to have declined continuance of tour merely. Striking out is not a point, and of course cannot be declined.
当然，如果同一击没有取得其他得分，回合就结束了。这一原则的运用，与一击双得分有关。放弃单独一次有效撞球，效果等同于同时放弃贴球击送和继续回合；但如果放弃的是行程步骤，该步骤便仍是应做的步骤，必须重做，回合也随之结束。如果玩家要这样处理，就必须明确表示，自己放弃认定此次过门或撞折返桩；否则会被推定，只是放弃继续本回合。撞桩退场不是得分，当然也不能放弃。

Case.—A ball passes through its bridge and recoils under the arch. Can the player decline the run, leaving the ball in position? No. If it ran the bridge, it passes under the arch in the wrong direction in recoiling. So also if the bridge declined is the second of two consecutive ones run, or a single blow—a case more likely to occur, as continuance of tour is then retained by virtue of the first run.
判例——球通过自己的球门，又退回拱下。玩家能否放弃认定过门，同时把球留作处于进门位置？不能。因为 如果它曾经完整过门，退回拱下时，就是从错误方向进入。同样的道理，也适用于被放弃的球门是连续通过的两门中的第二门，或由单次击打完成的情况；后一种情形更可能出现，因为此时仍可凭第一门的通过而保留继续回合的权利。
37. If a player decline one of two points made on the same blow, he may continue his tour by virtue of the other.
37. 玩家若放弃同一击取得的两个得分之一，可以凭另一得分继续本回合。
He should signify which one he intends to decline; and unless he does so, either by words or by the course of play, he may be presumed not to have declined either.
应当表明自己准备放弃哪一个。如果既未以言语表明，也未通过后续打法表明，就可推定两个都未放弃。
38. A step on the round made and declined must be made again, and when made constitutes a point.
38. 已完成又被放弃的行程步骤，必须重做；重做时，仍构成得分。

For instance, a ball makes roquet upon another ball, and accidentally glances through its own bridge. If it should be in position after croqueting, it may prefer to decline the run and make it again. It must be remembered that it is not in position if placed under the arch to croquet, and that the roquet must have been legitimate at the time of contact, otherwise the run is the only point made, for the right to re-roquet cannot be antedated.
例如，一球有效撞击另一球，又意外擦过自己的球门。如果贴球击送后仍处于进门位置，玩家也许宁愿放弃认定此次过门，重新通过一次。必须记住：如果是为贴球击送而把球放到门拱下，就不算处于进门位置；而有效撞球也必须在接触发生时就合法，否则唯一的得分只有过门，因为不能把后来取得的再撞权追溯到此前。

Case.—A ball makes roquet and runs a bridge at the same shot. After croqueting, he attempts to run the bridge and fails. Can he adopt the previous run? No. The attempt to run the bridge shows that he elected to decline the bridge. If he wishes to play in the direction of the bridge without declining he should signify his election, and then an accidental run will not constitute a point. If he plays in another direction, the bridge is not declined unless he so signify. He has the option at the time, but must make his choice at once; and if he says nothing before he plays, he is committed to that alternative which his play seems naturally to indicate.

判例——一球在同一次击球中有效撞球并通过一门。 贴球击送后，他尝试重新过门，却失败了。能否改为接受先前那次过门？不能。尝试过门本身，就表明他选择放弃了先前的过门。如果想朝球门方向打，却不放弃原来的过门，就应表明自己的选择；这样，意外再次过门也不构成得分。如果朝别的方向打，除非明确声明，否则不算放弃原来的过门。他当时有选择权，但必须立即选择；如果出手前什么也没说，就受其打法自然显露出的那种选择约束。
39. A step on the round made by a ball through concussion, croquet, or roquet-croquet from another ball, cannot be declined, and the next step becomes proper.
39. 一球因另一球的碰撞、贴球击送或无足击送而完成行程步骤，不能放弃认定；接下来的一项便成为应做步骤。
40. A step on the round made by flinch, accident, or misplay, is valid or not at the option of the enemy of the party in fault, who must make their decision at once.
40. 因脱脚、意外或错打而完成的行程步骤，是否有效，由有过失一方的敌方选择；必须立即作出决定。

In case of accident or displace through a misplaying ball, it depends upon whether the ball is left or replaced. In case of the misplayer's ball, or a flinching ball, the option is with the enemy. In the cases of Rule 39 there is no option, and in Rule 36 it rests with the player himself.
在意外或被错打球撞移的情形中，取决于球被留在现处，还是放回。在错打者本球或脱脚球的情形中，选择权属于敌方。第 39 条所述情形 没有选择权，第 36 条则由玩家自己选择。
41. If a ball makes two successive steps on the round with one blow of the mallet, and does not decline the latter, it may take ground up to a standard mallet's length before continuing its tour.
41. 一球若在球槌的一次击打中，连续完成两项行程步骤，而且不放弃后一项，就可以在继续回合之前，挪位不超过一把标准球槌的长度。

The first step cannot be declined from the nature of the case; the second may, but then there is no ground for the premium. The second point will be declined if it is possible to make very good position for the second bridge by roquet, or to glance off from the stake to advantage. If the mallet's length allows a ball to take ground on the reverse side of its proper bridge this will not count as a run, nor will the ball be in position if placed under the arch. Up to a mallet's length of course includes everything less.
依此种情形本身的性质，第一项步骤不能放弃；第二项可以，但放弃后就没有取得这项奖励的依据。如果可以通过有效撞球，为第二门取得极好的进门位置，或能从球桩旁有利地擦离，玩家就会放弃第二个得分。如果一槌长足以把球挪到应过球门的背面，这种挪位不算过门；把球放到拱下，也不算处于进门位置。“不超过一槌长”，当然也包括一切比它更短的距离。
42. A step on the round is not declined if it be made the ground for continuance of tour, re-roquet, or taking ground under the last two rules, and in such case it cannot be made again.
42. 如果玩家以某项行程步骤作为继续回合、取得再撞权，或按前两条规则挪位的依据，就不算放弃该步骤；这种情况下，也不能重新完成它。
Case.—A having already roqueted B's ball, can he decline the run? If he does the hit is no roquet, and no point has been made.
判例——A 已经有效撞过 B 的球，他能否放弃认定此次过门？如果放弃，这次击中就不算有效撞球，也就没有取得任何得分。

Case.—A runs a bridge and roquets a ball. The two balls rest in such relative positions that A can roquet the same ball back through the bridge. Can he, after doing this, re-run the bridge? Not on that tour; for if he continues his tour, the second hit must have been a roquet; the roquet on the first blow must have been declined; therefore the bridge could not have been declined. Or, if the bridge was declined, the first hit was a roquet and the second no point; therefore his tour is at an end.
判例——A 通过一门，并有效撞击一球。两球停下时的相对位置， 使 A 可以再次有效撞击同一球，反向穿回该门。这样做以后，他能否重新通过该门？在本回合内不行。因为如果回合能够继续，第二次击中就必须是有效撞球；第一击中的有效撞球就必定已被放弃认定；因此过门不可能也已被放弃。反过来，如果放弃的是过门，那么第一次击中是有效撞球，第二次却不构成得分，回合便已结束。
43. A roquet made and declined may be made again during the same tour, although the right to re-roquet has not been acquired, and when so made it constitutes a point.
43. 一次已经完成又被放弃认定的有效撞球，可以在同一回合内重新作出，即使尚未取得再撞权；重新作出时，仍构成得分。

The first hit was not a roquet if really declined. (See Rule 45.) A ball may be hit and moved by concussion before a roquet as well as after one. Thus if a step on the round and a roquet be made on the same blow, the player may at once croquet the roqueted ball, or roquet it again immediately or after other roquets. Not croqueting the ball is evidence enough of having declined, as there could never be any advantage in declining the croquet and not the roquet, if it can properly be declined.
如果确实放弃认定，第一次击中就不算有效撞球（见第 45 条）。球在有效撞球之前和之后，都可能被击中，并因碰撞移位。因此，如果同一击完成一项行程步骤，又作了一次有效撞球，玩家可以立即对被撞球执行贴球击送；也可以立即再次有效撞击它，或先有效撞击其他球，再回头撞它。不执行贴球击送，已足以证明放弃了认定，因为如果有效撞球确实可以被放弃，就绝不会有只放弃贴球击送、却保留有效撞球的好处。
44. A ball making ricochet—that is, roqueting several balls on the same blow—may croquet them all in the order of the roquets.
44. 一球完成连撞，即在同一击中有效撞击 数个球，可以依有效撞击发生的顺序，对它们全部执行贴球击送。

Any one of the roquets may be declined and made again after croqueting the other balls in their proper order. Not croqueting is sufficient evidence of declining; but if none are croqueted, and the ball is not moved to the side of any one, the player must declare which he means to decline. As soon as a step on the round is made, it no longer makes any difference whether a roquet was declined or not.
可以放弃其中任何一次有效撞球，先按规定顺序对其他球贴球击送，随后再作出那次有效撞球。不贴球击送，已足以证明放弃认定；但若所有球都不击送，而且本球也未挪到其中任何一球旁，玩家就必须声明准备放弃哪一次。只要完成一项行程步骤，之前某次有效撞球是否曾被放弃，便再无区别。
Case.—A ball makes roquet on two balls simultaneously. Can it croquet them both? Yes, and the player should have the option of either order.
判例——一球同时有效撞击两球。能否对两球都贴球击送？可以，而且玩家应有权任选先后顺序。

45. A roquet is not declined if it is made the ground for continuance of tour, croquet, or playing from the side of the roqueted ball; and in such case the same ball cannot be roqueted again during the same tour until the right to re-roquet has been acquired.
45. 如果有效撞球被用作继续回合、贴球击送或从被撞球旁出手的依据，就不算放弃认定；这种情况下，在取得再撞权之前，不能于同一回合内再次有效撞击同一球。
46. A ball running the last bridge by a direct blow of the mallet must be carried to the spot and played from thence as a rover, unless it strike out on the same blow.
46. 一球由球槌直接击打而通过最后一道球门，必须拿到开球点上，从那里以游走球身份打出；除非它已在同一击中撞桩退场。

The ball in this last case passes over the spot, and thus of itself complies with the condition and becomes a rover, after which it may strike out. Hence, also, if it does strike out, the bridge cannot be declined so as to save the ball.
后一种情况下，球会经过开球点，因而自行满足这一条 件并成为游走球，随后即可撞桩退场。也因此，如果它确实撞桩退场，就不能靠放弃认定过门来挽救这只球。
Case.—A ball runs the last bridge and roquets a ball on the same blow. Can it croquet? Not unless the bridge is declined, otherwise it must be placed on the spot immediately.
判例——一球在同一击中通过最后一门，并有效撞击另一球。能否贴球击送？除非放弃认定过门，否则不能；因为不放弃过门，就必须立即把本球放到开球点上。
47. A ball running the last bridge otherwise than by a direct blow of the mallet becomes a rover, but must be played from its final position like any other ball.
47. 一球不是由球槌直接击打，而以其他方式通过最后一门，也成为游走球；但它必须像其他球一样，从最后停下的位置打。
48. A rover having no bridges to run can never re-roquet.
48. 游走球已经没有球门要过，所以永远不能取得再撞权。
A rover can make no more points than the number of balls in the game, and can have but one more blow.
游走球能取得的得分数，不超过本局球的总数；此后只能再打一击。
49. A rover, but no other ball, may roquet-croquet a roqueted ball instead of croqueting it.
49. 只有游走球，才可以对已被有效撞击的球执行无足击送，以代替贴球击送；其他球都不可以。
If the player, however, elect to use the foot, and his ball flinch, he must suffer the penalty. If in flinching the rover strike the starting stake, he is out if the enemy so decide.
不过，如果玩家选择用脚压球，本球又脱脚，就必须承受处罚。如果游走球在脱脚后撞到起点桩，只要敌方如此决定，它就退场。
50. If a rover in roquet-croqueting hit another ball, it may accept or decline the roquet.
50. 游走球在无足击送中击中另一球，可以接受或放弃认定这次有效撞球。
It is entitled to another blow after roquet-croquet at any rate; therefore the roquet is not necessary to give continuance of tour.
不管怎样，完成无足击送后，它都有权再击一次；因此，不需要凭这次有效撞球来取得继续回合权。
51. A rover fails to roquet-croquet if the other ball is not moved, and the tour terminates unless another ball is roqueted on the same blow.
51. 游走球执行无足击送，若未使另一球移动，就算无足击送失败；除非在同一击中有效撞击了别的球，否则本回合结束。
The blow not being a roquet-croquet, a point must be made to entitle to continuance of tour. A roquet-croquet is precisely like a roquet when the balls are in contact. (See Rule 17 and remarks.)
这一击既然不算无足击送，就必须取得一次得分，才有权继续回合。两球本来接触时，无足击送的性质与有效撞球完全相同（见第 17 条及其解释）。
52. A rover is struck out whenever it touches the starting stake, except when in case of accident or misplay the enemy of the party in fault decide otherwise.
52. 游走球一旦接触起点桩，就应退场；但在意外或错打情况下，有过失一方的敌方作出相反决定时例外。
CHAPTER V
第五章
HINTS TO BEGINNERS
给初学者的提示
1. Leave your ball as far from your enemy and as near your friend as possible.
1. 尽量把本球留在远离敌球、靠近同伴球的地方。
2. If you are in advance, help your friend; if you are behind, call upon him to help you.
2. 如果你行程领先，帮助同伴；如果落后，请他来帮助你。

3. Recollect that position directly under the arch of your proper bridge enables you to command all the field in front of it. You can run the bridge and leave your own ball near any other you wish to croquet, as the run gives you another shot. It is many times advantageous to decline making any stroke from such position, and wait until you see an opportunity to do execution among the enemy.
3. 记住，在应过球门的拱下直接占据进门位置，便能控制门前整个场地。你可以通过该门，再把本球留在任何你想贴球击送的球旁，因为过门给了你又一次击球机会。许多时候，从这个位置暂不击球，等到有机会重创敌方再行动，反而更有利。
4. Take pains and exercise judgment on every stroke.
4. 每一击都要用心，并作出判断。
5. If you are a rover, leave yourself close to your friend. He can then croquet you towards the enemy who played last, whom you can afterwards demolish with impunity.
5. 如果你是游走球，就留在同伴球附近。他随后可以把你贴球击送到 最后出手的敌球旁，你接着便能安然无虞地摧毁它。
6. Play strictly according to rule; apply the laws rigidly, but be liberal in settling disputed questions of fact.
6. 严格遵守规则；执行规则要严，但裁定有争议的事实问题时，要宽厚。
7. Do not attempt difficult shots except in desperate circumstances.
7. 除非形势绝望，不要尝试高难度击球。

8. If the enemy have a rover, make every effort to put it out. One of you can then watch the remaining enemy while the other finishes the round. Your partner then relieves the guard while you make your bridges. The most desperate games can often be thus redeemed.
8. 敌方若有游走球，应竭尽全力使它退场。这样，你们一人可以盯住剩下的敌球，另一人完成全程；然后同伴接替看守，你再通过自己的各道球门。最绝望的局面，往往也能这样挽回。
9. Never despair because you are behind. The game is never out till it is played out.
9. 不要因为落后而绝望。没有打到最后，游戏就不算结束。

NEW LAMPS FOR OLD.

1. Propositions.
1. 命题。

There are three 'PROPOSITIONS' for you--the only three kinds we are going to use in this Game: and the first thing to be done is to learn how to express them on the Board.

Let us begin with
让我们从
"Some new Cakes are nice."
“有些新蛋糕是美味的。”
But before doing so, a remark has to be made--one that is rather important, and by no means easy to understand all in a moment: so please to read this VERY carefully.
但在着手之前，必须提出一个注记——这一注记颇为重要，且绝不容易一下子就完全理解：因此请务必极其仔细地阅读此段。

The world contains many THINGS (such as "Buns", "Babies", "Beetles". "Battledores". &c.); and these Things possess many ATTRIBUTES (such as "baked", "beautiful", "black", "broken", &c.: in fact, whatever can be "attributed to", that is "said to belong to", any Thing, is an Attribute). Whenever we wish to mention a Thing, we use a SUBSTANTIVE: when we wish to mention an Attribute, we use an ADJECTIVE. People have asked the question "Can a Thing exist without any Attributes belonging to it?" It is a very puzzling question, and I'm not going to try to answer it: let us turn up our noses, and treat it with contemptuous silence, as if it really wasn't worth noticing. But, if they put it the other way, and ask "Can an Attribute exist without any Thing for it to belong to?", we may say at once "No: no more than a Baby could go a railway-journey with no one to take care of it!" You never saw "beautiful" floating about in the air, or littered about on the floor, without any Thing to BE beautiful, now did you?

世界包含许多事物（如“面包”、“婴儿”、“甲虫”、“羽毛球拍”等）；这些事物拥有许多属性（如“烤过的”、“美丽的”、“黑色的”、“破碎的”等：事实上，任何能够被“归之于”某事物的东西，即所谓“属于”某事物的东西，皆是一种属性）。每当我们要提及某事物时，我们使用一个名词；每当我们要提及一种属性时，我们使用一个形容词。人们曾提出这样的问题：“能否存在没有任何属性归属于它的事物？”这是一个令人困惑的问题，我不愿尝试回答它：让我们耸起鼻子，以轻蔑的沉默对待它，仿佛这真的不值得注意一样。但是，如果他们换一种方式提问，问道：“能否存在没有任何事物可供其归属的属性？”，我们可以立即回答说：“不行，正如婴儿不能无人照料就去乘火车旅行一样！”你从未见过“美丽”在空气中漂浮，或散落在地板上，而没有某事物去“是美丽的”，难道不是吗？

And now what am I driving at, in all this long rigmarole? It is this. You may put "is" or "are" between the names of two THINGS (for example, "some Pigs are fat Animals"), or between the names of two ATTRIBUTES (for example, "pink is light-red"), and in each case it will make good sense. But, if you put "is" or "are" between the name of a THING and the name of an ATTRIBUTE (for example, "some Pigs are pink"), you do NOT make good sense (for how can a Thing BE an Attribute?) unless you have an understanding with the person to whom you are speaking. And the simplest understanding would, I think, be this--that the Substantive shall be supposed to be repeated at the end of the sentence, so that the sentence, if written out in full, would be "some Pigs are pink (Pigs)". And now the word "are" makes quite good sense.

那么，我这番冗长的絮叨究竟要说明什么呢？要点是这样的。你可以在两个事物的名称之间放入 is 或 are（例如，“有些猪是肥胖的动物”），也可以在两个属性的名称之间放入 is 或 are（例如，“粉红是浅红”），这两种情况都讲得通。但如果你在一个事物的名称与一个属性的名称之间放入 is 或 are（例如，“有些猪是粉红的”），除非你和听话的人已有某种默契，否则就讲不通了（因为事物怎么能是一个属性呢？）。我想，最简单的默契是：假定名词在句末重复出现。这样，句子完整写出来就是“有些猪是粉红的（猪）”。现在，are 这个词便完全讲得通了。

Thus, in order to make good sense of the Proposition "some new Cakes are nice", we must suppose it to be written out in full, in the form "some new Cakes are nice (Cakes)". Now this contains two 'TERMS'--"new Cakes" being one of them, and "nice (Cakes)" the other. "New Cakes," being the one we are talking about, is called the 'SUBJECT' of the Proposition, and "nice (Cakes)" the 'PREDICATE'. Also this Proposition is said to be a 'PARTICULAR' one, since it does not speak of the WHOLE of its Subject, but only of a PART of it. The other two kinds are said to be 'UNIVERSAL', because they speak of the WHOLE of their Subjects--the one denying niceness, and the other asserting it, of the WHOLE class of "new Cakes". Lastly, if you would like to have a definition of the word 'PROPOSITION' itself, you may take this:--"a sentence stating that some, or none, or all, of the Things belonging to a certain class, called its 'Subject', are also Things belonging to a certain other class, called its 'Predicate'".

因此，为了使命题“有些新蛋糕是美味的”具有明确意义，我们必须将其完整写出，形式为“有些新蛋糕是美味的（蛋糕）”。现在，该命题包含两个‘项’——其中一个是“新蛋糕”，另一个是“美味的（蛋糕）”。由于我们谈论的是“新蛋糕”，它被称为该命题的‘主词’；而“美味的（蛋糕）”则被称为‘谓词’。此外，该命题被称为‘特称’命题，因为它并非论及其主词的全体，而仅涉及其中的一部分。另外两种类型被称为‘全称’命题，因为它们论及其主词的全体——一个否定美味性，另一个则断言美味性，针对的是“新蛋糕”这一整个类别。最后，如果您希望获得‘命题’一词的定义，可参考如下表述：“陈述属于某一特定类别（称为其‘主词’）的某些事物、无一事物或所有事物，同时也属于另一特定类别（称为其‘谓词’）的句子”。

You will find these seven words--PROPOSITION, ATTRIBUTE, TERM, SUBJECT, PREDICATE, PARTICULAR, UNIVERSAL--charmingly useful, if any friend should happen to ask if you have ever studied Logic. Mind you bring all seven words into your answer, and your friend will go away deeply impressed--'a sadder and a wiser man'.
你将会发现这七个词语——命题、属性、项、主词、谓词、特称、全称——妙用无穷，倘若有任何朋友偶然询问你是否曾研习过逻辑。务必将这七个词语全部纳入你的回答之中，你的朋友便会离去时深受触动——“一个更悲伤也更智慧的人”。

Now please to look at the smaller Diagram on the Board, and suppose it to be a cupboard, intended for all the Cakes in the world (it would have to be a good large one, of course). And let us suppose all the new ones to be put into the upper half (marked 'x'), and all the rest (that is, the NOT-new ones) into the lower half (marked 'x''). Thus the lower half would contain ELDERLY Cakes, AGED Cakes, ANTE-DILUVIAN Cakes--if there are any: I haven't seen many, myself--and so on. Let us also suppose all the nice Cakes to be put into the left-hand half (marked 'y'), and all the rest (that is, the not-nice ones) into the right-hand half (marked 'y''). At present, then, we must understand x to mean "new", x' "not-new", y "nice", and y' "not-nice."

现在请看棋盘上的较小图式，并假设它是一个橱柜，专为世间所有的蛋糕而设（当然，它必须是一个相当大的）。让我们假设所有新的都被放入上半部分（标记为'x'），而其余的（即非新的）则放入下半部分（标记为'x''）。因此，下半部分将包含年长的蛋糕、老化的蛋糕、大洪水前的蛋糕——如果有的话：我自己也没见过多少——等等。让我们也假设所有美味的蛋糕都被放入左半部分（标记为'y'），而其余的（即不美味的）则放入右半部分（标记为'y''）。因此，目前我们必须将 x 理解为“新的”，x' 理解为“非新的”，y 理解为“美味的”，y' 理解为“不美味的”。
And now what kind of Cakes would you expect to find in compartment No. 5?
那么，你现在会期望在 5 号隔间里找到什么样的蛋糕呢？

It is part of the upper half, you see; so that, if it has any Cakes in it, they must be NEW: and it is part of the left-hand half; so that they must be NICE. Hence if there are any Cakes in this compartment, they must have the double 'ATTRIBUTE' "new and nice": or, if we use letters, they must be "x y."
你瞧，它属于上半部分；因此，如果其中有任何蛋糕，它们必须是新的：而且它属于左半部分；因此它们必须是美味的。所以，如果这个隔间中有任何蛋糕，它们必须具有双重“属性”——“新且美味”；或者，如果我们用字母表示，它们必须是"x y"。

Observe that the letters x, y are written on two of the edges of this compartment. This you will find a very convenient rule for knowing what Attributes belong to the Things in any compartment. Take No. 7, for instance. If there are any Cakes there, they must be "x' y", that is, they must be "not-new and nice."
请注意，字母"x"和"y"写在这个格子的两条边上。你会发现这是一条非常方便的规则，用于知晓任何格子中属于事物的属性。以编号为"7"的格子为例：如果那里有蛋糕，它们必须是"x' y"，也就是说，它们必须是“非新的且美味的”。

Now let us make another agreement--that a red counter in a compartment shall mean that it is 'OCCUPIED', that is, that there are SOME Cakes in it. (The word 'some,' in Logic, means 'one or more' so that a single Cake in a compartment would be quite enough reason for saying "there are SOME Cakes here"). Also let us agree that a grey counter in a compartment shall mean that it is 'EMPTY', that is that there are NO Cakes in it. In the following Diagrams, I shall put '1' (meaning 'one or more') where you are to put a RED counter, and '0' (meaning 'none') where you are to put a GREY one.

现在让我们达成另一项约定：隔间内的红色筹码表示该处为“被占据”，即其中含有“有些”蛋糕。（在逻辑学中，“有些”一词意指“一个或多个”，因此隔间内仅有一块蛋糕便已足以作为断言“此处有‘有些’蛋糕”的理由）。同时，我们也约定：隔间内的灰色筹码表示该处为“空”，即其中不含任何蛋糕。在下述图式中，凡需放置红色筹码之处，我将标以"1"（意指“一个或多个”）；凡需放置灰色筹码之处，我将标以"0"（意指“无”）。
As the Subject of our Proposition is to be "new Cakes", we are only concerned, at present, with the UPPER half of the cupboard, where all the Cakes have the attribute x, that is, "new."
既然我们命题的主项是“新蛋糕”，那么目前我们只关心橱柜的上半部分，那里的所有蛋糕都具有属性 x，即“新的”。
Now, fixing our attention on this upper half, suppose we found it marked like this,
现在，将注意力固定在这一上半部分，假设我们发现它被标记如下，
that is, with a red counter in No. 5. What would this tell us, with regard to the class of "new Cakes"?
也就是说，在编号为 5 的格中放置一枚红色筹码。这关于“新蛋糕”这一类事物会告诉我们什么呢？

Would it not tell us that there are SOME of them in the x y-compartment? That is, that some of them (besides having the Attribute x, which belongs to both compartments) have the Attribute y (that is, "nice"). This we might express by saying "some x-Cakes are y-(Cakes)", or, putting words instead of letters,
这难道不是在告诉我们，在 x y 格室中存在着一些它们吗？也就是说，其中的一些（除了拥有同时属于两个格室的属性 x 之外）还拥有属性 y（即“好”）。我们可以用这样的话来表达：“有些 x-蛋糕是 y-(蛋糕)”，或者，用词语代替字母，
"Some new Cakes are nice (Cakes)",
“有些新的蛋糕是美味的（蛋糕）”，
or, in a shorter form,
或者，用更简短的形式表述，
"Some new Cakes are nice".
“有些新蛋糕是美味的。”

At last we have found out how to represent the first Proposition of this Section. If you have not CLEARLY understood all I have said, go no further, but read it over and over again, till you DO understand it. After that is once mastered, you will find all the rest quite easy.
终于，我们找到了表示本节第一个命题的方法。如果你尚未清晰地理解我所说的一切，请勿继续往下读，而应反复阅读，直到你真正理解为止。一旦这一点被掌握，你会发现其余部分都相当容易。

It will save a little trouble, in doing the other Propositions, if we agree to leave out the word "Cakes" altogether. I find it convenient to call the whole class of Things, for which the cupboard is intended, the 'UNIVERSE.' Thus we might have begun this business by saying "Let us take a Universe of Cakes." (Sounds nice, doesn't it?)
在推导其余命题时，若我们约定彻底略去“蛋糕”一词，便可省去些许麻烦。我发现将橱柜所容纳的整个事物类别称为‘宇宙’颇为便利。因此，我们本可如此开启此项工作：“让我们取一个由蛋糕构成的宇宙。”（听起来不错，不是吗？）

Of course any other Things would have done just as well as Cakes. We might make Propositions about "a Universe of Lizards", or even "a Universe of Hornets". (Wouldn't THAT be a charming Universe to live in?)
当然，其他任何东西也会像蛋糕一样同样有效。我们可以就“蜥蜴论域”或甚至“黄蜂论域”作出命题。（住在这样的论域里，岂不妙极了？）
So far, then, we have learned that
至此，我们已了解到
means "some x and y," i.e. "some new are nice."
表示“有些既是 x 又是 y”，即“有些新的是美味的”。
I think you will see without further explanation, that
我想您无需进一步解释便能明白，
means "some x are y'," i.e. "some new are not-nice."
意指"x 中有些是 y'"，即“有些新的并非好的”。
Now let us put a GREY counter into No. 5, and ask ourselves the meaning of
现在，让我们将一个灰色的筹码放入编号为 5 的格子中，并问自己其含义为何。
This tells us that the x y-compartment is EMPTY, which we may express by "no x are y", or, "no new Cakes are nice". This is the second of the three Propositions at the head of this Section.
这表明 x y 隔间是空的，我们可以将其表述为"x 都不是 y"，或“没有新的蛋糕是美味的”。这是本节开头的三个命题中的第二个。
In the same way,
同样地，
would mean "no x are y'," or, "no new Cakes are not-nice."
表示“没有 x 是 y′”，也就是说，“没有新蛋糕是不美味的”。
What would you make of this, I wonder?
我不禁想问，你会如何解读这一情形？
I hope you will not have much trouble in making out that this represents a DOUBLE Proposition: namely, "some x are y, AND some are y'," i.e. "some new are nice, and some are not-nice."
我希望您不会在辨认出这代表一个双重命题时遇到太多困难：即"x 中有些是 y，且有些是 y'"，换言之，“有些新的是美味的，也有些新的是不美味的”。
The following is a little harder, perhaps:
以下这道题或许更难一些：

This means "no x are y, AND none are y'," i.e. "no new are nice, AND none are not-nice": which leads to the rather curious result that "no new exist," i.e. "no Cakes are new." This is because "nice" and "not-nice" make what we call an 'EXHAUSTIVE' division of the class "new Cakes": i.e. between them, they EXHAUST the whole class, so that all the new Cakes, that exist, must be found in one or the other of them.
这表示“没有 x 是 y，也没有 x 是 y′”，即“没有新的是美味的，也没有新的是不美味的”；这得出一个颇为奇特的结果：“不存在新者”，也就是“没有蛋糕是新的”。这是因为“美味的”和“不美味的”对“新蛋糕”这一类构成了我们所谓的“穷尽性”划分：也就是说，二者合起来穷尽整个类，因此所有实际存在的新蛋糕，都必定落在其中一类之中。

And now suppose you had to represent, with counters the contradictory to "no Cakes are new", which would be "some Cakes are new", or, putting letters for words, "some Cakes are x", how would you do it?
现在假设你需用筹码来表示“没有蛋糕是新的”这一命题的矛盾命题，即“有些蛋糕是新的”，或者用字母代指词语，表述为“有些蛋糕是 x"，你将如何操作？

This will puzzle you a little, I expect. Evidently you must put a red counter SOMEWHERE in the x-half of the cupboard, since you know there are SOME new Cakes. But you must not put it into the LEFT-HAND compartment, since you do not know them to be NICE: nor may you put it into the RIGHT-HAND one, since you do not know them to be NOT-NICE.
这恐怕会让你感到有些困惑。显然，你必须将一枚红色筹码放在柜子的 x 半区中的某个地方，因为你已知有一些新的蛋糕。但你不能把它放进左边的隔间，因为你不知道它们是美味的；你也绝不能把它放进右边的隔间，因为你不知道它们是不美味的。

What, then, are you to do? I think the best way out of the difficulty is to place the red counter ON THE DIVISION-LINE between the xy-compartment and the xy'-compartment. This I shall represent (as I always put '1' where you are to put a red counter) by the diagram
那么，你该怎么做呢？我认为摆脱这一困境的最佳办法是将红色筹码置于 xy 格室与 xy′格室之间的分界线上。我将用图式来表示这一点（正如我始终在应放置红色筹码处标注'1'一样）：

Our ingenious American cousins have invented a phrase to express the position of a man who wants to join one or other of two parties--such as their two parties 'Democrats' and 'Republicans'--but ca'n't make up his mind WHICH. Such a man is said to be "sitting on the fence." Now that is exactly the position of the red counter you have just placed on the division-line. He likes the look of No. 5, and he likes the look of No. 6, and he doesn't know WHICH to jump down into. So there he sits astride, silly fellow, dangling his legs, one on each side of the fence!
我们天资聪颖的美国表亲们发明了一个短语，用来形容那种想要加入两个政党之一（例如他们的民主党与共和党），却拿不定主意究竟该选哪一个的人。这样的人被称为“骑在篱笆上”。现在，你刚刚放置在分界线上的那个红色筹码所处的位置正是如此。它既喜欢 No. 5 的样子，也喜欢 No. 6 的样子，却不知道应该跳进哪一个。于是它就那样跨坐在篱笆上，这个傻瓜，双腿悬空，一边在篱笆的这一侧，一边在那一侧！
Now I am going to give you a much harder one to make out. What does this mean?
现在我要给你们出一道更难理解的题目。这究竟是什么意思？

This is clearly a DOUBLE Proposition. It tells us not only that "some x are y," but also that "no x are NOT y." Hence the result is "ALL x are y," i.e. "all new Cakes are nice", which is the last of the three Propositions at the head of this Section.
这显然是一个双重命题。它不仅告诉我们"x 中有些是 y"，还表明"x 中没有一个是非 y"。因此得出的结论是"x 都是 y"，即“所有新的蛋糕都是美味的”，这正是本节开头三个命题中的最后一个。
We see, then, that the Universal Proposition
由此可见，全称命题
"All new Cakes are nice"
“所有新的蛋糕都是美味的。”
consists of TWO Propositions taken together, namely,
由两个命题共同构成，即，
"Some new Cakes are nice," and "No new Cakes are not-nice."
“有些新蛋糕是美味的，”以及“没有新蛋糕是不美味的。”
In the same way
同样地
would mean "all x are y' ", that is,
将意味着"x 所有都是 y'"，即，
"All new Cakes are not-nice."
“所有新的蛋糕都不是美味的。”
Now what would you make of such a Proposition as "The Cake you have given me is nice"? Is it Particular or Universal?
那么，对于这样一个命题“你给我的蛋糕很好吃”，你会作何感想？它是特称的还是全称的？
"Particular, of course," you readily reply. "One single Cake is hardly worth calling 'some,' even."
“特称，当然，”你爽快地回答，“哪怕‘有些’也几乎不值得用来称呼‘一块蛋糕’。”

No, my dear impulsive Reader, it is 'Universal'. Remember that, few as they are (and I grant you they couldn't well be fewer), they are (or rather 'it is') ALL that you have given me! Thus, if (leaving 'red' out of the question) I divide my Universe of Cakes into two classes--the Cakes you have given me (to which I assign the upper half of the cupboard), and those you HAVEN'T given me (which are to go below)--I find the lower half fairly full, and the upper one as nearly as possible empty. And then, when I am told to put an upright division into each half, keeping the NICE Cakes to the left, and the NOT-NICE ones to the right, I begin by carefully collecting ALL the Cakes you have given me (saying to myself, from time to time, "Generous creature! How shall I ever repay such kindness?"), and piling them up in the left-hand compartment. AND IT DOESN'T TAKE LONG TO DO IT!

不，我亲爱的冲动读者，这是“全称”的。请记住，它们虽少（我承认不可能再少了），但它们（或者更确切地说，“它是”）就是你所给我的全部！因此，如果（暂且不论“红色”）我将我的蛋糕论域分为两类——你给我的蛋糕（我将其分配在橱柜的上半部分），以及你没有给我的蛋糕（这些将放在下面）——我发现下半部分相当满，而上半部分几乎空无一物。然后，当被告知在每个半部分中放入一个垂直划分，将“美味”的蛋糕留在左边，将“不美味”的蛋糕放在右边时，我首先仔细收集所有你给我的蛋糕（时不时对自己说：“慷慨的人！我将如何报答这样的好意？”），并将它们堆在左边的隔间里。这做起来并不花多长时间！

Here is another Universal Proposition for you. "Barzillai Beckalegg is an honest man." That means "ALL the Barzillai Beckaleggs, that I am now considering, are honest men." (You think I invented that name, now don't you? But I didn't. It's on a carrier's cart, somewhere down in Cornwall.)
这是又一个供你思考的全称命题：“巴兹莱·贝克阿利格是个诚实的人。”其含义是：“我此刻所考虑的所有巴兹莱·贝克阿利格都是诚实的人。”（你以为这个名字是我编造的，对吗？其实不是。它写在康沃尔某处的一辆运货马车上。）
This kind of Universal Proposition (where the Subject is a single Thing) is called an 'INDIVIDUAL' Proposition.
这种全称命题（其中主项是单一事物）被称为“个别”命题。
Now let us take "NICE Cakes" as the Subject of our Proposition: that is, let us fix our thoughts on the LEFT-HAND half of the cupboard, where all the Cakes have the attribute y, that is, "nice."
现在让我们以“美味的蛋糕”作为我们的命题的主项：也就是说，让我们将思绪固定在橱柜的左半部分，那里的所有蛋糕都具有属性 y，即“美味”。
Suppose we find it marked like this:-- What would that tell us?
假设我们发现它被标记如下： 那会告诉我们什么呢？
I hope that it is not necessary, after explaining the HORIZONTAL oblong so fully, to spend much time over the UPRIGHT one. I hope you will see, for yourself, that this means "some y are x", that is,
我希望在如此详尽地解释了水平长方形之后，不必再花费太多时间去阐述垂直长方形。我希望你们能自行看出，这意指"y 中有些是 x"，即，
"Some nice Cakes are new."
“有些不错的蛋糕是新的。”

"But," you will say, "we have had this case before. You put a red counter into No. 5, and you told us it meant 'some new Cakes are nice'; and NOW you tell us that it means 'some NICE Cakes are NEW'! Can it mean BOTH?"
“但是，”你会说，“我们以前遇到过这种情况。你把一枚红色筹码放入第 5 号格中，并告诉我们它意味着‘有些新蛋糕是好吃的’；而现在你又告诉我们它意味着‘有些好吃的蛋糕是新的’！它能同时表示这两者吗？”

The question is a very thoughtful one, and does you GREAT credit, dear Reader! It DOES mean both. If you choose to take x (that is, "new Cakes") as your Subject, and to regard No. 5 as part of a HORIZONTAL oblong, you may read it "some x are y", that is, "some new Cakes are nice": but, if you choose to take y (that is, "nice Cakes") as your Subject, and to regard No. 5 as part of an UPRIGHT oblong, THEN you may read it "some y are x", that is, "some nice Cakes are new". They are merely two different ways of expressing the very same truth.

这是一个非常深思熟虑的问题，亲爱的读者，您问得极好！它确实同时意味着两者。如果您选择将 x（即“新蛋糕”）作为主项，并将第 5 号视为一个横向长方形的部分，那么您可以将其读作"x 有些是 y"，也就是说，“有些新蛋糕是美味的”；但是，如果您选择将 y（即“美味的蛋糕”）作为主项，并将第 5 号视为一个纵向长方形的部分，那么您就可以将其读作"y 有些是 x"，也就是说，“有些美味的蛋糕是新的”。它们仅仅是表达同一真理的两种不同方式。

Without more words, I will simply set down the other ways in which this upright oblong might be marked, adding the meaning in each case. By comparing them with the various cases of the horizontal oblong, you will, I hope, be able to understand them clearly.
不再赘言，我将直接列出这种直立长方形可标记的其他方法，并逐一说明其含义。希望通过与水平长方形的各种情形加以比较，您便能清晰地理解它们。
You will find it a good plan to examine yourself on this table, by covering up first one column and then the other, and 'dodging about', as the children say.
你会发现，按照此表自我检验是个好办法：先遮住一列，再遮住另一列，就像孩子们所说的“躲来躲去”那样。
Also you will do well to write out for yourself two other tables--one for the LOWER half of the cupboard, and the other for its RIGHT-HAND half.
此外，你最好为自己另外写出两张表格——一张用于橱柜的下半部分，另一张用于其右半部分。
And now I think we have said all we need to say about the smaller Diagram, and may go on to the larger one.
至此，我想我们已把关于较小图式所需说的话说完了，可以继续探讨较大的那个了。

Two more remarks about Propositions need to be made.
关于命题还有两点需要说明。

One is that, in every Proposition beginning with "some" or "all", the ACTUAL EXISTENCE of the 'Subject' is asserted. If, for instance, I say "all misers are selfish," I mean that misers ACTUALLY EXIST. If I wished to avoid making this assertion, and merely to state the LAW that miserliness necessarily involves selfishness, I should say "no misers are unselfish" which does not assert that any misers exist at all, but merely that, if any DID exist, they WOULD be selfish.
其一，凡以"some"或"all"开头的每一个命题，都断言了“主项”的实际存在。例如，若我说“所有吝啬鬼都是自私的”，我的意思是吝啬鬼确实存在。倘若我欲避免作出此项断言，而仅陈述吝啬必然涉及自私这一法则，我便应说“没有吝啬鬼是不自私的”。此句并不断言有任何吝啬鬼存在，而仅仅表明：倘若真有吝啬鬼存在，他们便会是自私的。

The other is that, when a Proposition begins with "some" or "no", and contains more than two Attributes, these Attributes may be re-arranged, and shifted from one Term to the other, "ad libitum." For example, "some abc are def" may be re-arranged as "some bf are acde," each being equivalent to "some Things are abcdef". Again "No wise old men are rash and reckless gamblers" may be re-arranged as "No rash old gamblers are wise and reckless," each being equivalent to "No men are wise old rash reckless gamblers."
另一种情况是，当一个命题以“有些”或“没有”开头，且包含超过两个属性时，这些属性可以重新排列，并随意从一个项移至另一个项。例如，“有些 abc 是 def"可重新排列为“有些 bf 是 acde"，二者均等价于“有些事物是 abcdef"。又如，“没有明智的老者是鲁莽且轻率的赌徒”可重新排列为“没有鲁莽的老赌徒是明智且轻率的”，二者均等价于“没有人是明智的、老的、鲁莽的、轻率的赌徒”。
2. Syllogisms
2. 三段论

Now suppose we divide our Universe of Things in three ways, with regard to three different Attributes. Out of these three Attributes, we may make up three different couples (for instance, if they were a, b, c, we might make up the three couples ab, ac, bc). Also suppose we have two Propositions given us, containing two of these three couples, and that from them we can prove a third Proposition containing the third couple. (For example, if we divide our Universe for m, x, and y; and if we have the two Propositions given us, "no m are x'" and "all m' are y", containing the two couples mx and my, it might be possible to prove from them a third Proposition, containing x and y.)

现在假设，我们按照三种不同的属性，以三种方式分别划分我们的事物宇宙。由这三种属性可以组成三对不同的组合（例如，若它们是 a、b、c，便可组成 ab、ac、bc 这三对）。又假设给定两个命题，涉及这三对中的两对，并且可以从它们证明一个涉及第三对的第三个命题。（例如，若我们按 m、x、y 这三种属性划分事物宇宙，又给定“没有 m 是 x′”与“所有 m′ 都是 y”这两个命题，涉及 mx 与 my 这两对，那么有可能从中证明一个涉及 x 与 y 的第三个命题。）
In such a case we call the given Propositions 'THE PREMISSES', the third one 'THE CONCLUSION' and the whole set 'A SYLLOGISM'.
在这种情况下，我们将给定的命题称为“前提”，第三个称为“结论”，而整个集合则称为“三段论”。
Evidently, ONE of the Attributes must occur in both Premisses; or else one must occur in ONE Premiss, and its CONTRADICTORY in the other.
显然，必须有同一个属性在两个前提中都出现；或者，一个属性出现在一个前提中，而它的矛盾属性出现在另一个前提中。

In the first case (when, for example, the Premisses are "some m are x" and "no m are y'") the Term, which occurs twice, is called 'THE MIDDLE TERM', because it serves as a sort of link between the other two Terms.
在第一种情况（例如，前提是“有些 m 是 x”和“没有 m 是 y′”）下，出现两次的项被称为“中项”，因为它充当了另外两个项之间的一种联结。
In the second case (when, for example, the Premisses are "no m are x'" and "all m' are y") the two Terms, which contain these contradictory Attributes, may be called 'THE MIDDLE TERMS'.
在第二种情形下（例如，前提是“没有 m 是 x'"和“所有 m' 都是 y"）这两个包含这些矛盾属性的项可称为‘中项’。
Thus, in the first case, the class of "m-Things" is the Middle Term; and, in the second case, the two classes of "m-Things" and "m'-Things" are the Middle Terms.
因此，在第一种情形中，"m-事物”这一类是中项；而在第二种情形中，"m-事物”与"m'-事物”这两类则是中项。
The Attribute, which occurs in the Middle Term or Terms, disappears in the Conclusion, and is said to be "eliminated", which literally means "turned out of doors".
出现在一个或两个中项中的属性，会在结论中消失，这称为“被消去”，字面意思是“被赶出门外”。
Now let us try to draw a Conclusion from the two Premisses--
现在让我们尝试从两个前提中得出一个结论——
"Some new Cakes are unwholesome; No nice Cakes are unwholesome."
有些新蛋糕是不健康的； 没有美味的蛋糕是不健康的。

In order to express them with counters, we need to divide Cakes in THREE different ways, with regard to newness, to niceness, and to wholesomeness. For this we must use the larger Diagram, making x mean "new", y "nice", and m "wholesome". (Everything INSIDE the central Square is supposed to have the attribute m, and everything OUTSIDE it the attribute m', i.e. "not-m".)
为了用筹码表示它们，我们需要按三种不同的属性分别划分蛋糕：是否是新的、是否美味、是否有益健康。为此，必须使用较大的图式，使 x 表示“新的”，y 表示“美味的”，m 表示“有益健康的”。（假定中央方格内的所有事物都具有属性 m，方格外的所有事物都具有属性 m′，即“非 m”。）
You had better adopt the rule to make m mean the Attribute which occurs in the MIDDLE Term or Terms. (I have chosen m as the symbol, because 'middle' begins with 'm'.)
你最好采用这条规则：让 m 表示出现在一个或两个中项中的属性。（我选用 m 作符号，是因为英语 middle（中间的）以 m 开头。）

Now, in representing the two Premisses, I prefer to begin with the NEGATIVE one (the one beginning with "no"), because GREY counters can always be placed with CERTAINTY, and will then help to fix the position of the red counters, which are sometimes a little uncertain where they will be most welcome.
现在，在表述两个前提时，我倾向于从否定命题（即以“没有”开头的那个）开始，因为灰色筹码总能被确定地放置，随后它们将有助于固定红色筹码的位置，而后者有时对于其最适宜安放之处尚存些许不确定。

And now what counters will this information enable us to place in the SMALLER Diagram, so as to get some Proposition involving x and y only, leaving out m? Let us take its four compartments, one by one.
那么，这些信息将使我们能够在较小的图式中放置哪些筹码，以便得出仅涉及 x 和 y 的某个命题，而排除 m？让我们逐一考察它的四个部分。

First, No. 5. All we know about THIS is that its OUTER portion is empty: but we know nothing about its inner portion. Thus the Square MAY be empty, or it MAY have something in it. Who can tell? So we dare not place ANY counter in this Square.
首先，关于 5 号。我们已知的是其外部部分是空的：但我们对其内部部分一无所知。因此，方格可能是空的，也可能含有某物。谁能说得清？所以，我们不敢在此方格中放置任何筹码。

Secondly, what of No. 6? Here we are a little better off. We know that there is SOMETHING in it, for there is a red counter in its outer portion. It is true we do not know whether its inner portion is empty or occupied: but what does THAT matter? One solitary Cake, in one corner of the Square, is quite sufficient excuse for saying "THIS SQUARE IS OCCUPIED", and for marking it with a red counter.
其次，关于第 6 号又如何？在此我们稍好一些。我们知道其中必有某物，因为其外部区域有一枚红色筹码。诚然，我们尚不知其内部区域是空着还是被占据：但这又有什么关系呢？在方格的一个角落里仅有一枚孤立的蛋糕，就足以作为宣称“此方格已被占据”的理由，并为其标记上一枚红色筹码。
As to No. 7, we are in the same condition as with No. 5--we find it PARTLY 'empty', but we do not know whether the other part is empty or occupied: so we dare not mark this Square.
至于编号 7，我们处于与编号 5 相同的境地——我们发现它部分为“空”，但我们不知道其余部分是空还是被占据：因此我们不敢标记这个方格。
And as to No. 8, we have simply no information at all.
至于第 8 号，我们完全没有任何信息。

Our 'Conclusion', then, must be got out of the rather meagre piece of information that there is a red counter in the xy'-Square. Hence our Conclusion is "some x are y' ", i.e. "some new Cakes are not-nice (Cakes)": or, if you prefer to take y' as your Subject, "some not-nice Cakes are new (Cakes)"; but the other looks neatest.
因此，我们的“结论”必须从这一点相当贫乏的信息中得出：xy′ 方格中有一枚红筹码。所以结论是“有些 x 是 y′”，即“有些新蛋糕是不美味的（蛋糕）”；或者，如果你愿意以 y′ 为主项，也可以说“有些不美味的蛋糕是新的（蛋糕）”。不过，前一种说法最简洁。
We will now write out the whole Syllogism, putting the symbol ∴ for "therefore", and omitting "Cakes", for the sake of brevity, at the end of each Proposition.
我们现在将写出完整的三段论，用符号∴表示“因此”，为求简略起见，在每个命题的末尾省略“蛋糕”一词。
"Some new Cakes are unwholesome; No nice Cakes are unwholesome ∴ Some new Cakes are not-nice."
“有些新蛋糕是不健康的； 没有好吃的蛋糕是不健康的； ∴ 有些新蛋糕不是好吃的。”

And you have now worked out, successfully, your first 'SYLLOGISM'. Permit me to congratulate you, and to express the hope that it is but the beginning of a long and glorious series of similar victories!
至此，您已成功推导出第一个“三段论”。请允许我向您表示祝贺，并期望这只是漫长而辉煌的一系列类似胜利的开始！

We will work out one other Syllogism--a rather harder one than the last--and then, I think, you may be safely left to play the Game by yourself, or (better) with any friend whom you can find, that is able and willing to take a share in the sport.
我们将再推演一个三段论——其难度较前一个更大一些——然后，我想，你就可以放心地独自玩这个游戏了，或者（更佳）与任何你能找到的、且有能力并愿意参与这项运动的友人一同游戏。
Let us see what we can make of the two Premisses--
让我们看看能从这两个前提中得出什么结论——
"All Dragons are uncanny; All Scotchmen are canny."
“所有龙都是非 canny 的（uncanny）； 所有苏格兰人都是 canny 的（精明的）。”

Remember, I don't guarantee the Premisses to be FACTS. In the first place, I never even saw a Dragon: and, in the second place, it isn't of the slightest consequence to us, as LOGICIANS, whether our Premisses are true or false: all WE have to do is to make out whether they LEAD LOGICALLY TO THE CONCLUSION, so that, if THEY were true, IT would be true also.
请记住，我并未保证前提为事实。首先，我从未见过龙；其次，对我们逻辑学家而言，前提是真还是假都无关紧要：我们只需阐明它们是否合乎逻辑地推导出结论，使得若它们为真，则结论亦为真。

You see, we must give up the "Cakes" now, or our cupboards will be of no use to us. We must take, as our 'Universe', some class of things which will include Dragons and Scotchmen: shall we say 'Animals'? And, as "canny" is evidently the Attribute belonging to the 'Middle Terms', we will let m stand for "canny", x for "Dragons", and y for "Scotchmen". So that our two Premisses are, in full,
你看，我们现在必须放下“蛋糕”，否则这些橱柜就对我们毫无用处了。我们必须选取一类包含龙与苏格兰人的事物作为“论域”：就说“动物”，如何？而“精明的”（canny）显然是属于“中项”的属性，因此我们让 m 表示“精明的”（canny），x 表示“龙”，y 表示“苏格兰人”。这样，我们的两个前提完整写出就是：
"All Dragon-Animals are uncanny (Animals); All Scotchman-Animals are canny (Animals)."
“所有龙类动物都是非 canny 的（uncanny，动物）； 所有苏格兰人类动物都是 canny 的（精明的，动物）。”
And these may be expressed, using letters for words, thus:--
这些可用字母代表词语，表述如下：——
"All x are m'; All y are m."
所有的 x 都是 m'； 所有的 y 都是 m。
The first Premiss consists, as you already know, of two parts:--
第一个前提正如你已所知，由两部分组成：——
"Some x are m'," and "No x are m."
"有些 x 是 m'，"且"没有 x 是 m。"
And the second also consists of two parts:--
第二个前提也由两部分组成：——
"Some y are m," and "No y are m'."

Let us take the negative portions first.
让我们先来看否定部分。

And now what Conclusion can we read off from this? Well, it is impossible to pack such abundant information into ONE Proposition: we shall have to indulge in TWO, this time.
那么，我们又能从这得出什么结论呢？嗯，不可能将如此丰富的信息塞进一个命题中；这次我们将不得不使用两个命题。
First, by taking x as Subject, we get "all x are y'", that is,
首先，以 x 为主语，我们得到"x 都是 y'"，即，
"All Dragons are not-Scotchmen":
“所有龙皆非苏格兰人”：
secondly, by taking y as Subject, we get "all y are x'", that is,
其次，以 y 为主语，我们得到"y 都是 x'"，即，
"All Scotchmen are not-Dragons".
“所有苏格兰人皆非龙。”
Let us now write out, all together, our two Premisses and our brace of Conclusions.
让我们现在将我们的两个前提和一对结论全部写出来。
"All Dragons are uncanny; All Scotchmen are canny. ∴ All Dragons are not-Scotchmen; All Scotchmen are not-Dragons."
“所有龙都是非 canny 的（uncanny）； 所有苏格兰人都是 canny 的（精明的）。 ∴ 所有龙都不是苏格兰人； 所有苏格兰人都不是龙。”

Let me mention, in conclusion, that you may perhaps meet with logical treatises in which it is not assumed that any Thing EXISTS at all, but "some x are y" is understood to mean "the Attributes x, y are COMPATIBLE, so that a Thing can have both at once", and "no x are y" to mean "the Attributes x, y are INCOMPATIBLE, so that nothing can have both at once".
最后再提一点：你或许会遇到一些逻辑著作，其中并不预设有任何事物实际存在，而把“有些 x 是 y”理解为“属性 x、y 是相容的，因此一个事物能够同时具有这两种属性”，把“没有 x 是 y”理解为“属性 x、y 是不相容的，因此没有任何事物能够同时具有这两种属性”。
In such treatises, Propositions have quite different meanings from what they have in our 'Game of Logic', and it will be well to understand exactly what the difference is.
在诸如此类的论著中，命题的含义与我们《逻辑游戏》中的含义截然不同，因此最好确切地理解二者之间的差异。

First take "some x are y". Here WE understand "are" to mean "are, as an actual FACT"--which of course implies that some x-Things EXIST. But THEY (the writers of these other treatises) only understand "are" to mean "CAN be", which does not at all imply that any EXIST. So they mean LESS than we do: our meaning includes theirs (for of course "some x ARE y" includes "some x CAN BE y"), but theirs does NOT include ours. For example, "some Welsh hippopotami are heavy" would be TRUE, according to these writers (since the Attributes "Welsh" and "heavy" are quite COMPATIBLE in a hippopotamus), but it would be FALSE in our Game (since there are no Welsh hippopotami to BE heavy).

首先取“有些 x 是 y"。在此，我们理解“是”意味着“作为实际事实‘是’"——这当然蕴含有些 x-事物存在。但那些作者（撰写其他论著者）仅将“是”理解为“可以是”，这并不意味任何事物存在。因此他们的含义少于我们的：我们的含义包含他们的（因为当然“有些 x 是 y"包含“有些 x 可以是 y"），但他们的含义不包含我们的。例如，根据这些作者，“有些威尔士河马是重的”为真（因为属性“威尔士的”与“重的”在河马身上完全兼容），但在我们的游戏中则为假（因为根本没有威尔士河马，因而无从说它们是重的）。

Secondly, take "no x are y". Here WE only understand "are" to mean "are, as an actual FACT"--which does not at all imply that no x CAN be y. But THEY understand the Proposition to mean, not only that none ARE y, but that none CAN POSSIBLY be y. So they mean more than we do: their meaning includes ours (for of course "no x CAN be y" includes "no x ARE y"), but ours does NOT include theirs. For example, "no Policemen are eight feet high" would be TRUE in our Game (since, as an actual fact, no such splendid specimens are ever found), but it would be FALSE, according to these writers (since the Attributes "belonging to the Police Force" and "eight feet high" are quite COMPATIBLE: there is nothing to PREVENT a Policeman from growing to that height, if sufficiently rubbed with Rowland's Macassar Oil--which is said to make HAIR grow, when rubbed on hair, and so of course will make a POLICEMAN grow, when rubbed on a Policeman).

第二，取“没有 x 是 y”。这里，我们只是把“是”理解为“作为实际事实是”——这丝毫不能推出“没有 x 能够是 y”。但他们把这个命题理解为：不但没有 x 实际上是 y，而且没有 x 可能是 y。因此，他们表达的比我们多：他们的含义包含我们的含义（因为“没有 x 能够是 y”当然包含“没有 x 实际上是 y”），但我们的含义不包含他们的。例如，“没有警察身高八英尺”，在我们的游戏中为真（因为就实际事实而言，从未发现过如此出色的标本）；但按照那些作者的理解，它却是假（因为“属于警察队伍”与“八英尺高”这两个属性完全相容：如果在警察身上充分涂擦 Rowland's Macassar Oil，没有什么能阻止他长到那样高——据说这油抹在头发上能让头发生长，因此当然，抹在警察身上就能让警察长高）。

Thirdly, take "all x are y", which consists of the two partial Propositions "some x are y" and "no x are y'". Here, of course, the treatises mean LESS than we do in the FIRST part, and more than we do in the SECOND. But the two operations don't balance each other--any more than you can console a man, for having knocked down one of his chimneys, by giving him an extra door-step.
第三，取“所有 x 都是 y”，它由“有些 x 是 y”和“没有 x 是 y′”这两个部分命题组成。这里，当然，在第一个部分，那些论著表达的比我们少；在第二个部分，它们表达的又比我们多。但这两种变化并不会相互抵消——就像你推倒了一个人的一座烟囱，不能靠再给他一层门阶就使他得到安慰一样。

If you meet with Syllogisms of this kind, you may work them, quite easily, by the system I have given you: you have only to make 'are' mean 'are CAPABLE of being', and all will go smoothly. For "some x are y" will become "some x are capable of being y", that is, "the Attributes x, y are COMPATIBLE". And "no x are y" will become "no x are capable of being y", that is, "the Attributes x, y are INCOMPATIBLE". And, of course, "all x are y" will become "some x are capable of being y, and none are capable of being y'", that is, "the Attributes x, y are COMPATIBLE, and the Attributes x, y' are INCOMPATIBLE." In using the Diagrams for this system, you must understand a red counter to mean "there may POSSIBLY be something in this compartment," and a grey one to mean "there cannot POSSIBLY be anything in this compartment."

若遇到这种三段论，你可以用我给出的系统轻易演算：只需让“是”表示“能够是”，一切就会顺利进行。“有些 x 是 y”就会变成“有些 x 能够是 y”，即“属性 x、y 是相容的”。“没有 x 是 y”会变成“没有 x 能够是 y”，即“属性 x、y 是不相容的”。当然，“所有 x 都是 y”会变成“有些 x 能够是 y，而且没有 x 能够是 y′”，即“属性 x、y 是相容的，而且属性 x、y′ 是不相容的”。将图式用于这种系统时，必须把红色筹码理解为“这个隔间里可能有某物”，把灰色筹码理解为“这个隔间里不可能有任何东西”。
3. Fallacies.
3. 谬误。

And so you think, do you, that the chief use of Logic, in real life, is to deduce Conclusions from workable Premisses, and to satisfy yourself that the Conclusions, deduced by other people, are correct? I only wish it were! Society would be much less liable to panics and other delusions, and POLITICAL life, especially, would be a totally different thing, if even a majority of the arguments, that are scattered broadcast over the world, were correct! But it is all the other way, I fear. For ONE workable Pair of Premisses (I mean a Pair that lead to a logical Conclusion) that you meet with in reading your newspaper or magazine, you will probably find FIVE that lead to no Conclusion at all: and, even when the Premisses ARE workable, for ONE instance, where the writer draws a correct Conclusion, there are probably TEN where he draws an incorrect one.

因此，您想必也认为，逻辑在现实生活中的主要用途，是从可操作的前提推导出结论，并确信他人得出的结论是正确的？我多么希望事实果真如此！倘若散布于世界各地的论点中，即便有半数以上是正确的，那么社会将少得多恐慌及其他妄想，尤其是政治生活，也将全然不同。但恐怕恰恰相反。每遇到一个在报刊杂志阅读中能导向逻辑结论的可操作前提对（此处指能推导出逻辑结论的前提对），您大概会发现五个根本无法导向任何结论的前提对；而且，即便前提确实是可操作的，每有一例作者得出正确结论的情况，恐怕就有十例得出错误结论的情况。
In the first case, you may say "the PREMISSES are fallacious": in the second, "the CONCLUSION is fallacious."
在第一种情形下，你可以说“前提是谬误”；在第二种情形下，则说“结论是谬误”。
The chief use you will find, in such Logical skill as this Game may teach you, will be in detecting 'FALLACIES' of these two kinds.
你将在本游戏所能教授的这种逻辑技巧中找到的主要用途，在于识别这两类“谬误”。

The first kind of Fallacy--'Fallacious Premisses'--you will detect when, after marking them on the larger Diagram, you try to transfer the marks to the smaller. You will take its four compartments, one by one, and ask, for each in turn, "What mark can I place HERE?"; and in EVERY one the answer will be "No information!", showing that there is NO CONCLUSION AT ALL. For instance,
第一类谬误——“谬误前提”——当你在大图式上标出标记后，试图将这些标记转移到小图式时，便会察觉出来。你将依次取它的四个部分，对每一个分别发问：“我在此处能放置什么标记？”；而在每一个部分，答案都是“没有信息！”，这表明根本没有任何结论。例如，
"All soldiers are brave; Some Englishmen are brave. ∴ Some Englishmen are soldiers."
“所有士兵都是勇敢的； 有些英国人是勇敢的。 ∴有些英国人是士兵。”

looks uncommonly LIKE a Syllogism, and might easily take in a less experienced Logician. But YOU are not to be caught by such a trick! You would simply set out the Premisses, and would then calmly remark "Fallacious PREMISSES!": you wouldn't condescend to ask what CONCLUSION the writer professed to draw--knowing that, WHATEVER it is, it MUST be wrong. You would be just as safe as that wise mother was, who said "Mary, just go up to the nursery, and see what Baby's doing, AND TELL HIM NOT TO DO IT!"
看上去极像是一个三段论，很容易诱使经验不足的逻辑学家上当。但你不会被这种诡计所蒙蔽！你只需列出前提，然后平静地指出“前提谬误！”；你不会屈尊去询问作者声称推导出了什么结论——因为你知道，无论它是什么，必定是错误的。你将像那位明智的母亲一样安全，她说：“玛丽，到楼上的育儿室去，看看宝宝在做什么，叫他别做！”

The other kind of Fallacy--'Fallacious Conclusion'--you will not detect till you have marked BOTH Diagrams, and have read off the correct Conclusion, and have compared it with the Conclusion which the writer has drawn.
另一种谬误——“错误的结论”——你只有在标记了两个图式、读出了正确的结论，并将其与作者所推导出的结论加以比较之后，才能察觉。

But mind, you mustn't say "FALLACIOUS Conclusion," simply because it is not IDENTICAL with the correct one: it may be a PART of the correct Conclusion, and so be quite correct, AS FAR AS IT GOES. In this case you would merely remark, with a pitying smile, "DEFECTIVE Conclusion!" Suppose, for example, you were to meet with this Syllogism:--
但请注意，切勿仅因其不与正确答案完全相同便断言其为“谬误结论”：它可能是正确结论的一部分，因此在其所及范围内是完全正确的。在这种情况下，你只需带着怜悯的微笑评道：“有缺陷的结论！”举例来说，假如你遇到如下这个三段论：
"All unselfish people are generous; No misers are generous. ∴ No misers are unselfish."
“所有无私的人都是慷慨的； 没有吝啬鬼是慷慨的。 ∴ 没有吝啬鬼是无私的。”
the Premisses of which might be thus expressed in letters:--
其前提可如此用字母表述如下：——
"All x' are m; No y are m."
"所有的 x' 都是 m； 没有任何一个 y 是 m。"

Here the correct Conclusion would be "All x' are y'" (that is, "All unselfish people are not misers"), while the Conclusion, drawn by the writer, is "No y are x'," (which is the same as "No x' are y," and so is PART of "All x' are y'.") Here you would simply say "DEFECTIVE Conclusion!" The same thing would happen, if you were in a confectioner's shop, and if a little boy were to come in, put down twopence, and march off triumphantly with a single penny-bun. You would shake your head mournfully, and would remark "Defective Conclusion! Poor little chap!" And perhaps you would ask the young lady behind the counter whether she would let YOU eat the bun, which the little boy had paid for and left behind him: and perhaps SHE would reply "Sha'n't!"

此处正确的结论应为“所有 x' 都是 y'"（即，“所有不自私的人都不是吝啬鬼”），而作者得出的结论却是"y 没有一个是 x'"（这与"x' 没有一个是 y"相同，并且只是"x' 都是 y'"的一部分）。在此情况下，你只需说“结论有缺陷！”同样的事情也会发生：如果你身处一家糖果店，一个小男孩走进来，放下两便士，然后得意洋洋地拿着一个售价一便士的小圆面包离开。你会悲哀地摇摇头，并评论道：“结论有缺陷！可怜的小家伙！”也许你会询问柜台后面的那位年轻女士，是否允许你吃掉那个小男孩付过钱并遗留下的圆面包；而她或许会回答：“不行！”

But if, in the above example, the writer had drawn the Conclusion "All misers are selfish" (that is, "All y are x"), this would be going BEYOND his legitimate rights (since it would assert the EXISTENCE of y, which is not contained in the Premisses), and you would very properly say "Fallacious Conclusion!"
但是，如果在上述例子中，作者得出的结论是“所有吝啬鬼都是自私的”（即，“所有 y 都是 x"），这就超出了他的合法权利（因为它断言了 y 的存在，而这一存在并不包含在前提之中），那么您完全有理由说：“谬误性的结论！”

Now, when you read other treatises on Logic, you will meet with various kinds of (so-called) 'Fallacies' which are by no means ALWAYS so. For example, if you were to put before one of these Logicians the Pair of Premisses
现在，当你阅读其他逻辑学论著时，你会遇到各种各样的（所谓的）“谬误”，它们绝非总是如此。例如，如果你将这些前提对中的一对摆在这些逻辑学家面前，
"No honest men cheat; No dishonest men are trustworthy."
“诚实的人从不欺诈； 不诚实的人不可信赖。”

and were to ask him what Conclusion followed, he would probably say "None at all! Your Premisses offend against TWO distinct Rules, and are as fallacious as they can well be!" Then suppose you were bold enough to say "The Conclusion is 'No men who cheat are trustworthy'," I fear your Logical friend would turn away hastily--perhaps angry, perhaps only scornful: in any case, the result would be unpleasant. I ADVISE YOU NOT TO TRY THE EXPERIMENT!
若有人问他由此得出的结论为何，他大概会回答：“毫无结论！你的前提违背了两条截然不同的规则，且谬误之甚已达极致！”再假设你胆大妄为地宣称“结论是‘没有欺诈的人是可信赖的’"，我恐怕你那位逻辑学朋友会仓促转身离去——或许带着怒气，或许仅含轻蔑；无论如何，结果都将令人不快。我劝你不要尝试这项实验！

"But why is this?" you will say. "Do you mean to tell us that all these Logicians are wrong?" Far from it, dear Reader! From THEIR point of view, they are perfectly right. But they do not include, in their system, anything like ALL the possible forms of Syllogisms.
“可是，这又是为什么呢？”你会说，“难道你是想告诉我们，所有这些逻辑学家都错了吗？”恰恰相反，亲爱的读者！从他们自己的观点来看，他们是完全正确的。但是，在他们的体系中，并未包含所有可能的三段论形式。

They have a sort of nervous dread of Attributes beginning with a negative particle. For example, such Propositions as "All not-x are y," "No x are not-y," are quite outside their system. And thus, having (from sheer nervousness) excluded a quantity of very useful forms, they have made rules which, though quite applicable to the few forms which they allow of, are no use at all when you consider all possible forms.
他们对于以否定词开头的属性怀有一种神经质的恐惧。例如，诸如"所有非 x 都是 y"、"没有 x 是非 y"这样的命题，完全超出了他们的体系。因此，由于纯粹的神经质而排除了大量非常有用的形式后，他们制定了一些规则；这些规则虽然完全适用于他们所允许的少数形式，但当你考虑到所有可能的形式时，却毫无用处。

Let us not quarrel with them, dear Reader! There is room enough in the world for both of us. Let us quietly take our broader system: and, if they choose to shut their eyes to all these useful forms, and to say "They are not Syllogisms at all!" we can but stand aside, and let them Rush upon their Fate! There is scarcely anything of yours, upon which it is so dangerous to Rush, as your Fate. You may Rush upon your Potato-beds, or your Strawberry-beds, without doing much harm: you may even Rush upon your Balcony (unless it is a new house, built by contract, and with no clerk of the works) and may survive the foolhardy enterprise: but if you once Rush upon your FATE--why, you must take the consequences!

亲爱的读者，让我们不要与他们争吵！世界上有足够的空间容纳我们双方。让我们平静地采纳我们的更广泛的体系：倘若他们执意闭目无视所有这些有用的形式，并声称“它们根本不是三段论！”那我们只能退立一旁，听任他们冲向他们的命运！在你的一切事物中，几乎没有比冲向你的命运更为危险的了。你可以冲向你的土豆田或草莓田而不至于造成多大伤害；你甚至可能冲向你的阳台（除非那是一座新盖的、凭合同建造且没有工地监工的房屋），而且可能在这场鲁莽的冒险后仍然生还：但一旦你冲向你的命运——那么，你就必须承担后果！

CROOKED ANSWERS.
曲折的答案
"I answered him, as I thought good, 'As many as red-herrings grow in the wood'."

1. Elementary.
1. 基础问题。

1. Whatever can be "attributed to", that is "said to belong to", a Thing, is called an 'Attribute'. For example, "baked", which can (frequently) be attributed to "Buns", and "beautiful", which can (seldom) be attributed to "Babies".
1. 凡能“归属于”某物，也就是“说成属于”某物的，便称为“属性”。例如，“烤熟的”这个属性（常常）可以归给“小圆面包”；“美丽的”这个属性（很少）可以归给“婴儿”。
2. When they are the Names of two Things (for example, "these Pigs are fat Animals"), or of two Attributes (for example, "pink is light red").
2. 当它们是两种事物的名称时（例如，“这些猪是肥胖的动物”），或是两种属性的名称时（例如，“粉红色是浅红色”）。
3. When one is the Name of a Thing, and the other the Name of an Attribute (for example, "these Pigs are pink"), since a Thing cannot actually BE an Attribute.
3. 当一个是事物的名称，另一个是属性的名称时（例如，“这些猪是粉红色的”），因为事物实际上不可能是属性。
4. That the Substantive shall be supposed to be repeated at the end of the sentence (for example, "these Pigs are pink (Pigs)").
4. 应当认为句末重复了一次那个名词（例如，“这些猪是粉红色的〔猪〕”）。

5. A 'Proposition' is a sentence stating that some, or none, or all, of the Things belonging to a certain class, called the 'Subject', are also Things belonging to a certain other class, called the 'Predicate'. For example, "some new Cakes are not nice", that is (written in full) "some new Cakes are not nice Cakes"; where the class "new Cakes" is the Subject, and the class "not-nice Cakes" is the Predicate.
5. “命题”是这样一种句子：它陈述属于某个类（称为“主项”）的事物中，有些、没有一个或所有，也属于另一个类（称为“谓项”）。例如，“有些新蛋糕不好吃”，完整写出就是“有些新蛋糕是不好吃的蛋糕”；其中，“新蛋糕”这个类是主项，“不好吃的蛋糕”这个类是谓项。
[See p. 37]
[参见第37页]
6. A Proposition, stating that SOME of the Things belonging to its Subject are so-and-so, is called 'Particular'. For example, "some new Cakes are nice", "some new Cakes are not nice."
6. 陈述其主项所属事物中“有些”是如此这般的命题，称为“特称命题”。例如，“有些新蛋糕好吃”，“有些新蛋糕不好吃”。
A Proposition, stating that NONE of the Things belonging to its Subject, or that ALL of them, are so-and-so, is called 'Universal'. For example, "no new Cakes are nice", "all new Cakes are not nice".
陈述其主项所属事物中“没有一个”或“所有”是如此这般的命题，称为“全称命题”。例如，“没有新蛋糕是好吃的”，“所有新蛋糕都不好吃”。
7. The Things in each compartment possess TWO Attributes, whose symbols will be found written on two of the EDGES of that compartment.

9. As a name of the class of Things to which the whole Diagram is assigned.

11. When the whole class, thus divided, is "exhausted" among the sets into which it is divided, there being no member of it which does not belong to some one of them. For example, the class "new Cakes" is "exhaustively" divided into "nice" and "not-nice" since EVERY new Cake must be one or the other.

If the Universe of Things be divided with regard to three different Attributes; and if two Propositions be given, containing two different couples of these Attributes; and if from these we can prove a third Proposition, containing the two Attributes that have not yet occurred together; the given Propositions are called 'the Premisses', the third one 'the Conclusion', and the whole set 'a Syllogism'. For example, the Premisses might be "no m are x'" and "all m' are y"; and it might be possible to prove from them a Conclusion containing x and y.
22. 如果把事物的论域按三个不同属性划分，给定两个命题，各包含这些属性中不同的一对；又能由此证明第三个命题，包含此前未曾一起出现的两个属性，那么，给定的命题称为“前提”，第三个命题称为“结论”，这一整组称为“三段论”。例如，前提可以是“没有 m 是 x′”与“所有 m′ 都是 y”；由此也许能够证明一个包含 x 和 y 的结论。

注意：这不是合格的前提，因为结论实际上已经是第二个前提的一部分，第一个前提因而是多余的。用字母可以这样表示：

"All xm are y" contains "Some xm are y", which contains "Some x are y". Or, in words, "All rainy days are tiresome" contains "Some rainy days are tiresome", which contains "Some rainy periods are tiresome".
“所有 xm 都是 y”包含“有些 xm 是 y”，后者又包含“有些 x 是 y”。或者用文字说，“所有下雨的日子都令人厌倦”包含“有些下雨的日子令人厌倦”，后者又包含“有些下雨的时段令人厌倦”。
